- The extension and server used different heuristics to extract YouTube video IDs, causing the background worker to miss valid `youtu.be`, Shorts, embed, and live URLs and incorrectly report "no transcript" for those pages.
- Centralizing the parsing logic prevents contract drift between packages and ensures consistent transcript lookup and fallback behavior across extension and server.

### Description
- Added a shared helper `shared/youtubeUrl.ts` that robustly extracts a canonical YouTube video id for watch, `youtu.be`, `/shorts/:id`, `/embed/:id`, and `/live/:id` URL shapes, and rejects non-YouTube hosts.
- Updated the extension background to import and use `extractYouTubeId` for both transcript fetching and YouTube source metadata creation (`extension/src/background/index.ts`).
- Replaced the server-local parser implementation with a re-export of the shared helper (`server/src/utils/youtube.ts`) and expanded `server/src/utils/youtube.test.ts` with tests for embed, live, and non-YouTube host rejection.
- Files changed: `shared/youtubeUrl.ts`, `extension/src/background/index.ts`, `server/src/utils/youtube.ts`, and `server/src/utils/youtube.test.ts`.

- Ran server unit tests with `cd server && npm test`, and all tests passed after the change (previous failing non-YouTube-host test fixed).

author: somanysteves
body:
## Summary

- `Manager_onShellMessage` called `Window_getHidden` on every shell event, which unconditionally ran `WinGetTitle` (`GetWindowText` → `SendMessage WM_GETTEXT`, no timeout). When Edge/Slack windows were slow to service `WM_GETTEXT` post-reconnect (sleep/resume, network reconnect), the AHK thread blocked for seconds — bug.n appeared hung, required Ctrl+Alt+Del to recover, and repeated until the window settled.
- Class-first short-circuit: `WinGetClass` without `DetectHiddenWindows` returns non-empty for any visible top-level window, so a populated class alone proves visibility — no title fetch needed on the fast path. The slow path (class empty without DHW) re-queries with DHW and uses `Window_getTitleNonBlocking`, preserving hang protection for the rare hidden-window case.
- `ByRef wndTitle` is now empty when the function short-circuits; the one caller that needs the title for visible windows (`Manager_getWindowInfo`, the hotkey-driven debug helper) fetches it directly.

## Validation

Local A/B against `master`, same session, 3 runs per bench scenario:

| metric | master | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| `window_spawn / Manager_onShellMessage` median (the hang) | ~1350 ms (3/3 runs) | 523 ms (1 run), no slow-path samples in 2/3 runs |
| `view_switch_populated / Monitor_activateView_hide` median | 66 ms | 127 ms |

The hang path effectively stops firing — when a slow window has a non-empty class on the first `WinGetClass` (the normal case), the title fetch never happens, so there's nothing to block on.

The `Monitor_activateView_hide` median is ~60 ms above master on populated view-switches. Code-wise the new function does strictly less work than master (`WinGetClass` + assignment vs `WinGetClass` + `WinGetTitle`), so I expected it to be faster; the residual gap is small (~0.6 ms per Window_getHidden call) and within scheduling-noise territory but reproducible. Net trade is multi-second hang ↔ ~60 ms on populated view-switches.

Several other phases improved over master (`view_switch_populated/Tiler_stackTiles` −45 %, `Window_activate` −21 %, `Bar_updateView` p95 −67 %).

## Test plan

- [x] `build.bat` passes
- [x] `test.bat` — 126/126 pass
- [x] Bench: `perf`, `urgent`, `dispatch`, `titlestorm` — 3 runs each, all PASS
- [ ] Hang repro: click Slack in Edge after sleep/resume; verify bug.n no longer freezes

author: chuangw6
body:
### Context

We are using openrl as part of a self-hosted continuous learning stack (OpenRL -> OpenClaw-RL -> OpenClaw) where an AI agent (OpenClaw) learns from live user interactions in real time. Each user turn is intercepted, scored, and submitted by OpenClaw-RL to the open-rl training server as an RL training datum — a full prompt + response sequence. The system prompt carries a large tool list, so prompts reach **12,000–13,000 tokens** by the third conversational turn.

Once a batch is collected, OpenClaw-RL triggers the open-rl server to run a forward and backward pass through the full prompt + response sequences on a LoRA-wrapped Qwen3-4B model.

### Problem

Training crashes with CUDA OOM on A100 80GB when the first batch triggers `forward_backward`.

Without gradient checkpointing, the backward pass requires retaining **all intermediate activation tensors across all 36 layers** of Qwen3-4B simultaneously. For 13k-token sequences this accumulates to ~70 GiB of activations — exceeding the GPU before the backward pass even begins.

### Solution

Enable gradient checkpointing on the PEFT model in `create_adapter`, reducing activation memory from ~70 GiB to a few GiB by recomputing layer activations on demand during backward instead of storing them all. The trade-off is ~30% slower training steps due to the recomputation.

Two calls are required together:
- `gradient_checkpointing_enable()` — stops storing all intermediate activations
- `enable_input_require_grads()` — PEFT/LoRA compatibility fix: without it, checkpointing silently no-ops because frozen base model inputs have `requires_grad=False`

Togglable via `ENABLE_GRADIENT_CHECKPOINTING` env var (default: on).

author: babychucks
body:
Implemented the foundational portal architecture and initial official-facing onboarding workflow for the FlashID frontend. Also added some initial routing functionality to system.

### Portal Routing & Shared Layout Architecture

*  Introduced the (portal) route group structure using the Next.js App Router to allow for 'protected' pages to be grouped together and portals to share a `layout.tsx`.
* Implemented a reusable `AppShell` layout wrapper for all authenticated portal pages.
* Centralised shared portal UI structure in `Appshell`:
  * Sidebar
  * Top navigation bar
  * Scrollable content area


### Navigation System Updates

Updated `navigation.ts` to support:

* Officials navigation sections
* Route configuration for official portal pages
* Sidebar integration with route-based navigation
* Dynamic sidebar icon mapping


### Dynamic Page Header Configuration

* Added configurable page header mapping system.
* Implemented route-based title and description rendering inside `AppTopBar`.
* Decoupled page metadata from `AppShell` logic for easier scalability and maintainability.

### Onboard Citizen Frontend

Implemented the initial frontend workflow for the Home Affairs Official onboarding process, including:

* Retrieve identity record UI
* Contact detail capture
* Consent confirmation
* Pending account creation flow
* Activation code workflow
* Audit log preview
* Onboarding status indicators

### Under Construction Placeholder Page

Created a reusable `UnderConstructionPage` component for unfinished routes/pages.

This allows:

* Navigation to incomplete features without breaking routing
* Placeholder support for future portal modules
* Cleaner incremental frontend development


### Notes

* Organised page components by role:
  * `officials`
  * `citizen`
  * `gov-admin`

This PR focuses on establishing scalable frontend architecture and the initial official onboarding experience. Backend integration, session management, and real data wiring will be added in future iterations.

author: iwasa-kosui
body:
## 背景

PR作成ワークフローは `/pr` slash command として運用してきたが、明示的にコマンドを打たないと起動しない。実装が一区切りした自然な文脈や、「PRを作って」「リモートに上げて」程度の発話でも、PR description が「背景／内容／論点」原則に沿った状態で自動的に組み立たって欲しい。

## 内容

slash command を skill 形式に移行することで、Claude Code の skill triggering 機構（description に列挙したフレーズと意図のマッチ）に PR 作成ワークフローを委ねる。明示呼び出しを前提とした command UI を捨て、自動発動できる skill 一本に集約することで、`/pr` を打ち忘れた場合のフォールバックや、agent driven のシナリオでも同じワークフローが走るようにする。description は強めに（積極的にトリガーするよう）書くことで under-triggering を回避している。ポリシー本体（Conventional Commits・draft 強制・「背景／内容／論点」3点構成）は変更せず移植のみ。

## 論点

- skill 一本化に伴い `/pr` command UI は撤去した。明示的にスラッシュコマンドで呼びたいケースが残るなら、薄いラッパー command（skill への委譲だけ書く）を復活させる選択肢もある
- description のトリガーフレーズ列挙は現状の感覚で書いたものなので、実運用で over/under triggering が観測されたら skill-creator の description optimization で調整する余地がある

## Test Plan

- [ ] このPR自体が skill によって作成されていること（dogfooding）
- [ ] マージ後 `chezmoi apply` で `~/.claude/skills/pr/SKILL.md` が展開されること
- [ ] 新規セッションで「PRを作って」と言うだけで skill が発動すること

The repo had an unstable blog-post update workflow due to feed endpoint/parsing fragility, and production deployment to Hostinger was requested. This PR makes feed selection resilient and adds a dedicated production deploy workflow.

    - `production` environment

    - deploy target `/public_html/`
    - excludes for `.git` and `.github` paths

- name: Pull in posts

## Summary
This PR implements a complete chapter president onboarding flow and dashboard experience, allowing newly approved chapter presidents to get set up with their chapters and manage day-to-day operations.

## Key Changes

### Onboarding Flow
- **New onboarding page** (`app/(app)/chapter/onboarding/page.tsx`): Redesigned with a 4-step checklist (Meet Your Team, Set Chapter Goals, Review Resources, Send Intro Message)
- **Step-specific UI**: Each step has dedicated content—roster display for team introductions, text areas for goals and messages, resource links
- **Progress tracking**: Visual progress bar and completion status with congratulations message when done
- **Server actions**: New `saveChapterGoals()` and `saveIntroMessage()` actions to persist president input
- **Status recomputation**: Onboarding status automatically transitions to COMPLETED when all steps are done

### President Dashboard
- **New dashboard page** (`app/(app)/chapter/dashboard/page.tsx`): Central hub for chapter presidents to manage their chapter
- **Key metrics**: Display student/instructor/parent counts and upcoming events
- **Chapter goals display**: Shows goals set during onboarding with expandable original vision statement
- **Quick actions grid**: Links to recruiting, calendar, channels, updates, settings, and member-facing chapter view
- **Onboarding banner**: Prompts incomplete onboarding with progress indicator
- **Recent roster**: Shows 8 most recently added members

### Chapter President Application Enhancements
- **Interview scheduling UI** (cp-detail-panel.tsx): Admins can now schedule interviews with optional meeting URLs (Zoom/Google Meet links)
- **Recommendation workflow**: New fields for `decisionRecommendation` and `recommendationRationale` allowing reviewers to submit recommendations before final approval/rejection
- **Status transitions**: Added INFO_REQUESTED status and proper state management for interview scheduling and recommendation submission
- **External intake support**: New `createExternalChapterPresidentApplicant()` function mirrors instructor intake, supporting Google Forms and manual admin entry with optional pre-scheduled interviews

### Admin External Applicant Intake
- **Applicant kind selector**: Admin-only toggle to create either Instructor or Chapter President applicants
- **CP-specific fields**: Interview date/time and meeting URL inputs for chapter president applications
- **Form validation**: Proper URL validation and date/time handling

### Navigation & Routing
- **New navigation entries**: Added President Dashboard to navigation catalog
- **Redirect updates**: Updated auth redirects to use `/login` instead of `/auth/signin`
- **Page guards**: Dashboard uses `requirePageRoles()` to enforce ADMIN/CHAPTER_PRESIDENT access

### Database & Schema
- **New migrations**: Added `decisionRecommendation` and `recommendationRationale` fields to ChapterPresidentApplication
- **Interview meeting URL**: Added `interviewMeetingUrl` field for storing Zoom/Meet links
- **Status tracking**: Added `completedAt` timestamp for onboarding completion

### UI/UX Improvements
- **Consistent styling**: Uses page-shell, page-header, card, and button components throughout
- **Role labels**: Centralized ROLE_LABELS mapping for consistent user role display
- **Resource links**: Contextual resource cards on onboarding page linking to key features
- **Status page integration**: Application status page now displays interview meeting URLs when available

## Notable Implementation Details
- Onboarding status is computed server-side from individual step flags, automatically transitioning to COMPLETED
- Interview scheduling and recommendation submission are separate operations with proper validation and error handling
- External chapter president applicant intake mirrors the instructor pipeline but with CP-specific fields
- Dashboard metrics are fetched in parallel using Promise.all for performance
- All pages use `force-dynamic` to ensure fresh data on each request

body:
## Conceptual + visual upgrade

### Conceptual: 切 → 分裂 (more accurate articulation)

Per Ööna's signal-check: "切" (cut, external action) doesn't quite capture what's actually happening. The real word is **分裂** (fragmentation/splitting — internal, structural, self-induced). We don't get *cut* by the world — we *split* ourselves: shadow from light, parts from whole, role from role.

Applied throughout signa/index.html:
- 不切 → **不分裂** / not splitting
- 根本不能切 → **我們本來就是不可分裂的整體** / we have always been an indivisible whole
- All instances of 切 as verb → 分裂
- Added Ööna's shadow-splitting framing: 「我們把自己的 shadow 跟光明面分裂、把不同的自己分裂出去、把該整合的部分推到看不見的地方」 / "We split our shadow from our light, split parts of ourselves into the unseen, push aside what was meant to be integrated."

author: jeong-sik
body:
## 요약

`lib/keeper/keeper_unified_turn.ml:448` 의 livelock guard가 *같은 (keeper, turn_id) 튜플*에 대해 30초 주기 supervisor sweep마다 동일 ERROR 라인을 재방출.

**System_log 2026-05-19 evidence (10min slice)**:
- `sangsu turn=651` × 28회
- `nick0cave turn=766` × 29회
- `echo turn=61` × 25회
- `analyst turn=445` × 25회
- **합 107회/10min → 약 15K events/day** steady-state projection

guard 자체는 *correct* (block 시점에 turn이 progress 불가). 문제는 *log noise* — 같은 사실이 turn당 30번씩 재방출.

## 변경 (옵션 A — typed escalation)

신규 sub-library `lib/keeper_livelock_state/`:
- **Closed sum type** `gate_kind` 2-variant (`Attempts_exhausted` / `Stuck_age_exceeded`) — `Keeper_turn_livelock.gate_reason` mirror
- `record_outcome` = `` [`First | `Repeated | `Threshold_park] ``
- `default_park_threshold = 5` (5회 동일 block 후 single ERROR escalation + counter)
- Hashtbl + Mutex + (keeper, turn_id, gate_kind) fingerprint
- `record_block`, `reset_for_keeper`, `cardinality`, `block_count` API

`lib/keeper/keeper_unified_turn.ml` patch — guard Blocked 시 `record_block` 호출:
- `` `First `` → 기존 ERROR 유지 (behavior 보존)
- `` `Repeated `` → DEBUG demote
- `` `Threshold_park `` → 단일 ERROR + Prometheus `metric_keeper_livelock_threshold_park_total` increment

## 검증

- `opam exec -- ocamlformat --check` (touched 5 files) → clean
- `git diff --check origin/main..HEAD` → clean
- **Standalone alcotest 13/13 PASS in 9ms** (ocamlfind direct compile, dune lock 회피)
  - record_block 6 cases (First/Repeated×3/Threshold_park/distinct keepers/distinct kinds)
  - reset 2 cases (targeted keeper / all kinds)
  - introspection 2 cases (cardinality / missing key)
  - production scenario 1 case: *4 keepers 2026_05_19* (실제 system_log 패턴 검증)
  - 추가 boundary 2 cases

## 측정 예측 (24h)

`keeper turn livelock guard blocked dispatch` ERROR 라인 ≈ 90% 감소:
- 4 keeper × 5 First + 4 Threshold_park = ~24 ERROR + ~83 DEBUG demote (현재 107회 → ~24회).
- Steady-state 15K/day → ~1.5K ERROR + 13.5K DEBUG.

## WORKAROUND-CARRYOVER

이 모듈은 *symptom suppression* — root fix는 `Keeper.Unified_turn` / supervisor가 livelock 후 turn finalize (`Disp_pause_human`) 또는 next sweep back-off. 그 변경은 supervisor lifecycle 영향 큰 *별도 RFC* scope. 본 PR은 *log noise 90% 감소*만 즉시 적용, root fix는 deferred.

RFC-WAIVED: `lib/keeper_livelock_state/` 신규 sub-library + keeper_unified_turn.ml call-site patch만, credential/sandbox/operator 영역 미변경, MASC/OAS Error-Warn Reduction Goal §P5 keeper_stale_watchdog SSOT 인접 인용.

Co-Authored-By: Claude (subagent ETA-LIVELOCK + main wrap-up after watchdog stall, /loop iter 18, 2026-05-19)

### Motivation

- The agent service needs an endpoint to record Maya→human handoffs and trigger Twilio SMS fan-out to either currently-available staff or an after-hours fallback list. 
- `src/modules/ai/socket.server.ts` (WebSocket chat server) is dead code and should be removed to reduce maintenance burden.

### Description
- Moved/reintroduced the Block 109/112 SQL into the top-level `migrations/` directory as `migrations/2026_05_18_call_events_v109.sql` and `migrations/2026_05_18_tasks_assignee_outbound_v112.sql`, and added idempotent migrations `migrations/2026_05_18_outbound_caller_id_seed_v112b.sql` and `migrations/2026_05_18_maya_fallback_recipients_v115.sql` to seed the BF outbound caller ID and ensure the `staff_presence` availability index. 
- Added `src/services/notifications/staffSms.ts`, a Twilio SMS fan-out helper that selects recipients from either currently-available staff (via `staff_presence` join) or the `MAYA_FALLBACK_SMS_NUMBERS` env CSV and logs delivery/partial-failure details. 
- Added a new route `POST /api/communications/maya-handoff` (mounted at `/api/communications/maya-handoff`) which requires Admin/Staff roles, validates `recipients`, inserts into `maya_escalations` and `communications_messages` (`type='maya_handoff'`), and invokes the SMS fan-out helper.

### Testing

author: rjwalters
body:
## Summary (post-judge-feedback scope reduction)

Ships the infrastructure half of #3063: a new `_try_lateral_via_escape()` helper that retries strict-mode in-pad deferrals with an off-pad via along the natural escape direction, plus a fix for an origin-related bounds bug in `_can_place_via`, plus 10 synthetic-fixture tests.

**The board-04 customer half of #3063 was reverted in this PR.** The judge ran the originally-proposed strict-mode opt-in against a fresh baseline and found it regresses board 04 (9/9 nets -> 8/9 nets + 7 new DRC errors including segment/segment overlaps). The builder's "6/9 -> 8/9" comparison had been measured against a stale baseline.

**Follow-up filed**: #3073 (investigate WHY strict-mode + lateral helper regresses board 04; the helper SHOULD find a clean candidate for the dropped net's pin).

## Key changes (preserved)

- **`src/kicad_tools/router/escape.py`**
  - New `_try_lateral_via_escape()` helper: walks outward along the escape direction in 0.05 mm steps, validating each candidate via `_can_place_via` (same predicate as the in-pad rescue). The search budget is auto-derived from pad geometry (`proj_half + via_radius + clearance + step`) so fine-pitch oblong pads (LQFP-48 0.3 x 1.5 mm) get enough room to escape the own pad copper.
  - Wires the lateral helper into all 3 dispatcher call sites that forward `strict_in_pad_clearance` to `_try_in_pad_escape`. The QFP-alternating site uses `primary_dir` (perpendicular outward from chip body) -- NOT the alt direction, which for odd-index pins is along-edge and would search into the next pin in the row.
  - **Fixes `_can_place_via` grid bounds check to be origin-aware**: pre-fix was `0 <= x <= grid.width`, which was implicitly correct only for grids constructed with `origin_x=origin_y=0`. Boards whose grid sits at non-zero origin (e.g. board 04 at world coords ~(95, 90)) had every world-coord candidate rejected on bounds. The fix uses `origin_x <= x <= origin_x + grid.width`. Without this fix the lateral re-attempt is a no-op on real boards.

- **`tests/test_escape_lateral_recovery.py` (NEW, 10 tests)**: pins
  - Success case: open lane, lateral via found at smallest valid offset (0.10 mm with pinned geometry note)
  - Failure cases: blocked SOUTH lane, unsupported manufacturer, `VIA_DOWN` sentinel direction
  - Strict-gating contract: legacy mode (strict=False) skips the lateral helper
  - Dispatcher wiring: spy assertions on both strict-on and strict-off
  - `_can_place_via` bounds: origin-aware acceptance and rejection on offset grids (pins the grid-origin fix against regression)

## Changes (reverted post-judge-feedback)

- **`boards/04-stm32-devboard/generate_design.py`**: the `--strict-in-pad-clearance` opt-in has been removed. `--seed 42` is kept (generic determinism win from #3039, unrelated to strict mode). The docstring records the experiment outcome and references the follow-up investigation (#3073).
- **`boards/04-stm32-devboard/output/*`**: regenerated WITHOUT strict mode. Routing reports **9/9 nets (100%)**; `kct check --mfr jlcpcb-tier1` reports **6 DRC errors** (3 `clearance_segment_via`, 2 `clearance_pad_via`, 1 `connectivity` GND-stitch). Matches the origin/main baseline.

## Why the strict-mode opt-in was reverted

Judge's measurements at `--seed 42`:

| Metric | Pure baseline (origin/main) | This PR with `--strict-in-pad-clearance` |
|---|---|---|
| Nets connected | **9 / 9** | 8 / 9 |
| Total DRC errors | **6** | 13 |
| Includes severely overlapping copper (-0.200 mm clearance)? | no | **yes** |

The builder's earlier "6/9 -> 8/9" win was measured against a stale baseline that did not include the routing improvements that have since landed on `main`. Net-net the strict-mode opt-in is a regression on this customer board today.

The lateral helper itself is sound (10 synthetic-fixture tests pass).  The question of why it does not find a clean candidate for board 04's dropped pin is captured in follow-up issue #3073.

## Board 04 results (after revert, `--seed 42`, full `kct route` pipeline)

| Metric | Value |
|---|---|
| Nets connected (routing) | **9 / 9 (100%)** |
| Total DRC errors (`kct check --mfr jlcpcb-tier1`) | **6** |

body:
## Summary

Removes the unconditional `t.Skip` from `cli/e2e_orch_test.go` so all three Tier 1 orch-variant tests (`TestE2E_ThreeWorkers_StarFanout`, `TestE2E_FullMissionLoop`, `TestE2E_HubRestart_MidMission`) now actually run under `-tags=orch_e2e`. They drive real `orch-spawn claude --sesh-session <label>` subprocesses through committed recipe fixtures executed by a stub-claude script.

Addresses **item 1** of [sesh#75](https://github.com/danmestas/sesh/issues/75). Items 2 (T1.3 budget instrumentation) and 3 (mock/orch consolidation tradeoff) are deferred to separate PRs.

## What landed

**Fixtures (`cli/testdata/orch_e2e/`):**

- `stub-claude.sh` — non-interactive stand-in for `claude`. Ignores all CLI flags (`--dangerously-skip-permissions`, `--append-system-prompt-file`, etc.). Reads a recipe path from `$SESH_E2E_RECIPE` env var or the `./.stub-claude-recipe` pointer file in cwd, runs the recipe via `bash`, writes a `.stub-claude-done` marker, and exits.
- `worker-mission.recipe`, `verifier-mission.recipe` — T1.2 fixtures (full mission loop).
- `fanout-alpha.recipe`, `fanout-beta.recipe`, `fanout-gamma.recipe` — T1.1 fixtures (star fanout).
- `hubrestart-pre.recipe`, `hubrestart-post.recipe` — T1.3 fixtures (hub restart).
- `README.md` documenting the fixture wiring and the operator override surface.

**Test wiring (`cli/e2e_orch_test.go`):**

- Per-test PATH shim with `claude` -> `stub-claude.sh` so `orch-spawn claude` resolves to the stub.
- Per-test `ORCH_HEADLESS_SESSION` isolates the test's tmux pane from the operator's real `orch-headless` session.
- `ORCH_SESH_BIN` points orch-spawn's `sesh worker-cwd` shellout at the test-built binary.
- `--no-shim --no-fleet --headless` flags drop the NATS-bus shim, fleet-doctrine prompt file, and host-tmux requirement.
- Recipe handoff is via `.stub-claude-recipe` written into the checkout before invoking orch-spawn. The file is a single-line pointer to the source-of-truth recipe. (tmux's existing server strips most env vars from new panes — `$SESH_E2E_RECIPE` would not propagate through tmux; a file in cwd is the robust handoff.)

## Auto-resolve behavior

Default behavior requires **no operator env-var setup**. Tests auto-resolve to fixtures under `cli/testdata/orch_e2e/`. They SKIP cleanly when `orch-spawn`, `tmux`, or `fossil` isn't on PATH.

To override (e.g. point at real claude):

```bash
SESH_E2E_CLAUDE=/path/to/claude \
SESH_E2E_RECIPE_DIR=/path/to/recipes \
go test -tags=orch_e2e ./cli/ -run TestE2E -v
```

## Finding surfaced

Recipes register a synthetic e2e user via `fossil user new <name> <name> '' || true` then commit as `USER=<name> fossil commit -m "..."`. The sesh-seeded project repo only has `hub` and `nobody` in its user table; without an entry for the committer, `fossil commit` rejects with "cannot determine user". Real orch workers run under an operator already in the user table; the fixture stands that step in. Documented in `cli/testdata/orch_e2e/README.md`.

Not filed as an upstream issue — the seed user-table is correct as-is (the seed code commits via libfossil's direct path, which bypasses fossil-CLI's user check). The real-world worker path also bypasses this because operators are typically registered. The test fixture is the only path that needs the synthetic user.

## Test plan

- [x] `go test -tags=orch_e2e ./cli/ -run TestE2E -count=1 -timeout 360s -v` — 3 passed locally (T1.1, T1.2, T1.3).
- [x] `go test ./... -count=1 -timeout 600s` — 233 passed locally (full default suite green).
- [x] `go vet ./...` clean.
- [x] `go vet -tags=orch_e2e ./...` clean.
- [x] `gofmt -l` clean on touched files.
- [x] No leftover tmux sessions or zombie processes after test runs.
- [x] stub-claude.sh committed with executable bit (`100755`).
- [ ] CI green on linux runner.

## What's deferred

- Item 2 of sesh#75 — T1.3 budget instrumentation (record first-success latency, possibly tighten the 15s budget to 5s).
- Item 3 of sesh#75 — mock/orch file consolidation tradeoff. Now that the orch variant is runnable (not scaffold), the Ousterhout change-amplification concern is materially smaller. Item 3 stays parked unless the parallel-file maintenance burden gets noisy.

author: anbangr
body:
## Summary

Closes the **PREMATURE_COMPLETION** skill-fault class observed in four 2026-05-18 mitosis incident reports, plus hardens the manual-recovery path that the same incident reports relied on.

The original investigation reports asserted "checkboxes are written incrementally per sub-step." That mechanism does not exist in shipped code (5 flip sites in cli.ts, all gated). Re-investigation under this branch found the **actual** mechanism: `restartFeatureFromOriginIssues` rewinds a `committed` phase to `tests_green` to re-run review, but did NOT un-flip the plan markdown checkboxes. A subsequent re-run failure → status=failed + checkboxes=[x][x][x] → PREMATURE_COMPLETION fires. Plus three of the four faults were rescued by `--mark-phase-committed` silently force-marking over a dirty worktree, leaving the next phase to start on inconsistent state.

**Three layers of fix** (all defensive, all backwards-compatible):

- **Atomic `unflipPhaseCheckboxes`** ([plan-mutator.ts](build/orchestrator/plan-mutator.ts)) — the symmetric counterpart of `reconcilePhaseCheckboxes`. Validates all targets first, then ONE atomic temp+rename write. ANY validation error → no writes, errors returned, plan markdown unchanged byte-for-byte. Markdown follows state backward as faithfully as it follows forward.

- **Fail-closed `restartFeatureFromOriginIssues`** ([cli.ts](build/orchestrator/cli.ts#L3465)) — run un-flip BEFORE advancing state. If un-flip returns errors, pause the feature with `plan markdown drift` reason and explicit manual-recovery instructions. **Phase status STAYS `committed`**; the rewind never happens, so the markdown's [x][x][x] is still accurate. PREMATURE_COMPLETION cannot fire.

- **`--commit-dirty` / `--force-dirty` flags on `--mark-phase-committed`** ([cli.ts](build/orchestrator/cli.ts#L5439)) — refuses to mark a phase committed when the worktree is dirty unless the operator explicitly chose a policy. Plus fail-closed when `git status` itself errors (e.g. stale `.git/index.lock`), bypassed only by `--force-dirty`.

## Reviews

| Review | Verdict | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Internal combined review (lens: structural + maintainability + adversarial) | CLEAR (1 finding auto-fixed) | Caught the silent-pass-on-git-status-error case (fixed in `1a9e7f98`). |
| Codex adversarial challenge (read-only, model_reasoning_effort=high) | **BLOCK on first pass** → CLEAR after `c24a0e01` | Codex correctly identified that the original un-flip wrapper console.warn'd on error but still advanced state, recreating the PREMATURE_COMPLETION bug class. This was the killer finding. Fixed: atomic un-flip + fail-closed restart. |
| Existing review log | No prior reviews on this branch | Ship ran the full pre-landing review pipeline. |

## Test Coverage

Coverage audit (ship-time subagent): **65% → ~80%** after closing two gaps surfaced by the audit (parseArgs flag wiring, unflipPhaseCheckboxes error-accumulation path).

```
unflipPhaseCheckboxes              ★★★ — 6 tests (atomicity + round-trip + idempotent + markers + error path)
restartFeatureFromOriginIssues     ★★★ — 5 tests (legacy callers + rewind + FAIL-CLOSED on drift)
markPhaseCommittedAfterManualRecovery dirty-guard
                                   ★★★ — 12 tests (7 happy paths + git-error fail-closed + --force-dirty bypass)
parseArgs --force-dirty/--commit-dirty
                                   ★★  — 5 tests (defaults, each flag, both, --help text)
```

Tests: **1373 pass / 0 fail across 56 orchestrator test files** (was 1304 before this branch).

## Pre-Landing Review

5 findings, 1 auto-fixed (silent-pass-on-git-error), 4 deferred as known limitations (TOCTOU between dirty snapshot and flip step is a narrow window — recovery still better than the unguarded baseline). Quality score: 9/10.

## Scope Drift

```
Scope Check: CLEAN
Intent:    Fix the 4 PREMATURE_COMPLETION skill-fault reports from 2026-05-18
Delivered: Two narrow orchestrator fixes (un-flip on rewind, --mark-phase-committed
           dirty guard) + adversarial-review-driven hardening
```

## Plan Completion

2/2 DONE (Fix 1 = `381cf844`, Fix 4 = `bfdd569e`), 0 NOT DONE, 0 UNVERIFIABLE. The plan also names 3 items explicitly out of scope (defensive markFailed across 22 sites, Gemini smoke-test gate, fault-report falsifiability lesson).

## Verification Results

Plan verification skipped — no dev server / not a webapp.

## TODOS

No TODO items completed in this PR (no TODOS.md entries matched the diff).

## Documentation

Docs synced to match what shipped (commit `7e325b5`):

- **`docs/orchestrator-state-machine.md`** — §6 hygiene gate now cross-references the recovery-path dirty-tree guard; new §6.6 documents `restartFeatureFromOriginIssues`'s atomic un-flip + fail-closed contract; §8 `markPhaseCommittedAfterManualRecovery` invariants gain the dirty-tree guard policy table; §9 glossary refreshed with current cli.ts line numbers.
- **`build/orchestrator/README.md`** — Failure-modes table gains three rows for the new guards. New **Manual phase recovery** section explains when to use `--commit-dirty` vs `--force-dirty`.
- **`build/SKILL.md.tmpl`** — Short "Dirty-tree guard" paragraph inline next to existing `--mark-phase-committed` guidance.
- **`build/SKILL.md`** — Regenerated via `bun run gen:skill-docs`.

No CHANGELOG / top-level VERSION bump (fork-local rule per CLAUDE.md; `/build` skill frontmatter bumped 1.23.0 → 1.24.0 in commit `87264247`).

author: zaimy
body:
## 何を解決したいのか

GitHub の workflow runs API は workflow_dispatch / repository_dispatch などで起動された run について `name` や `head_branch` を null で返すことがある。 これまで `Run` および `RunRec` の同フィールドを non-optional な `String` として deserialize していたため、 該当する run を含むレスポンスを取得すると `"invalid type: null, expected a string"` の serde error で octx が失敗していた。

## 設計

`src/api_ext.rs` の `Run` と `src/workflows.rs` の `RunRec` の `name` / `head_branch` を `Option<String>` に変更する。 `From<Run> for RunRec` は同型同士の move なので追加修正は不要。 CSV 出力時、 null は空文字列としてレンダリングされる ( BigQuery の `--autodetect` は NULLABLE STRING として推論する )。

author: friskydevelopments
body:
🎯 **What:** 
The `catalog_pack_feature` and `catalog_pack_react` API endpoints did not properly authenticate requests, allowing anyone to act as any user by providing a `user_id` parameter.

⚠️ **Risk:** 
Attackers could send arbitrary JSON payloads featuring random packs or manipulating reaction counts on packs, potentially using any user's ID because the endpoints relied on client-supplied data rather than authenticated session data.

🛡️ **Solution:** 
The endpoints now use the `@require_miniapp_auth` decorator which requires valid Telegram Mini App Init Data in headers to authenticate the request. Furthermore, the `user_id` is now sourced securely from the validated session via `g.miniapp_user_id` instead of the request body.

---
*PR created automatically by Jules for task [16455897054312063199](https://jules.google.com/task/16455897054312063199) started by @FriskyDevelopments*

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Tightens authentication on two public-facing catalog write endpoints; main risk is breaking existing clients that were sending `user_id` in the body or not providing Telegram init data.
> 
> **Overview**
> Locks down catalog write actions by requiring `@require_miniapp_auth` on `POST /api/catalog/packs/<pack_name>/react` and `POST /api/catalog/packs/<pack_name>/feature`.
> 
> Both endpoints stop accepting a client-supplied `user_id` and instead derive the acting user from `g.miniapp_user_id` (validated Telegram Mini App init data), removing the prior `user_id` input validation and updating the documented request bodies accordingly.
> 
> <sup>Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit b08018b257837df88bf40bcd1b3e8990312e990c. Bugbot is set up for automated code reviews on this repo. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).</sup>

# Vercel Web Analytics Configuration Update

## Summary
Updated the Vercel Web Analytics implementation to match the latest official documentation from https://vercel.com/docs/analytics/quickstart.

## What Was Changed

### Modified Files
- `index.html` - Updated Vercel Web Analytics script order

## Changes Made

### 1. Analyzed Project Structure
This is a static HTML website (no build system, no package.json). Since there's no framework like Next.js, React, or Vue, the installation method follows the "Static HTML" approach from Vercel's documentation.

### 2. Fetched Latest Documentation
Retrieved the most current installation instructions from the official Vercel documentation at https://vercel.com/docs/analytics/quickstart to ensure the implementation follows best practices.

### 3. Updated Analytics Script Order
**Previous implementation:**
```html
<script defer src="/_vercel/insights/script.js"></script>
<script>window.va = window.va || function () { (window.vaq = window.vaq || []).push(arguments); };</script>
```

**Updated implementation (following official docs):**
```html
<!-- Vercel Web Analytics -->
<script>
  window.va = window.va || function () { (window.vaq = window.vaq || []).push(arguments); };
</script>
<script defer src="/_vercel/insights/script.js"></script>
```

**Why this matters:** According to Vercel's documentation, the `window.va` initialization must come BEFORE the script.js load to ensure the analytics queue is ready when the script loads. This prevents any potential race conditions where analytics events might be triggered before the queue function is defined.

### 4. Added Documentation Comment
Added a clear comment `<!-- Vercel Web Analytics -->` to improve code documentation and make it easier for future developers to identify this section.

## Implementation Notes

### Why No Package Installation?
This is a pure static HTML site with no build system or package.json. For static HTML sites, Vercel Web Analytics is installed via script tags rather than npm packages. The `@vercel/analytics` npm package is only needed for framework-based projects (Next.js, React, Vue, etc.).

### Existing Features Preserved
- The site was already using Vercel Analytics and has custom event tracking in place (tracking WhatsApp clicks)
- Microsoft Clarity integration remains unchanged
- All existing functionality preserved

### Script Path
The path `/_vercel/insights/script.js` is the correct production path used by Vercel for Web Analytics on deployed sites. This path is automatically available after enabling Web Analytics in the Vercel dashboard.

## Verification

The updated implementation:
✅ Follows the official Vercel documentation structure
✅ Maintains proper script initialization order
✅ Preserves all existing analytics tracking functionality
✅ Includes proper documentation comments
✅ Is production-ready and will work immediately upon deployment

## Next Steps for the User

1. **Enable Web Analytics in Vercel Dashboard** (if not already enabled):
   - Go to your project in the Vercel dashboard
   - Navigate to the Analytics tab
   - Click "Enable Web Analytics"

2. **Deploy the changes**:
   ```bash
   vercel deploy
   ```

3. **Verify tracking is working**:
   - After deployment, visit your site
   - Open browser DevTools → Network tab
   - Look for requests to `/_vercel/insights/view` or `/_vercel/insights/script.js`
   - These requests confirm analytics is tracking correctly

## Additional Information

The site is already configured to track custom events, specifically WhatsApp link clicks. This custom tracking will continue to work with the updated implementation.

author: cbrownpax8
body:
## Summary

The existing hand-curated demo fixture (~12 companies, dozens of subs/orders) is excellent for screenshots and onboarding but silently hides bugs that only manifest at portfolio scale — most of which were caught by hand during pre-publish review. This PR introduces a generated large-portfolio fixture so future regressions of the same class are caught by CI.

**Shape** (deterministic, seeded):
- 1,000 companies (plausible MSP names + a deliberately-hostile tail with shell-meta, Unicode, embedded quotes/backticks)
- 100 products across the vendor catalog
- 5,000 subscriptions with every `BillingTerm` value represented
- 45,000 orders dating from 2013 → today
- 1–3 contacts per company (~2,000 total)
- Mixed currencies: USD 70% / EUR / GBP / CAD

**Cost**: ~400ms at process start, pay-per-use. Normal `PAX8_DEMO=1` flow loads the small fixture and pays zero overhead.

## Usage

```bash
PAX8_DEMO=1 PAX8_DEMO_SCALE=large pax8 orders list
PAX8_DEMO=1 PAX8_DEMO_SCALE=large pax8 dashboard --json
```

The small fixture stays the default — both coexist. Documented in CLAUDE.md (env-var table) and CONTRIBUTING.md (under Demo Mode).

## Implementation

| File | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `packages/core/src/mock/large-fixture.ts` | Mulberry32 PRNG + deterministic generators for companies, products, subscriptions, orders, contacts. Explicit weights for currencies, statuses, billing terms |
| `packages/core/src/mock/fixture.ts` | Selector — picks small vs. large based on `PAX8_DEMO_SCALE`. Re-exports all entity arrays so callers don't need to know which fixture they're on |
| `packages/core/src/mock/mock-client.ts` | One-line change: imports entity arrays from `./fixture.js` instead of `./demo-data.js`. Types continue to come from `./demo-data.js` |
| `packages/core/src/mock/large-fixture.test.ts` | 9 invariant tests: counts, determinism, BillingTerm coverage, mixed currencies, hostile names present, sub/order referential integrity to companies/products |
| `packages/core/src/mock/fixture.test.ts` | 3 selector tests: small fixture untouched, large fixture is strict superset, webhookTopicDefinitions reused |

## What this enables (and what comes later)

This PR lays the foundation. Each of the open launch blockers below should add its own scale-matrix assertion alongside the fix:

- [#462](https://github.com/pax8labs/pax8-cli/issues/462) — exec the hostile-name `orderCommand` strings in a sandboxed shell and assert no substitution fires
- [#465](https://github.com/pax8labs/pax8-cli/issues/465) — assert `One-Time`/`Trial`/`Activation` subs contribute 0 to portfolio MRR
- [#472](https://github.com/pax8labs/pax8-cli/issues/472) — assert non-USD subs render with the correct currency symbol
- [#478](https://github.com/pax8labs/pax8-cli/issues/478) — assert `orders list --json` exposes `page.totalElements`, default sort is `createdAt DESC`, company names populate beyond the 200-cap
- [#483](https://github.com/pax8labs/pax8-cli/issues/483) — same assertions across every list command

Empty arrays for `invoices`, `usageSummaries`, `quotes`, `webhooks`, `webhookLogs` for now — those entity types don't have a scale-matrix assertion called out yet. Trivial to add when needed; `webhookTopicDefinitions` is reused from the small fixture because it's a Pax8 global catalog, not tenant data.

## Test plan

- [x] `pnpm test` — 1942 passing, 6 skipped (up from 1930 — 12 new fixture tests; nothing broken).
- [x] `pnpm build` — clean.
- [x] End-to-end smoke: `PAX8_DEMO=1 pax8 orders list` → small fixture (first ID `ord-summ...`).
- [x] `PAX8_DEMO=1 PAX8_DEMO_SCALE=large pax8 orders list --json --size 25` → large fixture (first ID `ord-0000...`, first company "Anvil Insurance").
- [x] Fixture generation deterministic across runs (test invariant).

Closes #484

author: ylabonte
body:
## Summary

Revert the mechanical Dependabot floor bump landed in [9f4ca31](https://github.com/ylabonte/proconip-pypi/commit/9f4ca31) (PR #73), restoring the v2.0.0 runtime floors:

- `aiohttp>=3.13.5,<4` -> `aiohttp>=3.10,<4`
- `yarl>=1.23.0,<2` -> `yarl>=1.9,<2`

No code change in the library - the actual aiohttp/yarl surface (`BasicAuth`, `ClientSession.get`/`post`, `ClientResponse.status`/`raise_for_status`/`text`, `ClientError`, `URL.with_path`) is long-stable. Independently verified: **151/151 tests pass with `aiohttp==3.10.11` and `yarl<2` installed.**

## Why now

The tight floors gratuitously prevent downstream `proconip-hass` HACS releases from targeting older HA Core lines. After this lands, the integration's HA floor can drop from 2026.5.2 to whatever HA Core release first required Python 3.13.

## Recurrence prevention

Second commit narrows the Dependabot pip config: drops the `aiohttp-stack` group, adds an `ignore:` block filtering minor+patch updates on `aiohttp` and `yarl`. Only majors (rare) and security advisories will reach a PR for these two going forward.

## Test plan

- [x] `pytest -q` against this branch (current pins) - 151/151 pass, coverage 94.26%
- [x] `pytest -q` after `pip install 'aiohttp==3.10.11' 'yarl<2'` - 151/151 pass (verified in a separate session)
- [ ] CI `lint.yml`, `test.yml`, `codeql.yml`, `docs.yml` green on the PR

## Release

On squash-merge, release-please will pick up the `fix:` Conventional Commit and open a `chore(main): release 2.1.1` PR.

author: froide-hayashi
body:
## Summary

プロジェクトの進行を **Scrum** で管理する仕組みを追加します。Velocity を計測し、経験主義のループ (Plan → Do → Review → Improve) を回す本格的な Scrum 機能で、単にスプリント区切りでタスクを並べるだけのカンバン的運用とは一線を画します。**オプトイン**（`project.yml` の `scrum.enabled: true`）で有効化、デフォルトは無効。

## 新規ファイル

| ファイル | 役割 |
|---|---|
| `agents/scrum-master/AGENT.md` | Scrum プロセスのファシリテーター。判断は持たず、Product Owner (ユーザー) に委ねる議論パートナー |
| `skills/sprint/SKILL.md` | `/sprint plan / review / retro / status`（user-invocable） |
| `skills/backlog/SKILL.md` | `/backlog add / list / priority / sp / status / remove`（user-invocable、Story Point 付与含む） |
| `skills/scrum-event-format/SKILL.md` | 各 Scrum イベントの進行テンプレート（参照 Skill） |
| `skills/scrum-backlog-format/SKILL.md` | Backlog アイテムのデータモデル（type 別 body、Modified Fibonacci、状態遷移）（参照 Skill） |
| `skills/scrum-velocity/SKILL.md` | Velocity 計算ロジックと履歴管理（参照 Skill） |

## ロール対応

| Scrum | Michinushi |
|---|---|
| Product Owner | ユーザー（最終判断） |
| Scrum Master | `scrum-master` Agent |
| Dev Team | architect / designer / implementer / tester / reviewer |

## コマンドフロー

```
/sprint plan    → Sprint 開始（過去 Velocity 提示 → Backlog から Sprint Backlog 構築）
   ↓
/run <id>       → Sprint Backlog のアイテムを既存架構（architect→implementer→tester→reviewer）で実装
/sprint status  → 任意のタイミングで進捗確認
   ↓
/sprint review  → 完了確認・Definition of Done 検証・Velocity 履歴更新
   ↓
/sprint retro   → KPT で振り返り、改善 Try 抽出
   ↓
/sprint plan    → 次の Sprint
```

## 設計判断（議論済み）

- **Velocity 計測は MVP に含める** — 単にスプリント区切りで並べるだけだと Scrum の核（経験主義）が機能しない
- **B. オプトイン拡張** — 既存 `todo` / `triage` は `scrum.enabled` でオプトイン拡張、無効時は今まで通り
- **A. `/sprint` サブコマンド** — `/setup update` / `/triage sentry` と同じパターンで揃える
- **Type 4 種類** — story / bug / tech-debt / spike。type ごとに body 構造を最適化
- **Modified Fibonacci 固定（デフォルト）** — `scrum.yml` で他スケールに切替可能
- **AC は story / bug で必須** — 品質担保
- **GitHub モードで Issue を Backlog 本体として使う** — 別保存にせず Issue を拡張
- **Sprint 長デフォルト 2 週間 / Retrospective KPT 固定** — シンプルに始める
- **DoD のテンプレートを 6 項目で配布**:
  - 全 acceptance-criteria が満たされている
  - reviewer のコードレビューで MUST 指摘が 0 件
  - architect が必要と判断したテスト工程がすべて pass
  - ドキュメントが変更内容と整合
  - CI が green
  - PR がターゲットブランチにマージされている

## 既存への変更

- `skills/setup/SKILL.md` — Step 1.7 で `scrum.enabled` を対話確認、有効化時に `scrum.yml` を初期生成
- `skills/process.md` — エージェント構成・参照 Skill 一覧に scrum-* 追加、「Scrum モード（オプトイン）」セクション追加

author: sfabbro
body:
💡 **What:** Replaced dynamic boolean array indexing (`input[mask]`) in `MaskedMSELoss` and `MaskedMAELoss` with statically sized in-place operations (`.masked_fill(~mask, 0.0)`) and manual reductions for `mean` and `sum` options.
🎯 **Why:** Under the hood, boolean masking requires `nonzero()` calls, triggering Device-to-Host (D2H) synchronizations to determine output shapes and forcing dynamic memory allocations during the backward pass. This introduces large overhead in tight training loops.
📊 **Impact:** This optimization yields a roughly ~2x speedup in computing the metric per pass during training loops when `reduction="mean"` or `reduction="sum"` is used by entirely sidestepping variable-shape output memory allocations, while retaining exact backward compatibility.
🔬 **Measurement:** Running equivalent `(input - target)**2` tests shows iteration time on CPU falling from ~5.0s to ~2.6s over 500 iterations, with verified identical backward path gradients down to precision limits.

## Summary

PR3 (and final) of the F-WIN-FFMPEG (Windows FFmpeg coexistence) series. PR1 (#39) added the Cargo skeleton + DLL fetch tooling; PR2 (#51) added the NVENC encoder adapters + dispatch; PR3 adds the **decoder** counterpart.

## What changed

### Foundational refactor
- **`crates/media-ffmpeg/src/hdr10_sei.rs`** (NEW) — cross-platform HDR10 SEI parser. Extracted from `decoder_common.rs`, ungated from `target_os = "linux"`, so the Windows NVDEC decoder can reuse the same `extract_hdr10_sidecar` math.
- `crates/media-ffmpeg/Cargo.toml` — `rusty_ffmpeg` moved to cross-platform deps (still `optional = true` via `ffmpeg` feature).

### Windows NVDEC decoder modules
- **`crates/media-win/src/ffmpeg/nvdec_decoder.rs`** (NEW) — 8-bit HEVC NVDEC adapter (`HevcNvdecFfmpegDecoderWindowsAdapter`). Emits `Nv12Frame`.
- **`crates/media-win/src/ffmpeg/nvdec_main10_decoder.rs`** (NEW) — Main10 + HDR10 adapter. Emits `Nv12Frame16` with per-frame `Hdr10Metadata` via `Hdr10SidedataTracker`.
- **`crates/media-win/src/ffmpeg/hdr10_sidedata.rs`** (NEW) — stateful tracker caching last-non-None HDR10 metadata across frames.

### Viewer dispatch
- `crates/viewer/src/lib.rs` + `src/platform/win.rs` — `--decoder ffmpeg-nvdec-hevc[-main10]` CLI aliases. Bails with the documented error string when the matching feature is missing (mirrors PR2.A5 pattern).

author: jakechampion
body:
## Summary

First visible output through the binary backend. A program that emits `OpCallDirect "__lang_print"` with a `(data, len)` string on the stack actually prints to stdout under wasmtime.

```text
hello, world
```

## Pipeline

1. **Import section** emits `wasi_snapshot_preview1.fd_write` with signature `(i32, i32, i32, i32) → i32`.
2. **Funcidx shift**: imported functions occupy funcidx `0..N-1`; user functions and synthetic helpers shift up by N. `funcIdx`, export funcidxs, and element-section funcidxs all consult the post-shift mapping.
3. **`__lang_print` helper** takes `(data, len)`, copies bytes through `__lang_str_byte` into a fresh `__lang_alloc`'d buffer (so inline-form strings work — the SSO seam pulls each byte from the packed pair), writes an iovec to `memory[48..56]`, and calls `fd_write(1, 48, 1, 56)`.

## New infrastructure

- `internal/codegen/wasmbin/wasi.go` — `importSpecs` registry parallel to the runtime-helpers registry. Each entry holds module name + import name + signature; today only `wasi_fd_write`.
- `scanImports(prog, helpers)` returns the deterministic ordered set of imports the module needs.
- `scanRuntimeHelpers` gains an `OpCallDirect "__lang_print"` detector that chains in all the required helpers + the WASI import.

Memory section gating already covers `__lang_alloc` / `__lang_str_byte` so no extra wiring needed; the import alone doesn't trigger memory.

## Tests

- `TestEmitPrintHeapLiteral` — `"hello, world\n"` (13 bytes, heap form) prints exactly. `wasmtime run` invokes the `_start` export as a WASI command.
- `TestEmitPrintInlineLiteral` — `"hi\n"` (3 bytes, inline form) prints exactly. Verifies the inline-aware byte copy lands correctly in linear memory.
- `TestImportSectionOnlyWhenPrintUsed` — pure-arithmetic program walks sections and asserts id 2 (import) is absent.

## Test plan

- [x] `go test ./internal/codegen/wasmbin/...` — 124/124 pass.
- [x] Full suite, no regressions.

## What's next

- Closures (`OpMakeClosure`, `OpMakeEnv`) — alloc + capture-store + closure-pair pointer.
- Preview-2 component wrapping for `-target wasm-bin` so the resulting wasm can be served by `wasmtime serve` and edge runtimes.

body:
## Summary

ChatGPT's web-search output now wraps citations as `([Source][1])` (reference-style) or `([Source](https://…))` (inline-link). The existing cleanup in `stripCitations()` only matched the bare `[N]`, so the `[1]`/`[2]` got stripped but `([Source])` was left behind as an orphan in the pasted output.

This adds:

- `([Source][N])` and `([A][1], [B][2])` — parens-wrapped reference-style citations
- `([Source](https://…))` and the multi-source variant — parens-wrapped inline-link citations, restricted to `http(s)` URLs so legitimate parenthetical markdown links pointing at relative paths or anchors are preserved
- `[1]: https://…` trailing reference-link definitions

The new patterns run **before** the bare `[\d+]` cleanup so they can anchor on the `[N]` to make the match unambiguous (and to avoid the "orphan parens" symptom that caused this report). The help-panel description is updated to list the new formats.

## Test plan

- [x] Screenshot scenario: `validate. ([Edunewsletter][1])` → `validate.` (no orphan parens)
- [x] Multiple sources: `([NYTimes][1], [WSJ][2])` → stripped
- [x] Inline-link wrapped: `([source.com](https://source.com))` → stripped
- [x] Trailing `[1]: https://…` definitions → stripped
- [x] Regular markdown link preserved: `See [the docs](https://example.com) for more.`
- [x] Parenthetical relative/anchor links preserved: `(see [docs](/docs/intro) for more)`, `(see [this](#section))`
- [x] Pre-existing patterns (`[1]`, `【…】`, `[cite:…]`, `(Source: …)`, trailing References section) still work

## Summary

When the focus-session timer hits 00:00, only a text prompt ("خلصت الجلسة!") appears. ADHD users set the timer precisely so they don't have to watch it — relying on a silent visual cue is a design contradiction. Adds a non-visual layer:

- **Success vibration** on platforms with `navigator.vibrate` (Android Chrome mostly; iOS Safari ignores)

Both fail silently when the browser/OS refuses (autoplay block, no vibration support), so the visible prompt remains the source of truth.

## Why re-use arrival.wav?

One fewer asset to maintain. The file is already cached after page load (preload="auto" in the arrival hook), so the alert fires with zero latency.

author: thunzers
body:
## Summary
\`erp-affiliate-bridge mark_payout_paid\` did 4 separate \`supabase-js\` calls: fetch payout → update payout → update commissions → READ \`partner.lifetime_paid_thb\` + ADD in JS + UPDATE. The last step is a classic read-modify-write race: two concurrent calls for the same partner can both read X, both write X+amount, and the partner's lifetime total ends up missing one payment OR double-counting one depending on which writer wins.

This PR moves the entire financial state transition behind a single SECURITY DEFINER RPC (\`mark_payout_paid_v2\`), eliminating the race at the database layer.

## Changes
### Migration \`20260519034841_mark_payout_paid_v2_bump_lifetime.sql\`
Replaces \`mark_payout_paid_v2\` (stacked on the Phase 2A atomic fix in #40) with a body that also bumps \`partners.lifetime_paid_thb\` in a single \`UPDATE\` statement at the end:
\`\`\`sql
UPDATE public.partners
   SET lifetime_paid_thb = COALESCE(lifetime_paid_thb, 0) + COALESCE(v_amount_thb, 0)
 WHERE user_id = v_partner_user_id;
\`\`\`
Return shape adds \`lifetime_paid_thb_delta\` for the caller's audit log.

### Edge function \`erp-affiliate-bridge/index.ts\`
\`case "mark_payout_paid"\`:
- Replace the 4-call sequence with one \`db.rpc("mark_payout_paid_v2", …)\` invocation.
- Map the SECURITY DEFINER exceptions (\`payout_not_approved\` / \`commission_state_mismatch\`) to HTTP 409 and other errors to 500.
- Keep ERP-side metadata (\`processed_by\` / \`processed_at\` / \`proof_url\`) as a follow-up single-statement \`UPDATE\` — these columns don't participate in any race because they're write-only metadata, not counters.

### Test
Extend Phase 2A's \`TEST 1\` to also assert \`partners.lifetime_paid_thb = amount_thb\` after the RPC. All three TEST cases pass locally.

## Risks
- This PR is stacked on #40 (Phase 2A). It MUST merge after #40, or you'll lose the atomicity fix from that PR.
- Existing partners' \`lifetime_paid_thb\` is whatever the bridge happened to write before this PR. If the race ever happened in prod, the value is wrong already — this PR doesn't backfill. Sweep with:
  \`\`\`sql
  SELECT p.user_id,
         p.lifetime_paid_thb AS stored,
         COALESCE(SUM(pr.amount_thb), 0) AS sum_of_paid_payouts
    FROM partners p
    LEFT JOIN payout_requests pr
      ON pr.partner_user_id = p.user_id AND pr.status = 'paid'
   GROUP BY p.user_id, p.lifetime_paid_thb
  HAVING p.lifetime_paid_thb <> COALESCE(SUM(pr.amount_thb), 0);
  \`\`\`
- The legacy admin v1 RPC (\`mark_payout_paid\`) and any other code path that updates \`payout_requests.status='paid'\` directly will NOT update \`lifetime_paid_thb\` automatically. After merging, that admin v1 path is dead code per CLAUDE.md; the bridge is the only writer.

## Test plan
- [x] \`TEST 1\` (happy path) — payout flipped, commissions paid + backlinked, \`lifetime_paid_thb\` advanced by amount_thb
- [x] \`TEST 2\` (mismatched commission state) — exception, no side effects (including lifetime_paid_thb)
- [x] \`TEST 3\` (pending payout, not approved) — \`payout_not_approved\` exception

## Related
Round-2 audit follow-up. Companion PRs:
- #40 — Phase 2A: atomic mark_payout_paid_v2 (this PR's base branch)
- (Phase 2C) — \`commission_events.payout_id\` FK + index (independent, separate PR)

author: claude[bot]
body:
Fixes #542

## Summary

For tools like `insert`/`edit` whose input is a paragraph of prose, the visible latency is the LLM **composing** the input — not the tool's actual execution. Previously the UI showed only streaming assistant text and went silent between the user's message and the tool result. This PR adds a "Drafting…" chip that appears as soon as the LLM starts a `tool_use` content block, before any `input_json_delta` arrives.

- **Main → Renderer.** Forward `content_block_start` for `tool_use` via a new `llm:stream:tool-call:start` IPC event carrying `{streamId, toolCallId, toolName}`. The existing `contentBlockStart` handler already received the event but only logged it — the only new send is a fan-out to the renderer.
- **Plumbing.** New event type `LLMStreamToolCallStart`, preload subscriber `onLLMStreamToolCallStart`, browser API fallback, shared `ElectronAPI` interface.
- **Renderer state.** In `useChat`, a new subscription appends a self-closing `<tool-drafting id="…" name="…">` marker to the streaming assistant message on each start. When the tool result is appended later in the existing tool-execution loop, the matching drafting marker is stripped by id (so the result chip replaces the drafting chip rather than appearing alongside it).
- **Chip UI.** `ChatMessage.parseToolTags` recognizes `tool-drafting` segments. `ToolCallIndicator` gains a `drafting` status variant — same violet `Sparkles` + pulse styling as `executing`, but with copy `Drafting <toolName>…`. Verb copy lives in a single `DRAFTING_LABEL` constant so it can be tuned without hunting.

## Verification of the streaming-pipeline question from the trigger

The issue noted the `content_block_start` event "may already be forwarded — verify." It wasn't. `src/main/ipc.ts` had a `contentBlockStart` listener but only `console.log`'d on tool_use; nothing was sent to the renderer. Adding the new event is necessary.

## Acceptance criteria

1. ✅ Multi-sentence `insert`/`edit` shows the **Drafting…** chip immediately, before the tool result lands. (Chip appears on `content_block_start`, before any `input_json_delta`.)
2. ✅ Chip transitions to executing/result when args finish — the drafting tag is stripped by id at the moment the inline result marker `*[Tool: name] result*` is appended.
3. ✅ Chip transitions to success/error on result — handled by the existing inline marker rendering.
4. ✅ For short/cheap tools the drafting phase is brief — `read_document` etc. flicker through drafting → result fast enough that the chip is essentially imperceptible. No regression to the existing behavior since the strip-by-id is a no-op when no drafting tag was appended for that id.
5. ✅ Verb copy in one place — `DRAFTING_LABEL` constant in `ChatMessage.tsx`.

## Out of scope (per the issue)

- Streaming tool-args content INTO the document.
- Cancellation of a drafting tool call (the existing abort path still applies — drafting tags simply remain in the message if streaming is aborted mid-draft).

## Test plan

- [ ] Pull the branch and `npm run dev`.
- [ ] In chat (Editor mode), send a message that prompts a multi-sentence edit (e.g., "Rewrite the second paragraph in a more formal tone"). Confirm a violet **Drafting `insert`…** (or `edit`) chip appears before the tool result lands.
- [ ] Send a message that prompts a quick read (e.g., "What's in this document?"). Confirm `read_document` either flickers through drafting briefly or skips visibly — no extra chip lingers.
- [ ] After the tool runs, confirm only the success/error chip is visible — no leftover drafting chip.
- [ ] Try a multi-tool turn (e.g., "Read the doc, then add a closing paragraph"). Confirm each tool gets its own drafting → result transition without crosstalk.
- [ ] Abort a stream mid-draft (stop button while a long `insert` is composing). Confirm graceful behavior; a frozen drafting chip is acceptable.
- [ ] Verify in Chat Mode (read-only tools) — drafting still appears briefly for `read_document`/`get_outline`.

author: tikazyq
body:
## Summary

Closes #267 — the final batch of adapter-aware CLI migrations plus markdown-only guards for commands with no non-markdown equivalent.

### Migrated commands

- **`update`** — fetch-transform-push through `adapter.update()`. Status / priority / tags / assignee resolve via the schema's semantic hints; body flags (`--replace`, `--section`, `--check`, `--append`, `--content`) apply pure-string utilities to the `content` field and work on any adapter that exposes one. Draft-skip and completion-verification guards stay markdown-scoped.
- **`search`** — delegates to `adapter.search()`, resolves each hit's title via `adapter.get()` for a list-style render.
- **`archive`** — calls `adapter.delete()` (status flip on markdown, issue close on remote backends) with an adapter-aware confirmation label. Rejects fuzzy substring matches on markdown so destructive ops still need an exact id or numeric prefix.
- **`stats`** — groups by the schema's status / priority / tags semantic fields, preserves enum-declared display order, and includes a token total + relationship summary in `--detailed`.

### Markdown-only guards

New `commands/shared.rs` exposes `require_markdown_project(command)`, which inspects the configured adapter name without instantiating it — so the guard fires before any remote-backend authentication. Wired into:

`analyze`, `backfill`, `check`, `compact`, `deps`, `gantt`, `rel`, `split`, `templates`, `timeline`, `tokens`, `validate`

A non-markdown project running any of these gets:

```
`gantt` requires a markdown adapter.
Active adapter: github

Run `leanspec capabilities` to see what operations are available.
```

### Markdown adapter

`SpecWriter::update_metadata` now records status transitions and stamps `completed_at` on first transition to Complete, matching the parser-level behaviour the legacy CLI path relied on so adapter-mediated updates pick it up too.

author: chaliy
body:
## What
Harden LocalFileSaver so base_dir saves cannot escape through symlinked parent directories or final symlink targets. Update safety tests and specs/threat model for the mitigated behavior.

## Why
LocalFileSaver previously depended on lexical path checks plus check-then-write behavior. In embeddings that expose save_to_file with a filesystem-backed base directory, symlinks could redirect writes outside the intended sandbox.

## How
Use Unix directory file descriptors with no-follow opens for save-time traversal and final file creation. Keep the existing non-Unix fallback checks, add final-symlink regression coverage, and document the mitigation.

## Risk
- Low / Medium / High: Medium
- What can break: Unix save_to_file now rejects symlinked paths that may previously have worked. Intended behavior for sandboxed LocalFileSaver usage.

## Checklist
- [x] Tests added or updated
- [x] Backward compatibility considered
- [x] Specs are up to date and not in conflict
- [x] Documentation updated where behavior is specified

author: hndrewaall
body:
## Summary

The container README's own rule on the prior PID-1 layer said tini was sufficient until we hit three long-running services. We're now at three: claude-watch daemon + crond + cw-watcher-supervisor (plus the foreground tmux session). Time to migrate.

Replaces tini with **process-compose** (single static Go binary, docker-compose-style YAML schema) at PID 1. Service declarations live in `/etc/claude-code/process-compose.yml` with restart policies and `depends_on` ordering. Adds the long-asked-for **baked default cron entries** so a fresh `docker compose up` works out of the box on any host — no operator-side cron setup required.

(Originally stacked on #226 which has now merged.)

## What changes

### process-compose as PID 1

| Process | Role | Restart policy |
|---------|------|----------------|
| `setup-tmux-session` | Oneshot — creates the in-container tmux session in detached mode. | `restart: no` |
| `tmux-attach` | Interactive foreground process — attaches stdin/stdout/stderr to the tmux session. | `restart: no` |
| `claude-watch` | Long-running daemon — observes the in-container claude pane via tmux capture-pane. | `restart: on_failure` |
| `crond` | Long-running daemon — runs `/etc/cron.d/cw-default` + any operator entries in `/etc/cron.d/private/`. | `restart: on_failure` |
| `cw-watcher-supervisor` | Long-running supervisor — respawns the operator-baked watchers (claude-event-tail etc). | `restart: on_failure` |

`entrypoint.sh` continues to do setup (PATH wiring, hooks-shim generation, trust-workspace, obligations-init) then `exec`s process-compose. From there, process-compose is PID 1 — it forwards SIGTERM/SIGINT to its supervised children, reaps zombies, and exits when all foreground processes complete.

The legacy `CLAUDE_CONTAINER_DAEMON=0` / `CLAUDE_CONTAINER_CRON=0` / `CLAUDE_CONTAINER_WATCHER_SUPERVISOR=0` opt-out env vars are mapped to the process-compose-style `*_DISABLED` variant so existing operator `.env` files don't see a behaviour change.

### Baked default cron entries

`/etc/cron.d/cw-default` bakes the two cron lines every deployment needs:

```cron
* * * * *   hndrewaall /usr/local/bin/claude-watch active-agents --json --write-state /var/lib/claude-watch/active-agents.json > /dev/null 2>>/tmp/claude-watch-cron-active-agents.log
* * * * *   hndrewaall /usr/local/bin/claude-watch metrics > /tmp/claude-watch-cron-metrics.log 2>&1
```

Both run as the `hndrewaall` user (uid 1000) — cron itself runs as root and `setuid()`s into the user named in each `/etc/cron.d/` entry.

### `/etc/cron.d/private/` slot

Reserved for operator-specific recurring jobs (PR-watch loops, custom event emitters). Empty by default; populated via a bind-mount in `docker-compose.override.yml`:

```yaml
services:
  claude-container:
    volumes:
      - "/host/path/to/private-cron.d/:/etc/cron.d/private/:ro"
```

`compose.yml` has a commented-out example mount line so operators can uncomment + set the path.

## Why process-compose, not s6-overlay

process-compose's `depends_on` + `restart:` + YAML shape maps 1:1 onto the outer `docker-compose.yml` operators already use — lower onboarding cost. s6-overlay is strictly more flexible but has a steeper learning curve; documented as the fallback if process-compose hits a gap.

## Verification

- [x] `make test-entrypoint` — full container test suite green locally (41 tests, including the new `process-compose-pid1.test` + `cron-default-baked.test`)
- [x] `process-compose up -f container/process-compose.yml --dry-run` — validates 5 processes
- [x] `docker compose -f container/compose.yml config` — validates compose file with the new commented `/etc/cron.d/private` mount slot
- [ ] CI green on this branch
- [ ] (manual, deferred) runtime smoke-test on workbot: `docker compose up -d`, verify `cat /proc/1/comm` reports `process-compose`, confirm `active-agents.json` written to `/var/lib/claude-watch/` after 60s, simulate a `claude-watch` SIGKILL and confirm restart

## Migration notes

- **tini removed** from the apt-install layer. process-compose handles SIGCHLD reaping and signal forwarding.
- Existing `tini-pid1.test` replaced by `process-compose-pid1.test`.
- `entrypoint.sh` no longer contains `nohup setsid ... &` daemon-spawn blocks; those moved to `process-compose.yml` as supervised processes.

## Test plan

- [ ] CI green
- [ ] Manual: workbot smoke-test post-merge

author: yaroslavbaienko
body:
## Summary
- Adds `scripts/clean-logs.sh`, a conservative log-cleanup script intended for the Hetzner host (works on any systemd Linux).
- Audits disk/log usage first, then: vacuums journald to 7d / 500MB, force-rotates via logrotate, truncates active `*.log` files >100MB (preserves open file handles so services don't need restart), deletes rotated logs older than 14 days, truncates large docker / nginx / apache logs.
- Supports `--dry-run` for audit-only.

## Why this is safe
- `truncate -s 0` keeps files open by running services intact — `rm` on a live log file leaves the inode held by the process and doesn't reclaim space until restart.
- Only *already-rotated* artifacts (`.gz`, `.xz`, `.1`, `.old`, etc.) older than 14 days are deleted; current logs are kept.
- Never touches `/var/lib/docker/overlay2`, package caches, or `/tmp` — those have separate failure modes and deserve their own decision.
- Idempotent and re-runnable.

## Usage on the server
```bash
git pull
sudo bash scripts/clean-logs.sh --dry-run   # audit only
sudo bash scripts/clean-logs.sh             # audit + clean + re-audit
```

## Test plan
- [ ] Run `sudo bash scripts/clean-logs.sh --dry-run` on the Hetzner host and review the audit output.
- [ ] If the numbers look sane, run without `--dry-run`.
- [ ] Confirm `df -h /` shows reclaimed space and that services (nginx / docker containers) are still logging.

author: dbharris2
body:
Adds a Chrome MV3 extension as a parallel deploy alongside the
existing standalone server. Both share the same React UI, hook,
and sanitizer.

## Why

The standalone deploy works but has real adoption friction: four
CSP directives + an HTML script tag + load-order foot-gun + conflict
with the official Relay DevTools extension. An extension neutralizes
all of those: zero CSP edits, content script in the page's MAIN world
gets the hook installed at `document_start`, panel slots into the
DevTools tab strip next to Components / Network / GraphQL Network.

## What's in here

Six commits, intentionally not squashed for review readability:

1. **`refactor(ui)`** — extract a transport abstraction from
   `useInspector`. No behavior change; this is the seam the
   extension slots its `chrome.runtime`-based transport into.
2. **`feat(extension): scaffold`** — CRXJS-based extension structure
   (manifest, devtools page, panel that renders App with a stub
   transport). Panel appears in DevTools but doesn't transport data yet.
3. **`feat(extension): wire chrome.runtime transport`** — actual
   end-to-end pipeline: main-world hook installer →
   `window.postMessage` → content script → `chrome.runtime.Port` →
   service worker (routes by tab) → panel.
4. **`docs`** — README and AGENTS rewritten to cover both deploys.
5. **`fix(extension): scan src/ui from the panel's Tailwind build`** —
   Tailwind v4 with `@tailwindcss/vite` uses the Vite root as its
   scan base, so with `extension/` as root the panel's CSS was missing
   all the utilities from `src/ui/*.tsx` (4 KB vs the standalone's
   13 KB). `@source` directives in `src/ui/index.css` fix it.
6. **`fix(extension): reconnect + per-deploy empty state`** — the
   service worker hibernates after ~30 s idle and the panel port
   stuck on 'closed'; added 1 s-backoff reconnect on the panel side
   and a single-shot retry in the content script so the first message
   after a wakeup isn't lost. Also makes the empty-state copy
   per-deploy (script-tag instructions for standalone, page-reload
   instructions for extension).

## How to try

```sh
pnpm install
pnpm build:extension
```

Then in Chrome:
1. \`chrome://extensions\` → Developer mode → Load unpacked → \`dist/extension/\`.
2. Disable any other Relay DevTools extension (race for the same hook).
3. Open DevTools on a Relay app, click "Relay Inspector" in the tab strip.
4. Reload the page so our hook attaches before \`new Environment(...)\`.

## Known limitations

- If the inspected page was loaded *before* DevTools opened, the
  panel shows an empty state until the page is reloaded. A future
  follow-up could add a "panel-hello → main-world re-publish"
  handshake to skip the reload.
- The service worker's port pairing is in-memory; if the worker
  hibernates between events, the next message reconnects fine but
  any messages emitted during the brief reconnect window are lost.

## Test plan
- [x] \`pnpm typecheck\`, \`test\`, \`lint\`, \`format:check\`, \`build\`, \`relay:check\` all green
- [x] Extension load tested on a real Next.js + Relay app — initial
      records appear, ref-chip navigation works, reload clears and
      repopulates the store, status badge recovers from service-worker
      hibernation
- [ ] CI green on this PR

author: vinodhalaharvi-claude
body:
## What

A new `agents.WithOAuth` Behavior that wraps an agent's `Run` arrow with OAuth credential resolution, token injection, and refresh-on-401 retry. Agents in a DAG opt in individually by listing it in their `Spec.Behaviors`; agents that don't need OAuth are unchanged.

## Why

Sibyl's worker process runs multiple users' workflows concurrently. Env-var-based credentials can't multiplex by user; closure-captured tokens go stale across hours-long workflows; refresh tokens need persistent storage anyway. The `auth/oauth` package already provides the durable, identity-keyed token machinery — this PR is the per-agent adapter that lets a DAG node opt into it.

The `Vendors` field on `Spec` has been sitting unused since the agents package was added, with a comment about "future auth-as-arrow work uses this to resolve credentials." This is that work — though Vendors stays declarative (manifest only), and `WithOAuth` is the explicit wiring. Decoupling them means tooling can audit cross-agent vendor coverage without dictating injection shape, and an agent can be wired to multiple identities per provider via multiple `WithOAuth` layers.

## Design

Both policy seams are weft arrows, matching the shape of `oauth.Provider`'s arrow bundle. No interface, no method seams:

```go
type OAuthPolicy[Req any] struct {
    Provider        string
    ResolveIdentity weft.Arrow[Req, oauth.Identity]
    Inject          weft.Arrow[InjectInput[Req], Req]
}
```

Per-invocation pipeline:

```
policy.ResolveIdentity >>> oauth.WithRefresh(
    inner-call = policy.Inject >>> inner,
    refresh, store, identity, policy.Provider,
)
```

The load-call-refresh-retry loop is **not** reimplemented — `oauth.WithRefresh` is the source of truth and this behavior delegates to it. The only translation we do is converting `oauth.ErrTokenNotFound` into a typed `MissingCredentialError` so callers don't have to `errors.Is` on a low-level sentinel.

## Built-in helpers

| Helper | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `InvokedByIdentity[Req](provider)` | Default resolver — reads `AgentContext.InvokedBy` |
| `FixedIdentity[Req](id)` | Service-account agents (fixed identity, ignores ctx) |
| `StructFieldInjector[Req](mutate)` | Inject token into a struct field via a mutator func |

## Failure modes

| Condition | Result |
|---|---|
| No `InvokedBy` and no override | `MissingIdentityError` (hard) |
| Token absent from store | `MissingCredentialError` (hard, per pilot design call) |
| `AuthenticationError` from inner | Refresh once + retry once (delegated to `oauth.WithRefresh`) |
| Non-auth error from inner | Bubbled up unchanged |
| Refresh fails | Bubbled up wrapped |

`MissingCredentialError` unwraps to `oauth.ErrTokenNotFound` for callers that want low-level matching.

## Tests

13 new tests in `agents/oauth_test.go`, all `-race` clean:

- happy path (token loaded + injected, no refresh)
- auth error triggers refresh + retry exactly once, retry uses refreshed token
- refreshed token persisted to store post-retry
- missing credential = hard typed error, inner never called
- missing `InvokedBy` = hard typed error, store never touched
- `FixedIdentity` works without `AgentContext`
- `StructFieldInjector` doesn't mutate caller's input
- non-auth error not retried, refresh not called
- behavior is opt-in: declared `Vendors` without `WithOAuth` runs auth-free
- constructor panics: nil store, empty provider, empty canonical, nil mutator

## What this PR does NOT do

- No changes to existing agents or workflows. Purely additive.
- No UI work. UI wiring comes next, once the framework piece is in.
- No auto-pause workflow on `MissingCredentialError` (that's a workflow-level concern; `OAuthFlowWorkflow` infrastructure already supports the durable-wait pattern).
- No per-vendor convenience wrapper that auto-applies `WithOAuth` from `Vendors`. The injector shape is per-agent-type, so auto-application can't pick the right one.
- No multi-identity demo (mechanism is supported: stack multiple `WithOAuth` behaviors at different layers).

## Stats

- 2 files added, 0 modified
- ~280 LoC implementation, ~470 LoC tests
- `go test ./agents/... -race` clean
- `go build ./...` clean
- `go vet ./...` clean
- `go test ./auth/oauth/...` still clean (no regressions)
