author: colinc86
body:
## Summary

Step-6 of #81 — adds the inter-sibling version-skew tripwire that #163 explicitly deferred. One new `Check` impl, one catalog line, count-bumps in two snapshot guards. Catalog grows from 20 to 21.

## Why now

`binary.tape.version` (Step-2) catches "the `tape` on `$PATH` doesn't match the doctor I just ran" — bundled-vs-system skew. It can't catch the inter-sibling case: a plugin upgrade replaces `tape` but leaves a stale `tape-hook` on `$PATH`. The recording pipeline then loads the mismatched hook and corrupts cassettes silently.

`binary.versions.consistent` runs `--version` on all three and Fails if they disagree.

## Behavior

| condition | outcome |
| --- | --- |
| any sibling missing on `$PATH` | `Na` (the `.present` check already reports) |
| any subprocess fails to exec | `Harness` |
| any `--version` non-zero exit | `Fail "<path> exited <code>"` |
| any `--version` output unparseable | `Fail "could not parse..."` |
| all three agree | `Pass "all three sibling binaries report <v>"` |
| any divergence | `Fail "version skew: tape=<v1>, tape-hook=<v2>, tape-mcp-wrap=<v3>"` + fix line |

Mirrors the existing `TapeVersion` branch structure exactly. No new `Env` field; reuses `find_on_path` + `parse_version_line`.

## Test plan

- [x] Six new unit tests in `crates/tape-cli/src/doctor/checks/binary.rs` cover every branch
- [x] One new integration test `inter_sibling_version_skew_is_detected` — proves the orthogonality (`[OK] binary.tape.version` + `[XX] binary.versions.consistent` in the same run)
- [x] `known_good_environment_exits_zero` bumps `13 pass` → `14 pass`
- [x] `catalog_listing_has_one_line_per_check` and `list_checks_is_stable` bump 20 → 21
- [x] `cargo test --workspace` — all pass, zero regressions
- [x] `cargo fmt --check` clean

body:
Implement up_backtrace() for TriCore by walking the CSA chain and collecting return addresses from upper CSA A11 register.

## Summary

Add backtrace support for TriCore architecture. Users can use up_backtrace to find the current active call stack, which is quite useful for debugging, like sched_backtrace() and sched_dumpstack().

This feature depends on the TriCore CSA chain, where the upper CSA A11 register saves the return address of each function call.

## Impact

Depends on TriCore CSA hardware support. No impact on other architectures.

## Testing

## 요약

- Windows 설치에서 Codex CLI 기본 경로를 native `codex.cmd`가 아니라 WSL(Ubuntu) 안의 Codex CLI로 바꿨습니다.
- 설치 스크립트가 `wsl.exe`/배포판을 확인하고, 배포판이 없으면 `wsl --install -d Ubuntu`를 시도한 뒤 재부팅/Ubuntu 첫 사용자 설정이 필요하면 명확히 멈추도록 했습니다.
- WSL 안에서는 nvm을 준비하고 `nvm install 22` → `npm install -g @openai/codex@latest` → `codex --version`으로 Codex CLI를 검증합니다.
- Windows Desktop runner와 sidecar runtime은 `SOLO_CODEX_WINDOWS_MODE=wsl`을 사용하며, Codex login/status/app-server는 `wsl.exe -- bash -lc ...`로 실행합니다.
- native fallback은 유지했습니다. `SOLO_SUPERMAN_CODEX_WINDOWS_MODE=native`일 때는 기존 `codex.cmd --version failed with exit -1073741515` / `0xC0000135` 감지와 `Microsoft.VCRedist.2015+.x64` 복구를 계속 수행합니다.
- 최신 `origin/main`의 `_KO`/`_EN` 문서 분리 구조에 맞춰 README, troubleshooting_KO/EN, docs verifier, install-run 계약 테스트를 갱신했습니다.

## 근거

- OpenAI Codex Windows 문서는 native Windows와 WSL2 경로를 모두 안내하며, WSL2는 Linux-native tooling 또는 native sandbox가 맞지 않는 환경에서 사용하는 경로로 설명합니다.
- Microsoft WSL 문서는 관리자 PowerShell의 `wsl --install`, Ubuntu 기본 배포판 설치, 첫 실행 시 Linux 사용자 정보 설정 필요성을 안내합니다.
- 사용자가 확인한 Windows native Codex 실행 불안정성을 설치 단계에서 흡수하기 위해, 앱 실행용 Windows Node/pnpm과 Codex 전용 WSL toolchain을 분리했습니다.

## 검증

- `pnpm vitest run apps/sidecar/src/runtime/index.test.ts scripts/verify-install-run-docs.test.mjs scripts/verify-doc-contracts.test.mjs --passWithNoTests` — 3 files / 40 tests passed
- `pnpm verify:docs` — doc contract checks passed
- `pnpm verify` — typecheck/lint/test/docs passed, 76 files / 658 tests passed
- `pnpm verify:prod-bundle` — passed, `build_auto_local_smoke`, token mismatch 401, managed child cleanup/temporary app data cleanup 확인
- `git diff --check`

## Not tested

- Windows 실기기에서 WSL 설치, Ubuntu 첫 사용자 생성, nvm+Codex 설치, WSL-backed `codex auth login`/account status는 현재 macOS 환경이라 직접 확인하지 못했습니다.
- `pwsh`가 이 호스트에 없어 PowerShell parser 검증은 건너뛰었습니다.

author: dcyfr
body:
## Summary
- Bumps `express-rate-limit` `7.5.1` → `8.5.2` (supersedes #89)
- Applies the required v7→v8 keyGenerator migration: wraps `getClientIp(req)` in `ipKeyGenerator()` so v8's IPv6 subnet aggregation runs on it

Closes #89.

## Why a fresh PR instead of merging #89?
`#89` was a pure dependabot bump. The v7→v8 transition is **not** drop-in: v8 reshuffled IP-based keyGenerator handling for IPv6 subnet aggregation. A custom keyGenerator that returns what's effectively an IP string now MUST be wrapped in `ipKeyGenerator()`. Without the wrap:
- v8 emits a `keyGeneratorIpFallback` validation warning on every request
- Every IPv6 client gets collapsed into a single rate-limit bucket (the loopback / wildcard /60), defeating per-client limits for IPv6 traffic

Per the v8 types in `node_modules/express-rate-limit/dist/index.d.ts`:
> "If you write a custom keyGenerator that allows a fallback to IP address for unauthenticated users, return `ipKeyGenerator(req.ip)` rather than just `req.ip`."

Our keyGenerator returns `getClientIp(req)` (X-Forwarded-For first hop, falling back to `req.ip`). Wrapping with `ipKeyGenerator()` keeps IPv4 behavior identical and applies the v8 default /60 subnet for IPv6.

## Test plan
- [x] `npm run typecheck` clean
- [x] **58/58 integration tests pass** across `tests/integration/{auth-flow,posts-api,users-api}.test.ts` (the test files that exercise the rate-limit middleware via `__resetAllRateLimiters()`)
- [x] Runtime export check: `node -e "console.log(typeof require('express-rate-limit').ipKeyGenerator)"` → `function`
- [ ] Manual smoke: 100 reqs from one IP to `/api/posts` → 429 + `Retry-After`
- [ ] Staging IPv6 client validation (out of scope for this PR — sanity check during deploy)

author: samoca95
body:
## Summary

This PR improves data consistency and permission handling across the backup and session management systems by wrapping concurrent database operations in Dexie transactions and refining the file system permission request logic.

## Key Changes

**Database Transactions:**
- Wrapped the session save operation (`AddEditSessionPage.tsx`) in a single `db.transaction()` call to ensure all related tables (sessions, techniques, taps, flows) are updated atomically
- Wrapped retry queue operations (`retryQueue.ts`) in transactions to prevent concurrent writes from clobbering each other when multiple destinations are processed in parallel
- Ensures `enqueueRetry()`, `recordSuccess()`, and `recordFailure()` are idempotent and race-condition-safe

**File System Permission Handling:**
- Added error handling in `ensureFolderPermission()` to catch `SecurityError` when permission requests occur outside a user-activation window, returning the current state instead of throwing
- Refined `verifyFolderConnection()` to distinguish between `'denied'` (user explicitly blocked) and `'prompt'` (permission lapsed):
  - Only sets the reconnect banner for `'denied'`; `'prompt'` allows lazy re-request on next write
- Updated `fileSystemDestination.isEnabled()` to return `true` for `'prompt'` state so write operations can request permission automatically within the user-gesture window
- Updated `fileSystemDestination.write()` to request permission with `requestIfNeeded: true` since it runs within a mutation context
- Improved `fileSystemDestination.list()` to only set reconnect flag on explicit denial

**Google Drive Resilience:**
- Added `isFolderGoneError()` helper to detect 404/403 errors indicating the app folder was manually deleted
- Enhanced `googleDriveDestination.write()` to catch folder-gone errors, clear the cached folder ID, and retry with a fresh folder creation

**Backup Scheduler:**
- Added drain logic in `runBackupNow()` to process queued components after the lock is released, covering callers outside the scheduled loop (e.g., `drainRetryQueue`)
- Fixed `mergeBackupPayload()` to include `sessionFlows` and `sessionFlowTaps` when merging incoming backups
- Removed `runStartupBackupIfDue()` (unused entry point)

**Tests:**
- Updated `verifyFolderConnection` and `fileSystemDestination.isEnabled` tests to reflect the new `'prompt'` handling behavior

body: ## 📝Overview This pull request implements critical optimizations in memory resource management and game engine performance, while also adjusting the ergonomics of touch controls to improve the overall user experience. ## 🚀 Key Features & Changes - **Memory Management:** Implemented an LruCache system for NPC sprites and rounded health values within cache keys. This prevents excessive RAM consumption and avoids unexpected Out-of-Memory (OOM) crashes. - **Game Loop Optimization:** The main logic cycle was moved to a background thread (Dispatchers.Default), eliminating interface "jank" and allowing for much smoother input response. - **Resource Cleanup:** Added logic to the onRelease callback to formally destroy Map and Web components (MapView and WebView) when exiting the screen, freeing the processor from unnecessary rendering tasks. - **Control Ergonomics:** Reduced the base size of Joysticks and action buttons to 150dp, resulting in a less intrusive and more comfortable gameplay interface. - **Error Prevention:** Refactored data persistence by injecting the DAO directly into the ViewModel, ensuring that map modifications (Designer Mode) are saved atomically and securely. ## 👍 Results - Optimized RAM usage through intelligent texture and sprite caching. - Stable 30 FPS by decoupling game physics from the main UI rendering thread. - Zero memory leaks detected when navigating between the main menu and the world map. - Cleaner UI featuring compact controls that remain fully scalable via settings. ## 📸 Change Snapshots

author: gfx
body:
## Summary

The previous `-O2` inline threshold (14) sat directly on a discrete
performance cliff for Gale-generated parser/highlighter workloads:
on `benchmark-syntax-highlight` the per-iteration time jumps from
~13.5 ms (threshold 13) to ~17.9 ms (threshold 14) — a +33% regression
caused by a single Gale action function with 14 expressions chain-inlining
and degrading downstream code. As a result `-O2` was measurably *slower*
than `-O1` on this workload, and `-O3` (threshold 40) was both slower and
~2.5x larger than `-O2`.

### New defaults

| Level | Iterations | Inline threshold | Rationale |
|-------|-----------:|-----------------:|-----------|
| -O1   | 2          | **4** (was 5)    | sweep showed no speed cost; saves a small amount of wasm |
| -O2   | 10         | **13** (was 14)  | last value before the syntax-highlight regression cliff at 14; this is the per-attribute "best perf" level |
| -O3   | 30         | **32** (was 40)  | last value before another discrete size cliff at 33 on syntax-highlight (859 KB → 1049 KB, crossing 1 MB); speed at 32 is indistinguishable from 35/40 |

The selection was done by binary search holding the rest of the opt
pipeline fixed at `-O2`, sweeping only `--optimize-inline-threshold`,
with several trials per point to filter cold-start noise.

### Effect on benchmarks (Wado-vs-native ratios; lower is better)

|                  | before | after |
|------------------|-------:|------:|
| syntax-highlight |  9.38x | **2.65x** |
| sqlite-parse     |  5.86x | **3.30x** |
| json-catalog v2  |  7.33x | **4.82x** |
| json-twitter     | 16.69x | **11.73x** |
| sieve            |  1.92x | **1.49x** |
| mandelbrot       |  1.12x | **1.07x** |
| count-prime      |  1.03x | 1.03x |
| fts              |  1.71x | 1.80x |
| zlib total       |  9.06x | **8.82x** |
| json-catalog v1  | 16.52x | 15.68x |
| json-canada      | 13.55x | 15.00x¹ |

¹ json-canada's apparent regression is mostly the native `serde_json`
baseline tightening between machines — Wado's absolute time is similar.

### Effect on wasm size

`sqlite_highlight` at `-Os` shrinks 511,983 → **486,702** bytes; other
size-relevant programs see ≤ +1 KB drift from the new pipeline.

### Notes

- All 6207 e2e fixtures pass at every opt level.
- `benchmark/README.md` and `wasm-size/README.md` are refreshed with new
  measurements; rows for toolchains that need `wasi-sdk` (C, moonbit,
  Rust tree-sitter) are footnoted as "not re-measured this round" and
  retain their previous values (sizes are toolchain- not host-dependent).
- `wasi-sdk` is temporarily commented out in `benchmark/mise.toml` and
  `wasm-size/mise.toml` to avoid GitHub API rate-limit failures during
  artifact install. Restore once that constraint is gone.

ERROR: failed to build: unable to prepare context: path "./discord-bot" not found

## Summary

Fixes #101

The root logger was hardcoded to `DEBUG` unconditionally at startup. Production deployments had no way to reduce log noise without patching source code. Debug output can also inadvertently log sensitive request payloads.

## Changes

**`webapp/app/__init__.py`**
- Move `basicConfig` after `app.config.from_object("config")` so `LOG_LEVEL` is available from config
- Read the level name from `app.config.get("LOG_LEVEL", "WARNING")` with a safe fallback

**`webapp/config.py.template`**
- Add `LOG_LEVEL = "WARNING"` with a comment explaining the valid values

```python
# Before — hardcoded DEBUG always
logging.getLogger().setLevel(logging.DEBUG)

# After — driven by config, defaults to WARNING
_log_level_name = str(app.config.get("LOG_LEVEL", "WARNING")).upper()
_log_level = getattr(logging, _log_level_name, logging.WARNING)
logging.getLogger().setLevel(_log_level)
```

## Test plan

- [ ] Start app with default `config.py.template` — verify only WARNING+ messages appear in logs
- [ ] Set `LOG_LEVEL = "DEBUG"` in config and restart — verify DEBUG messages appear
- [ ] Set `LOG_LEVEL = "INVALID"` — verify app falls back to WARNING without crashing

author: dskarzh
body:
## Summary

`GeminiCacheManager` keyed its in-memory slot solely by the static `cacheKey` (e.g. `"ai-assistant"`) and stored a separate per-content checksum on the slot. When the content under that key changed between turns, it synchronously DELETEd the server-side cache and CREATEd a new one. With a JVM-singleton manager serving many chats whose tool sets diverge (the situation produced by on-demand skill loading), concurrent chats with different tool sets evict each other's caches every turn — paying the full create-call cost, getting zero read hits, and adding two HTTP round-trips per turn.

The fix folds the content checksum into the map key:

```
effectiveKey = cacheKey + ":" + sha256(systemInstruction, tools, toolConfig)
```

Divergent content coexists as separate slots instead of evicting each other. A cache miss now means "no slot for this content yet," never "wrong content in this slot," so the delete-on-mismatch branch is unreachable and removed. The map's `compute()` keeps the per-key single-flight guarantee — concurrent calls with the same effective key result in exactly one create.

The displayName stored server-side is exactly the effective key, so `listCachedContents` on restart rebuilds the in-memory map directly — no parsing.

## Making the hash deterministic across JVMs

For the effective key to be stable across nodes and restarts, the serialized form of the hash input must be deterministic. Two sources of non-determinism are fixed:

- **Function declarations within each `GeminiTool` are sorted by name.** The upstream tools list is derived from a `Set.of(...)` whose iteration order is JVM-randomized (JEP 269). Without sorting, the same logical tool set hashes differently per JVM. The actual list passed to `createCachedContent` keeps its original order — only the hash input is normalized.

- **Map entries inside parameter schemas are emitted in key order.** `GeminiSchema.properties` is a `Map<String, GeminiSchema>` built by `Collectors.toMap(...)` in `SchemaMapper`, which defaults to a `HashMap`. Jackson's default config doesn't sort map entries, so two JVMs produce different JSON for the same logical schema. A dedicated `ObjectMapper` with `SerializationFeature.ORDER_MAP_ENTRIES_BY_KEYS` enabled is used for the hash; outgoing requests to Gemini still go through the existing `Json` utility unchanged.

## Behavior changes

- **`deleteCachedContent` removed.** Orphaned caches (e.g. from prompt updates between deploys, or rare cross-node races) are left to expire passively via TTL. Storage cost is negligible at typical prompt sizes.
- **`extendTtl` near expiry retained.** A frequently-hit slot near its TTL bumps itself rather than recreating — more valuable now that hot effective keys see more sustained hits.
- **Logging includes both `cacheKey` (operator-readable) and `effectiveKey` (unique)** on every cache-related log line.

## Migration note

Caches created before this change were hashed with the prior non-canonical serialization and will not be matched by the new hash for the same logical content. They become orphans and expire passively — one-time transition cost.

body:
## Summary

Expand the bullet-list service-account descriptions under "Identity and workload binding > Control plane / Data plane" into per-SA tables (one per IRSA role / GSA), covering scope, permissions, and the "why" behind each grant.

Adds AWS coverage at the same level of detail as the GCP-only first pass shipped earlier in this branch. Uses `{{< tabs >}}` (AWS / GCP) to mirror the rest of the doc's per-section pattern (Networking, Database, Logging, etc.).

## What's new

- **`#### Control plane service account IAM`** — per-SA tables for flyteadmin / artifacts on both clouds.
- **`#### Data plane service account IAM`** — per-SA tables for backend / flyte-worker / fluentbit (AWS IRSA) and backend / worker GSA (GCP), plus the EKS/GKE node IAM grants kubelet needs to pull task images.
- **`#### Linking Kubernetes service accounts to cloud identities`** — the chart-annotation pattern (`eks.amazonaws.com/role-arn` for IRSA, `iam.gke.io/gcp-service-account` for WI). Cloud IAM alone is not sufficient — pods still get `403 Forbidden` if the KSA annotation isn't pointing at the right cloud identity.
- **`#### Common pitfalls`** — five real failure modes surfaced during the mike-apple-gcp validation:
  - GCS `objectAdmin` alone doesn't include `storage.buckets.get` → stow driver startup-crashes; need `bucketViewer` too
  - GKE node SA must have `artifactregistry.reader` (kubelet pull uses node identity, not pod WI)
  - EKS equivalent: node IAM role needs ECR repo access
  - GCP SA `account_id` 6-30 char limit when composing org+cluster+role names
  - Signed-URL flows need `serviceAccountTokenCreator` self-grant on the GSA

## What's intentionally not in the GCP backend table

A `tokenCreator` binding to the `union-system` WI principal (`principal://...subject/...` form) that earlier docs drafts mentioned. Empirically verified unused on `mike-apple-gcp` via `flyte get logs` end-to-end — on GKE, `google.DefaultTokenSource` resolves credentials via the metadata server, which transparently exchanges the projected KSA token → GSA access token before reaching `iamcredentials.SignBlob`. The GSA self-impersonation member alone covers every signed-URL flow. The dead binding was also removed from the terraform module in cloud commit `289506e4cb`.

## Stack

Based on `peeter/selfhosted-docs-v2`. Will land with the v2 selfhosted docs revamp.

## Source of truth

All AWS claims grounded in `cloud/infra/terraform/modules/selfmanaged/aws/dataplane/{union_iam,fluentbit_iam,image_builder}.tf` and `aws/controlplane/`. All GCP claims grounded in `cloud/infra/terraform/modules/selfmanaged/gcp/{control,data}plane/` plus the `mike-apple-gcp` end-to-end validation runs (recorded in the `mike/fab-238-image-builder-gcp-validation` and `mike/fab-238-iam-consolidation-and-docs` branches on `unionai/cloud`).

author: ghenghis
body:
## Summary

Replaces the EPG's hard 4-hour rolling window with three day tabs:

- **Now** — 4-hour rolling, anchored at "now - 30min" (legacy behaviour)
- **Today** — from "now - 30min" to tonight's midnight
- **Tomorrow** — 24 hours from tomorrow 00:00 local

Sherri can now actually plan "what's on tonight" or "what's airing tomorrow morning" without the Guide cutting off after 4 hours.

## Why

`EPGGrid` was hard-coded to `defaultHours = 4`, and the backend's `hours` query param was capped at 12. Together that meant the Guide was effectively a "currently airing + next 4h" view — too narrow for any planning behaviour. The XMLTV pipeline already returns days of data; only the request shape was holding us back.

## What this PR does

### Backend — `services/hermes-tv-api/src/routes/epg.js`
- Optional `start` query param (ISO-8601). When supplied + parseable, the program-filter window anchors there instead of `now - 30min`. `_meta.requested_start` echoes it back.
- `hours` cap raised from 12 → 48. The XMLTV upstream cache already shares parsed feed data across all requests, so a wider window doesn't multiply upstream fetches — only the in-memory `.filter()` cost grows, linearly.

### Client — `apps/hermes-web-tv/src/api/epgClient.js`
- `fetchEPG(providerId, hoursAhead, startIso?)` — new optional third arg. When omitted, the call shape is identical to before this PR.

### Client — `apps/hermes-web-tv/src/components/EPGGrid.jsx`
- New optional `windowStartMs` and `hoursForward` props. Defaults preserve current behaviour (4h from now).
- The existing "now" indicator line was already gated on `nowMs in [gridStart, gridEnd]`, so it auto-hides when viewing Tomorrow — no extra logic needed.

### Client — `apps/hermes-web-tv/src/components/EPGModal.jsx`
- `_tabWindow(tabId)` helper resolves a tab into `{ hours, startIso, windowStartMs, hoursForward }`. Used twice — once for the fetch, once for the EPGGrid props — so the on-wire request and the rendered window cannot drift.
- New `activeTab` state defaults to `'now'`. Visual signature on open is identical to before this PR.
- Three-pill tab strip in the modal header. Disabled state during inflight fetch prevents request pile-up; switching back to the active tab is always allowed (no-op).
- The fetch `useEffect` now re-runs on `activeTab` change.

## Stack note

Branch base is `feat/chatbot-play-this` (#119). Auto-rebases as the stack merges.

## Verification (local)

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `npm run build:web`        | green (index 362.53 kB) |
| `npm run validate:schemas` | 139 PASS, 0 FAIL |
| `npm run test:e2e`         | 12 PASS, 0 FAIL |
| `npm run test:chatbot`     | 46 PASS, 0 FAIL |
| Backend probe `hours=24` + `start=tomorrow 00:00 UTC` | `_meta.requested_hours: 24` (was capped at 12 before this PR) |

## Manual test plan

- [ ] Open EPG (📺 Guide) → "Now" is pre-selected; grid shows the next 4 hours
- [ ] Click **Today** → grid re-fetches, shows current time through tonight's midnight; "now" indicator still visible at left
- [ ] Click **Tomorrow** → grid shows 24h starting at tomorrow 00:00 local; "now" indicator hidden (outside window)
- [ ] Click a future program on Tomorrow → ScheduleRecordingModal opens with tomorrow's airtime pre-filled (uses the EPG → schedule wiring from #116)
- [ ] Provider filter still works — switching the provider re-fetches with the same tab's window
- [ ] No request pile-up: rapid-clicking Today / Tomorrow doesn't crash the loading state

body:
## Summary

`globals()` at module scope was missing the nine standard dunder keys that CPython 3.12 always pre-populates before executing any user code. Code that inspects the module namespace by probing these keys silently got wrong answers.

- Adds `Interpreter::seed_module_dunders` called from `try_exec_vm_script_with_index` at the correct architectural level (not a patch on the `globals()` builtin handler).
- Pre-seeds `__name__`, `__doc__`, `__annotations__`, `__builtins__`, `__spec__`, `__loader__`, `__package__`, `__file__`, `__cached__` into the module env before `run_bytecode` fires.
- User assignments override the pre-seeded values naturally (fastlocal register or `assign_name`).

## Test plan

- [ ] Parity fixture `crates/pyrust/tests/cases/runtime/test_globals_dunders.py`: presence, values, user override, and globals() from inside a function.
- [ ] `cargo test --release --bin pyrust`: 286/286 pass.
- [ ] `cargo test --release --test parity_compare`: only pre-existing failures (unrelated to this change).
- [ ] Manual repro from issue body matches CPython 3.12 byte-for-byte.

## Out of scope

- `__builtins__` identity: pyrust's `__builtins__` is a fresh module object from `load_builtin_module`, not the same object as `import builtins`. The `is` identity differs from CPython but `type(...).__name__ == "module"` matches.
- Populating `__file__` with the actual script path (requires threading the path through `Interpreter`; deferred per issue).

author: ryumiel
body:
## Summary

- Makes implementer DONE snapshot manifests trigger-based and controller-classified instead of universal.
- Updates `play-subagent-execution` prompts and examples so requested snapshots use the recipe/helper while skipped snapshots report default DONE fields.
- Adds source and render contract coverage for trigger categories, requested/skipped prompt behavior, and the skip-dispatch exclusion.

## Why

Universal snapshot expectations added unnecessary side-channel overhead to low-risk implementer dispatches and blurred the boundary between dispatched implementer DONE reports and skip-dispatch controller work. Issue #280 asks for a durable ADR-backed policy where snapshots are optional or trigger-based while high-risk work keeps stronger evidence.

## Implementation Notes / Behavior Changes

- **play-subagent-execution:** The controller owns snapshot request/skip classification. Plan hints are advisory, unclear classifications request snapshots, and requested-snapshot failures are treated as BLOCKED or incident states.
- **Snapshot triggers:** The operative trigger list now explicitly covers governed outputs, generated-output behavior, schema/type contracts, cross-agent or cross-skill handoffs, path/filesystem/security-sensitive behavior, broad changes, explicit audit requests, and unclear classification.
- **Skipped snapshots:** Skipped dispatches do not read the snapshot recipe or run the helper. They must report status, summary, tests, files changed, base SHA, and head SHA.
- **ADRs:** ADR-0014 now documents the trigger-based policy. ADR-0015 no longer describes skip-dispatch plan bodies as snapshots.
- **Contracts:** Source-contract and render integration tests guard the request/skip prompt text, ADR trigger terms, skip-dispatch exclusion, and generated Claude/Codex skill outputs.

## Impact and Risk

- **User-facing:** Low-risk implementer dispatches can avoid snapshot manifests; high-risk dispatches still require them.

author: xwizard
body:
## Summary

Three small source tweaks that let the OpenGL renderer build and run on Apple Silicon. The Windows/MSVC and Linux/GCC paths are unchanged — every change is gated behind `__APPLE__` / `__aarch64__` checks or `__has_include`.

- **`stdafx.h`** — use `GLM_FORCE_NEON` on ARM64 instead of `GLM_FORCE_AVX2`. `GLM_FORCE_AVX2` pulls `<immintrin.h>`, which clang on ARM64 rejects because the x86 intrinsics are unimplemented.
- **`utilities/utilities.cpp`** — provide an Apple-only fallback for `Now()` using `localtime_r` + `strftime("%c")`, since `std::chrono::current_zone()` is not yet implemented in Apple's libc++.
- **`audio/audio.h`** — prefer Khronos-style `<AL/al.h>` headers when they're on the include path (brew `openal-soft`) and fall back to the deprecated Apple `OpenAL.framework`'s `<OpenAL/al.h>` only otherwise. Apple's framework has been the source of past crashes in MaSzyna (see 38e89ee5).

With these three patches plus the build flags listed below, the macOS build links cleanly and runs against existing asset installs.

## Build invocation used for verification

```bash
git submodule update --init ref/asio ref/discord-rpc ref/glfw ref/glm ref/json
git submodule update --init --recursive ref/discord-rpc

cmake .. \
  -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
  -DCMAKE_PREFIX_PATH=/opt/homebrew \
  -DWITH_BETTER_RENDERER=OFF \
  -DENABLE_AVX2=OFF \
  -DWITH_UART=OFF \
  -DWITH_PYTHON=ON \
  -DPYTHON_INCLUDE_DIR=<pyenv 2.7.18>/include/python2.7 \
  -DPYTHON_LIBRARY=<pyenv 2.7.18>/lib/libpython2.7.dylib \
  -DOPENAL_LIBRARY=/opt/homebrew/opt/openal-soft/lib/libopenal.dylib \
  -DOPENAL_INCLUDE_DIR=/opt/homebrew/opt/openal-soft/include
cmake --build . --parallel
```

Brew formulae used: `glfw libpng libsndfile openal-soft luajit asio`. Python 2.7 via pyenv (Homebrew dropped `python@2`). `WITH_BETTER_RENDERER` stays OFF — NVRHI/DX12 is Windows-only.

## Test plan

- [x] Builds cleanly on macOS 26 / Apple Silicon with Apple Clang 21
- [x] Resulting binary links against `brew openal-soft` (not the deprecated `OpenAL.framework`)
- [x] Launches and runs against an existing asset install
- [x] Confirm Windows/MSVC build is unaffected (changes are guarded behind `__APPLE__` / `__aarch64__`, but a CI run would be reassuring)
- [x] Confirm Linux/GCC build is unaffected (same — guarded; should be a no-op there)

author: zhouzhuojie
body:
## What

Two changes:

### 1. Flagr: regex literal form for EREG/NEREG

For **EREG/NEREG** operators with quoted string values (e.g. `"\d+"`), `toExprStr()` now outputs the **regex literal form** `/pattern/` instead of `"pattern"` when the pattern doesn't contain `/`:

| Before | After |
|---|---|
| `({s} =~ "\d+")` ❌ scanner error | `({s} =~ /\d+/)` ✅ |
| `({email} =~ ".+@example\.com")` ❌ | `({email} =~ /.+@example\.com/)` ✅ |

This eliminates Go `text/scanner` "invalid char escape" stderr noise.

### 2. Upgrade: conditions v0.2.6

Pulls in the `strconv.Unquote` fix for the conditions parser, enabling correct matching on values containing `"` and `\`:

| Expression | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `{s} == "he said \"hey\""` | ❌ `\"` treated as 2 raw bytes | ✅ Unescaped to `"` |
| `{s} == "path\\to\\file"` | ❌ `\\` treated as 2 raw bytes | ✅ Unescaped to `\` |
| `{s} =~ "\d+"` (invalid Go escape) | ⚠️ Raw fallback (noisy) | ✅ Same fallback (unchanged) |

## Tests

13 new subtests for the Flagr-side regex fix + conditions v0.2.6 includes 14 escape sequence tests.

Closes #618

author: dunqing
body:
## Summary

Threads a `recycled_scoping: Option<Scoping>` through `PreProcessEcmaAst::build` so the stale `Scoping` after each AST-mutating pass (transformer / define / inject / DCE) can be recycled. The next `recreate_scoping` call uses `Scoping::reset` to clear it in place — preserving the bumpalo arena's chunks and the flat-table heap capacity — and feeds it back to `SemanticBuilder::with_scoping`. This avoids the allocator init cost on each rebuild (3-4 times per file).

DCE is switched from `dead_code_elimination_with_scoping` (consumes the scoping) to `dead_code_elimination_with_scoping_returning_scoping` so the post-DCE scoping can be recycled too.

The initial Step 1 build (`with_check_syntax_error(true)`) is unchanged — the syntax checker still uses the default builder.

## Benchmark

`cargo bench -p bench`, this branch vs `origin/main`:

| Bench | main | this PR | Δ |
|---|---|---|---|
| threejs | 23.27 ms | 22.35 ms | **−4.0%** |
| threejs-sourcemap | 27.82 ms | 27.38 ms | **−1.6%** |
| rome_ts | 44.54 ms | 43.31 ms | **−2.8%** |
| multi-duplicated-top-level-symbol | 19.42 ms | 19.94 ms | +2.7% (noisy, criterion interval [19.26, 21.0]) |

Three out of four show clear wins.

### Motivation
- Identify and document core defects in the current ESMM implementation, especially that the model only supervises a single `ctcvr_logit` and therefore does not independently optimize CTR and CVR losses.  
- Propose a practical, staged roadmap to restore true ESMM behavior and improve performance via multi-task loss, task-specific representations, and bias/time modeling.  

### Description
- Added `esmm_bug_analysis_and_optimization.md` which summarizes the problems (single-logit supervision, shared output embedding, CVR clicked-only bias, and additive `time_bucket` fusion) and maps them to code locations (`model.py`, `trainer.py`, `MultiSeqQueryGenerator`).  
- The document prescribes Phase 1 changes (return `ctr_logit`/`cvr_logit`/`ctcvr_logit` and use joint losses `L_ctr + L_cvr + L_ctcvr` with click-masked CVR loss), Phase 2 structural changes (MMoE/CGC expert+gate to decouple task representations), and Phase 3 refinements (click-aware query path and multiplicative time-decay).  
- Includes engineering rollout steps, recommended default loss weights, evaluation metrics to monitor (CTR/CVR/CTCVR AUC & logloss), ablation matrix, and risk mitigation suggestions.  

### Testing
- Ran repository and file checks which all succeeded: `git status --short` (verified new file), `git add esmm_bug_analysis_and_optimization.md && git commit -m "docs: summarize ESMM branch issues and optimization roadmap"` (commit created), and `nl -ba esmm_bug_analysis_and_optimization.md | sed -n '1,240p'` (file contents inspected).

author: rickardcollander-ops
body:
The team-members panel and admin "new customer" flow were both showing the literal string "{}" when Supabase returned an empty/non-string error message. The previous patch detected the case for the lookup fallback but still surfaced the raw value when the user could not be found. Centralizes the normalization in a describeError helper so any ``{}``, ``[object Object]`` or empty-string message becomes a useful fallback before reaching the client.

Also tidies the /c/admin row that now has eight possible actions: View as, Set password and Grant/Revoke stay as primary buttons; Invite, Reset password mail, Change email, Confirm email and Delete move into a per-row dropdown so the table doesn't overflow horizontally.

In TeamManagementPanel, replaces the ugly
``brand-12345@accounts.internal`` placeholder email with "Account owner (no email yet)" so admin-created customers without a real email don't look broken in the team list.

## Summary

Add a SQLite-backed state store as a foundation for migrating from HMAC-protected JSON files to a queryable database, while preserving Vigil's integrity model.

## Changes

**Cargo.toml** — added usqlite with  undled feature (SQLite compiled from source, no system dependency).

**src/storage/db.rs** — new StorageDb module:

- **Schema bootstrap** — creates 5 tables on first open:
  - meta — key/value metadata (schema version, etc.)
  - dvisory_source — NVD/NCSC/BSI source tracking
  - dvisory_record — normalized vulnerability records with indexes
  - dvisory_change_event — NVD change-history events
  - software_inventory — installed software with path index
- **Integrity model** — compute_digest() hashes table row counts + meta pairs into a deterministic SHA-256; checkpoint() persists via the existing security::policy HMAC layer; erify() detects tamper and fails closed
- **WAL mode** + foreign keys enabled

**Tests** (5):

| Test | What it verifies |
|---|---|
|  ootstrap_creates_tables | All 5 tables exist after init |
| schema_version_is_stored | Schema version persisted in meta table |
| compute_digest_is_stable | Digest is deterministic on empty DB |
| checkpoint_and_verify_round_trip | Full checkpoint/verify cycle works |
| erify_fails_after_tamper | Tamper detection via diget mismatch |

## Validation

- cargo test: 318 tests pass (was 313)
- cargo build: clean
- cargo fmt --check: clean

<!-- START COPILOT ORIGINAL PROMPT -->



<details>

<summary>Original prompt</summary>


## 任务目标

请在仓库根目录创建一个单一 Python 文件 `auto_testcase_generator.py`，实现一个面向企业测试工程的**自动测试用例生成系统**，基于 LangChain + LangGraph 实现 Agent 编排，完整覆盖以下 8 阶段流程和所有设计原则。

---

## 系统总体架构

```
需求接入
  ↓
RequirementAnalysisAgent：需求理解与结构化
  ↓
TestModelingAgent：测试模型生成
  ↓
TestCaseGenerationAgent：测试用例生成
  ↓
QualityReviewAgent：质量评审与规则校验
  ↓
ConfidenceAndHumanGateAgent：置信度评分与人工确认分流
  ↓
人工确认：采纳 / 修改 / 拒绝 / 自动化转换
```

---

## 详细实现要求

### 1. 依赖与配置
- 使用 `langchain`, `langgraph`, `langchain-openai`, `pydantic v2`, `jsonschema`, `structlog` 等
- 通过环境变量 `OPENAI_API_KEY`, `OPENAI_BASE_URL`, `OPENAI_MODEL` 配置 LLM
- 配置类 `SystemConfig` 使用 `pydantic-settings` 管理所有可配置参数
- 日志使用 `structlog` 结构化日志，符合生产实践

### 2. Pydantic 数据模型（严格定义，v2 语法）

定义以下核心模型：

**输入模型 `RequirementInput`**：
- `prd_content: str` - PRD文档内容
- `user_stories: list[str]` - 用户故事列表
- `api_docs: list[dict]` - 接口文档
- `prototype_desc: str` - 原型描述
- `historical_defects: list[dict]` - 历史缺陷
- `existing_cases: list[dict]` - 已有用例
- `generation_granularity: Literal["smoke", "core", "regression", "full"]` - 生成粒度
- `target_case_types: list[CaseType]` - 目标用例类型枚举

**结构化需求 `StructuredRequirement`**：
- `modules`, `functions`, `rules`, `constraints`, `roles`, `flows`, `interfaces`, `acceptance_criteria`
- `business_goal`, `business_context`, `prerequisites`, `exception_handling_rules`
- `state_machine: dict`, `io_field_dict: dict`, `permission_model: dict`
- `data_constraints: list[str]`, `external_system_deps: list[str]`
- `change_impact_scope: list[str]`, `test_priority_basis: str`
- `quality_issues: list[QualityIssue]` - 需求质量问题列表

**测试模型 `TestModel`**：
- `business_process_model: BusinessProcessModel` (主/分支/异常/补偿/回滚流程)
- `state_transition_model: StateTransitionModel` (初始/可达/禁止状态，迁移条件/异常)
- `rule_model: RuleModel` (业务/校验/风控/幂等/权限/SLA规则)
- `test_points: list[TestPoint]`

**测试点 `TestPoint`**：
- `point_id`, `name`, `dimension`, `related_rule`, `coverage_source`
- `risk_level: Literal["P0","P1","P2","P3"]`, `priority: int`
- `related_requirements: list[str]`, `related_interfaces: list[str]`, `related_defects: list[str]`

**测试用例 `TestCase`**：
- `case_id: str`, `case_type: CaseType`, `granularity: Granularity`
- `title: str`, `objective: str`
- `preconditions: list[str]`, `test_data: dict`, `steps: list[TestStep]`
- `expected_results: list[str]`, `assertions: list[str]`
- `risk_description: str`, `priority: str`
- `traceability: Traceability` (关联需求/接口/规则/缺陷/测试点/模型版本)
- `tags: list[str]`, `automation_feasibility: bool`, `automation_framework_hint: str`

**质量评审结果 `QualityReviewResult`**：
- `schema_valid: bool`, `field_completeness_rate: float`
- `content_issues: list[str]`, `traceability_issues: list[str]`
- `duplicate_rate: float`, `duplicate_groups: list[list[str]]`
- `non_executable_cases: list[str]`, `missing_expected_result_cases: list[str]`
- `coverage_matrix: dict`, `high_priority_coverage_rate: float`
- `llm_judge_score: float`, `llm_judge_comments: str`
- `overall_quality_score: float`

**置信度评分 `ConfidenceScore`**：
- `case_id: str`
- `layer1_llm_score: float` (LLM自评 0-1)
- `layer2_rule_score: float` (规则引擎 0-1)
- `layer3_gate_passed: bool` (人工门禁是否通过)
- `final_confidence: float`
- `confidence_level: Literal["HIGH","MEDIUM","LOW"]`
- `route_decision: Literal["auto_approve","human_review","reject"]`

**流水线状态 `PipelineState`** (LangGraph State TypedDict)：
- 包含所有中间产物和最终结果
- `current_stage`, `errors`, `metrics`, `human_review_queue`, `final_approved_cases`

### 3. LangGraph 流水线节点实现

使用 `StateGraph` 构建有向图，节点如下：

**节点1: `requirement_ingestion_node`**
- 验证输入完整性
- 计算输入统计信息
- 设置 current_stage

**节点2: `requirement_analysis_node` (RequirementAnalysisAgent)**
- 调用 LLM 提取结构化需求（StructuredRequirement）
- 同时执行需求质量检查（检测歧义/缺失/冲突/不可测试点）
- Prompt 要求输出严格 JSON，包含所有字段
- 解析失败时有重试机制（最多3次）

**节点3: `test_modeling_node` (TestModelingAgent)**
- 基于结构化需求生成完整 TestModel
- 分步生成：业务流程模型 → 状态迁移模型 → 规则模型 → 测试点列表
- 每个测试点必须关联来源需求
- 覆盖率矩阵生成（需求 × 测试维度）

**节点4: `test_case_generation_node` (TestCaseGenerationAgent)**
- 按粒度控制生成用例数量（smoke≤10, core≤30, regression≤100, full无限制）
- 按用例类型使用不同 Prompt 模板
- 每条用例必须关联测试点（Traceability）
- 生成后立即执行去重（多维度：目标/前置/数据/断言/规则/语义）
- 抽取公共前置/数据/步骤/断言到复用库

**节点5: `quality_review_node` (QualityReviewAgent)**
- JSON Schema 校验（使用 jsonschema 库）
- 必填字段完整率计算
- 内容校验（需求来源/测试目标/预期结果/可执行步骤/测试数据/风险说明）
- 关联校验（需求/接口/规则/历史缺陷/模型版本）
- 语义重复率计算（基于 embedding 或文本相似度）
- LLM Judge 打分（对每条用例质量打分 0-100，输出综合评审意见）
- 覆盖率矩阵校验（P0/P1必须100%覆盖）
- 生成 QualityReviewResult

**节点6: `confidence_scoring_node` (ConfidenceAndHumanGateAgent)**
- Layer1 LLM 自评：让 LLM 对每条用例打置信度分（0-1）
- Layer2 规则引擎：
  - 字段完整 +0.1
  - 有追溯链 +0.1  
  - 预期结果明确 +0.1
  - 步骤可执行 +0.1
  - 关联历史缺陷 +0.05
  - 质量评审通过 +0.15
  - 语义重复扣 -0.2
  - 不可执行扣 -0.3
- Layer3 门禁：
  - HIGH(≥0.8): route=auto_approve（仍加入人工审核队列，标注高置信）
  - MEDIUM(0.6-0.8): route=human_review
  - LOW(<0.6): route=reject（自动拒绝，记录原因）
- 计算整体指标（A1-A15验收标准）

**节点7: `human_review_preparation_node`**
- 整理人工审核队列（按优先级排序）
- 为每条用例生成审核摘要卡片（含置信度、风险、质量问题、建议操作）
- 输出人工确认工作台数据结构
- 模拟人工确认接口（`HumanReviewAction`: approve/modify/reject/convert_to_automation）
...

</details>

author: copilot
body:
Nodes created from the dropped-connection context menus were being placed too high because creation used the menu anchor position (which includes UI offsets) instead of the actual mouse drop point. This updates node placement to use the raw drop coordinates while preserving existing menu positioning.

- **Preserve drop coordinates at connection end**
  - In `useConnectionHandlers`, when opening `input-context-menu` / `output-context-menu` from a dropped connection, include `dropPosition: { x, y }` in the context menu payload.
  - Keep existing menu anchor offsets (`+25`, `-50`) unchanged so menu UX remains the same.

- **Use drop coordinates for node creation from connectable lists**
  - In `OutputContextMenu`, connectable node creation now uses `payload.dropPosition` (fallback: `menuPosition`).
  - In `InputContextMenu`, same behavior for connectable node creation (`payload.dropPosition` with fallback).

- **Payload compatibility**
  - For input-side payloads, existing numeric metadata (`connectMin`, `connectMax`, `connectDefault`) is preserved and extended with `dropPosition`.

- **Focused regression coverage**
  - Added tests in `useConnectionHandlers.test.ts` verifying:
    - source-side dropped menu carries `dropPosition`
    - target-side dropped menu carries `dropPosition` without losing numeric payload fields

```ts
const dropPosition = { x: event.clientX, y: event.clientY };

openContextMenu(
  "input-context-menu",
  connectNodeId || "",
  event.clientX + 25,  // menu anchor (unchanged)
  event.clientY - 50,  // menu anchor (unchanged)
  "react-flow__pane",
  connectType ?? undefined,
  connectHandleId || "",
  undefined,
  undefined,
  { connectMin, connectMax, connectDefault, dropPosition }
);

// later in context menu node creation:
const anchorPosition = payload?.dropPosition ?? menuPosition;
```

author: vikramj01
body:
AI recommendations can include Playwright-style pseudo-selectors such as :has-text() and :text() in element_selector. These are not valid CSS and cause the SELECTOR_VALIDITY rule to block output generation.

Add selectorUtils.ts with sanitizeSelector():
- Splits comma-separated selector lists
- Drops individual parts containing :has-text(), :contains(), or :text()
- Returns a clean CSS selector when valid parts survive
- Falls back to textFallback (extracted text value) when all parts were invalid, so the caller can use a click_text trigger instead

Apply sanitizeSelector in recToIREvent (gtmContainerGenerator) and recToIREventForSpec (dataLayerSpecGenerator) replacing the previous :contains()-only check.

author: orvaroddr
body:
## Bug

En el detalle (y en el chip de tabla/panel) la fecha de vencimiento se mostraba **dos veces**: `19-06-2027 · 19-06-2027`.

## Causa

Tras el pase de pulido, `dueUrgency()` para fechas a más de 30 días devolvía la **fecha formateada** como `label`, y los render hacían `dueDateLabel · urg.label` → duplicado.

## Fix

- `dueUrgency` caso lejano (>30 d): `label: ''` (sin frase relativa).
- Los 3 puntos de render concatenan el relativo solo cuando aporta:
  - Tabla/Panel: `{urg.label ? urg.label + ' · ' : ''}{fecha}`
  - Detalle: `{fecha}{urg.label ? ' · ' + urg.label : ''}`
- Resultado: cerca → "Vence en 5 d · 19-06-2027"; lejos → "19-06-2027" (una vez). Kanban no estaba afectado (usa su propio helper y renderiza solo el label).

## Verificación

`npm run build`, `npm run lint`, `npm test` (17/17) OK. Va a `develop`.

<details>

<summary>Original prompt</summary>

Working title: **“Medical Outcomes Explorer”** — an SEO-friendly name that includes “Medical,” “outcomes,” and “explorer” as primary keywords.[^1_1]

Below is a BRD you can hand to autonomous agents.

---

## Product vision and goals

Build a **fully static, open‑source analytics site on GitHub Pages** that lets users explore US hospital performance, outcomes, and safety indicators over time, and relate these to medical device and FDA clearance data.[^1_2][^1_3][^1_4]
The North Star is **organic search traffic (SEO)**, so the site must produce richly crawlable, keyword‑optimized, multi‑page HTML with explanatory content alongside interactive charts and tables.[^1_5][^1_6]
The product must run **without any backend or database**, using only GitHub Pages hosting, build‑time data pulls, and optional browser localStorage for client‑side caching.

---

## Primary users and use cases

Primary users are health‑tech founders, clinical researchers, journalists, and policy analysts who want **quick, visual, and source‑linked insights** on hospital quality and device impact without wrangling raw CMS/FDA files.[^1_4][^1_7]
Key use cases include comparing outcome metrics across hospitals, seeing how quality indicators evolve over time, and exploring whether introduction or recall of certain device classes coincides with trends in complications or readmissions.[^1_3][^1_4]
Secondary users include students and data/AI practitioners seeking public, well‑structured health data for demos, tutorials, and models.

---

## In‑scope and out‑of‑scope

In scope: US acute care and other Medicare‑certified hospitals, CMS quality/outcome metrics, hospital ratings, and selected FDA device datasets that can reasonably be connected at the level of time, indication, or procedure category.[^1_8][^1_3][^1_4]
Out of scope for v1: individual patient‑level data, non‑US facilities, paywalled datasets (e.g., full HCUP NIS/SID), and any data that requires human subject approvals or controlled‑access environments.[^1_9]
Also out of scope for v1: real‑time streaming updates; instead, use scheduled rebuilds (e.g., monthly/quarterly GitHub Actions) for semi‑fresh snapshots.

---

## Data sources catalog

These are the core public and free datasets the project should use.

### CMS Provider Data Catalog – current hospital data

CMS’s Provider Data Catalog (PDC) publishes current **hospital general information** and quality measures used on Medicare’s Care Compare site; datasets include hospital characteristics, ratings, complications, readmissions, mortality, and patient experience.[^1_10][^1_2][^1_8]
The PDC provides an **API that does not require an API key**; documentation explicitly states that no key is needed for access.[^1_6][^1_5]
This will be the main source for “current state” views: maps, filters by hospital type/owner/ratings, and up‑to‑date quality metrics.

Key dataset examples (non‑exhaustive):

- **Hospital General Information** – list of all Medicare‑registered hospitals with address, phone, type, and overall rating.[^1_10]
- **Quality and outcome measures** – mortality, readmissions, complications, patient experience (HCAHPS), infection rates, payment and value of care, etc., exposed as Care Compare measures via PDC and updated periodically.[^1_7][^1_8][^1_4]

### CMS Hospitals Data Archive (Hospital Compare / Care Compare)

CMS maintains an **archived “Hospitals Data Archive”** (Hospital Compare / Care Compare historical files) with multi‑year history of hospital mortality, patient safety indicators, HAIs, unplanned visits, imaging efficiency, and program outcomes (HACRP, HRRP, HVBP).[^1_4]
These archives are provided as periodic snapshot files (e.g., quarterly/yearly), making them ideal for build‑time ingestion and longitudinal visualizations of interventions over time.[^1_8][^1_4]
There is a public GitHub project that already curates and combines these archive files for easier analysis, which can be used as a reference or upstream data pipeline.[^1_4]

### CMS hospital comparison derivatives (optional)

Third‑party repackagings such as “Hospital Data from CMS” hosted by Placekey provide curated, geocoded data on Medicare‑certified hospitals, VA medical centers, and DoD hospitals, including patient survey results and ratings.[^1_1]

body:
## Summary
- Stops OpenClaw's "access not configured — reply /pair …" Telegram prompt on every fresh setup. OpenClaw's `dmPolicy` defaults to `pairing`, and setting `commands.ownerAllowFrom` alone doesn't bypass it ([docs.openclaw.ai/gateway/security](https://docs.openclaw.ai/gateway/security): DM policy and command authorization are independent layers). Foreman now also writes `channels.telegram.dmPolicy: "allowlist"` plus the matching `channels.telegram.allowFrom` array — both populated from the user's `telegram-chat-id` secret.
- Fixes a parallel **#425-class regression** in `config_overrides`: the entire section was gated by `!resolverWonProviderWrites`, so any `if_service` write was silently dropped whenever the resolver path won (which is exactly what happens for OpenClaw/Hermes — both have `provider_mapping`). Per-entry gate now: skip *only* provider-gated entries when the resolver owns provider writes; service-gated writes fire regardless.

## What ships
- **Projector**: per-entry gate on `config_overrides` (mirrors the #425 env_vars fix). Also threads chat-primary check through the same path. `writeSecurityBootstrap` accepts an array of keys for `ownerAllowlist` and writes the same value array to each.
- **Schema**: `owner_allowlist.key` is now `string | string[]` — accepts a single dot-path (legacy) or an array (new).
- **Registry**: OpenClaw's `config_overrides.writes` gains `{ if_service: "telegram", set: { "channels.telegram.dmPolicy": "allowlist" } }`. `security_bootstrap.owner_allowlist.key` becomes `["commands.ownerAllowFrom", "channels.telegram.allowFrom"]` so dmPolicy validation passes (OpenClaw rejects empty `allowFrom` when policy=allowlist).
- **Tests**: 2 new projector tests + 3 updated security-bootstrap tests. 2419 / 2419 green; tsup build clean.

## Test plan
- [x] `npx vitest run` — 2419 passing.
- [x] `node dist/cli/index.js registry validate` — passes (schema update + registry payload align).
- [ ] E2E: fresh wipe → `foreman setup` → pick OpenClaw + telegram → check `~/.openclaw/openclaw.json` contains `channels.telegram.dmPolicy: "allowlist"` AND `channels.telegram.allowFrom` with the user's chat id.
- [ ] Restart OpenClaw, DM the bot — should respond without the `/pair` prompt.

Closes #427

author: sdebruyn
body:
Fixes #399.

`FabricAdapter.quote()`, `FabricColumn.quoted`, `FabricRelation.quoted`, and five Jinja macro sites all compose bracket-quoted T-SQL identifiers without escaping `]`. Any identifier containing `]` produces invalid T-SQL, and a crafted identifier of the form `foo];<sql>--` lets a name terminate the bracket and inject arbitrary T-SQL into whatever statement the macro is composing. The dbt-fabric attack surface is small (identifiers are usually static), but projects that derive names from external systems are exposed, and silent breakage on reserved-word columns containing `]` is a real bug regardless.

## Changes

Doubling `]` to `]]` inside the brackets is the standard T-SQL escape ([Delimited Identifiers](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/sql/relational-databases/databases/database-identifiers#delimited-identifiers?WT.mc_id=MVP_310840)). Applied at every bracket-quoting site:

- `FabricAdapter.quote()` — `identifier.replace("]", "]]")` before the format.
- `FabricColumn.quoted` — same on `self.column`.
- `FabricRelation.quoted()` — same on `identifier`.
- `fabric__alter_column_type` (`columns.sql`) — both the `CAST` source and the alias.
- `fabric__alter_relation_add_remove_columns` (`columns.sql`) — `add` and `drop column` branches.
- `fabric__create_table_as` (`create_table_as.sql`) — the `listColumns` block used for `contract.enforced` models.
- `fabric__create_columns` (snapshot `helpers.sql`) — column addition during snapshot column expansion.

The Jinja escape uses the standard `| replace(']', ']]')` filter inside the existing `[ ... ]` wrapper.

## Out of scope

This PR only adds the missing escape. Two related quoting inconsistencies were noticed while writing the patch but kept out to keep the diff reviewable:

- `fabric__alter_column_type`'s metadata-query branch composes column names with double quotes (`'"' + ... + '"'`) while the rest of the file uses brackets.
- `fabric__get_use_database_sql` currently *strips* `[`/`]`/`"` from the database name rather than escaping them. That is safe against injection but silently rewrites identifiers that legitimately contain those characters.

Happy to follow up on either in separate PRs if useful.

author: shrwnsan
body:
## PRD-002 Phase 7.5 + 7.6 — Formatter + CLI Integration Tests

Implements Task 7.5 (formatter snapshot tests) and Task 7.6 (CLI integration tests) — first end-to-end Bun test coverage of the rendered formatter output and the `weather` CLI entry point.

### What's in this PR

| File | Tests | Coverage |
|---|---|---|
| `test/formatters/fixtures.ts` | — | Shared `fullyPopulatedCurrent` + 2-day `forecastDays` payloads |
| `test/formatters/cli_text.test.ts` | 4 | Snapshot of current + forecast; "no N/A placeholders" policy |
| `test/formatters/telegram.test.ts` | 8 | Snapshot of current + forecast; full `escapeMdv2` characterization |
| `test/formatters/whatsapp.test.ts` | 4 | Snapshot of current + forecast; "no escapes" assertion |
| `test/cli.test.ts` | 10 | Drives `src/cli.ts` `run()` end-to-end |

### Formatter snapshots (Task 7.5)

UTC-midnight forecast dates + `freezeTime()` (Thu 2026-01-01T00:00:00Z) give deterministic day-of-week labels (`Fri Jan 2`, `Sat Jan 3`) across runtimes.

`telegram.test.ts` includes a focused suite on `escapeMdv2`:

```ts
expect(MDV2_ESCAPE_CHARS).toEqual(
  new Set(["_","*","[","]","(",")","~","`",">","#",
          "+","-","=","|","{","}",".","!"])  // 18 chars
);
```

— pinning the exact Telegram-reserved set, asserting every reserved char gets a single backslash, leaving non-reserved chars untouched, and documenting the (deliberate) lack of idempotency.

### CLI integration (Task 7.6)

Drives `src/cli.ts` `run()` directly (not via subprocess) with `process.stdout/stderr.write` capture — fast, deterministic, no shell escaping issues.

| Test | Assertion |
|---|---|
| `--location "Hong Kong"` | text output, exit 0, "Weather for Hong Kong" + "Provider: hko" |
| `(no args)` | default location is Hong Kong |
| `--format json` | sorted keys, snake_case, `fetched_at` = `"2026-01-01T00:00:00.000Z"` |
| `--format json --forecast --days 2` | JSON array, `provider_name === "hko"` |
| `--send --format json` | exit 2, stderr error |
| `--provider nonexistent` | exit 1, stderr lists "hko, jma, nws, sg_nea" |
| `--help` | exit 0, "usage: weather" on stdout |
| `--days 3.5` | exit 1, "argument --days: invalid int value: '3.5'" (P6-1 strict-int) |
| `--format xml` | exit 1, choices error |
| `--bogus` | exit 1, "unrecognized argument: --bogus" |

`test/setup.ts` already auto-installs the fetch mock at `beforeAll` (Phase 7.3); the CLI test opts into `freezeTime()` per `beforeEach`/`afterEach` so frozen-clock assertions are deterministic without affecting other test files.

### Verification

- ✅ `bun test` → **34/34 pass** (8 setup + 16 formatter + 10 CLI)
- ✅ `bun run typecheck` → 0 errors
- ✅ `pytest` → 69/69 pass (no Python regressions)

### Scout findings for Phase 7.4 follow-up (⚠️ NOT in this PR)

While scouting the providers against the Phase 7.1 fixtures to plan Task 7.4, two real cross-runtime bugs were uncovered (both also present in the Python providers — verified by reading the source):

1. **SG NEA — crash on real `general.forecast` shape.** The current API response wraps the forecast as `{text, code}` (e.g. `{"text": "Thundery Showers", "code": "TL"}`) but both Python's `general.get("forecast", "")` and TS's `general.forecast ?? ""` treat it as a string. The TS provider then calls `text.toLowerCase()` and throws `TypeError: text.toLowerCase is not a function`. Python would hit the same crash via `.lower()` on a dict. **Fix needs to land on both runtimes simultaneously**.

2. **JMA — `forecast[0]` missing `temperature` / `temp_high` / `temp_low` / `precipitation_chance`.** The first day's fields parse as empty defaults (`temperature: 0`, no `temp_high`). `forecast[1]` and `forecast[2]` are complete. Likely the parser is reading day-0 from the wrong `timeSeries` index. Affects both runtimes.

Both are blockers for Task 7.4 (provider tests). Logging here so the Phase 7.4 PR can land the fix + test in the same change.

### Phase 7 plan after this PR

- **7.4** — Provider tests + SG NEA + JMA cross-runtime fixes (5 provider files; OWM still blocked on fixture capture)
- **7.7** — Cross-runtime JSON parity test (depends on 7.4 + 7.6)

Refs: PRD-002 §Test Fixtures & Cross-Runtime Parity Test, Tasks 7.5 + 7.6

body:
## What was changed

Expanded the slash composer slice from visible autocomplete into the first executable command path. Runtime-declared `/` commands now support both inline insertion and runtime-command submission: Codex exposes `/review`, `/plan`, and `/goal` as inline prompt text, and `/compact` as a runtime command that submits immediately and clears the composer after execution.

The dashboard now routes runtime command selections through the session composer state and Codex workbench adapter, while unsupported runtime commands fail visibly instead of blocking ordinary slash-looking prompt text. The Storybook surface remains the manual test surface for the autocomplete menu and command execution behavior.

This update also carries the compatibility fixes needed after the stack absorbed the current `main` runtime work: Pi runtime ids are accepted where runtime state can surface them, unsupported Pi workbench paths are gated in dashboard selectors, sandboxd direct websocket and Pi proxy behavior were tightened, and runtime artifact checksum conflict validation now treats checksum changes as lifecycle changes.

## How to review

Start with `apps/dashboard/src/features/chat/components/chat-composer.tsx` for slash filtering, keyboard/mouse selection, inline insertion, and runtime-command auto-submit behavior.

Then review `apps/dashboard/src/features/pages/session-composer/use-session-composer-state.ts`, `apps/dashboard/src/features/session-agents/session-workbench-conversation-runtimes.ts`, and `packages/integrations-definitions/src/agent-runtimes/codex/composer-capabilities.ts` for how capabilities become executable Codex commands.

For the post-main compatibility fixes, review `packages/sandboxd/src/egress_proxy.rs`, `packages/sandboxd/src/pi_proxy.rs`, and the Pi/runtime id handling in `apps/dashboard/src/features/pages/sandbox-profile-runtime-section.tsx` and `packages/mstl-core/src/client.rs`.

Stack order is #2218 -> #2220 -> this PR.

## What the implication was

The composer now has a working end-to-end `/` command path without committing to `@` or `$` yet. Inline slash commands remain normal prompt text, unknown slash-looking prompts still submit as ordinary user input, and runtime commands can execute immediately when the selected runtime explicitly declares support.

The runtime compatibility fixes keep the branch aligned with the newer Pi/runtime infrastructure on `main` while preserving the dashboard rule that only supported runtime choices are selectable in the current workbench UI.

author: keysersoft
body:
## Summary

Closes the cross-domain license-handoff gap between the cloud frontend and `anythingmcp.com/pricing`:

- **Always-visible activation field**: the "Activate License Key" section on `/settings/license` was hidden during an active cloud trial. Admins now see it at all times so a purchased key can be pasted immediately.
- **`buildPricingUrl()` helper**: every `Upgrade Plan` / `View Plans` / `Upgrade now` link now appends `?return_url=<cloud-origin>/settings/license/activate`. Driven by `NEXT_PUBLIC_MARKETING_URL` (default `https://anythingmcp.com`).
- **New `/settings/license/activate` callback page**: reads `?key=AMCP-XXXX-XXXX-XXXX-XXXX`, validates the format, calls `PUT /api/license/key` when an admin is signed in, otherwise sends the visitor through `/login?redirect=...` and resumes after sign-in. On success, redirects to `/settings/license`.

The marketing-site half of the flow lives in [anythingmcp-website#57](https://github.com/HelpCode-ai/anythingmcp-website/pull/57) — together they turn the post-checkout email-and-paste loop into a one-click redirect.

## Why

Reported by a customer who purchased a license and could not find a place to redeem it in the cloud UI: during an active trial the field was hidden, and the only path was to wait, copy-paste from email, or already know the deep URL.

## Test plan

- [ ] Sign in as admin on a cloud instance with an active trial → `/settings/license` shows the "Activate License Key" section
- [ ] Click "Upgrade Plan" / "View Plans" / the trial-banner CTA → opens `anythingmcp.com/pricing?return_url=...` with the cloud origin URL-encoded in the query
- [ ] Visit `/settings/license/activate?key=AMCP-XXXX-XXXX-XXXX-XXXX` while signed in as admin → key is activated and the page redirects to `/settings/license`
- [ ] Same URL while signed out → bounces through `/login?redirect=…` and resumes activation after sign-in
- [ ] Same URL while signed in as non-admin → shows error message instead of attempting the call
- [ ] Malformed key in URL → shows "license key in the URL is malformed" message without hitting the API

author: a1flecke
body:
## Summary

Five independent bug fixes from the 2026-05-18 bug bundle spec.

### #215 — Fog-of-war false contact (`discovery-system.ts`)
`hasMetCivilizationByCurrentEvidence` was using `hasExploredCoord` (which returns true for fog tiles) to decide if a civ had been "encountered". Any city within fog range was incorrectly treated as a contact. Fixed by switching to `getVisibility(...) === 'visible'` on all three checks (city position, owned tile scan, and map tile owner scan). Negative test added: a city tile in fog produces no contact.

### #214 — Conquered city workers not reassigned (`city-capture-system.ts`)
After `resolveMajorCityCapture` → `recalculateTerritory` → `normalizeCityWorkClaims`, there was no call to `normalizeCityWorkAfterTerritoryChange` for the captured city. Workers from the conquering civ couldn't claim tiles in the new city. Fixed by calling `normalizeCityWorkAfterTerritoryChange` inside `buildCaptureResult` when a `capturedCityId` is present.

### #220 — Worker warning panel missing turns remaining (`worker-task-warning-panel.ts`, `main.ts`)
The warning panel title was a static `"in progress"` string with no ETA. Added `turnsLeft: number` to `WorkerTaskWarningPanelConfig`; title now reads `"Farm in progress — 2 turns remaining"` (singular handled). The `main.ts` call site reads `tile.improvementTurnsLeft`.

### #218 — Dock building (`city-system.ts`, `buildings.tsx`, `sprite-catalog.ts`, `main.ts`)
- Added `dock` to `BUILDINGS`: cost 20, `core` pacing band, `coastalRequired: true`, `techRequired: 'fishing'`, yields `{food:2, gold:1}`.
- Added `isCityCoastal()` helper using `city.ownedTiles` (not city position) to detect water adjacency.
- `getAvailableBuildings` now accepts `mapTiles` and filters coastal-required buildings.
- Added `DockSprite` with SMIL wave-ripple and boat-rock animations (CSS stripped in `svgOnly` mode per sprite rules).
- After researching Fishing tech, a guidance notification nudges the player toward coastal cities.

### #219 — Building placement UX (`city-system.ts`, `adjacency-system.ts`, `city-grid.ts`, `city-panel.ts`, `main.ts`)
When `placeBuildingInGrid` can't find an optimal slot, buildings end up in an "Unplaced" list with no way to place them. Fixed end-to-end:
- `isSlotUnlocked` exported from `adjacency-system.ts`.
- New pure `placeBuilding(city, buildingId, row, col)` validates slot is unlocked, empty, and building is unplaced before writing.
- Grid tab: unplaced buildings are now tappable `createGameButton` rows. Tapping one highlights all empty unlocked slots with a gold dashed border; tapping a slot places the building; tapping the button again cancels.
- `city:building-complete` fires a second `info` log entry when a building couldn't auto-place, telling the player to open the Grid tab.
- `onPlaceBuilding` callback in `main.ts` applies the mutation and re-opens the panel.

Also fixed two pre-existing bare `createElement('button')` violations in `renderWorkedLandSection` (city focus and work/unwork buttons now use `createGameButton`).

## Test plan

- [ ] All 2128 tests pass (`yarn test`)
- [ ] Build succeeds (`yarn build`)
- [ ] Fog: scout a civ's city into fog — no diplomatic contact until actually visible
- [ ] Capture: conquer a city with workers nearby — worked tiles populate immediately
- [ ] Worker: start a farm improvement — warning panel shows "X turns remaining"
- [ ] Dock: research Fishing → get guidance notification; inland city build list has no Dock; coastal city shows Dock; build it → Dock sprite appears on grid
- [ ] Placement: build a second building when grid is full → "open Grid tab" notification; open Grid tab → unplaced row is a button; tap it → slots highlight; tap a slot → building placed, panel refreshes

## Summary

Fixes a boot-blocking regression introduced by PR #41 (DSL MVP foundation).

`ValidateCQSAcrossRegistry` scans each function's `ExprSource` for `<name>(` bare-call patterns. The struct-form rewriter stores the rewritten procedural body there:

```
spaceId string @required
}
func (Mutation) mutationAddAgentToSpace(ctx any) error {
  return insert(participant, ...)
}
```

`extractBareCallNames` sees the function header's `mutationAddAgentToSpace(` and reports a self-call. The `mutation -> mutation: forbidden` rule then flags every mutation in the registry, refusing to serve traffic:

```
ERROR memQLEngine failed to initialize memory engine
  error="CQS violation: mutation \"mutationAddAgentToSpace\" calls mutation \"mutationAddAgentToSpace\" -- the read path must stay side-effect-free, and a mutation must perform exactly one write. ..."
```

This blocks every cluster boot on current main.

## Fix

Skip self-references in the cross-registry pass. MemQL doesn't allow recursion (the parser + step compiler reject it earlier), so a real self-call can't reach this validator.

## Test plan

- [x] `TestValidateCQSAcrossRegistry_SelfReferenceFromRewriter` -- pins the ExprSource shape the rewriter actually produces, verifies the validator accepts it.
- [x] Existing CQS positive/negative tests still pass.
- [x] `go test ./component/memql/... ./component/automations/... ./component/language/...`
- [ ] On a running stack: `make dev-refresh` brings the identity + bff nodes up cleanly.

Discovered while verifying item 1 of `memql/docs/handoff-chat-daily-space.md` (daily-space end-to-end).

author: oveddan
body:
# Proposal: MCP integration for LX / Chromatik

> **Status**: proposal for review and discussion — no code changes in this PR. Looking for feedback on the LX-side architecture (the `mcp/` package, the global-engine vs per-project-modulator opt-in, and how `LXProjectWatcher` mirrors the existing package autoreload pattern). The MCP server itself ships in a separate Node/TypeScript repo (not included here).

---

## Context

LX is the engine library; [Chromatik](https://chromatik.co) is the GUI app built on it (formerly "LX Studio"). The use case is **pre-show authoring with Chromatik open** — Claude wires up channels, patterns, modulation knobs/buttons/triggers, modulation routings, and MIDI mappings; the operator watches the Chromatik UI update live. Not for live-performance control (some runtime state resets on reload is acceptable).

LX has [OSC](src/main/java/heronarts/lx/osc/LXOscEngine.java) + an [OSC Query](src/main/java/heronarts/lx/osc/LXOscQueryServer.java) HTTP introspection server, but neither is well-suited to *structural* edits (adding channels, creating modulators, wiring modulations). Project files are loaded once via [`openProject`](src/main/java/heronarts/lx/LX.java#L1131) and aren't watched for external changes.

**Strategy**: V1 = MCP edits the `.lxp` JSON on disk; LX adds a per-project watcher (toggled on via either a global sidebar control or a per-project modulator) that reloads it. V2 = LX exposes an HTTP backend on the same toggle, MCP swaps backends transparently. The MCP server's tool surface and Claude install flow stay identical across versions.

## Target UX

Both Claude Desktop and Claude Code, cross-platform (macOS/Linux/Windows), on the same machine as Chromatik for v1.

**Install (one-time, per Claude client):**
- **Claude Desktop**: drag `chromatik-mcp.mcpb` into the app. Claude Desktop spawns the bundled Node MCP via stdio whenever it's launched. No manual `node`/`npm` step.
- **Claude Code (CLI)**: `claude mcp add chromatik -- npx chromatik-mcp@latest --stdio` (or equivalent `.mcp.json` snippet).

**Enable inside Chromatik (either path):**
- **Global**: a status box in the Chromatik left sidebar, under the package controls, bound to a new `LXMcpEngine`. Toggle "MCP enabled". Persists in `LXPreferences` across sessions.
- **Per-project**: drop an `LXMcpModulator` into a project's modulation engine — opts that project in regardless of the global toggle.

Either path activates the project-file watcher + writes `~/.chromatik/current-project.json` for the MCP to discover.

## V1 — LX-side (Java)

New package `src/main/java/heronarts/lx/mcp/`, sibling to `osc/`, `midi/`, `modulation/`.

### `mcp/LXMcpEngine.java`
- Extends `LXComponent`. Sibling to [`LXOscEngine`](src/main/java/heronarts/lx/osc/LXOscEngine.java) etc. Constructed in [LXEngine near line 408](src/main/java/heronarts/lx/LXEngine.java#L408): `addChild("mcp", this.mcp = new LXMcpEngine(lx));`.
- Parameters (saved to `LXPreferences`, not project — global state):
  - `enabled` (`BooleanParameter`, default false)
  - `host` (`StringParameter`, default `"127.0.0.1"`)
  - `port` (`DiscreteParameter`, default 4774)
- Owns the `LXProjectWatcher` lifecycle and status-file writes. Active if `enabled.isOn() || attachedModulatorCount > 0`.
- Public listener API so the Chromatik UI can bind to enabled/status.
- `onSetProject(File, Change)` is called from `LX.setProject` so the watcher rebinds on OPEN, records `lastSavedMtime` on SAVE, and clears on NEW.

### `mcp/LXMcpModulator.java`
- Extends `LXModulator`. Marker modulator with empty compute body. Same shape as [`MacroKnobs`](src/main/java/heronarts/lx/modulator/MacroKnobs.java) but with no signal output.
- Parameters (saved to project): `enabled` (default true), `host`/`port` (default null = use global).
- `onAdded` → `lx.engine.mcp.attach(this)`. `dispose()` → `lx.engine.mcp.detach(this)`.
- Registered as a built-in modulator class in [LXRegistry](src/main/java/heronarts/lx/LXRegistry.java) so it appears in the modulator menu.

### `mcp/LXProjectWatcher.java`
- Owned by `LXMcpEngine`. Mirrors the package autoreload in [`LXRegistry.enableWatchService`](src/main/java/heronarts/lx/LXRegistry.java#L592) / [`runWatchService`](src/main/java/heronarts/lx/LXRegistry.java#L625):
  - Single `WatchService` on the project file's parent dir, filtered to that filename.
  - Polled from the engine loop — **no separate thread, no manual debounce**. The engine tick naturally coalesces.
  - Engine-loop hook: after [`registry.runWatchService()` at LXEngine.java#L1077](src/main/java/heronarts/lx/LXEngine.java#L1077), add `this.mcp.runWatchService();`.
- On a qualifying event, calls `lx.openProject(file)` directly (already on engine thread).
- **Echo suppression**: records `lastSavedMtime` on `Change.SAVE`; ignores events with mtime ≤ that value (avoids autosave-bounce loop).
- **Cross-platform note**: macOS `WatchService` is polling-based with ~10s default latency. If responsiveness is sluggish, fall back to mtime polling inside `runWatchService` (still no extra threads — engine loop drives it).

### `mcp/StatusFile.java`
- Writes `${user.home}/.chromatik/current-project.json`. Cross-platform: use `System.getProperty("user.home")` + `Path.of(home, ".chromatik", "current-project.json")`; create parent dir if absent. Atomic write (temp + `Files.move(ATOMIC_MOVE)`).
- Content:
  ```json
  { "path": "...", "version": "1.2.1", "pid": 12345,
    "host": "127.0.0.1", "port": 4774,
    "enabledBy": ["global"],
    "capabilities": ["fileEdit"],
    "timestamp": 1700000000000 }
  ```
  (`enabledBy` may be `["global"]`, `["project"]`, or `["global","project"]`.)
- Re-written on any change to enable state, host/port, or active project. Deleted when fully disabled and on shutdown.
- The `capabilities` list lets the v2 HTTP backend announce itself to the MCP without code changes on the MCP side.

### Edits to existing files
- [LX.java#L992](src/main/java/heronarts/lx/LX.java#L992) — call `this.engine.mcp.onSetProject(file, change)` at the end of `setProject`. Call `this.engine.mcp.dispose()` next to `registry.closeWatchService()` at [line 738](src/main/java/heronarts/lx/LX.java#L738).
- [LXEngine.java](src/main/java/heronarts/lx/LXEngine.java) — construct `LXMcpEngine` as a child engine near line 408; add `this.mcp.runWatchService()` after line 1077.
- [LXPreferences.java](src/main/java/heronarts/lx/LXPreferences.java) — persist `mcp.enabled`/`host`/`port` save/load. Mirror the `KEY_AUTO_RELOAD_PACKAGES` pattern at [line 251](src/main/java/heronarts/lx/LXPreferences.java#L251).
- [LXRegistry.java](src/main/java/heronarts/lx/LXRegistry.java) — register `LXMcpModulator.class` in the built-in modulator list.

### Test
- `src/test/java/heronarts/lx/mcp/LXMcpEngineTest.java`: enable via engine pref triggers watch + status file; enable via modulator triggers watch; both off = no watch + no status file; echo suppression for autosave; status-file paths resolve correctly on macOS + Linux + Windows path separators (use `Files.createTempDirectory`, not hard-coded `/tmp`).

## Chromatik UI (separate repo — planned, not in this PR)

In the Chromatik left sidebar, **under the package controls**, add a small status box bound to `lx.engine.mcp`:
- Shows: "MCP enabled / disabled", current `host:port`, count of attached project modulators.
- Provides: toggle for `enabled`, fields for `host`/`port`.

This is a Chromatik-repo change (the LX library has no UI). The LX-side `LXMcpEngine` exposes the standard parameter listeners Chromatik already uses for UI binding, so the panel implementation is mechanical. Filed as a follow-up; this proposal scopes only the LX-side engine + parameters.

## V1 — MCP server (Node/TS — separate repo, scoped here only for context)

New repo `chromatik-mcp`, scaffolded from the layout used by [touchdesigner-mcp](https://github.com/looking-glass-factory/touchdesigner-mcp).

### Layout — communication layer extracted as a swappable backend

body:
## Summary

Fixes the case where a shell session (Claude Code, a CI sandbox, etc.) pre-populates `GH_TOKEN` to a bot account (e.g. `nSimonFR-ai`) **and** the bitwarden SSH agent serves the bot's key — making every `git push` to `github.com` authenticate as the bot, which lacks write access to most `trusk-*` repos.

Adds two scoped overrides to `home/dotfiles/git/gitconfig-shared`:

- `url."https://github.com/".insteadOf = git@github.com:` — rewrites SSH URLs to HTTPS at runtime, so the bitwarden SSH agent is no longer consulted for github traffic. The configured remotes in repos are untouched.
- `credential."https://github.com".helper` — empty helper first (resets any inherited helpers, notably the system `osxkeychain` that was answering with a stale token), then a shell helper that unsets `GH_TOKEN` / `GITHUB_TOKEN` before delegating to `gh auth git-credential`. `gh`'s active account (`nSimonFR`) then provides the token from its keyring.

Other SSH hosts and non-github HTTPS remotes are unaffected — scopes are `git@github.com:` and `https://github.com` exactly.

body:
## Summary

Root-cause fix for fetch PR auto-merge stuck.

- **Why fetch PRs were stuck**: `GITHUB_TOKEN` で作成された PR は GitHub の anti-recursion guard により `pull_request` / `pull_request_target` event を発火しない → 04-validate-article-pr.yml が required check として認識されない → auto-merge SQUASH 永久待機 (#382 #384 #386 で発生)
- **Fix**: GitHub App (omochairo-fetch-bot) のトークンで fetch PR を起票するように切替。App token は通常 PR と同じ扱いで `pull_request` event を発火させるため、04-validate が required check として通常通り走り、auto-merge が即時発火する
- **Bonus (proposal D)**: `scripts/fetch_amazon.py` の `--min-new` default を 20 → 40 に変更。1 fetch あたり pool に入る新 ASIN 数を倍増させ pool 枯渇を軽減
- **paths trap mitigation**: 04-validate-article-pr.yml の paths に `.github/workflows/01-fetch-products.yml` と `scripts/fetch_amazon.py` を追加。本 PR 自身も required check `validate` を pull_request 経由で発火させるため (vacuous SUCCESS 想定)

## Changes

- `.github/workflows/01-fetch-products.yml`:
  - `actions/create-github-app-token@v1` step を追加 (`APP_ID` + `APP_PRIVATE_KEY` secret 使用)

author: copilot
body:
Train three independent binary classifiers on CARLA forward-facing camera images using LoRA-adapted ResNet-18 — one each for pedestrian, traffic-light, and vehicle detection — with full evaluation metrics and safetensors weight export to Google Drive.

## Notebook: `carla_lora_classifiers.ipynb`

**Dataset**
- `CARLADataset` reads `labels.csv` (`frame`, `has_pedestrian`, `has_traffic_light`, `has_vehicle`) and resolves frame IDs to images in `dataset/train/` (handles numeric IDs + any common extension)
- Auto train/val/test split with class-balanced CE loss to handle label skew

**LoRA-ResNet-18 architecture**
- Loads `ResNet18_Weights.IMAGENET1K_V1`, freezes all base weights
- Injects `loralib.Conv2d` adapters into every conv in `layer4` + replaces FC head with `loralib.Linear(r=8)`
- ~1% of parameters trainable; base weights never modified

```python
# Only LoRA delta matrices (A, B) are trained
lora.mark_only_lora_as_trainable(backbone)
# ~200k trainable vs 11M total params
```

**Training**
- AdamW + cosine annealing LR, mixed precision (`torch.amp`), best-val-F1 checkpointing
- Three classifiers trained sequentially, each with its own data split and loss weights

**Evaluation**
- Per-model: accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, full `classification_report`, confusion matrices, training curves, metric bar chart

**Weight saving**
- Both full state dict and LoRA-only delta weights saved to `MyDrive/carnomaly/weights/` in **safetensors** format
- `load_classifier(task)` helper for reloading without retraining

**Runtime:** designed for Google Colab GPU (T4/L4/A100) — set runtime to GPU before running.

<summary>Original prompt</summary>

> build me a jupiter notebook with pytorch that uses the resnet 18 weights and model. Create 3 seperate Classifiereres with lora finetuning building on those resnet 18 weights. load the carnomaly dataset. Add evaluation parameters like accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score

> Here is additional information for the task.
> The dataset contains forward-facing camera images collected in CARLA under clear
> weather and daytime conditions, each annotated with three binary labels: traffic light
