author: vladimir-ea
body:
1. 
```
thread '<unnamed>' (72057) panicked at crates/common/src/spine/stream_id.rs:86:18:
misaligned pointer dereference: address must be a multiple of 0x8 but is 0x1
```
when a slot was skipped the `TCache` `Consumer` would return an empty buffer - in the gossip tile we try to dereference the buffer as a `P2pStreadId` without checking the length. 

Fix: skip the skipped slots in the consumer - never return an empty buffer. 

2. 
```
thread '<unnamed>' (84446) panicked at crates/common/src/spine/tcache.rs:143:9:
100432192 - 60653568 > 33554432
```
The cache consumer had run more than buffer length bytes ahead of a consumer. The issue here is that the the consumer had never published its tail sequence b/c it was stuck in a consume loop reading a large set of synced blocks and `free()` (which publishes the tail seq) was only being called once consuming has finished.

Fix: add `auto_free` option on the `RandomAccessConsumer` so that the tail is published every time an `AcquiredRead` is dropped.

author: andrussal
body:
## 1. What does this PR implement?

For security reasons, wallet HTTP endpoints should live behind the admin API instead of the public node API.

Consider the scenario reproduced locally: a node has a funded wallet loaded, and an external client can reach the public HTTP API. Before this change, that client could call the wallet signing endpoint to obtain a valid ZK signature for an attacker-chosen transaction hash, then call the wallet transfer endpoint to spend funds from the loaded wallet to an arbitrary recipient. The repro moved funds from the victim wallet to a random attacker wallet and observed the victim balance decrease.

This PR moves wallet balance, transfer, and signing routes to the admin API, removes them from the public OpenAPI surface, and updates framework/test/CLI callers that legitimately need wallet access to use the admin endpoint.

## 2. Does the code have enough context to be clearly understood?
Yes

body:
## Summary

Completes the consolidation started in Flight 5C: S4 and S7 instance
methods now use `MethodContext::emit_method_prelude` like the other
five class generators, dropping the inline-vs-block branching that
was kept around to avoid a doubled `{ ... }` wrap.

## What changes

**`miniextendr-macros/src/miniextendr_impl/s4_class.rs`** —
single instance-method emission site. Drops the `if prelude_needed { … } else { inline }`
branch; always emits the block form.

**`miniextendr-macros/src/miniextendr_impl/s7_class.rs`** —
two instance-method sites (external generic + new generic). Same drop.
S7 `convert_from` / `convert_to` keep `build_s7_inline` since they
emit `function(from, to, ...) <return_expr>` inline without an outer
block.

**`miniextendr-macros/src/method_return_builder.rs`** —
new `build_s7_body` / `build_s4_body` methods returning
`Vec<String>` body lines for embedding inside the outer
`function(...) { ... }`. Mirrors the existing `build_r6_body` /
`build_s3_body` pattern. Inline variants are retained for the
\`convert\` sites that need a single-expression body.

## Snapshot diffs

`snapshot_s4_basic` and `snapshot_s7_basic` re-indent the method
body from 4-space (legacy inline-block style) to 2-space (matching
R6 / S3). Functionally identical R code:

\`\`\`r
# before
S7::method(get, Counter) <- function(x, ...) {
    .val <- .Call(C_Counter__get, .call = match.call(), x@.ptr)
    if (inherits(.val, ...) ...) return(...)
    .val
  }

# after
S7::method(get, Counter) <- function(x, ...) {
  .val <- .Call(C_Counter__get, .call = match.call(), x@.ptr)
  if (inherits(.val, ...) ...) return(...)
  .val
}
\`\`\`

## Test plan

- [x] \`cargo test -p miniextendr-macros\` — 316 passed
- [x] \`cargo clippy -p miniextendr-macros --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings\` — clean
- [ ] CI green

Closes #619

## Summary
- P0 diagnostic for **log-audit-20260518-001**: the 2026-05-17 `ESP_RST_TASK_WDT` (reset reason 6) reboot left no `/crashlog` because the next OTA wiped RTC_NOINIT.
- Investigation found `CONFIG_ESP_TASK_WDT_PANIC=1` is **already on** via the precompiled arduino-framework libs (`sdkconfig.defaults` is inert under `framework = arduino`) — so the existing `panic_handler` + coredump already captures a TWDT backtrace on the next non-clobbered event. No config change needed.
- The one missing signal: only IDLE0 is TWDT-subscribed, so the panic names IDLE0, not the task hogging CPU0. This adds an `esp_task_wdt_isr_user_handler` weak-symbol override (ESP32-only, ISR-safe: `esp_rom_printf` + `xTaskGetCurrentTaskHandleForCore` + `pcTaskGetName`) that prints the running task on each core before the panic.
- Comments the inert `TASK_WDT` keys in `sdkconfig.defaults` — they had already caused one misdiagnosis.

## Verification
- `pio run -e ratgdo_esp32dev` — clean link, no `multiple definition` on the weak-symbol override; panic-handler `-Wl,--wrap` still resolves.
- code-review: APPROVED. ISR safety, ESP8266 `#ifdef ESP32` gating, and panic-chain preservation all confirmed.
- Acceptance is latent — verified on the next non-OTA-clobbered reset-reason-6 event.

## Deferred queue item (filed in QUEUE.md)
- **code-review-20260519-001** (P3, conditional) — the new ISR hook lacks `IRAM_ATTR`. Technically correct as-is (TWDT is a software timer, flash cache normally active). Worth adding only if a future TWDT shows the diagnostic line missing.

## Test plan
- [ ] Flash `ratgdo_esp32dev`, confirm normal boot, no first-boot crash.
- [ ] On the next reset-reason-6 event without an immediately-following OTA: `/crashlog` shows `Task watchdog got triggered.` + backtrace, and UART shows `TWDT ISR: running CPU0=... CPU1=...`.

# Pull Request

Thanks for submitting a PR! Please fill in this template where appropriate:

## Category

Core Functionality, CI

## Feature/Issue Description

**Q:** Please give a brief summary of your feature/fix

**A:** Upgrades ESLint from v7.32.0 to v10.4.0 and migrates the configuration from the legacy `.eslintrc.json` format to the new flat config (`eslint.config.js`). Also pins all devDependency versions exactly and adds `.npmrc` with `min-release-age=3` for supply-chain safety.

**Q:** Give a technical rundown of what you have changed (if applicable)

**A:**

- **Deleted `.eslintrc.json`** — ESLint 10 removed support for the legacy config format entirely.
- **Created `eslint.config.js`** — Equivalent flat config with the same rules, globals, and ignore patterns. Uses `@eslint/js` for `recommended` rules and the `globals` package for browser globals (replaces `"env": { "browser": true }`).
- **Updated `package.json`**:
  - `eslint`: `7.32.0` → `10.4.0`
  - Added `@eslint/js`: `10.0.1`
  - Added `globals`: `17.6.0`
  - All versions pinned exactly (no `^` or `~`)
  - Lint scripts updated to target `.` (flat config handles ignores internally)
- **Created `.npmrc`** — Sets `min-release-age=3` to refuse packages published less than 3 days ago (requires npm 11.10+, currently active in CI on Node 24).
- **Updated `.github/workflows/eslint.yml`** — Changed `npx eslint "**/*.js"` to `npx eslint .` in the report-only job to align with flat config file resolution.
- **Regenerated `package-lock.json`** with the new dependency tree.

## Test Cases

**Q:** Describe your test cases, what you have covered and if there are any use cases that still need addressing.

**A:** Ran both CI jobs locally using `act`:

- `lint-all-files` — ESLint 10 ran successfully against the full codebase. 5654 pre-existing errors reported (same issues ESLint 7 would flag). Job completed with success (non-blocking, `continue-on-error: true`).
- `lint-changed-files` — No JS files in the test diff, correctly skipped linting. Job completed with success.

No new lint errors were introduced by this change. All errors are pre-existing codebase issues.

N/A — no new user-facing features. The linting infrastructure is transparent to contributors; `npm run lint` continues to work as before.

body:
## Summary

- **`ssa.ts`**: Add `User-Agent` header to SSA `fetch`/`HEAD` requests. The SSA (Akamai CDN) returns 403 for headerless requests, which was silently preventing the weekly cron from picking up the 2025 dataset.
- **`scripts/ingest-ssa.ts`**: New standalone script that downloads `names.zip`, classifies all `(name, sex)` pairs across all years, and writes SQL files to `migrations/ssa-ingest/` for `wrangler d1 execute --remote`.
- **`package.json`**: Adds `npm run ingest-ssa` convenience alias.

## Why the cron wasn't picking up 2025 data

The SSA's Akamai CDN returns `403 Forbidden` for requests without a `User-Agent`. The worker's `fetch()` and `HEAD` calls had no `User-Agent`, so every weekly cron run was silently failing at the ETag check or zip download step.

## How to get 2025 data into production

### Path 1 — Deploy & trigger the worker (recommended)

```bash
npm run deploy:ingest

# Force-trigger immediately (requires TRIGGER_SECRET):
curl -X POST https://<worker-subdomain>.workers.dev/run?force=1 \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TRIGGER_SECRET"
```

### Path 2 — Standalone script (if worker still can't reach ssa.gov)

```bash
# 1. Download names.zip from a browser:
#    https://www.ssa.gov/oact/babynames/names.zip

# 2. Generate SQL files:
npx tsx scripts/ingest-ssa.ts --zip=./names.zip

# 3. Apply to remote D1:
ls migrations/ssa-ingest/*.sql | sort | \
  xargs -I{} wrangler d1 execute name-vitals --file={} --remote
```

## Test plan

- [ ] Deploy ingest worker: `npm run deploy:ingest`
- [ ] Trigger with `force=1` or wait for Monday cron
- [ ] `SELECT value FROM meta WHERE key='max_year'` returns `2025`
- [ ] `SELECT * FROM name_years WHERE year=2025 LIMIT 5` returns rows

author: ancongui
body:
## Summary

A second-pass audit on top of #23 found that the atomic-claim fix had a regression: when a worker crashes mid-RUN, the EDA redelivery's `mark_running` is rejected by the fresh lease, the bus cursor advances past the event, and the job is stuck in `RUNNING` forever. Four other orphan classes shared the same shape.

This adds a periodic reaper (`JobReaper` + `BboxReaper`) that closes the gap.

## The five orphan classes (all confirmed against real Postgres before this change)

| # | Status | Cause | Reaper |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `QUEUED` | Submit handler crashed between row INSERT and outbox PUBLISH (the two are not co-transactional) | `JobReaper` |
| 2 | `RUNNING` | Worker crashed mid-extraction; fresh-lease redelivery is rejected, cursor advances | `JobReaper` |
| 3 | `QUEUED` | Worker's retry-path `_delayed_publish` task was killed before its `asyncio.sleep` completed | `JobReaper` |
| 4 | `PARTIAL_SUCCEEDED` | Main worker crashed between `mark_partial_succeeded` and the bbox-refine publish | `BboxReaper` |
| 5 | `REFINING_BBOXES` | Bbox worker crashed mid-grounding past its lease | `BboxReaper` |

## How the reaper works

Each worker process now runs a reaper as a sidecar task alongside its main consume loop. Every `reaper_sweep_interval_s` (default 60s) the reaper queries for rows in stuck states past their threshold and republishes a fresh `IDPJobSubmitted` / `IDPBboxRefineRequested` event. Duplicate publishes from multiple replicas are deduped at claim time by the atomic `mark_*` transitions from #23 — running the reaper in every worker replica is safe.

## Lease tweaks

Tightens defaults from `2 * timeout` to `timeout + 60s`:

| Setting | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `job_run_lease_s` | 2400 | 1260 |
| `bbox_refine_lease_s` | 1200 | 660 |

Crash-recovery time is now bounded by `reaper_sweep_interval_s + job_run_lease_s` ≈ ~22 min default, and falls proportionally for tighter `async_timeout_s` overrides.

## New settings

```python
reaper_sweep_interval_s: int = 60
queued_orphan_threshold_s: int = 600           # 2x retry_max_delay_s
partial_succeeded_orphan_threshold_s: int = 1320  # async_timeout_s + 120
```

## Test plan

- [x] `tests/unit/test_reapers.py` — 10 unit tests covering each new repository finder + reaper sweep behaviour + clean-shutdown + publisher-error resilience.
- [x] `tests/integration/test_reaper_postgres.py` — 3 real-Postgres tests proving end-to-end revival of all five orphan classes plus a full crash-recovery cycle (claim → backdate started_at → reaper → fresh worker claims with `attempts=2`).
- [x] Full unit + integration + pyfly EDA: **353 passed, 2 skipped** (was 340; +13 net).
- [x] CLI smoke import for both `cmd_worker` and `cmd_bbox_worker` after the new `asyncio.wait(FIRST_COMPLETED)` wiring.

### Motivation
- Centralize and enforce execution policy checks at the infrastructure layer so all agent execution commands are validated through NemoClaw.
- Prevent unsafe code-execution when NemoClaw is unhealthy while still allowing documentation-only tasks in degraded mode.
- Surface policy rejections as structured, actionable errors for workflows and reviewer flows to enable clear remediation.
- Provide startup validation and health visibility for the presence/status of `nemoclaw-policy.yaml`.

### Description
- Added `src/infrastructure/security/execution_adapter.py` which implements `NemoClawExecutionAdapter`, `NemoClawHealth`, and `PolicyRejectionError` with `startup_validate`, `health`, and `execute` methods and command-level checks via `prism_check`.
- Routed agent execution through the adapter by calling `execution_adapter.execute(...)` inside `BaseAgent.process` before model routing.
- Updated `OmniWorkflow.process_task` to catch `PolicyRejectionError` and return structured rejection strings (`WORKFLOW_POLICY_REJECTION` / `REVIEWER_POLICY_REJECTION`) containing `source`, `reason`, and `remediation` fields.
- Added an API startup hook to run `execution_adapter.startup_validate()` and extended the `/api/v1/health` response to include NemoClaw status and `nemoclaw_reason`.
- Added `tests/test_execution_adapter.py` with tests for an allowed command path, a blocked command path, and degraded-mode behavior allowing documentation-only tasks.

### Testing
- Ran `PYTHONPATH=. pytest -q tests/test_execution_adapter.py`, which passed (3 tests passed).
- Attempting broader test runs (`pytest -q tests/test_execution_adapter.py tests/test_workflows.py tests/test_api.py`) failed in this environment due to missing test dependencies (`fastapi`, `httpx`) and initial module-path setup, not due to the new adapter logic.
- Notes: environment-specific failures observed when `PYTHONPATH` was not set or required packages were absent, but the newly added execution adapter tests succeed under `PYTHONPATH=.`.

author: chanyavrc
body:
## Summary

- `str.find`, `str.rfind`, `str.index`, and `str.count` panicked with a Rust `begin > end` slice panic when called with an inverted window (`start > stop`).
- CPython 3.12 treats an inverted window as an empty search range and returns -1 / 0 / raises `ValueError`.
- Fixed `str_slice_args` to clamp `end_char >= start_char` before returning (both ASCII fast path and Unicode path).
- Fixed `str_index` and `str_rfind` (`str.rindex`) to raise `ValueError` instead of `RuntimeError` when the substring is not found.

## What Changed

`str_slice_args` in `crates/pyrust-builtins/src/string.rs` computed independently clamped `start_char` and `end_char` but did not enforce `end_char >= start_char` before returning. Added `.max(start_char)` at both return sites — matching the `adjust_indices` treatment CPython applies.

## Self-review caught

`str_index` and the `raise_on_miss=true` branch of `str_rfind` (i.e. `str.rindex`) were raising `PyError::Runtime` (→ `RuntimeError`) instead of `PyError::named("ValueError", ...)`. This broke the `except ValueError` catch that callers and the fixture rely on. Fixed in the same PR because both errors live in the same functions, and the acceptance criteria explicitly requires `ValueError`.

## Out of scope

The `bytes` methods (`bytes.find`, `bytes.index`, `bytes.count`, `bytes.rfind`) were identified in the issue as likely having the same inverted-window bug — not fixed here, to be addressed in a separate issue.

## Test plan

- New parity fixture: `crates/pyrust/tests/cases/string/test_find_inverted_range.py`
  - ASCII inverted window (`"hello".find("l", 4, 2)` etc.)
  - Unicode inverted window (`"héllo".find("l", 4, 2)` etc.)
  - Equal-index zero-length range (`"hello".find("l", 2, 2)`)
  - Normal (non-inverted) calls — regression guard
- `cargo test --release --bin pyrust` — 286 passed, 0 failed
- `cargo test --release --test parity_compare` — 1 passed, 0 failed
- Manual repro confirmed: all four methods match CPython 3.12 output exactly

Closes #693

## Summary

- **Fixes impossible retry counters** (`attempt 11/5`): `bootstrapFailCountRef` was a lifetime-cumulative counter but was always logged against `MAX_BOOTSTRAP_RETRIES` (5) as the denominator, even after 5 attempts. The log now distinguishes two phases: `bootstrap attempt X/5` (during bootstrap budget), and `continuous poll (N total failures, backing off)` (after budget exhaustion).
- **Adds 10s backoff after bootstrap budget exhaustion**: `scheduleNext` previously always used `POLL_MS` (2s) forever, creating tight retry loops during slow startup. It now switches to `BACKOFF_POLL_MS` (10s) once the bootstrap budget is exhausted, reverting to 2s on successful recovery.
- **Fixes `coreStatePollFailureWarningMessage`**: updated message text to say "bootstrap poll failed" so the `X/Y` format in the warning never has `X > Y`.

**Note:** PR #2167 addresses the same file and overlaps on the log-format change. This PR is a superset — it covers the logging fix and adds the backoff behavior that #2167 does not include.

author: akollad
body:
This pull request was created by @kiro-agent on behalf of @akollad :ghost:

Comment with **/kiro fix** to address specific feedback or **/kiro all** to address everything.
<sub>[Learn about Kiro autonomous agent](https://kiro.dev/autonomous-agent)</sub>

---
## Contexte

Le serveur USA retourne les slots par `visaClass`. Un slotId détecté par un compte **F1** n'est **PAS** valide pour un compte **B1/B2** — le serveur répond `409 "No free slots available on the selected date and time"`.

Le blind booking cross-visaClass est **impossible**. Les slotIds ne sont pas universels, ils sont liés au type de visa.

## Solution : Segmentation en micro-meutes homogènes

```
[Éclaireur F1]    ───> Canal "F1"    ───> [Confinés F1]
[Éclaireur B1/B2] ───> Canal "B1/B2" ───> [Confinés B1/B2]
```

## Changements

### Backend (Convex)
- **`convex/visaClassifications.ts`** (nouveau) : Liste complète des visas US (56 NIV + 20 IV), helpers `getVisaCategory()`, `getVisaClassForBroadcast()` (normalisation par groupes portail)
- **Schema** : `applications` a `usVisaCode`, `usVisaCategory` (NIV/IV), `broadcastVisaClass` + index. `slotBroadcasts` a `visaClass` obligatoire + index composé
- **`slotBroadcast.ts`** : `internalCreate` et `internalGetPending` prennent et filtrent par `visaClass`
- **`http.ts`** : Routes POST/GET `/hunter/slot-broadcast` passent `visaClass`
- **`hunter.ts`** : `getActiveJobs` retourne `broadcastVisaClass`
- **`applications.ts`** : `create()` dérive automatiquement `usVisaCode`/`usVisaCategory`/`broadcastVisaClass` depuis le type de visa sélectionné. Nouvelle mutation `assignVisaClass` pour override admin
- **`constants.ts`** : USA visa types enrichis (15 types courants au lieu de 5)

### Slot Hunter (Railway bot)
- `SlotBroadcastEvent` a le champ `visaClass`
- `ScanSlotsConfig`, `ScanSessionConfig`, `DiscoveryCollectorConfig` passent `visaClass`
- `pollBlindBookingEvents()` filtre par `visaClass` du confiné (canal strict)
- `HunterJob` a `broadcastVisaClass`

### Frontend (Joventy)
- **Client** : Badge NIV/IV informatif après sélection du type de visa USA
- **Admin** : Section "Canal Visa — Meute Homogène" dans HunterConfig avec dropdown de tous les canaux et bouton d'assignation

## Rétro-compatibilité
- Fallback `"B1/B2"` si `visaClass` absent (dossiers existants non migrés)
- Les dossiers existants continuent de fonctionner — l'admin assigne le canal au cas par cas

## Tests effectués
- Vérification de la cohérence du schéma
- Vérification du passage de `visaClass` de bout en bout (éclaireur → Convex → confiné)

author: moscowchill
body:
## Summary

Three medium-priority follow-ups Gemini left on the (already-merged) streaming-size-cap PR #42.

### 1. Null \`response.body\` check

Fetch API spec allows \`response.body\` to be null (e.g. 204 No Content). The current code calls \`.getReader()\` unconditionally — TypeError gets caught by the outer block and returned as 'gateway unreachable', which is misleading. Add an explicit null check that returns 502 'gateway error' with a log line.

### 2. AbortError re-throw from inner catch

\`FETCH_TIMEOUT_MS\` AbortController can fire AFTER the response headers come back but mid-body. In that case \`reader.read()\` throws an AbortError that the inner catch was labelling as 502 'gateway stream error', bypassing the outer 504 'gateway timeout' path. Re-throw AbortError from the inner catch so timeouts during streaming are reported consistently.

### 3. Drop redundant \`Buffer.from\` in concat

\`Buffer.concat\` natively accepts Uint8Array chunks; the previous \`.map(c => Buffer.from(c))\` was wasted allocation in a hot path. One-line cleanup.

## Tests

Two new cases:
- Null body → 502 'gateway error'
- AbortError mid-stream → 504 'gateway timeout' (not 502)

Total: 71 passing, lint + format:check clean.

## Risk

Behaviour change is strictly more accurate error codes; no regression to existing happy / error paths.

author: starius
body:
## Summary

This updates the next formatter to handle the formatting shapes found during downstream adoption: compacting simple nested calls, keeping short return/result groups packed, normalizing awkward partial signature splits, improving printf/error formatting, and making elided composite literal formatting more consistent. The examples below are representative of the behavioral changes rather than a commit-by-commit list.

## Compact simple nested single-argument calls

Before:

```go
maxPrepayRoutingFee := getMaxRoutingFee(
	btcutil.Amount(
		quote.PrepayAmtSat,
	),
)
```

After:

```go
maxPrepayRoutingFee := getMaxRoutingFee(
	btcutil.Amount(quote.PrepayAmtSat),
)
```

## Keep blank lines before final returns

After compacting prior calls, the formatter still keeps the generic blank-line-before-return rule.

Before:

```go
err := finalizedHtlcTx.Deserialize(
	bytes.NewReader(
		row.FinalizedHtlcTx,
	),
)
return err
```

After:

```go
err := finalizedHtlcTx.Deserialize(
	bytes.NewReader(row.FinalizedHtlcTx),
)

return err
```

## Pack simple multi-result returns

Simple nested calls in return values are packed when they fit.

Before:

```go
return args.Get(0).(chan *chainntnfs.TxConfirmation), args.Get(1).(chan error), args.Error(
	2,
)
```

After:

```go
return args.Get(0).(chan *chainntnfs.TxConfirmation),
	args.Get(1).(chan error), args.Error(2)
```

## Move single named params only in the already-split result shape

The single named parameter compaction is intentionally narrow: it applies to signatures where arguments are already split and the results start after `) (`. It does not use this rule to rewrite already-good shapes such as a multiline parameter with inline results.

Before:

```go
func rpcRouteCancel(
	details *outCancelDetails) (
	*veryLongRouteCancelResponseWithAdditionalSuffix, error) {

	return nil, nil
}
```

After:

```go
func rpcRouteCancel(details *outCancelDetails) (
	*veryLongRouteCancelResponseWithAdditionalSuffix, error) {

	return nil, nil
}
```

## Normalize partial return-list splits

When a partial return-list split is awkward, the formatter moves the parameter down and packs short results.

Before:

```go
func unmarshalFixedPoint2(fp *looprpc.FixedPoint) (*rfqmath.BigIntFixedPoint,
	error) {

	return nil, nil
}
```

After:

```go
func unmarshalFixedPoint2(
	fp *looprpc.FixedPoint) (*rfqmath.BigIntFixedPoint, error) {

	return nil, nil
}
```

## Split long printf/error format strings while keeping short arguments attached

Before:

```go
return fmt.Errorf("this is a long error message with a couple (%d) place holders", len(things))
```

After:

```go
return fmt.Errorf("this is a long error message with a couple (%d) "+
	"place holders", len(things))
```

## Keep nested errorf format strings inline when the nested call fits

Before:

```go
return f.HandleError(
	fmt.Errorf(
		"invalid swap invoice hash: expected %x got %x",
		preimage.Hash(), payReq.Hash,
	),
)
```

After:

```go
return f.HandleError(
	fmt.Errorf("invalid swap invoice hash: expected %x got %x",
		preimage.Hash(), payReq.Hash),
)
```

## Compact single-element composite literals

This is generic and does not special-case any type name. The `lntypes.Hash` fixture is just a representative type-shaped example.

Before:

```go
SwapHash: lntypes.Hash{
	1,
},
Marker: sampleMarker{
	"ready",
},
```

After:

```go
SwapHash: lntypes.Hash{1},
Marker:   sampleMarker{"ready"},
```

## Keep simple elided composite elements packed

Before:

```go
hops := []*RouteHop{
	{},
	{},
	{},
}
```

After:

```go
hops := []*RouteHop{
	{}, {}, {},
}
```

## Expand keyed elided composite values

Adjacent keyed entries no longer share a line.

Before:

```go
requiredOps := map[string][]PermissionOp{
	"/service/Action": {{
		Entity: "swap",
		Action: "execute",
	}, {
		Entity: "service",
		Action: "read",
	}},
}
```

After:

```go
requiredOps := map[string][]PermissionOp{
	"/service/Action": {
		{
			Entity: "swap",
			Action: "execute",
		},
		{
			Entity: "service",
			Action: "read",
		},
	},
}
```

## Validation

- `make self-check`
- `make lint`

author: robotsix-mill[bot]
body:
Now I have a thorough understanding of both the module and the test suite. Let me write the spec.

## Problem

`run_scout_agent()` in `src/robotsix_mill/agents/scouting.py` (lines 442–539) is the module's main seam (~97 lines) but the only function in the module not decomposed. It interleaves model enrichment, per-role candidate evaluation, regression detection, improvement detection, draft building, and proposal tracking — all in one body. The rest of the module is well-factored (`_evaluate_model`, `_build_draft_body`, `_parse_memory`, `_best_candidate`, etc.), but the central per-role loop (lines 488–535) remains a monolith. This makes regression logic and improvement logic impossible to unit-test independently, and every change to scouting rules requires touching the same large function.

## Scope

- **Extract `_evaluate_role()`** — a new private function containing the entire per-role body currently at lines 488–535. Signature:

  ```python
  def _evaluate_role(
      *,
      env_var: str,
      attr: str,
      tier: str,
      label: str,
      configured_id: str,
      enriched: dict[str, ModelInfo],
      candidate_ids: list[str],
      already: set[str],
      settings: Settings,
  ) -> list[tuple[str, str, str]]:
  ```

  Returns a list of `(draft_title, draft_body, model_id)` tuples — at most one element, empty if no draft is warranted. The `model_id` in the return allows the caller (`run_scout_agent`) to reconstruct `new_proposals` entries without parsing draft bodies.

  Internally, `_evaluate_role` does:
  1. Looks up `current_info` from `enriched`, returns `[]` if missing.
  2. Calls `_evaluate_model(configured_id, label, env_var, tier, current_info)` → `current_eval`.
  3. Evaluates each candidate in `candidate_ids` (skipping `configured_id`, skipping missing entries in `enriched`) via `_evaluate_model`.
  4. Runs regression checks on `current_eval`/`current_info` (zero providers, preview, single provider — exact same three conditions as today).
  5. If a regression is found: picks `_best_candidate(candidates)`, checks against `already`, builds draft via `_build_draft_body(reason_kind="regression", ...)`, returns `[(title, body, best.model_id)]`.
  6. Otherwise: runs improvement check — `_best_candidate(candidates)` where `best.score > current_eval.score + 10.0`, checks against `already`, builds draft via `_build_draft_body(reason_kind="improvement", ...)`, returns `[(title, body, best.model_id)]`.
  7. If nothing triggers, returns `[]`.

- **Refactor `run_scout_agent()`** to call `_evaluate_role()` inside the per-role loop. The loop reduces to:

  ```python
  for env_var, (attr, tier, label) in role_configs.items():
      configured_id = getattr(settings, attr, "")
      if not configured_id:
          continue
      candidate_ids = CHEAP_CANDIDATES if tier == "cheap" else CAPABLE_CANDIDATES
      already = proposed_set.get(env_var, set())
      results = _evaluate_role(
          env_var=env_var, attr=attr, tier=tier, label=label,
          configured_id=configured_id, enriched=enriched,
          candidate_ids=candidate_ids, already=already, settings=settings,
      )
      for title, body, model_id in results:
          drafts_titles.append(title)
          drafts_bodies.append(body)
          new_proposals.append((env_var, model_id, label))
  ```

  Target: `run_scout_agent` body ~55 lines (down from ~97).

- **Target for `_evaluate_role`**: ~45 lines.

## Acceptance criteria

1. **Behavioral equivalence** — all 10 existing `test_scout.py` tests for `run_scout_agent` pass without modification (they monkeypatch `_fetch_models`/`_fetch_endpoints`, not the internals of the loop).

2. **`_evaluate_role` is importable and testable** — a new test can import `_evaluate_role` directly, pass synthetic `EvalResult`/`ModelInfo` objects and `already` sets, and assert draft output (or empty) without needing HTTP mocks.

3. **Regression-detection logic is unchanged** — the three conditions (zero providers, preview model, single provider) produce the exact same `reason_text` strings as before, in the same priority order, with the same `continue`-to-next-role behavior after emitting a regression draft.

4. **Improvement-detection logic is unchanged** — the 10-point score threshold (`best.score > current_eval.score + 10.0`) and the `already` dedup check remain identical.

5. **`run_scout_agent` stays under 60 lines** — measured from `def run_scout_agent(` to the final `return ScoutResult(...)`.

6. **`_evaluate_role` stays under 50 lines** — measured from `def _evaluate_role(` to its final `return`.

7. **`ScoutResult` shape is unchanged** — the returned `ScoutResult` has the same `updated_memory`, `draft_titles`, `draft_bodies` content as before for any given input.

8. **No new imports needed** — `_evaluate_role` reuses all existing helpers (`_evaluate_model`, `_build_draft_body`, `_best_candidate`); no additional dependencies.

## Out of scope / constraints

- **Do not change** the signatures or behavior of `_evaluate_model`, `_build_draft_body`, `_best_candidate`, `_parse_memory`, `_build_updated_memory`, `_fragile_text`, `_latency_timeout_note`, or any other existing helper.
- **Do not split `_evaluate_role` further** into separate `_check_regression` / `_check_improvement` functions in this change — the draft spec mentions that as an option, but the primary goal is extracting the single `_evaluate_role` helper. Further decomposition can be a follow-up.
- **Do not change** `CAPABLE_CANDIDATES`, `CHEAP_CANDIDATES`, `ALL_ROLES`, or any role/tier definitions.
- **Do not touch** `src/robotsix_mill/scout_runner.py` or the CLI — the `run_scout_agent` public signature (`settings: Settings, memory: str = ""`) and `ScoutResult` return type remain identical.
- **Do not add** new data types/dataclasses unless strictly needed — the return type `list[tuple[str, str, str]]` is sufficient and avoids adding a class that would need its own tests.
- **Tests are out of scope** for this spec — the change must be a pure refactor that passes the existing test suite, but this ticket covers only the extraction, not writing new tests for `_evaluate_role`.

---

author: a-bilaiya
body:
Previously `get-info` ran against exactly one ESXi host. Extend it so a user can either:
  - pass / enter a comma-separated list of ESXi IPs (matches the hw-info ergonomic), or
  - pass `--vcenter` (or pick option 2 at the prompt) to connect to a vCenter, pick a datacenter, and fan the read-only checks out across every host in that DC via a single connection.

Implementation
- Split the per-host work out of `step_get_info` into `_run_get_info_for_host(host, vm_arg, allow_vm_prompt, ...)` so it can be driven from either a direct-ESXi `si` or a vCenter `si`.
- New helpers `_pick_vms_on_host` / `_resolve_vms_for_host` scope VM resolution to a single host (the old `resolve_vms` would have listed every VM in vCenter, which is wrong for multi-host mode).
- New `_list_datacenters` / `_pick_datacenter` / `_hosts_in_datacenter` for the vCenter path.
- `_run_get_info_esxi` mirrors `_run_hw_info_multi`: prompts creds once, connects per host, runs the checks, prints a combined summary.
- `_run_get_info_vcenter` opens one vCenter connection, picks a DC, iterates hosts, and prints a combined summary. Falls back to single- host mode if the target turns out not to be vCenter.
- `_run_get_info_multi` is the new entry point; routes on `--vcenter` vs `--host` vs an interactive mode prompt.
- VM picker is only shown in single-host mode; in multi-host mode VM checks run only when `--vm <names>` is supplied, to avoid prompting N times in a long fan-out.

CLI
- New `--vcenter` flag on `get-info`.
- `--host` on `get-info` now accepts a comma-separated list, like `hw-info` / `rename-portgroup` / `setup-network`.
- Subcommand help updated to mention both.

author: ilirassail
body:
## Summary

`task_poller` processes one `hunt_agent_tasks` row at a time (see its module docstring), but the HTTP registration payload didn't include `max_concurrent_tasks` — so the platform used the `hunt_agents.max_concurrent_tasks` schema default of **5**. Companion fix in `ares/services/api-hunt-service` now throttles dispatch to `~3x` the agent's advertised parallelism; with the wrong value, that means 15 tasks queued at a serial agent. The per-chunk timer was always going to fire on the chunks at the back of the queue.

Prod hunt `df39c730-6821-4a00-80c9-b83237297d87` (2026-05-18) abandoned 197/256 chunks of a `/16` this way while the agent was actually healthy and kept processing in the background.

This PR is a 4-line change: add `"max_concurrent_tasks": 1` to the registration payload.

## Companion PRs

- `ares#1323` — the platform side: started_at-based per-chunk deadline, throttled dispatch, `hunt_agents` counter updates, and a registration handler that accepts the new field (defaulting to 1 when the agent doesn't send it). Land both around the same time.

## Test plan

- [ ] Rebuild the agent image, re-register against staging, confirm `SELECT max_concurrent_tasks FROM hunt_agents WHERE id = '<agent>'` returns 1.
- [ ] Run a small CIDR hunt; confirm dispatch tops out at ~3 outstanding tasks instead of 15.

author: christiaanjs
body:
Implements build-plan.md Stage 1 (skeleton with one working data path) and the remaining Stage 2 work (credential storage, storage backends, settings UI).

## What's in this PR

### Stage 1 — Skeleton with one working data path

**Worker**
- `POST /api/storage/resolve` — accepts a list of `r2://bucket/key` URIs (authenticated), returns a map of URI → short-lived signed Worker URL. The token is a 1-hour JWT signed with `JWT_SECRET`.
- `GET /api/storage/obj/:token` — validates the token and streams the R2 object, including `Range` request support so DuckDB's `httpfs` can do partial reads.
- R2 bucket binding added to `wrangler.toml` for both production (`data-shack-storage`) and staging (`data-shack-storage-staging`).

**Frontend**
- DuckDB-WASM initialised with `httpfs` extension on first use (singleton). Uses the official CDN bundle + `importScripts` blob-worker pattern to avoid Cloudflare Pages' 25 MiB file size limit while satisfying the browser's same-origin Worker restriction.
- **Query panel**: URI resolver text area + SQL editor. Before executing, the frontend extracts all `r2://` URIs from the SQL, calls `/api/storage/resolve`, substitutes the returned HTTPS URLs, then runs the query in DuckDB. Results rendered in a scrollable table.
- Tab navigation added (Query / Settings).

### Stage 2 (remainder) — Credential storage, storage backends, settings UI

**Worker**
- `migrations/0002`: `credentials` and `storage_backends` tables. Both store encrypted config blobs alongside plaintext `name` and `type`.
- `src/crypto.ts`: AES-GCM-256 `encryptConfig`/`decryptConfig`. Key is derived from `JWT_SECRET` via HKDF (separate `info` tag = independent key — no new secrets needed).
- CRUD endpoints behind `requireAuth`: `GET/POST/DELETE /api/credentials` and `GET/POST/DELETE /api/storage-backends`. List responses return metadata only (no decrypted config).

**Frontend**
- **Settings panel**: lists credentials and storage backends with add/delete. Credential types: `akahu`, `google_oauth`, `generic_token`. Backend types: `r2-bound`, `s3`, `r2-s3compat`, `gcs`, `azure`, `https`. Config is entered as JSON.

### Other
- `.claude/` added to `.gitignore`.
- Staging Pages deploy now passes `--branch main` so it gets the root `data-shack-staging.pages.dev` URL instead of a per-commit preview URL.
- 112 tests pass (up from 43); 13 new tests cover the storage resolve/proxy endpoints and credential/backend CRUD.

## Testing

### Prerequisites
- A staging deploy with an R2 bucket bound and at least one object uploaded. Upload a test file:
  ```
  echo '{"name":"Alice","amount":42}\n{"name":"Bob","amount":17}' > sample.ndjson
  wrangler r2 object put data-shack-storage-staging/sample.ndjson --file sample.ndjson --env staging
  ```

### Query panel
1. Sign in at `https://data-shack-staging.pages.dev`.
2. The **Query** tab should load by default and show "Initialising DuckDB…" briefly, then the editor.
3. In the SQL editor, enter:
   ```sql
   SELECT * FROM read_json('r2://data-shack-storage-staging/sample.ndjson')
   ```
4. Click **Run Query**. The two rows should appear in the results table.
5. Try an invalid URI (e.g. `r2://data-shack-storage-staging/missing.ndjson`) — expect a DuckDB error message, not a crash.

### Settings panel
1. Switch to the **Settings** tab.
2. Under **Storage Backends**, add a backend: name `primary-r2`, type `r2-bound`, config `{"bucket":"data-shack-storage-staging"}`. It should appear in the list.
3. Delete it — it should disappear.
4. Repeat for **Credentials** with type `generic_token` and config `{"token":"test"}`.

### Auth / security
- Confirm `POST /api/storage/resolve` returns 401 without a valid token.
- Confirm `GET /api/storage/obj/<tampered-token>` returns 401.
- Confirm credentials list does not expose the `encrypted_config` field.

author: jeong-sik
body:
## 요약

FSM hub footer 의 `mem 909/722` (126%) 처럼 독립 lifetime counter 두 개를 `X/Y` slash-format 으로 표시해 ratio 처럼 보이던 모순을 typed semantic 분리로 root-fix.

- `memory_injected_count` 와 `memory_flushed_count` 는 독립 monotonic counter — `injected ≤ flushed` 같은 invariant 없음. 정상 동작 중에도 `injected > flushed` 가능.
- 기존 `mem ${injected}/${flushed}` 는 "used / quota" ratio 를 강하게 implicate.
- **Telemetry-as-fix 안티패턴**: counter 두 개를 typed semantic 없이 같은 ratio UI 에 박은 결과.

## 변경

### `dashboard/src/components/counter-format.ts` (new, +52)
두 헬퍼로 의미 분리:
- `formatRatioPair({ numerator, denominator })` → `"N/M"`. caller 가 `numerator ≤ denominator` invariant 를 도메인 차원에서 보장하는 경우에만 사용 (예: `manifest_returned_rows / manifest_total_rows`).
- `formatIndependentCounters({ leftLabel, leftValue, rightLabel, rightValue })` → `"label N · label M"`. ratio implication 제거.

JSDoc 으로 두 함수의 사용 조건 명시. 형식적 타입 강제(brand type 등)는 어렵지만 helper 이름 + 주석 + 호출부 의도가 코드 리뷰 시점에서 잡힘.

### `dashboard/src/components/fsm-hub.ts` (~34 LoC delta)
`RuntimeEvidenceSummary` footer chip + `runtimeTraceTitle` 모두 라우팅:

**Independent counters** (slash 제거):
- `memory injected/flushed: 909/722` → `memory: injected 909 · flushed 722`
- `memory flush ok/error: X/Y` → `memory flush: ok X · error Y`
- footer chip `mem 909/722` → `mem inj 909 · flush 722`

**True invariant pairs** (slash 유지, helper 경유):
- `manifest rows: returned/total`
- `provider attempts: finished/started` (finished ≤ started, 인자 순서 정정)
- `context compaction: compacted/started`
- footer chip `ctx X/Y`

### `dashboard/src/components/counter-format.test.ts` (new, +56)
6 케이스: `formatRatioPair` 3개, `formatIndependentCounters` 3개. 회귀 케이스로 `inj=909, flush=722` 입력이 `/` 를 절대 포함하지 않음을 명시 (`not.toMatch(/\d+\/\d+/)`).

## Before / After

**Before** (live keeper screenshot evidence):
```
mem 909/722        ← 126% 처럼 보임
```

**After**:
```
mem inj 909 · flush 722
```

Title tooltip 도 동일:
```
memory: injected 909 · flushed 722
memory flush: ok 12 · error 0
```

## 검증

- `pnpm typecheck` PASS (no `any`, no new lint).
- `pnpm vitest run src/components/counter-format.test.ts` → 6/6 PASS.
- `pnpm vitest run src/components/fsm-hub` → 9 files, 255/255 PASS.

## 사이드 사이트 (out of scope)

같은 `mem ${injected}/${flushed}` 패턴이 `dashboard/src/components/journey-panel.ts:238` 에도 존재. 본 PR scope (FSM hub footer 모순 #5) 와 별개라 미포함. 동일 helper 로 후속 PR 에서 정리 가능.

`dashboard/src/components/keeper-detail-runtime.ts:932-934` 의 `inj ${present}/${injected}` (present ≤ injected 는 진짜 invariant pair) 와 `flush ${success}/${error}` (독립) 는 mixed — 별도 검토 필요. 본 PR 미포함.

## CONFLICT 체크

PR #16553 은 `fsm-hub.ts` line 347+ (reducer/view projection) 영역만 건드림. 본 PR 은 line 263-323 영역 (`runtimeTraceTitle`, `RuntimeEvidenceSummary`) 만 수정 → **conflict 없음** (`git diff origin/main --stat` 기준 fsm-hub.ts 단일 파일).

Closes: 모순 #5 (keeper detail FSM hub mem 909/722 ratio implication)

author: vdekrijger
body:
## Problem

The `subscription_delivery` SLO surfaced a recurring `ActivityError` "Activity task timed out" — 22 failures across 4 teams over the last 7 days, with an average failure duration of ~940 seconds. That maps cleanly to three full 5-minute retries on `create_export_assets`, which has **no heartbeat**: Temporal can't tell a stalled activity from a slow one, so both die at the start_to_close ceiling. The same gap exists on `deliver_subscription`, whose SMTP / Slack calls can stall similarly.

The fix mirrors the established pattern in `posthog/temporal/exports/activities.py:21` (`export_asset_activity`), which already wraps its body in `Heartbeater` paired with `heartbeat_timeout=2 min` on the workflow side.

## Changes

`posthog/temporal/subscriptions/activities.py`:
- Import `Heartbeater` from `posthog.temporal.common.heartbeat`.
- Wrap the bodies of `create_export_assets` and `deliver_subscription` in `async with Heartbeater():`. No other logic change — the indentation accounts for almost all of the diff size.

`posthog/temporal/subscriptions/workflows.py`:
- `create_export_assets` invocation: bump `start_to_close_timeout` from 5 → 15 minutes (per-insight snapshot serialization on large dashboards needs headroom; the heartbeat keeps a genuinely hung activity from running the full ceiling), and add `heartbeat_timeout=2 minutes`.
- `deliver_subscription` invocation: keep `start_to_close_timeout=5 minutes`, add `heartbeat_timeout=2 minutes`.

The 2 hour workflow `execution_timeout` still bounds the worst case (45 min create + 25 min deliver + per-insight fan-out fits comfortably).

## How did you test this code?

I'm an agent. I ran:
- `ruff check posthog/temporal/subscriptions/` — clean.
- `python -c '... inspect.getsource(create_export_assets) ...'` — confirmed `async with Heartbeater():` is present in both activity bodies.
- Did NOT run the activity tests locally (the test fixtures need ClickHouse, which is not running in this worktree). CI will run them.

## Publish to changelog?

no

## Docs update

(no docs changes needed)

## 🤖 Agent context

Authored by Claude Code (agent). The investigation came out of `/slo-failures-daily` triage: the `slo_operation_completed` event with `outcome=failure`, `area=analytic-platform`, `operation=subscription_delivery`, `error_type=ActivityError` had 22 occurrences over 7 days with avg `duration_ms=940858` — three retries × 5-minute `start_to_close` ceiling on `create_export_assets`.

Reviewed via `/review-swarm` (vasco + sre + xp + superpowers:code-reviewer):

- **Overall A** — no HIGH/CRITICAL findings. Several LOWs and NITs about comment density, worst-case slot occupation (15min × 3 retries = 45min on a poison-pill subscription), and `deliver_subscription`'s 5-min ceiling being tight for very large email recipient lists. None are blockers; the slot-occupation point is worth post-deploy observation (p99 duration on `create_export_assets`).
- One round of polish: trimmed verbose activity-side comments to match the sibling `export_asset_activity` pattern (zero comments — workflow-side comments carry the rationale).

Two follow-ups flagged for separate consideration, intentionally not in this PR:
1. If post-deploy data shows `create_export_assets` still routinely hitting the 15min ceiling, consider dropping `maximum_attempts` from 3 to 2 to cap worst-case slot occupation at 30min.
2. If large email subscription recipient lists start showing the same timeout pattern on `deliver_subscription`, that activity also needs a higher `start_to_close_timeout`.

Agent-authored — requires human review before merging.

author: tadevshi
body:
## Problem
Production PostgreSQL logs show repeated error:
```
ERROR:  function round(double precision, integer) does not exist
HINT:  No function matches the given name and argument types.
```

This broke the analytics/stats endpoint for event organizers.

## Root Cause
PostgreSQL does not support `ROUND(double_precision, integer)`. The expression:
```sql
ROUND((qs.quiz_completed::float / qs.quiz_started) * 100, 2)
```
returns `double precision`, but PostgreSQL's `ROUND` with two arguments requires `numeric`.

## Fix
Cast the division result to `::numeric` before `ROUND`:
```sql
ROUND(((qs.quiz_completed::float / qs.quiz_started) * 100)::numeric, 2)
```

## Verified
- `go build ./internal/handlers/...` passes
- Only one occurrence of this pattern in the entire codebase

body:
## Summary

Adds a new playlist feature that allows users to paste multiple YouTube/Google Drive URLs, which are automatically downloaded to the server, saved to the Videos collection (with thumbnails/duration), and streamed sequentially as a playlist.

**Backend:**
- New `POST /api/streaming/playlist-from-urls` endpoint: accepts `slotId` + array of URLs, kicks off background download via yt-dlp, saves each video to MongoDB `videos` collection, then starts FFmpeg concat streaming
- New `GET /api/streaming/playlist-job/{job_id}` endpoint: returns download progress (downloaded count, total, status)
- Downloads run as a background `asyncio.create_task` so the HTTP response returns immediately with a job ID
- Each downloaded video gets a thumbnail, duration, and appears in the user's Videos page for future reuse

**Frontend (LiveSlotsPage + AdminSlots):**
- Playlist tab in Start Stream modal now has two sub-modes: "Uploaded Videos" (existing) and "YouTube/Drive Links" (new)
- URL mode provides dynamic multi-input fields (add/remove URLs)
- Job status indicator shows download progress after submission

## Review & Testing Checklist for Human

- [ ] **Blocking subprocess in async task**: `_download_and_stream()` uses synchronous `subprocess.run(timeout=600)` inside an `asyncio.create_task`. This blocks the event loop during each download (up to 10 min per video). With multiple URLs, the server may become unresponsive. Consider wrapping in `asyncio.to_thread()` or using `asyncio.create_subprocess_exec` for downloads too.
- [ ] **No frontend polling of job status**: `getPlaylistJobStatus` API is wired up but the frontend never polls it after initial submission — progress indicator will be stale. Verify the UX is acceptable (user sees "Downloading 0/N" then nothing updates until page refresh).
- [ ] **Disk space / cleanup**: Downloaded videos persist indefinitely in `UPLOAD_DIR`. Verify the VPS has sufficient disk for accumulated downloads. No cleanup mechanism exists.
- [ ] **URL validation**: No server-side validation of URL format before passing to yt-dlp. Test with invalid URLs to confirm graceful failure (it should `continue` past failures).
- [ ] **End-to-end test**: Paste 2-3 YouTube URLs in the playlist modal, verify downloads complete, videos appear in Videos page, and stream starts on the configured platform.

### Notes
- The `import uuid as _uuid` and `from app.routes.videos import generate_thumbnail, get_video_duration` are inside the background task loop — functional but inefficient (re-imported each iteration).
- FFmpeg encoding is hardcoded to 720p@4500kbps in the URL playlist path, which differs from the existing `playlist-queue` endpoint that uses `-c:v copy`. This means URL-downloaded playlists will re-encode (more CPU) but guarantees codec compatibility across heterogeneous sources.
- The AdminSlots.tsx diff is large because it was rebuilt as a full-featured admin panel in a prior commit on this branch; the playlist URL changes within it are the same pattern as LiveSlotsPage.

All hard-coded physical constants are replaced by `config.json` as the single source of truth, a `--debug` CLI flag gates debug output globally, `WallFollower` is cleaned up per spec, and the unimplemented `Maze` interface declarations are removed. ### Plan Summary - **Unified physical config** — `config.json` sets `radius_cm=10` and adds `minimum_distance_to_wall=10`; `Config.h/.cpp` load and expose both; all call sites (`Simulation`, `ScenarioSimulation`, `WallFollower`) consume them via setters instead of hard-coded literals. - **`--debug` flag** — parsed in `main.cpp`, stored on `Config`, propagated to `WallFollower` via `setDebug()`; WallFollower trace redirected from `stdout` → `stderr`; per-step logging in `Simulation` gated behind the flag. - **WallFollower improvements** — `debug_` defaults to `false`; `extern Config config` dependency removed (replaced by `robot_radius_cm_` / `min_distance_to_wall_cm_` members set via setters); dead `right_mean` alias removed; all ~25 debug prints moved to `std::cerr`. - **`Maze` interface** — `hasWall` / `isWallBetween` declarations removed (no callers existed). - **`-Wall` cleanup** — constructor init-list ordering fixed in `Maze.cpp`, `PerformanceMetrics.cpp`, `SensorNoise.cpp`; dead variable in `Pathfinder.cpp` removed. ### Key design decisions - **Setters over constructor injection** for `WallFollower` (`setRobotRadius`, `setMinDistanceToWall`, `setDebug`) keeps the default constructor intact and avoids threading new parameters through `ScenarioSimulation`'s interface. - **`config.debug` bool on the `Config` struct** (not a separate flag object) is the simplest way to propagate the CLI flag through to both `Simulation` and `ScenarioSimulation` without changing their signatures. - **stderr for debug output** keeps `--scenario-suite` stdout clean for grep-based callers and CI, while `--debug` still surfaces full trace. author: dieterolson
body:
## Summary

Issue #653 reported that `deploy/runner-cleanup.sh` aborted on the first runner when `systemctl stop` raced with a job pickup (systemd returned exit 1, tripping `set -Eeuo pipefail`), silently skipping runners 2..N for the entire nightly cleanup pass.

**The fix is already on `main`** — PR #660 (`fix(deploy): tolerate per-runner stop/start failures in cleanup loop`) implemented the race-tolerant pattern. However that PR did not include `Fixes #653`, so the Verify-Issue-Closure guard reopened the issue.

This PR adds regression tests that pin the race-tolerance contract, providing both the closing evidence the guard requires and a safety net against future regressions.

## Changes

New file: `tests/deploy/test_runner_cleanup_race_tolerance.py`

6 static analysis tests verify `deploy/runner-cleanup.sh` without executing bash:

1. Script exists with `#!/usr/bin/env bash` shebang
2. `systemctl stop` uses `|| stop_rc=$?` to tolerate non-zero exit
3. `stop_rc` is inspected (not silently ignored)
4. `continue` appears in the stop-failure branch (loop skips the busy runner, never calls `cleanup_runner_*` on it)
5. `CLEANUP_STOP_FAILURES` counter is present and incremented for Prometheus

## Verification

- [x] `pytest tests/deploy/test_runner_cleanup_race_tolerance.py` — 6 passed
- [x] No changes to `runner-cleanup.sh` needed (fix is already on main from PR #660)
- [x] Tests are platform-independent (static analysis, no bash execution)

## What the fix does (already on main)

```bash
# Before PR #660 (broke on stop failure):
run systemctl stop "$unit"  # tripped set -e on exit 1

# After PR #660 (race-tolerant):
run systemctl stop "$unit" || stop_rc=$?
if (( stop_rc != 0 )); then
    CLEANUP_STOP_FAILURES=$((CLEANUP_STOP_FAILURES + 1))
    log "skip $unit: systemctl stop failed ..."
    continue  # move on to runner-2 through runner-N
fi
```

Fixes #653

author: felipealmeida-propmind
body:
## Description

PR 5c/6 do [PMT-513](https://linear.app/propmind/issue/PMT-513/otimizar-custo-da-review-automatica-de-pr-no-github-actions). Ativa o pipeline semgrep no workflow.

Companion configs (devem mergear primeiro para impacto, mas o workflow é **idempotente** — sem config no caller, step é no-op):
- [Propmind/propmind-core#287](https://github.com/Propmind/propmind-core/pull/287) — backend rules
- [Propmind/control-panel-ui#372](https://github.com/Propmind/control-panel-ui/pull/372) — frontend rules

## Changes

Novo step \`Run semgrep pre-pass\` entre \`Load review rules\` e \`anthropics/claude-code-action@beta\`:

1. **Guard:** \`if: hashFiles('.semgrep/propmind-conventions.yml') != ''\` — repos sem config não pagam nada
2. **Install:** \`pip install --quiet semgrep\` (~10s overhead por run)
3. **Run:** \`semgrep --config .semgrep/propmind-conventions.yml --baseline-commit origin/main .\` — só findings introduzidas pelo PR; pre-existing legacy fica silencioso
4. **Output:** parsed em Markdown e exposto via \`\${{ steps.semgrep.outputs.findings }}\`

Direct_prompt Phase 2 ganha nova seção **Deterministic findings (semgrep pre-pass)** instruindo o LLM:
- Findings semgrep são **autoritativas** (incluir verbatim)
- **NÃO re-emitir** findings equivalentes pela análise própria
- Severidade fixa por rule ID

## Hypothesis of impact

As 4 regras (size=sm em drawer, raw colors, session.commit ausente, marker pytest ausente) historicamente apareciam em ~30-40% dos reviews automáticos. Eram trabalho 100% determinístico que o LLM gastava tokens fazendo (achar padrão no diff, escrever bullet de finding). Agora:
- Semgrep faz match em milissegundos
- LLM lê findings prontas e copia
- Sobra orçamento de tokens pro LLM focar em coisas que linter não cobre (lógica, design, completude de teste, etc.)

Redução de turnos estimada: 5-15% nos PRs que tocam código frontend ou api/resources, conforme densidade dessas 4 regras no diff.

## Testing

- [x] YAML válido
- [x] Diff cirúrgico (1 arquivo, +44 linhas)
- [x] Guard \`hashFiles\` testado mentalmente — repo sem config skip o step
- [x] \`--baseline-commit\` documentado e validado localmente no probe
- [ ] **Validação live (precisa dos 3 PRs mergeados):**
  1. Merge \`propmind-core#287\` + \`control-panel-ui#372\` + este PR
  2. Abrir um PR de teste que viole uma regra (ex: \`<Button size=\"sm\">\` em drawer no control-panel-ui)
  3. Confirmar no review publicado: a regra aparece sob \"Findings → WARNING\" com rule ID \`propmind.frontend.*\`
  4. Confirmar nos logs: \`gh run view --log | grep semgrep\` mostra a invocação executando
  5. Re-rodar measure.sh em N runs após e comparar com baseline

## Ordem de merge sugerida

1. \`propmind-core#287\` (config backend) — idle
2. \`control-panel-ui#372\` (config frontend) — idle
3. **Este PR** — ativa o sistema. Próximo PR aberto nos 2 repos acima passa pelo semgrep.

body: **Contact:** [Nash Skipper](mailto:skipper.nash@epa.gov), U.S. Environmental Protection Agency **Type of code change:** Bug fix **Description of changes:** CMAS Center Forum user yanzcj identified two bugs in the STAGE calculation of mercury bidirectional flux here: https://forum.cmascenter.org/t/possible-issues-with-mercury-bidirectional-exchange-under-stage-in-cmaq-v5-5/6184 One issue is that the value of the variable `flux_hgII` in `CCTM/src/depv/stage/STAGE_MOD.F` does not multiply the deposition velocity by the concentration and is therefore not a flux in units ppm * m/s but is a deposition velocity in units of m/s. Original code: ``` flux_hgII = -Sum( Tile_Data%Lu_Vd( c,r,n_HgII,: ) * Tile_Data%LUFRAC( c,r,: ), mask = WATER) ``` Updated code: ``` flux_hgII = -cgridl1(n_HGII) * & Sum( Tile_Data%Lu_Vd( c,r,n_HgII,: ) * Tile_Data%LUFRAC( c,r,: ), mask = WATER ) ``` The second issue is that exponents are left off of the following parameters in `CCTM/src/depv/stage/HGSIM.F`: ``` REAL, PARAMETER :: satten = 7.58-1 REAL, PARAMETER :: kphot = 6.5-4 ! drm photoreduction rate 1/s REAL, PARAMETER :: kox = 7.2-4 ! dgm photo-oxidation rate 1/s ``` These should be: ``` REAL, PARAMETER :: satten = 7.58-1 REAL, PARAMETER :: kphot = 6.5-4 ! drm photoreduction rate 1/s REAL, PARAMETER :: kox = 7.2-4 ! dgm photo-oxidation rate 1/s ``` Thank you to user yanzcj for pointing out these issues. **Issue:** No github issue, but the issue was originally raised on the CMAS Center Forum: https://forum.cmascenter.org/t/possible-issues-with-mercury-bidirectional-exchange-under-stage-in-cmaq-v5-5/6184 **Summary of Impact:** Mercury bidirectional flux is not activated by default, so most users will see no difference in results. For the case with mercury bidirectional flux activated, impacts are summarized below. A one year simulation for the northern hemisphere for 2022 (with 1 month of spinup in December 2021) using the cb6r5m_ae7_aq chemical mechanism with mercury bidirectional flux activated (`setenv CTM_HGBIDI Y` in runscript) was conducted using the original and updated code to test the impacts of the change. Results below show the percent change ( `(updated code - original code) / original code` ) for the annual averages of `HG` and `HGIIGAS` concentrations in the average concentration output file (ACONC) for the surface layer. Also shown are the percent changes in annual average dry deposition values for `HG` and `HGIIGAS` and the annual average percent change in the `HG_Emis` diagnostic value from the dry deposition output file (DRYDEP). The differences in the annual averages are small. ### ACONC results ### DRYDEP results **Tests conducted:** The updated code was run for a 1 day benchmark test using both standard and debug compiler flags for the following compilers: * intel23.2 * gcc12.2 * pgi24.7 (aka nvhpc24.7) In addition to the benchmark tests, a one year simulation for the northern hemisphere for 2022 (with 1 month of spinup in December 2021) was conducted using the original and updated code to test the impacts of the change. See summary of impact section above for these results.

body:
## TL;DR
Fixes URL-only album playback on the album page, cleans up genre sourcing (drop deprecated Spotify path, filter generic labels), and adds self-healing genre population during daily album selection.

## Changes
- **AlbumPage URL playback**: Albums added via Bandcamp/artist URL now show an \"Open URL\" button in the player section. Albums with both a Spotify ID and a URL also get the extra button alongside existing service buttons.
- **Remove Spotify genres**: Spotify deprecated album-level genres; removed `genres` from `SpotifyAlbumResult` and all code paths that read from it. Apple Music is now the sole genre source.
- **Genre filtering**: Added `_IGNORED_GENRES` blocklist (`"music"`, `"music videos"`, `"musica"`) in `_get_or_create_genres` to silently drop top-level catch-all labels returned by Apple Music.
- **Self-healing on selection**: `trigger_daily_selection` now calls `_heal_genres` across all three return paths (existing selection, full chaos, and normal/chaos via `select_daily_albums`). `AlbumService.backfill_genres` makes an Apple Music lookup and stores genres if found; errors are swallowed so a failed lookup never blocks selection.
- **Backfill script**: New `scripts/backfill_genres.py` walks all albums with no genre associations and applies the same Apple Music lookup. Follows the pattern of `backfill_apple_music_ids.py` with batch commits and a triage JSON on completion.

## Testing
- [x] Nominate a Bandcamp album and confirm the album page shows an \"Open URL\" button
- [x] Confirm existing Spotify/Apple Music albums still show their full player buttons
- [x] Trigger daily selection for a group with albums missing genres; confirm genres populate after selection

## Problem
The GENTLE VANGUARD banner in TUI and scripts displayed corrupted characters (mojibake) on Windows terminals. Box-drawing Unicode characters (╗╔╝╚║═) were not rendering correctly.

## Root Cause
1. PowerShell on Windows defaults to ANSI/Windows-1252 encoding when files lack UTF-8 BOM

- Converted files to UTF-8 with BOM for proper PowerShell Unicode handling

author: madhan5422i
body:
## juspay_docs_mcp/server.py
   - Remove per-request ContextVar credential plumbing (docs MCP needs no auth)
   - Remove transcript injection and markdownify post-processing from fetch
   - Replace dynamic domain derivation with a static allowlist: *.juspay.io, *.juspay.in, dth95m2xtyv8v.cloudfront.net
   - Rewrite _url_allowed() to match netloc exactly or by suffix rather than string-prefix on the full URL (prevents false-positive on typosquats like evil-juspay.io)

   ## juspay_mcp/auth/middleware.py
   - Add skip_path_prefixes parameter to BearerAuthMiddleware; paths that match (exact or with a '/' separator) bypass the bearer token check entirely
   - Tighten the existing startswith check to path == p or path.startswith(p+'/') so a path like /juspay-docs-evil cannot sneak past a /juspay-docs skip rule

   ## juspay_mcp/auth/routes.py
   - Add OPTIONS to all well-known route method lists so MCP client CORS preflights (OPTIONS /.well-known/...) return 200 instead of 405

   ## juspay_mcp/main.py
   - In DASHBOARD mode give docs its own SseServerTransport on /docs-messages/ (separate from dashboard's /messages/) so docs SSE post-message requests are not blocked by OAuth middleware
   - Add /docs-messages/ to docs_skip_prefixes alongside /juspay-docs and /juspay-docs-stream so the full docs SSE flow (connect + post) is auth-free
   - make_sse_handler now takes the transport as an explicit parameter instead of closing over a single shared sse_transport_handler
   - SSE handler now returns _AlreadySentResponse() instead of None — fixes TypeError: 'NoneType' object is not callable in Starlette's route wrapper that was crashing the ASGI app after every SSE session ended
   - Move _AlreadySentResponse to outer scope so it is shared between SSE and StreamableHTTP handlers (removes the duplicate inner class)
   - Credential injection for docs app_key is skipped (docs has no auth context)

author: girlsmakemedrink
body:
## Summary

Three iter-7 plumbing fixes derived from iter-6 demo failures (see `docs/iterations/iter_6_demo_report.md`):

1. **Architect `llm_timeout_s` = 600s** (`agents/architect/agent.py`). iter-6 demo Architect timed out at 300s on the v2 ADR + system-design draft. Matches Backend / Frontend / DevOps's existing 600s overrides.
2. **`LLMTimeoutError` carries buffered stdout** (`core/llm/claude_code_headless.py`). Drain-after-kill pattern; `LLMTimeoutError(f"...{timeout_s}s; stdout={out!r}")`. Drain failure (rare — pipe closed mid-drain) degrades to an empty buffer + `llm.invoke.timeout.drain_failed` warning. iter-5 Phase 4 parity for the timeout path.
3. **Transitive drop cascade through HoldQueue** (`core/dispatcher/dispatcher.py`). Extracted `_cascade_drops(correlation_id, failed_task_id)` — queue-driven loop where every dropped task_id becomes a new failure trigger. Cycle-safe via HoldQueue's strictly-shrinking `_held` state and `on_drop`'s terminal-row guard. Closes iter-6 demo Failure 2 (fe + qa stuck `in_progress` after `design` was dropped).

Plus: 4 reducer integration tests in `tests/integration/test_task_state_reducer.py` (lifts iter-6's 68.8% diff-cover on the reducer); `scripts/demo_iter_7.sh` + Makefile alias.

## Real-LLM demo result

iter-7 demo (`docs/iterations/iter_7_demo_report.md`) validated all three deliverables end-to-end:
- **Architect completed for the first time across six demos** — 318s ($1.77), past iter-6's 300s wall and well under the new 600s.
- **`LLMTimeoutError` stdout field present** in Designer's synth-failed report (`stdout=''` this run — Designer hadn't flushed; the field is always present now).
- **Transitive cascade** — Designer FAILED → Frontend (depends_on=design) dropped via direct cascade + Backend FAILED → QA (depends_on=[be, fe]) dropped. Both Task rows correctly flipped to `failed` via `on_drop`; pre-iter-7 they would have stuck `in_progress`.

Chain still did **not** reach `pending_review` — two narrow new failure modes (one-line fixes each for iter-8):
- Designer hit the same 300s timeout iter-6's Architect hit (iter-7 only bumped Architect, not Designer).
- iter-6's `LLMBudgetExhaustedError` BLOCKED branch failed its first real-LLM test because `_is_budget_exhausted_stdout` requires a complete JSON parse but the adapter caps stdout at 2 KB — Backend's real `error_max_budget_usd` got routed to FAILED + cascade-drop instead of BLOCKED + owner retry.

Total spend ~$3.60 / $5.00 ceiling.

- [x] `make lint typecheck sec test test-integration smoke-llm` all green (356 unit + 8 integration = 364 tests)
- [x] `uv run ruff format --check .` clean
- [x] Diff-cover on iter-7 diff vs `origin/main`: **100%** (23 lines, all covered)
- [x] Real-LLM e2e demo run captured in `docs/iterations/iter_7_demo_report.md`

author: jmg698
body:
The mid-session reading interlude at every 25-card milestone was firing the
LLM generation request only when the user reached the milestone, blocking
the UI on the full ~13s response time. Two changes here cut that to a
near-instant transition in the common case:

1. Prefetch the upcoming interlude 7 cards before the milestone (card ~18
   for segment 0). The promise is parked in a ref and awaited by
   triggerInterlude, so by the time the user hits card 25 the sentences
   are usually already in hand. Falls back to on-demand if prefetch was
   skipped or failed.

2. Move WILD_SENTENCE_PROMPT into the `system` field with
   cache_control: ephemeral via the beta.promptCaching SDK namespace.
   The static ~3-4k-token prompt is cached after the first call, so the
   end-of-session closer (and any subsequent interlude within the cache
   TTL) skips re-processing that prefix.

author: sup3rshy
body:
Replace the Emscripten glue code loader with a custom minimal WASM instantiator that eliminates all Emscripten fingerprints (no Module, ccall, cwrap, HEAPU8 globals). Key material is now managed via opaque handles stored in WASM linear memory — raw key bytes never persist in the JS heap during normal encrypt flow.

Stealth features added:
- IIFE closure with frozen non-enumerable API (invisible to Object.keys)
- Native WASM key slot table with internal ChaCha-based PRNG (c_src)
- Dual-mode: auto-detects rebuilt vs legacy WASM binary
- Anti-tamper integrity checks on WASM exports each call
- Decoy WebCrypto traffic to pollute analyst hook logs
- Multi-pass memory wipe (0xAA→0→0x55→0) in both JS and WASM
- Key handle slot-0 bug fix (was falsy in cleanup check)

body:
## Summary

- Phase 1 step 0a previously only caught the **dead-area** shape — a stalled adjacent PR with no engagement for 30+ days. It missed the inverse shape.
- This change extends step 0a to also catch the **moving-target** shape — an *active* adjacent PR that reshapes the interface your fix calls into. Token dup-PR search returns nothing because the PRs touch different files; the risk is coordination (which signature do you call?), not duplication.
- Step renamed from "Adjacent-stalled-PR check" to "Adjacent-PR check" to reflect the broader scope. Both signals are BLOCKING.

## Motivating case (in CHANGELOG + references/case-studies.md)

2026-05-19 hunt — `topoteretes/cognee#2815` (small feature: plumb `node_name` through `ChunksRetriever`) passed every existing gate: freshness, token dup-PR search, "already fixed on main." But adjacent open PR #2712 (`fix: implement include_payload and node_name filter in ChromaDBAdapter`) was reshaping the shared `vector_db_interface.py` mid-review: 4 reviews, 6 comments, CodeRabbit auto-paused for active development. Token dup search returned nothing because the PRs are about different layers (retriever vs adapter). Caught only by a manual Phase 1 scan; without that scan, the contributor would have shipped against an interface that may not exist post-#2712-merge.

body:
Recreates the merged-then-reverted #1090 against `feature/h265-support` per @rodrigo-rodrigues-ctw's request, completing the three-PR stack so the parser + render (#1091) + seek-backfill (#1092) land into `develop` together.

- Original review history: #1090
- Revert that prompted recreation: #1107 (commit `c3a90ab`) — "Only makes sense to merge when all 3 PRs are reviewed."

Same HEAD as the merged #1090 (`28667fe`); no code change. Targeting `feature/h265-support` means the diff cleanly shows only the parser commits (merge base = `becbd13` on develop), and merging into `feature/h265-support` re-introduces what `c3a90ab` reverted, intentionally.

---

First of three PRs that replace #1062 per @rodrigo-rodrigues-ctw's request to split the original 3000+ line change into independently reviewable slices.

This PR contains only the codec-level work under `packages/den/video/`. It is independent of #1091 and #1092 in terms of code, and is the base of the stack.

## What's in this PR

**Parser**
- New H.265/HEVC parser in `packages/den/video/h265/` (Annex B framing, length-prefixed normalization, NALU iteration, slice-type and parameter-set extraction, keyframe and IRAP detection).
- Move the shared Annex B start-code finder out of `h264/` into a sibling `utils.ts` (renamed from `startCode.ts` per review) so both H.264 and H.265 parsers can use it without one codec depending on the other.
- Lift the `Bitstream` class from `h264/Bitstream.ts` to `video/Bitstream.ts` so the H.265 slice-header parser doesn't have to reach into the H.264 folder.
- New `H265FrameBuilder` under `packages/den/testing/builders/` that synthesizes minimal H.265 byte sequences for unit tests; the parser tests use it instead of inlining ad-hoc bytes.

**VideoPlayer**
- Replace the single-frame pending buffer with a timestamp-keyed map plus an insertion-order array. H.265 decoders can hold many submitted chunks in the pipeline before producing output, so the old single-slot model dropped frames.
- Introduce `decodeFrames()`, which accepts a dependency chain (e.g. keyframe + intervening P-frames) and returns a structured `DecodeFramesResult` naming whether we got the exact target, an intermediate frame, a timeout, or an abort. The single-chunk `decode()` helper now delegates to this.
- Add `awaitTargetFrame()` so callers can park on the still-decoding target after `decodeFrames()` resolves with an intermediate.
- Codec-aware decode timeouts: 30 ms for H.264, 2000 ms for HEVC. The HEVC ceiling matches worst-case software-fallback latency observed on real recordings.
- Try preferred hardware acceleration first, fall back to no-preference if the preferred config is rejected.
- Comprehensive JSDoc restored on all public methods plus inline comments on the new constants and pipeline state.

Drop `@lichtblick/log` from `packages/den`; the logger was only used by the previous VideoPlayer implementation.

## Validation

- `yarn tsc --noEmit --pretty false`
- `yarn jest packages/den/` — 167 tests, 24 suites
- `yarn eslint --config eslint.config.ci.mjs <changed files>`
- `yarn prettier --check <changed files>`

author: guysoft
body:
## Summary

Fixes the shared E2E test framework SSH stage and post-boot sudo, which were both broken by the combination of Raspberry Pi OS Trixie defaults and the headless `userconfig.service` removal we do in `prepare-image.sh`.

## Root causes

1. **SSH login failed for `pi`.** RPi OS Trixie ships the `pi` user with `/usr/sbin/nologin` as the default shell. The first-boot `userconfig.service` would normally rewrite it, but `src/distro_testing/scripts/prepare-image.sh` removes that service. Result: SSH authenticates but every session prints `This account is currently not available.` and exits 1, timing out the wait-for-ssh stage. Reproduced in FullPageOS run [24418025784](https://github.com/guysoft/FullPageOS/actions/runs/24418025784).

2. **`sudo` from the `pi` user required a password.** `userconfig.service` is also what normally drops `/etc/sudoers.d/010_pi-nopasswd`. With that service removed, `sudo apt-get install ...` and similar calls from post-boot hooks fail over non-TTY SSH (`sudo: a terminal is required to read the password`). This was previously masked by the SSH timeout above.

## Fix

In `src/distro_testing/scripts/prepare-image.sh`:

- Download `/etc/passwd` alongside `/etc/shadow`, sed-replace `:/usr/sbin/nologin` -> `:/bin/bash` for the `pi` user, re-upload.
- Add a guestfish `write /etc/sudoers.d/010_pi-nopasswd "pi ALL=(ALL) NOPASSWD: ALL\n"` with `chmod 0440`.

## Verification

Built `ghcr.io/guysoft/custompios:bugfix-e2e` from this branch, pointed FullPageOS `test/e2e-bugfix` at it. FullPageOS run [26096890001](https://github.com/guysoft/FullPageOS/actions/runs/26096890001) is fully green:

- `SSH is ready (took 98s)` (previously: 600s timeout)
- `test_boot.sh` -> PASSED
- `test_chromium.sh` -> PASSED (matchbox window detected, chromium kiosk running)
- `test_lighttpd.sh` -> PASSED
- `ALL TESTS PASSED`

## Commits in this PR

- `2a87cfb` Fix E2E SSH: set pi user shell to /bin/bash in prepare-image (cherry-picked from `feature/e2e`).
- `4f055f3` Seed /etc/sudoers.d/010_pi-nopasswd in prepare-image.
- `3b7827d` Add reusable E2E workflow, SSH helpers, and CI trigger for feature/e2e (cherry-picked from `feature/e2e`; needed because distros source `ssh-helpers.sh` from the docker image).
- `82c0ebf` ci: build docker image for bugfix/e2e branch (can be reverted on merge if desired, or left as a no-op once this branch is gone).

author: hculap
body:
## Summary

After `pipx install emodul`, users had to manually edit `claude_desktop_config.json` to wire up the MCP server, then separately run `emodul skill install` for Claude Code. This PR adds a single `emodul install <target>` command that handles everything per-client.

- `emodul install claude-code` → drops CLI-flavored `SKILL.md` into `~/.claude/skills/emodul/`
- `emodul install claude-desktop` → drops MCP-flavored `SKILL_MCP.md` (new file) into `~/.claude/skills/emodul-mcp/` AND adds `mcpServers.emodul` to `claude_desktop_config.json` with a timestamped backup
- `emodul install --all` → fans out to detected clients
- `emodul install --dry-run` → preview without writing
- `emodul uninstall <target>` → reverse

The two skill folders coexist (different `name:` YAML slugs), so each client picks the right one via description-keyword matching. Backward compat: `emodul skill install` / `emodul skill uninstall` keep working unchanged.

## Architecture

- `emodul/_client_paths.py` — per-platform config paths (macOS / Win / Linux) + client detection via marker-file probes
- `emodul/_config_writer.py` — atomic JSON merge with `tempfile + os.replace`, timestamped `.bak-YYYYMMDDTHHMMSS` (keep last 5), `fcntl.flock` for serialization, strict JSON parse (fail-loud on comments/non-object roots), shallow merge that preserves sibling top-level keys (`preferences`, other `mcpServers` entries)
- `SKILL_MCP.md` — MCP-flavored skill: 16-tool inventory, `{ok: false}` envelope semantics, no shell examples, `description:` keywords target Claude Desktop / Cursor chat / Continue / Cline / Zed
- `emodul/commands/install.py` — Click commands with JSON envelope output, conflict detection (requires `--force` to overwrite existing `emodul` entry with different args), idempotent (re-runs are `unchanged`)

## Test plan

- [x] `_config_writer` unit-tested (12 scenarios: missing file, empty, malformed JSON, non-object root, merge add/unchanged/conflict/force, remove + prune, atomic write + backup, UTF-8 roundtrip)
- [x] `emodul install claude-desktop --dry-run` → preview correct
- [x] `emodul install claude-desktop` → drops skill, merges config, creates backup, preserves siblings (`vkvm-local-poc`, `preferences`)
- [x] Re-run is `unchanged` (idempotent)
- [x] Manual config tampering → next install detects conflict, exits 1
- [x] `--force` → updates entry, creates new backup
- [x] `emodul uninstall --all` → removes both skill files + `mcpServers.emodul`, leaves siblings intact
- [x] Both skills auto-discovered by Claude (validated live: `emodul` + `emodul-mcp` both shown in available-skills list)
- [x] MCP server smoke test still passes (16 tools)
- [x] `ruff check --select=E,F,I,B` clean

## Release

After merge: tag `v0.1.4` → OIDC publish to PyPI.

body:
## Summary

Reminders no longer send a pre-canned text directly to Telegram. Instead, the scheduler now fires a synthetic `reminder_fired` event into the AI agent at delivery time. The agent receives the full chat-scoped context (system prompt, bot name, models, timezone, language, tools) and composes a fresh, in-character reply, which is then sent to the user.

## What changed

- **`Reminder` type** (`src/reminders/types.ts`) now carries `chatId` and `lang`, so settings can be looked up at fire time without guessing.
- **`schedule_reminder_{at,in}` tools** persist `chatId`/`lang` from the tool context; tool descriptions now make explicit that `text` is a private note the model writes for itself, not the user-facing message.
- **`buildInstruction`** documents the new `reminder_fired` envelope so the model knows how to recognize and respond to a fired reminder vs. a normal user message.
- **`deliverReminder`** is now AI-driven: it loads chat settings + user info, builds the reminder envelope, calls `ai.ask()` with the registered tools, sanitizes the HTML output, applies the bot-name prefix + effects top block (so a follow-up reminder scheduled mid-firing surfaces in the same blockquote style), and only then sends via Telegram. AI throw → transient retry; AI empty → fallback to the stored note.
- **`runReminderTick` / `startScheduler`** take an `AIClient` dependency; wired in `main.ts`.
- **`ToolCallContext`** gains `lang`; ask/guest handlers now pass `ctx.lang`.
- **`KeyDBStorage`** normalizes legacy reminders on read (chatId backfilled from delivery target; lang defaults to English) so existing scheduled reminders keep working.

## Test plan

- [x] `bun test` — 535 tests pass (added coverage for the new envelope shape, fallback path, AI failure modes, chat-scoped overrides at fire time, and the new instruction section)
- [x] `bunx tsc --noEmit` — clean
- [x] Manual: schedule a reminder via `/ask`, wait for it to fire, confirm the bot sends an in-character message (not the literal note) and uses the chat's bot name / persona.
- [x] Manual: confirm a legacy reminder created before this change still fires correctly after upgrade (KeyDB normalization path).
