author: donrhmexe
body:
## Summary
- advance gateway routes to compression-created child sessions without rewriting compression lineage as ordinary session switches
- keep Telegram DM-topic bindings aligned across both runtime and pre-agent hygiene compression splits
- resolve stale Telegram topic bindings to the latest compression tip before transcript/history load
- evict cached agents when their loaded session id disagrees with the canonical route session
- preserve Telegram topic routing when retrying sends after a stale/deleted reply anchor

## Why
Long Telegram DM-topic conversations can cross compression/hygiene thresholds and create child sessions. If the JSON route/session index advances but `telegram_dm_topic_bindings` still points at the pre-compression/root session, the next Telegram message reloads the old large transcript. That can cause repeated compression, stale cached-agent promotion, and visible topic/session chaos.

This patch is intentionally broader than a single rebind call. It treats compression as route publication, protects compression lineage, self-heals stale bindings, prevents cached-agent/session mismatches, and avoids falling back to the wrong Telegram topic when only the reply anchor is stale.

## Related issues and PRs consulted
- Related issue: #20470 — Telegram DM topic binding not refreshed after compression-induced session split, causing preflight compression loops.
- Related issue: #27166 — Telegram DM topic response routed to All Messages after a session split.
- Consulted PR: #20485 — refresh Telegram DM topic binding after session split. This covered the direct rebind shape but did not fully cover compression route publication / lineage preservation.
- Consulted PR: #23195 — sync Telegram topic binding after session split. This overlapped with binding carry-forward, but this PR folds that behavior into the broader compression-route path.
- Consulted PR: #26204 — publish compression route advances. This informed the distinction between route advancement and ordinary session switching.
- Consulted PR: #28524 — restore Telegram DM topic thread_id after session split. This addressed part of the thread recovery failure and is complemented here by stale-binding tip resolution and cached-agent eviction.

## Main changes
- Add `SessionStore.advance_session_after_compression()` as a narrow alternative to `switch_session()` for compression continuations.
- Add gateway helpers to:
  - follow `SessionDB.get_compression_tip()` for stale Telegram bindings
  - refresh Telegram topic bindings after session id rollover
  - recover a lost `source.thread_id` from the old binding before rebinding
  - evict cached agents with mismatched session ids
- Apply the route-publication path in:
  - inbound Telegram topic binding resolution before history load
  - pre-agent hygiene compression
  - runtime compression split handling after an agent turn
- Preserve `message_thread_id`/topic routing when Telegram rejects only a stale `reply_to_message_id`.

## Test plan
- `python -m pytest tests/gateway/test_telegram_topic_mode.py tests/gateway/test_telegram_thread_fallback.py -o 'addopts=' -q`

Result: `87 passed in 12.98s`

Additional local verification from the development session:
- dependency-focused subsets covering ACP/FastAPI/WebSocket collection passed: `434 passed`
- full suite was attempted but exceeded the local 600s timeout before completion

author: tushar15769
body:
📌 Description

This PR resolves a high-severity security and availability issue in the request-size enforcement middleware caused by relying exclusively on the Content-Length header for payload validation.

Previously, the middleware enforced upload limits only when requests provided a valid:
```
Content-Length
```
header value.

Requests that omitted the header bypassed validation logic entirely, allowing clients to stream arbitrarily large payloads into application memory without bounded enforcement.

In particular:

Payload validation depended exclusively on Content-Length
Requests without the header skipped middleware size checks
Large uploads proceeded without deterministic limits
Runtime memory consumption became attacker-controlled
Streaming payloads bypassed request-size protections
Middleware enforcement behavior varied by transfer mechanism

Because unknown-length requests were not monitored during ingestion, malicious clients could exploit the gap to trigger excessive memory allocation and degrade application availability.

As a result:

Request size protections became bypassable
Out-of-memory (OOM) conditions became possible
Resource exhaustion attacks became feasible
Application stability degraded under malicious uploads
Middleware enforcement became unreliable
Upload handling lost deterministic safety guarantees

This behavior introduced several critical security and operational concerns:

Request validation trusted client-provided metadata implicitly
Unknown-length uploads lacked runtime enforcement controls
Application memory usage became vulnerable to attacker influence
Upload protections behaved inconsistently across transfer modes
Resource exhaustion risks increased significantly
Middleware safeguards weakened under malformed request conditions

The updated implementation introduces deterministic request-size enforcement for uploads regardless of whether a Content-Length header is present.

Requests without declared payload sizes are now monitored during ingestion using runtime size tracking and bounded stream validation. Oversized uploads terminate safely once configured thresholds are exceeded.

With these changes:

Payload limits apply consistently across all request types
Unknown-length uploads enforce runtime size tracking
Oversized requests terminate safely before resource exhaustion
Middleware protections remain deterministic across transfer modes
Memory consumption remains bounded during upload handling
Application resilience against resource exhaustion improves significantly

These improvements strengthen upload security, eliminate request-size bypass behavior, and restore deterministic resource protection across middleware ingestion workflows.

✨ Changes Included

Added runtime size tracking for requests without Content-Length
Improved middleware enforcement for unknown-length uploads
Prevented request-size bypass through omitted headers
Strengthened protection against OOM and resource exhaustion attacks
Standardized upload validation across transfer mechanisms
Improved reliability of request-size enforcement workflows
Enhanced maintainability of middleware safety controls

🧪 Testing Done

Verified uploads without Content-Length enforce size limits correctly
Tested oversized streaming uploads terminate safely
Validated bounded memory usage during unknown-length requests
Confirmed resource exhaustion attempts are rejected properly
Tested middleware behavior across multiple transfer scenarios
Verified application stability during malformed upload attempts
Confirmed no regressions in standard upload functionality

closes #776

author: zhuocun
body:
## Summary

PR #269's full-reload-on-iOS fix worked around React Router's broken context propagation on iOS Safari WebKit, but the session was still being lost on iPhone for two compounding reasons:

1. **`refreshUser` logged out on any non-401 error.** Its "keep session on transient failure" branch required a cached user, but the `nativeNavigate("/projects")` full reload wipes the in-memory React Query cache. And `isUnauthorizedError` matched against the error *message*, while the backend's 401 body is `{"error": "empty JWT"}` — no "unauthorized" substring — so the check never matched in practice. Safari's `TypeError("Load failed")` and Vercel cold-start 5xx therefore looked indistinguishable from a real 401 and bounced the user to `/login`.

2. **iOS Safari Mobile commits `localStorage.setItem` to its disk-backed store asynchronously.** The login flow runs `setItem` → `queueMicrotask` → `window.location.assign("/projects")`; the document tear-down races the disk flush, the next page's `localStorage` comes up empty, and the route guard redirects to `/login` before any /users fetch is even attempted.

## Fix

- `api()` now plumbs the HTTP status onto rejected errors (`error.status = res.status`).
- `isUnauthorizedError` checks `status === 401` first, message regex as fallback.
- `refreshUser` only clears the session on a confirmed 401; transient errors keep the JWT (patching the cached user when present, otherwise leaving the cache empty until the next retry).
- `isNetworkFetchFailure` now also matches Safari's `TypeError("Load failed")` and `"The network connection was lost."` so user-facing fetch failures show the friendly i18n microcopy on iOS.
- `writeAuthToken` mirrors the JWT to a same-origin cookie (`Path=/`, `SameSite=Lax`, `Secure`-on-https, `Max-Age=86400`). Success is reported when EITHER storage path persists.
- `readAuthToken` prefers `localStorage` and falls back to the cookie, self-healing `localStorage` from the cookie value so subsequent reads and `useSyncExternalStore` subscribers see a consistent source of truth.
- `clearAuthToken` clears the cookie alongside the storage entry.
- Global test teardown clears `document.cookie` between cases so the new fallback doesn't leak between tests.

## Test plan

- [x] `npx jest` — 201 suites / 1555 tests pass (4 new tests added: cookie fallback, cookie URL-decoding, write-still-succeeds-when-storage-throws, 401-status-detection on `api()`, transient-failure session preservation in `refreshUser` without a cached user, Safari "Load failed" recognition).
- [x] `npx eslint` clean.
- [x] `npx tsc --noEmit` clean.
- [ ] Manual verification on iPhone Safari Mobile: log in, confirm the projects page loads and the session survives a refresh, an interaction, and a few minutes idle.

Closes #270.

author: zackees
body:
## Summary

First half of D2 from the LLDB darwin/x86_64 investigation. Upstream LLVM stopped publishing macOS x86_64 prebuilts after 19.x, so darwin/x86_64 will ship LLDB **19.1.7** while every other platform stays on 21.x.

This PR:

1. **Docs annotations** — README.md, CLAUDE.md, docs/LLDB.md tables flag the macOS x86_64 row with an asterisk + footnote.
2. **New build workflow** — ``.github/workflows/build-lldb-archive-darwin-x86.yml`` (manual ``workflow_dispatch``). Downloads ``LLVM-19.1.7-macOS-X64.tar.xz`` from upstream and runs the submodule's ``create_lldb_archives.py --version 19.1.7`` to produce ``lldb-19.1.7-darwin-x86_64.tar.zst`` as a CI artifact.
3. **Submodule bump** — picks up the ``--version`` override flag merged in [zackees/clang-tool-chain-bins#25](https://github.com/zackees/clang-tool-chain-bins/pull/25).

## Why ubuntu-latest (not macos-15-intel)

``create_lldb_archives.py`` is pure file-shuffling — ``tar -xJf`` extract, ``shutil.copy2``, ``tarfile`` + ``zstandard`` repack. It never runs ``codesign`` / ``otool`` / ``install_name_tool`` on the LLVM extracts. Apple-signed binaries pass through unmodified, and Linux CI minutes are ~10× cheaper than Intel-mac.

## What this PR does NOT do

Two follow-up steps remain after this lands:

- **Run the new workflow**, download the artifact, commit it into ``clang-tool-chain-bins/assets/lldb/darwin/x86_64/``, and update both LLDB manifests there.
- **Open the step-2 PR here**: bump the submodule pointer to that archive commit AND remove the broken ``Skip test (platform not yet supported)`` step in ``.github/workflows/test-lldb-macos-x86.yml`` (which currently runs ``exit 0`` in one step then lets every subsequent step run anyway — that's why ``test-lldb-macos-x86`` has been red).

Each step has its own next-action checklist in the workflow's ``GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY``.

## Background — why ``test-lldb-macos-x86`` has been red

``tests/test_lldb.py`` only ``skipTest()``s on errors containing ``404`` / ``Not Found`` / ``HTTP Error 404``. The actual error today is ``RuntimeError: LLDB platform darwin/x86_64 not found in manifest`` (raised by ``fetch_lldb_platform_manifest`` before any HTTP), which doesn't match the skip clause. The broken ``Skip test`` first step in ``test-lldb-macos-x86.yml`` runs ``exit 0`` — but ``exit 0`` only ends that step, not the job. Every step below it runs, fails, and turns the workflow red. The step-2 PR will remove that step now that an archive will actually be available.

## Test plan

- [x] ``python -c \"import yaml; yaml.safe_load(open('.github/workflows/build-lldb-archive-darwin-x86.yml', encoding='utf-8'))\"`` parses.
- [x] ``python tools/create_lldb_archives.py --help`` shows the new ``--version`` flag (verified pre-merge in [zackees/clang-tool-chain-bins#25](https://github.com/zackees/clang-tool-chain-bins/pull/25)).
- [ ] After merge: trigger the new workflow via the Actions tab. Confirm it produces a ``lldb-19.1.7-darwin-x86_64.tar.zst`` artifact (~7–15 MB expected).
- [ ] Open the step-2 PR with the archive + manifest updates and submodule bump.
- [ ] After step-2 lands, confirm the next ``lldb-macos-x86`` workflow run goes green.

author: johnpooch
body:
## What changed

PR #464 wired the shadow-mode adjudication harness into `adjudication.service.resolve()`, which calls `phase_to_canonical_game_state(phase)` on every phase resolution. The converter walked `phase.units`, `phase.supply_centers`, and `phase.phase_states -> orders` with no prefetching, reading FK relations (`nation`, `province`, `dislodged_by`, `parent`, and order `source`/`target`/`aux`/`named_coast`/`nation`) per row. That is an N+1 across several models, and the query count scaled with the number of units and orders in the phase.

- Added `PhaseQuerySet.with_canonical_state_data()` (plus the manager passthrough) that prefetches exactly the relations the converter reads. `order.nation` is a property resolving `phase_state.member.nation`, so it is covered by prefetching `phase_states__member__nation` rather than a non-existent `orders__nation` relation.
- `phase_to_canonical_game_state` now re-fetches the phase through that queryset, so the optimization holds regardless of how the caller obtained the phase (scheduled resolution, manual resolution, or a direct test call).

## Query counts

`phase_to_canonical_game_state`, measured with the `connection.queries` pattern, for a phase with 6 units/orders vs 30:

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| small (6 units, 6 orders) | 39 | 12 |
| large (30 units, 30 orders) | 159 | 12 |

The count no longer scales with unit/order count.

## variant_to_canonical_dict

Investigated as a suspect and found safe: it builds `nation_id_by_pk` / `province_id_by_pk` maps and reads raw FK id columns (`unit.nation_id`, `unit.province_id`), so there are no per-row queries. Its count is a constant 6 for both `italy-vs-germany` and `classical`. No change made; a regression-guard test locks the constant count.

One observation, not fixed here: when the variant is not prefetched, `variant.template_phase` falls back to `variant.phases.all()`, which loads every phase of every game on that variant in a single query. That is a row-volume cost, not a query-count regression, and is out of scope for this N+1 fix.

## Remaining shadow-mode cost

This fix addresses the query side only. The shadow harness also runs the full Python `Engine().adjudicate()` on every resolution — that is CPU cost, unaffected by prefetching. If resolution is still slow after this change, the engine compute should be profiled and addressed separately.

## Tests

- `phase/tests.py::TestPhaseToCanonicalGameStatePerformance` — small-game count is constant (12) and does not scale between a 6-unit and a 30-unit phase. Fails on `main` (39 ≠ 159).
- `variant/tests.py::TestVariantToCanonicalDict::test_query_count_does_not_scale_with_variant_size` — locks the constant count of 6.
- Existing `TestPhaseToCanonicalGameState` and `TestVariantToCanonicalDict` round-trip tests still pass, confirming converter output is unchanged.

Closes #467

## **Description**

Fixes inconsistent tooltip interactions and positioning issues on the MM Pay mUSD Convert screen.

**Problem:**

- Two different tooltip UX patterns were used on the same screen: one opened via hover (fee row, using legacy `react-tippy`) and another via click/tap (claimable bonus row, using `InfoPopoverTooltip`).

author: nestharus
body:
## What this means

Adds a shared, reusable contract for running the project's existing review steps against a freshly-applied code change and recording the results in one place. No user-visible behavior changes today; this is the contract that follow-on changes will plug callers into.

## What's broken

Today, the root-cause-analysis path can apply a fix and hand off downstream without running the same set of review checks the regular implementation flow runs against a change. There is no single owner that records which checks ran, against which version of the diff, with which result, and whether any check was skipped, ratified, or stood in for an unresolved inventory disagreement. The result is that a reviewer reading the post-change record cannot tell a deliberate skip from a forgotten check, cannot tell a stale prior result from a fresh one, and cannot tell whether a passing aggregate quietly absorbed a non-passing child check.

## What this PR does

Adds three new artifacts that together define the contract (no callers are wired in this PR):

- `agents/apply-gate-set.md` — a new shared operator that owns dispatching the relevant child review checks for a given caller, normalizing each child's verdict, writing a canonical join-manifest row per check, projecting those rows into the `agents/process-tree-auditor.md` expected-process schema, and refusing to advance the caller when required rows are missing, stale, malformed, non-passing, or backed only by convention prose.
- `workflows/apply-gate-set.md` — the companion workflow document. Carries the same `workflow_dispatch_contract` (inputs, expectations, outputs, non-goals) as the registry entry, and points readers at the operator as the active procedural owner.
- `workflows/index.json` — one new `apply-gate-set` registry entry so the workflow is discoverable in the same way as the existing `code-quality`, `audit`, and similar entries.

The operator's contract surface includes:

- Four named caller modes — `rca-post-apply`, `implementation-phase-4`, `implementation-phase-6`, `implementation-phase-8` — each with its own required inputs, required row kinds, and outputs.
- A join-manifest row schema with snake_case fields: `row_id`, `row_kind`, `gate_name`, `caller_mode`, `canonical_output_path`, `size`, `mtime`, `sha256`, `raw_verdict`, `verdict_line`, `normalized_verdict`, `applicability`, `runtime_claim_ref`, `producing_invocation_uuid`, `verified_at`, `skip_metadata`, `ratification_metadata`, `currentness_key`, `blocking_status`, `notes`.
- An adapter from a root-cause-analysis caller's artifacts (`root_cause_ref`, `fix_decision_ref`, `application_plan_ref`, `applied_artifact_ref`, `original_signal_verification_ref`, `verification_critic_ref`, `actual_diff_ref`, `runtime_claim_ref`, `scope_ref`, `cycle_id`) into the inputs the existing child review checks already accept.
- A runtime-claim transport contract that names how `runtime_claim` and the actual diff flow into the existing `workflows/code-quality.md`, `agents/proof-risk-auditor.md`, and `agents/validation-integrity-auditor.md` children.
- First-class row schemas for skips backed by the future hotfix-skip-with-followup convention (placeholder fields named, future convention path cited), for `bootstrap-exception` ratifications that consume `conventions/code-quality.md` § `Bootstrap exception`, and for `inventory_resolution` rows that carry explicit dual-score / folded-equivalent / non-applicability evidence for the proof-risk and supported-surface inventories.
- A currentness-key schema (`cycle_id`, `caller_mode`, `head_sha`, `base_ref`, `diff_sha256`, `scope_hash`, `runtime_claim_hash`, `contract_hashes`, `report_hashes`, `producing_invocation_uuid`, `verified_at`, `currentness_policy_ref`) and a `stale_refusal` row kind for rows whose key cannot be matched to the caller's current inputs.
- A child-dispatch shape locked to the non-interactive root policy: `agents -m <model> -f <prompt-file>` only; no bare `agents`, no host built-in sub-agent, no Task-shaped invocation.
- An audit-history append schema bound to `conventions/audit-history.md` § File Structure and § Required Schema, including the canonical round-summary, finding, and decision-register fields.

## How it works at runtime

When a future caller invokes this operator with `caller_mode` and the mode-specific inputs, the operator:

1. Validates required inputs and resolves the caller mode.
2. Builds child prompt files for each required review check that mode demands, dispatches them via `agents -m <model> -f <prompt-file>`, and collects their canonical output paths.
3. Stats and hashes each canonical output, parses each child's verdict, and writes one join-manifest row per check (or per skip / ratification / inventory-resolution / stale-refusal record).
4. Projects the manifest rows into an expected-process manifest that `agents/process-tree-auditor.md` consumes, then records the topology check's report path back on the manifest.
5. Appends round, finding, and decision-register entries to the caller-supplied audit-history file, following the existing convention's required schema rather than inventing extension fields in its place.
6. Returns a terminal aggregate decision (`LOW` / `PASS`, blocking, or one of the named refusal states) plus the canonical manifest, aggregate report, expected-process manifest, and topology report references to the caller.

## Why these design choices

- Operator + workflow + registry entry, not workflow-only. A passive workflow document by itself could not own dispatch, manifest writes, currentness refusal, or row-kind discipline — those need an active procedural owner so a caller cannot satisfy a required check with convention prose alone.
- Existing child checks are not reimplemented. PR-review, code-quality, proof-risk, validation-integrity, process-tree, test-audit, commit-hygiene, readiness, and supported-surface checks remain owned by their existing files. This operator adapts caller evidence into them and records the result; replacing them would expand the change far beyond what the contract needs to do.
- Skips, ratifications, and inventory disagreements are first-class rows rather than verdict overrides. A skip row, a `bootstrap-exception` row, and an `inventory_resolution` row each preserve the raw child verdict and record the separate exception alongside it. This keeps the "raw vs. accepted" distinction visible to reviewers and prevents a silent passing-aggregate.
- Currentness fields are defined now; invalidation rules are deferred. The manifest needs stable field names so callers and reviewers can rely on them, but the exact "when is a prior row stale?" decision is owned by sibling work (see Out of scope) and would be premature to lock in here.
- The proof-risk and supported-surface inventory disagreements are recorded as explicit dual-score / folded-equivalent / non-applicability rows rather than silently picking one reading. The disagreements have open follow-up work; recording both readings keeps the operator compatible whichever way they settle.

## Verification

- `git diff master...acr-291-apply-gate-set-operator --stat` is three files: two new markdown files and one registry entry added to `workflows/index.json`.
- `workflows/index.json` parses as JSON; the new entry mirrors the workflow file's `workflow_dispatch_contract` (inputs, expectations, outputs, non_goals) and uses only the existing `path` / `workflow` / `workflow_dispatch_contract` keys.
- The operator file declares `description`, `model: claude-opus`, and `output_format` frontmatter, and contains the section sequence the contract requires (`Declared roles`, `Adapter declarations`, `Role`, `Use When`, `Do Not Use When`, `Required Inputs`, `Optional Inputs`, `Caller modes`, `Join manifest schema`, `Process-tree expected-process schema`, `RCA contract adapter`, `Runtime-claim transport`, `Skip rows`, `Ratification rows`, `Currentness fields`, `Inventory-resolution rows`, `Aud

author: mgandal
body:
## Problem

All NanoClaw agents were writing Telegram-native `*single asterisk*` bold syntax directly. But the host runs `parseTextStyles(text, 'telegram')` which converts **standard Markdown** to Telegram syntax before sending. So `*single*` was being re-processed as _italic_, not bold.

This caused every digest and structured message to render titles and headers in italic instead of bold.

## Root cause

The preprocessor mapping in `src/text-styles.ts`:
- `*single*` → `_italic_` (Telegram italic)
- `**double**` → `*bold*` (Telegram bold)

Agents were writing `*single*` thinking it would be bold, but it was being converted to italic.

## Fix

Two files updated:

1. **`groups/global/CLAUDE.md`** — Telegram/WhatsApp formatting rule corrected:
   - Before: `*bold*` (single asterisks only) ... no `[links](url)`
   - After: `**bold**` (double asterisks — host converts to Telegram bold) ... `[links](url)` work fine

2. **`container/skills/telegram-formatting/SKILL.md`** — Full rewrite:
   - Documents the preprocessor architecture (write standard Markdown, host converts)
   - Corrects the bold row in the reference table
   - Removes the wrong "single asterisk for bold" rule
   - Updates example digest to use `**double**` bold
   - Adds preprocessor mapping table

## Testing

Confirmed in live Telegram: `**double asterisks**` renders as bold, `_underscores_` renders as italic, `[links](url)` renders as clickable links.

author: kushaldas
body:
The ThreadRow header opens message_ids[0], while the frontend renders only threadMessages[1..] as separate rows -- so message_ids[0] must be the chronologically-first email. SQLite GROUP_CONCAT(id) echoed rowid (insertion) order, which is not chronological after delta syncs, leaving the thread's first email represented by the header but never selectable.

- db/messages.rs: GROUP_CONCAT(id, '||' ORDER BY date ASC) so message_ids[0] is deterministically the thread root.
- stores/messages.ts: getVisibleIds() skips threadMessages[0] (the root, already counted via message_ids[0]) to avoid a duplicate range entry.
- Add regression test threaded_message_ids_are_ordered_by_date_ascending.

## Summary
- sort OpenAI tool schemas by function name after schema sanitization
- keep runtime-injected memory/context-engine tools in the same stable order
- sort the tool list before API kwargs and system prompt tool rendering
- re-sort at the final Chat Completions and Codex Responses request boundaries so provider-specific schema rewrites cannot reintroduce order drift
- preserve `disabled_toolsets` when `/reload-mcp` refreshes the active agent tool surface, so MCP reloads do not accidentally change the prompt tool inventory mid-session

## Evidence
Local llama.cpp/ik_llama.cpp prompt-cache replay showed equivalent tool sets being presented in different orders across requests, invalidating the common prefix:

```text

prompt:  {"name": "mcp_lean_ctx_ctx_call", "description": "Invoke any lean-ctx tool by name.", "parameters": {"properties
slot apply_checkp: id  0 | task 2640 | n_past = 7001, slot.prompt.tokens.size() = 122274, seq_id = 0, pos_min = 122273
slot apply_checkp: id  0 | task 2640 | forcing full prompt re-processing due to lack of cache data (likely due to SWA, see https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/13194#issuecomment-2868343055)
slot apply_checkp: id  0 | task 2640 | erased invalidated context checkpoint (pos_min = 120492, pos_max = 120492, size = 150.547 MiB)
slot apply_checkp: id  0 | task 2640 | erased invalidated context checkpoint (pos_min = 122273, pos_max = 122273, size = 150.560 MiB)
INFO [   launch_slot_with_task] slot is processing task | tid="136530539577344" timestamp=1779205209 id_slot=0 id_task=2563
======== Cache: cache_size = 116815, n_past0 =  7001, n_past1 =  7001, n_past_prompt1 = 7001,  n_past2 =  7001, n_past_prompt2 =  7001
Common part does not match fully
cache :  {"name": "mcp_lean_ctx_ctx_call", "description": "Invoke any lean-ctx tool by name.", "parameters": {"properties
prompt:  {"name": "feishu_doc_read", "description": "Read the full content of a Feishu/Lark document as plain text.
slot apply_checkp: id  0 | task 2563 | n_past = 7001, slot.prompt.tokens.size() = 116815, seq_id = 0, pos_min = 116814
slot apply_checkp: id  0 | task 2563 | forcing full prompt re-processing due to lack of cache data (likely due to SWA, see https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/13194#issuecomment-2868343055)
slot apply_checkp: id  0 | task 2563 | erased invalidated context checkpoint (pos_min = 116632, pos_max = 116632, size = 150.517 MiB)
slot apply_checkp: id  0 | task 2563 | erased invalidated context checkpoint (pos_min = 116814, pos_max = 116814, size = 150.519 MiB)
```

A later replay still showed the same failure class after the first fix, this time with the final request payload ordering `mcp_lean_ctx_ctx_call` before `feishu_doc_read`:

```text
INFO [   launch_slot_with_task] slot is processing task | tid="136007071322112" timestamp=1779224415 id_slot=0 id_task=9299
======== Cache: cache_size = 105293, n_past0 =  7001, n_past1 =  7001, n_past_prompt1 = 7001,  n_past2 =  7001, n_past_prompt2 =  7001
Common part does not match fully
cache :  {"name": "mcp_lean_ctx_ctx_call", "description": "Invoke any lean-ctx tool by name.", "parameters": {"properties
prompt:  {"name": "feishu_doc_read", "description": "Read the full content of a Feishu/Lark document as plain text.
slot apply_checkp: id  0 | task 9299 | n_past = 7001, slot.prompt.tokens.size() = 105293, seq_id = 0, pos_min = 105292
slot apply_checkp: id  0 | task 9299 | forcing full prompt re-processing due to lack of cache data (likely due to SWA, see https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/13194#issuecomment-2868343055)
```

This update adds defensive ordering at the final transport/preflight boundary so the wire payload remains stable even if a provider-specific sanitizer rewrites schemas after the central `agent.tools` sort.

A follow-up local trace showed another cache-break class where the active tool inventory changed mid-session rather than only reordering. The `/reload-mcp` refresh path rebuilt `agent.tools` with `enabled_toolsets` but omitted `disabled_toolsets`, so disabled platform/toolset filters could be lost after an MCP reload. This PR now preserves both filters during reload to avoid accidental prompt tool-surface changes.

author: stephane-segning
body:
## Summary

Phase 1 Week 3 of the [2h/week roadmap](planning/active/plan-09-two-hours-per-week-roadmap.md): **editor polish pass.** Two-thirds of the work was making the editor *testable* — Storybook had been broken for a while — and then a small, real polish: Cmd+K link insertion.

### 1. Unblock Storybook visual testing

The editor's Storybook playground had been crashing for two separate reasons:

**a) Tiptap version drift.** `@tiptap/extension-highlight` had picked up `3.23.5` against the rest of the toolkit's pinned `3.18.0`. Highlight 3.19+ imports `getStyleProperty` from `@tiptap/core`, which only exists in core 3.19+. Storybook's `optimizeDeps` blew up on the missing export. Pinned highlight to `~3.18.0` so only patches roll in until we do an intentional Tiptap version bump.

**b) Missing providers.** `desktop-editor/.storybook/preview.tsx` was wrapping stories in only a memory-router + MotionConfig. But `DocumentEditor` mounts `ActionMenu` from `@soma/ui`, which calls `useT()` → `useIntl()` → throws `[React Intl] Could not find required 'intl' object`. Mirrored the `@soma/ui` storybook preview: now wraps in `SomaIntlProvider` + `DensityProvider` + daisy `data-theme` + memory router.

After this, `pnpm --filter @soma/editor run storybook` actually loads.

### 2. Cmd+K link insertion

The Link extension shipped no keyboard shortcuts — the only way to add a link was clicking through the selection-bubble UI. Added an `addKeyboardShortcuts` override:

- Non-empty selection: prompt for URL (prefilled with current `href` if the selection already has a link mark), apply via `setLink({ href })`. Empty input clears the link.
- Empty selection: no-op (the bubble is the right surface for "insert link from scratch").

This uses `window.prompt` rather than reaching into the SelectionBubble's internal `mode` state — fewer cross-package contracts, and it works whether or not the bubble is currently visible.

### 3. Scenario stories for human visual testing

Three new stories so you can poke each note-taking surface after merge:

- **`Editor / DocumentEditor / Lists & nesting`** — bullet/ordered/task lists with a pre-nested structure. Exercises Tab / Shift-Tab / Enter (all default Tiptap behavior, but worth a regression surface).
- **`Editor / DocumentEditor / Format bubble`** — text pre-marked with bold / italic / code / highlight / link, plus a paragraph specifically prompting Cmd+K testing.
- **`Editor / DocumentEditor / Markdown shortcuts`** — a reference list of `# `, `## `, `### `, `> `, `- `, `1. `, ``` ``` ``` (three backticks) with empty lines below to try each.

### What the audit found that turned out to already work

The initial audit flagged "Tab/Shift-Tab list indent missing" and "no Markdown shortcuts for headings/blockquote/lists." Verifying against Tiptap's source: `extension-list-item` 3.18 ships `Tab → sinkListItem`, `Shift-Tab → liftListItem`, `Enter → splitListItem`, and the heading/blockquote/list extensions all ship `addInputRules` for their markdown triggers. The Storybook crash was the actual blocker — once you can run the playground, those features just work. No code added there.

## How to test (after merge)

```bash
pnpm --filter @soma/editor run storybook
```

Then visit each story:

- **Playground** — sanity check that the existing mixed-content story still renders without the React Intl error.
- **Lists & nesting** — click into a bullet, press `Tab` to indent, `Shift-Tab` to outdent. Press `Enter` on an empty item to exit the list. Toggle a task checkbox.
- **Format bubble** — select any text, the bubble should appear with all the format toggles. Click the link button to inspect/edit an existing link. Then select fresh text and press **Cmd+K** — a prompt should appear; submit a URL and watch the link mark land.
- **Markdown shortcuts** — click into an empty line and type `# `, then any text → should become an H1. Try the other triggers.

## Test plan

- [x] `pnpm --filter @soma/editor run test` — 20 passed
- [x] `pnpm --filter @soma/editor run typecheck` — clean
- [x] `pnpm --filter soma run test` — 122 passed
- [x] `pnpm --filter soma run typecheck:web` — clean
- [x] Visual: Playground story renders without `IntlProvider` error
- [x] Visual: each of the 3 new scenario stories renders the editor with pre-populated content
- [ ] Manual (reviewer): exercise Cmd+K, list indenting, and markdown shortcuts in each scenario story per "How to test" above

author: sahuagin
body:
## Summary

Initializes `.beads/` for claude-proxy and files two issues from today's outage triage:

- **claude-proxy-d8q** (P2 bug): proxy health-check + graceful per-backend startup degradation. Today's 23h silent outage (proxy crash-looping, `service status` reporting green) traces to a daemon(8)-wrapper-survives-inner-binary gap + per-backend hard-fail-on-startup pattern. Either fix alone prevents recurrence; together they make it impossible.

- **claude-proxy-269** (P3 refactor): extract shared anthropic-tls/oauth/aliasing crate between mu and claude-proxy. Today's 2 open dependabot alerts on claude-proxy (vs 0 on mu) are pure config drift — mu opted into rustls-tls, claude-proxy kept reqwest's default native-tls and inherited rust-openssl with its open CVEs. A separate one-line PR will close the immediate alerts; this bead is the structural fix to prevent re-divergence.

## What happened today

2026-05-19 14:00 EDT — diagnosed claude-proxy was running as a FreeBSD service (`service claude_proxy status` reported green for ~23 hours) but the inner binary had been crash-looping every ~1 second the entire time. Root cause: `/home/tcovert/.claude/.credentials.json` (claude_work backend's credentials) was root-owned (likely from an overnight cron). The proxy runs as tcovert and got "Permission denied"; since startup loads ALL configured backends and any failure is fatal, the proxy crashed and `daemon -r` respawned it for 23h.

Fix applied: `sudo chown tcovert:tcovert /home/tcovert/.claude/.credentials.json && sudo service claude_proxy restart`. claude_work also had an expired token, but the proxy correctly lazy-refreshes on first request — that's not the bug.

## What this PR does

- Runs `br init` in the repo (creates `.beads/` infra: config, metadata, issues JSONL)
- Files beads `claude-proxy-d8q` (proxy health) and `claude-proxy-269` (shared lib refactor)

No code changes. No behavior change. Pure tracking-infra.

## Test plan

- [ ] `br list` shows both beads in the open issues
- [ ] `.beads/` files are checked in

author: ksyed0
body:
The CI bash interpreter on macOS 15 ARM64 runners was treating the Unicode HORIZONTAL ELLIPSIS (U+2026, `…`) immediately after `$udid` as part of the variable name, causing `udid…: unbound variable` under `set -u`.

This was causing the nightly smoke tests for **iPhone, iPad, and watchOS** to fail every night.

**Fix:** replace all Unicode `…` with ASCII `...` and use `${var}` explicit brace syntax for any variable followed by non-ASCII characters.

## Summary

Adds a zen mode for distraction-free editing, toggled via `<space>tz`.

## Commits

- **feat(ui): add zen mode** — integrate [zen-mode.nvim](https://github.com/folke/zen-mode.nvim) with sensible defaults (hides scrollbar, status column, etc.) and a keybinding under the toggle group.
- **refactor(ui): modernize zen-mode scrollbar toggle callbacks** — use `vim.cmd.ScrollbarHide`/`ScrollbarShow` function form instead of passing strings, avoiding command re-parsing on each call.
- **fix(ui): close nvim-tree when entering zen-mode** — zen-mode opens a floating window on top of existing windows without closing them. When nvim-tree was open before entering zen-mode, the first `<space>ft` press would silently close the hidden tree window (appearing as a no-op), requiring a second press to actually toggle it open. Close nvim-tree on zen-mode open and restore it on close, tracked per-buffer so users who didn't have the tree open aren't surprised by it appearing.

## Test plan

- `<space>tz` toggles zen mode in/out.
- Scrollbar hides on enter and re-appears on exit.
- With nvim-tree open, entering and leaving zen-mode restores the tree; `<space>ft` toggles it as expected.
- With nvim-tree closed, entering and leaving zen-mode does not spawn it.

author: cglusky
body:
## Summary

- **ADR-045** (`docs/adr/045-graph-search-rule-chain.md`) proposes graph search decomp+fusion via a rule-chain coordinating four typed components (`decompose_intent` / `execute_subqueries` / `assess_sufficiency` / `synthesize_answer`). Cuts along the trained-ergonomics seam: LLM does language tasks at bounded structured-emit points; code does multi-tier graph orchestration. No new KV buckets, no persona dir, no workflow primitive — uses existing rule engine + AGENT_LOOPS + ObjectStore only.
- **`docs/concepts/14`** rewritten as canonical "How we do workflows in semstreams" pattern catalog (5 patterns: single trigger, linear pipeline, conditional branch, bounded iteration, async fan-out/fan-in). Replaces stale `reactive.NewWorkflow()` builder examples now that `processor/reactive/` is retired.
- **`CLAUDE.md` Orchestration Boundaries** updated: workflow-engine framing dropped, pattern table expanded, "engine gaps file as engine work" rule added with semspec trap callout.
- **`.claude/skills/orchestration-check`** rewritten to match: Two Layers reduced to rule engine + components, Quick Decision expanded to 5 patterns, examples updated to current JSON rule format.

## Architectural rationale (full discussion in the ADR)

Two prior architectural rounds were considered and rejected during the design conversation:

1. **Pre-LLM substrate enrichment** — wasteful (runs every loop), and deterministic decomp+fusion is hard to write well.
2. **Constrained-allowlist subagent loop** — LLMs lack trained ergonomics for graph-shape ReAct loops even when no alternative tools are present. The crimp isn't just about tool preference; it's about training-data coverage of multi-hop graph-walk + fuse trajectories.

The landing architecture (rule-chain + components) cuts along the trained-ergonomics seam and explicitly avoids the **semspec trap** (the 7,264 LOC of `workflow/reactive/` that became a migration blocker when an early app built its own state machines around rule-engine limitations).

## Test plan

- [ ] Doc-only — no code paths affected, no tests required
- [ ] Verify ADR-045 renders cleanly (markdown lint)
- [ ] Verify cross-links between ADR-045, doc 14, CLAUDE.md, and the orchestration-check skill resolve
- [ ] Operator review of ADR-045 before opening Phase 1 implementation work

  - estado del asistente;

`Patch({a:1,b:"hello"}, {a:3,b:4})` failed because the record overload required exact type matches for overlapping fields across update records. This change relaxes that rule so record patching can evolve field types while still computing a consistent return record type.

- **Record-overload type-checking change**
  - Updated `PatchRecordFunction.CheckTypes` to stop rejecting updates when an existing field appears with a different type.
  - Kept non-record argument validation intact.
  - Return type is now derived by unioning base/update record types across all update arguments, even when overlapping field kinds differ.

- **Regression coverage for record patching**
  - Added focused tests in `TexlTests.cs` for:
    - literal record patching with new and overlapping fields
    - overlapping field type changes (e.g., `b:n -> b:s`)
    - variable-based record patching, including `Unknown` (`$`) fields
  - Updated variable-based test inputs to pass variable names explicitly (avoids brittle parsing from expression text).

author: hndrewaall
body:
## Summary

The live-log modal in queue-minisite was silently broken for the `examples/compose` stack: clicking a running item opened the modal but the stream stayed empty. Root cause: the `claude-watch-state` named volume (which holds `active-agents.json`) was never shared with the queue-minisite container, so the app couldn't look up which JSONL transcript to tail.

- **`claude-container`**: add `${CW_STATE_PATH:-claude-watch-state}:/var/lib/claude-watch` volume mount — same pattern as `container/compose.yml` but missing from the examples stack.
- **`queue-minisite`**: add the same volume read-only at `/agents-state`, set `AGENT_STATE_JSON=/agents-state/active-agents.json` (live-log owner lookup) and `QUEUE_LOG_ARCHIVE_DIR=/queue-home/.config/session/queue-logs` (View-log button on done/abandoned items).
- **Top-level `volumes:`**: declare `claude-watch-state` so docker compose doesn't error when `CW_STATE_PATH` is unset.
- **New test** (`examples/compose/bin/tests/queue-minisite-agent-state-wiring.test`): locks the file-level wiring at the compose-YAML level, same pattern as `container/tests/state-volume-default.test`.

The `CW_STATE_PATH` override path still works: set it to an absolute host path (e.g. when native claude-watch writes to `/var/lib/claude-watch` on Linux) and both the `claude-container` and `queue-minisite` mounts resolve to the same host directory, bypassing the named volume.

## Test plan

- [ ] `python3 examples/compose/bin/tests/queue-minisite-agent-state-wiring.test` prints `OK`
- [ ] `python3 container/tests/state-volume-default.test` still prints `OK`
- [ ] `docker compose up` from `examples/compose/`, click a running queue item → live-log modal streams events

body:
## Summary

Adds classification badges and a Pitch Score chip to the premium Pitcher Breakdown card, plus an Order picker dropdown that defaults to **Pitch Score (best to worst)**.

- **Badges (max 4, priority-ordered).** Reuses `_sp_compute_tiers` so classifications stay consistent with the rest of the app. HR risk always renders first (the headline most prop bettors look for), followed by strength badges (K Dominator, Command Edge, Traffic Limiter, Matchup Boost), then softer context (BABIP, Fade Risk). Adds a projection-derived Matchup Boost fallback when nothing else fires but PROJ_K ≥ 7.5.
- **Pitch Score chip.** Renders on the card. Prefers the precomputed `Pitch Score` column from `build_slate_pitcher_table` (35% xwOBA-against + 25% K-BB% + 20% Whiff% + 20% Barrel%-against). Falls back to a documented blend of `PROJ_K (30%) / K-BB% (20%) / ERA (20%) / WHIP (15%) / HR/9 (15%)` so StatsAPI-only rows still get a stable score.
- **Sort dropdown.** New `Order picker` selectbox above the pitcher picker. Options: **Pitch Score (best to worst)** (default), `Slate order`, `Pitcher name (A-Z)`. The previously selected pitcher is preserved across re-sorts when it still exists in the new ordering. Slate order and alpha sort remain available so prior picker behavior is preserved.
- **Mobile bottom safe-area fix preserved** — no changes to `.pbd-tail` or the mobile media query.
- **Old clutter not reintroduced** — the simplified Pitcher Breakdown view continues to omit the old metric guide, downloads, Min IP filter, and slate dashboard renderer. The badge label strings (K Dominator, Command Edge, Traffic Limiter) only appear via `_sp_compute_tiers`, never inline in the view block (asserted by tests).

### Files changed

- `app.py` — adds `_pitcher_breakdown_pitch_score`, `_pitcher_breakdown_badges`, `render_pitcher_breakdown_badges`; new `.pbd-badge*` and `.pbd-sort-hint` CSS; updates view block to render the badges row and offer the Order picker.
- `tests/test_pitcher_breakdown_render.py` — 12 new tests covering the new helpers and view behavior; relaxes the forbidden-strings guard to allow badge labels coming from the helper (still forbidden as inline literals in the view block).

## Test plan

- [x] `python -m py_compile app.py`
- [x] `python -m pytest` — all **240 tests pass**, including 30 in `test_pitcher_breakdown_render.py`
- [ ] Manual smoke on the Streamlit app: pick a starter, verify badges render under the KPI grid, switch sort order and confirm the picker re-orders by Pitch Score, confirm selection survives re-sort, confirm mobile last-row scrollability is unchanged.

## Summary
- New `bin/merger-cron.ts` — operator's daily cron entry point. Reads `merger-sweep --dry-run` JSONL, aggregates all `hitl_*` PRs into ONE cluster HITL prompt (`taste`/`ask_choice`, `recommended=defer-all`, 24h timeout), logs the `ready` partition (merger subagent invocation deferred), and ignores `defer`/`skip`.

author: 100yenadmin
body:
## TL;DR **First PR of the LCM v4.1 stacked series** — the bones the next 12 PRs build on. Adds the v4.1 database schema (16 tables) + worker concurrency primitives. All-additive: new files plus append-only, idempotent migration steps. **No existing code path changes; no user-visible behavior change yet.** This PR ships the skeleton; the next 12 ship the muscles. ## The v4.1 story in one paragraph v4.1 rebuilds LCM the way a person actually remembers: **keep the raw conversation forever, embed it for similarity search, synthesize fresh views on demand.** The v3 `lcm_recent` tool produced summaries-of-summaries-of-summaries that got worse the further back you looked; v4.1 stops building rollups and adds an agent surface mapped to the five question types a person actually asks: > "What did we work on yesterday?" · "Have we ever discussed X?" · "What did X *exactly* say?" · "Tell me about person/project Y" · "Where did this claim come from?" This first PR is the SQL schema + worker coordination primitives that make the rest possible. ## Before / after — what this enables ```mermaid flowchart LR subgraph Before["Before — v3 rollup era"] M1[messages] --> L1[leaf summaries] L1 --> D[day rollup] D --> W[week rollup] W --> Mo[month rollup
summary OF summary
OF summary] style Mo fill:#f99 end subgraph After["After — this stack lands"] M2[messages
+ suppressed_at] --> L2[leaf summaries
+ suppressed_at] L2 -.->|sidecar| V[vec0 embeddings
this PR creates table] L2 -.->|sidecar| E[lcm_entities
this PR creates table] L2 -->|on demand only| S[synthesis_cache
this PR creates table] style V fill:#9f9 style E fill:#9f9 style S fill:#9f9 end ``` The green tables are what this PR creates; the next 12 PRs light them up. ## What this PR adds ### Schema (`src/db/migration.ts`) Append-only `runMigrationStep(...)` blocks creating the v4.1 surface: | Cluster | Tables | |---|---| | Embeddings substrate | `lcm_embedding_profile`, `lcm_embedding_meta`, `lcm_embedding_meta_cleanup_summary` (suppression-cascade trigger) | | Entity catalog | `lcm_entities`, `lcm_entity_mentions`, `lcm_entity_type_registry`, `lcm_extraction_queue` | | Synthesis | `lcm_prompt_registry`, `lcm_synthesis_cache`, `lcm_synthesis_audit` | | Eval | `lcm_eval_run`, `lcm_eval_query_result` | | Operator + workers | `lcm_worker_lock`, `lcm_feature_flags` | | Pre-existing extensions | `summaries.suppressed_at`, `messages.suppressed_at` columns | `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS` + `ALTER TABLE ADD COLUMN` only — no existing step modified, no column drops, no type changes. **Zero collisions with upstream's focus-mode** (focus uses `focus_*`; this uses `lcm_*` / extends `summaries`). ### Concurrency primitives (`src/concurrency/`) - **`model.ts`** — worker job kinds (`embedding-backfill`, `entity-coreference`, …) + `WORKER_LOCK_TTL_MS` / `WORKER_HEARTBEAT_MS`. Single source of truth that workers and locks agree on. - **`worker-lock.ts`** — advisory single-flight lock over `lcm_worker_lock`. Used by every background worker the next 11 PRs add. ```mermaid flowchart LR W1[Backfill autostart
5min cadence] -->|INSERT OR IGNORE| L[lcm_worker_lock
job-kind PK
expires_at TTL] W2[Entity coref autostart
60s cadence] -->|INSERT OR IGNORE| L L -->|heartbeat 30s
UPDATE WHERE expires_at > now| L L -.->|crash → expires_at < now| Stolen[next acquirer takes lock] ``` Verified against parallel writers via `worker_threads` in `test/v41-concurrency-invariants.test.ts` (full suite ships in pr12; the lock itself is tested here in `test/worker-lock.test.ts`). ### `src/db/connection.ts` (small additive) - `assertForeignKeysEnabled()` — verifies `PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON` actually took effect (silent-degrade-to-off was a real Wave-2 trap). - `new DatabaseSync(dbPath, { allowExtension: true })` — enables `sqlite-vec` loading in pr02. **Behavior-preserving when no extension loads** — the flag is a capability, not an activation. ### 13 tests Each table cluster has a schema-shape test; concurrency-model has 3; migration idempotence has 2. **The schema is verified before any consumer code lights it up.** ## Deferred on purpose The prompt-registry **default-prompt seeding** step is intentionally deferred to the Synthesis PR (#726). This PR creates `lcm_prompt_registry` but does not populate it — the `seedDefaultPrompts` migration option is accepted (so schema tests can pass `false`) but is a no-op until #726 wires in the `synthesis/seed-default-prompts.ts` seeder. Keeps the foundation PR free of any synthesis-layer code dependency. ## The science: why schema-first? Two ways to ship 16 cross-feature tables: (a) per-feature schema in each feature PR, or (b) one foundation PR. (a) means each feature PR re-audits its migration in isolation, but v4.1's migrations are tightly entwined — the shared `lcm_embedding_meta_cleanup_summary` trigger references both `lcm_embedding_meta` AND `summaries`; the extraction queue references `lcm_entity_mentions`. Slicing those across PRs creates cross-PR ordering risk and re-reviews the same migration safety multiple times. (b) concentrates the riskiest schema operation in one carefully-audited PR; downstream PRs become "what does this code do with tables that already exist" rather than "is this migration safe." Migrations are simple by design (`CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS`); the complexity is in the consumer code, which gets one PR per feature. Picked (b). body:
## Summary

The temperature graph in the menu bar dropdown is clipped at the top: only the legend (orange dot + "Temperature" label) is visible at the bottom of the graph box, the sparkline above it gets cut off. Other rows in the same `InfoViewController` stack view (Thermal Pressure, Temperature value, etc.) can also be clipped depending on layout state.

| Before (bug) | After (fix) |
| :---: | :---: |
| ![Clipped graph in the Hot dropdown — only the bottom legend is visible](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/pggpgg/Hot/pr-assets/bug-clipped-graph.png) | ![Hot dropdown rendering correctly with full graph and other rows visible](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/pggpgg/Hot/pr-assets/fixed-graph.png) |

> _Note: the two screenshots were taken in different system appearances (Dark mode for "before", Light mode for "after"), which is why the menu chrome and graph background look different. `GraphView` uses `NSColor.controlTextColor` for its rounded-rect background, and that's a dynamic system color that resolves differently between Dark and Light mode. No color-related code was changed by this PR._

## Root cause

`InfoViewController.view` is installed as a custom view on an `NSMenuItem` in `ApplicationDelegate.applicationDidFinishLaunching`:

```swift
self.menu.item( withTag: 1 )?.view = infoViewController.view
```

`NSMenu` measures the custom view's frame once at this point and caches the result for the menu item's host. It does **not** observe later Auto Layout changes to the view's intrinsic size.

`viewDidLoad` initializes `graphViewHeight.constant = 0`, so the view is initially short. A couple of seconds later, once two temperature samples have been collected, `update()` does:

```swift
self.graphViewHeight.constant = self.graphView?.canDisplay ?? false ? 100 : 0
```

Auto Layout grows the view to its new height, but the menu item's host frame stays at the original (smaller) value. The bottom-anchored portions of the graph (drawn at `rect.origin.y` in unflipped coords — the orange dot and "Temperature" label) remain visible, while the top of the graph — including the sparkline — is clipped off by the menu item's container.

## Fix

After the constraint change in `update()`:

1. Detect that the constraint actually changed (avoids re-laying out every refresh tick).
2. Call `view.layoutSubtreeIfNeeded()` to flush the pending Auto Layout pass.
3. Set `view.frame.size = view.fittingSize` to nudge `NSMenu` to re-measure the custom view's host item with the new size.

This is the minimal change that gets the menu to respect the dynamic content size.

## Test plan

- [x] Build patched Hot.app, launch, open the dropdown after ~4 seconds (enough time for two temperature samples to populate the graph). Graph is now fully visible.
- [x] Close and re-open the dropdown several times — graph renders correctly each time.
- [x] Verified on macOS 26.5 with Xcode 26.5 (Apple Silicon, MacBook Air).

> [!WARNING]
> Some dependencies could not be looked up. Check the Dependency Dashboard for more information.

### GitHub Vulnerability Alerts

#### [CVE-2026-45570](https://redirect.github.com/go-git/go-git/security/advisories/GHSA-m7cr-m3pv-hgrp)

### Impact

`go-git`'s SSH transport constructs the remote exec command by wrapping the repository path in single quotes without escaping single quotes embedded inside the path. This diverges from canonical Git, which shell-quotes the path through `sq_quote_buf` so that an embedded `'` becomes the `'\''` close-escape-reopen sequence and the whole path round-trips as a single quoted argument.

A repository path containing a single quote can therefore break out of the quoted region in the exec command and be appended as additional shell tokens. On SSH servers that evaluate the exec command through a shell (for example a user account whose login shell is `/bin/sh` or `/bin/bash`, or a `ForceCommand` wrapper that re-evaluates `$SSH_ORIGINAL_COMMAND`), those additional tokens execute in that account's command-execution context. SSH servers that tokenize the exec command without shell evaluation, including the canonical `git-shell` setup, are not affected.

The vulnerable behaviour is on the SSH server side, not in `go-git`: the same bytes can be produced by any SSH client. The change in `go-git` is defense-in-depth that restores parity with canonical Git's wire format and prevents `go-git` from being a vehicle for reaching shell-evaluating servers through attacker-influenced repository paths.

### Patches

Users should upgrade to a patched version in order to mitigate this issue. The fix ports `sq_quote_buf` from canonical Git into `go-git`'s SSH transport so that the wire output is byte-identical to what `git` itself would send for the same input.

Versions prior to `v5` are likely to be affected, users are recommended to upgrade to a supported go-git version.

### Credit

Thanks to @​N0zoM1z0 for reporting this to the `go-git` project. :bow:

#### [CVE-2026-45571](https://redirect.github.com/go-git/go-git/security/advisories/GHSA-crhj-59gh-8x96)

### Impact
A path validation issue in `go-git` could allow crafted repository data to affect files outside the intended checkout target, including the repository's `.git` directory.

These validations were introduced in upstream Git years ago, so the vulnerability arose from go-git drifting from those checks. Some attack vectors were platform-specific: certain payloads affected only Windows users, others affected only macOS users, and some applied across all supported platforms.

Using non-descendant `go-billy` filesystem instances, or different filesystem types, for the `Storer` and `Worktree` may provide some isolation against `.git` directory manipulation. For example, users that store the `.git` directory through `memfs` while using `osfs` for the worktree are not affected by this vulnerability in the main repository, because repository metadata is not materialized inside the worktree filesystem.

However, this isolation does not necessarily apply when the repository contains submodules, since submodule dotgit directories may still be represented or materialized within the worktree context.

It is important to note that exploitation requires a maliciously crafted repository payload. Users should always exercise caution when interacting with repositories or Git servers they do not trust.

### Patches
Users should upgrade to a patched version in order to mitigate this vulnerability. Versions prior to `v5` are likely to be affected, users are recommended to upgrade to a supported go-git version.

### Credits
Thanks to @​kodareef5, @​AyushParkara and @​N0zoM1z0 for reporting this to the go-git project in three separate reports. 🙇

body:
Closes #8 — implements all 7 tasks from `docs/plans/2026-05-19-clrepo-windows-ps-support.md` in one PR.

`clrepo.sh` stays canonical. Windows support is added via:

1. **Path helpers in `clrepo.sh`** — `_clrepo_is_windows` (`$OSTYPE` detection), `_clrepo_norm_path` (Win→POSIX via `cygpath -u` + pure-Bash fallback), `_clrepo_display_path` (POSIX→Win via `cygpath -w` + pure-Bash fallback).
2. **One-time normalization at entry** — `_CLREPO_BASE` is wrapped through `_clrepo_norm_path` so all downstream code uses POSIX paths regardless of how the env var was set.
3. **Display normalization** — the four prominent "under $_CLREPO_BASE" messages now show `C:\...` on Windows (no-op on POSIX).
4. **`clrepo.ps1` shim** — locates `bash.exe` (via `$env:CLREPO_BASH`, `git --exec-path`, well-known Program Files paths, `Get-Command`), sources `clrepo.sh`, forwards `@args`, and mirrors `$LASTEXITCODE`.
5. **`tests/test_norm_path.sh`** — first test file in the repo. Self-contained Bash assertions (no framework needed) covering platform detection, POSIX passthrough, Windows conversion with a cygpath shim, and the cygpath-less fallback. 11 assertions, all green on Linux.
6. **README** — new "Windows / PowerShell" section with prerequisites, PowerShell setup snippet, and the `cd`-doesn't-survive-back-to-PS caveat.
7. **Version bump** — 1.34.0 (skipping 1.31-1.33, reserved for PRs #11/#12/#13).

## Out of scope (per the spec / issue body)

- ADO is already first-class via the existing forge dispatch — no work needed.
- PowerShell-native tab completion.
- Making `clrepo <repo>` change the PowerShell session cwd.
- Windows CI; native PS port; binary rewrite.

## Heads-up: merge conflicts with concurrent Ralph PRs

This branch starts from `main` before PRs #11/#12/#13 land:
- **PR #13 (issue #3)** restructured the `_CLREPO_BASE` resolution block into an env > config-file > default precedence chain. This PR's normalization wrap (`_CLREPO_BASE=$(_clrepo_norm_path …)`) will conflict on the same area. Resolution: after the precedence chain decides the value, add `_CLREPO_BASE="$(_clrepo_norm_path "$_CLREPO_BASE")"` as a final line.
- **Version bumps** in `clrepo.sh` line and `CHANGELOG.md` top entry will conflict with whichever sibling PRs land first. Resolution: keep the highest version, merge changelog entries chronologically.

## Verification (Linux dev box)

- `bash tests/test_norm_path.sh`: `PASS` (11/11 assertions)
- `bash -n clrepo.sh`: OK
- `bash -c '. ./clrepo.sh && echo $_CLREPO_VERSION'`: `1.34.0`
- `bash -c '. ./clrepo.sh && echo $_CLREPO_BASE'`: `/home/me/projects/repos` (unchanged on Linux — norm is no-op)
- `grep 'under $_CLREPO_BASE' clrepo.sh`: only the comment on line 5 remains; no plain code refs

## Manual Windows verification (deferred to user, post-merge)

Per spec §5: PowerShell with `$env:CLREPO_BASE='C:\Develop\Repos'`, then with `'/c/Develop/Repos'`, then from Git Bash on the same box. ADO smoke. Bogus `$env:CLREPO_BASH` → exit 127.

author: drquasney
body:
## Symptom
User reported: started an interview on a drive with iPhone connected to car (CarPlay) AND headphones plugged in. Speaker test played through headphones fine. First interview question errored. Interview kept going — questions streamed as text, mic captured answers — but no audio for the rest of the session.

## Root cause
An iOS audio-session interruption (route change between car ↔ headphones, BT disconnect, incoming call) puts the \`<audio>\` element into a broken state. Subsequent \`.play()\` calls resolve "successfully" but produce no audible output. iOS doesn't repair the audio session; the element does. And the speechSynthesis fallback is also silent on iOS without a fresh gesture, so we just look like the interview proceeded with text-only output.

## Fix
1. \`tts.js\` exports \`resetAudioPlayback()\` — tears down the shared \`<audio>\` element and clears \`isPrimed\`.
2. \`tts.js\` exports \`onAudioPlaybackFailure(handler)\` for UI subscription.
3. \`createTtsPlayer\` 's error path resets the audio element AND notifies subscribers, so the next user gesture can prime a fresh element.
4. \`InterviewSession\` subscribes and surfaces a "Audio interrupted — tap to restore" banner above the mic dock.
5. Tapping the banner re-primes audio (fresh element activated inside the gesture) AND re-speaks the last assistant message so the user catches up on what they missed.

## Test plan
- [ ] iOS Safari real device: start interview with headphones plugged in, mid-session unplug them. First question after unplug errors → banner appears → tap banner → audio comes back, last question replays.
- [ ] CarPlay/BT scenario: start interview, change route (connect/disconnect BT). Banner appears on failure; tap restores.
- [ ] Desktop Chrome: no banner ever appears in normal use; if a synthetic error is fired, banner shows and tap recovers.
- [ ] Banner only renders during an active interview (not on Finish/complete states).

author: isaacgarza
body:
## What

- Replaces the all-or-nothing preflight data collection with greedy per-file packing: files are sorted by review tier priority and included until the byte budget is exhausted, so large PRs still get as many pre-collected files as fit instead of falling back to zero
- Adds an ERR trap with `set -E` to `claude-review` for better failure diagnostics
- Fixes the `set -e` function-last-statement pitfall (`[[ cond ]] && cmd` as terminal statement) across four scripts by appending `return 0`
- Adds `_diagnose_missing_output()` to parse session logs when review agents produce no output, surfacing the reason (max turns, error, etc.)
- Introduces `DEFAULT_MAX_TURNS_NO_PREFLIGHT` (30) so agents that must read files directly get more turns
- Documents the function-last-statement pitfall in `bash.md`

## Why

- Large PRs were silently losing all pre-collected file contents when the total exceeded 480KB, forcing agents to read every file individually and often hitting the turn limit before finishing
- Several scripts could silently exit with code 1 when a conditional at the end of a function evaluated to false under `set -e`, making failures hard to diagnose
- When review agents produced no output, the only message was "produced no output" with no indication of why — session log parsing now surfaces the root cause

## Testing

- Extended `tests/review_orchestrate.bats` with conditional preflight packing tests (partial fit, all fit, none fit, omitted files list)
- Added `tests/claude_review.bats` with ERR trap and `_append_orchestrate_flags` return-code tests
- Updated `tests/bin_scripts.bats` regex to accept `set -Eeo pipefail` variants

author: pedrosakuma
body:
Closes #40.

Completes the static-introspection story together with #38 (attributes) and #39 (hierarchy): you can now walk types → fields/properties/events → their custom attributes without ever decompiling a method body.

## Surface
- New `IMetadataIndex.ListMembers(mvid, typeToken, query)`: fields, properties, events of a TypeDef, with optional `Kind` / `NamePattern` / `SignatureContains` filters and cursor paging. Methods stay on `list_methods` (different shape: IL size + generic arity).
- New `MemberSummary` (`Handle`, `Kind`, `Name`, `Signature`, `Attributes`). Handles use new prefixes: `f:<mvid>:0x<token>` (field), `p:<mvid>:0x<token>` (property), `e:<mvid>:0x<token>` (event).
- `AttributeTargetKind` extended with Field / Property / Event so `list_attributes` accepts the same handles `list_members` returns.
- New MCP tool: `list_members`.

## Implementation
- `CollectFields` / `CollectProperties` / `CollectEvents` walk `TypeDef.GetFields()/.GetProperties()/.GetEvents()` and render concise C#-ish signatures (`int Field`, `string Name { get; set; }`, `event EventHandler Changed`).
- Field attributes formatted with the same access-modifier + static/readonly/const/specialname pattern used by `FormatAttributes(MethodAttributes)`.
- `GetAttributeHandles` dispatches to `FieldDefinition` / `PropertyDefinition` / `EventDefinition` via a new `TryEntityHandleOfKind` helper (the older `TryHandleOfKind<T>` was hard-coded to TypeDef/MethodDef).
- `BadImageFormatException` is caught per-row (same pattern as `list_attributes`).
- Cursor is a 1-based ordinal across the combined (fields, properties, events) sequence.

## Tests
- New `ListMembersTests` (8 tests): every-kind enumeration, kind filter, field modifier flags, property accessor rendering, combined name+signature filter, pagination uniqueness, `TokenWrongTable` for method tokens, plus a cross-surface test that `list_attributes` accepts Field/Property/Event handles.
- SampleLib gains `CustomerDto` (const string, static readonly int, private readonly Guid, public int field, init-only / get-set / get-only properties, EventHandler event with `[FixtureMarker]`) — minimal but covers every case.
- `FixtureMarkerAttribute` usage widened to Field/Property/Event.
- `ToolReturnTypeSchemaContractTests` stays green on the new return types.
- **181/181 passing** (was 173).

- `app/free/[slug]/page.tsx` — lead magnet opt-in pages with email capture

### Phase 4 — Revenue Ops Integration
- `app/api/revenue-ops/[...path]/route.ts` — authenticated proxy to Cloud Run backend (hides URL, adds auth header, 10s timeout)
- `app/api/lead/route.ts` — activated: logs leads + fires non-blocking event to autonomax

### Phase 5/6 — Conversion & Attribution
- `src/lib/attribution.ts` — UTM capture → sessionStorage, `appendAttribution()`, `trackCheckoutIntent()` via sendBeacon
- `components/AttributionInit.tsx` — client component; wired into root layout
- `components/ui/CheckoutButton.tsx` — wraps checkout links with UTM passthrough

- [ ] Set GitHub secrets: `VERCEL_TOKEN`, `VERCEL_ORG_ID`, `VERCEL_PROJECT_ID`

author: demoray
body:
Fixes #6418.

## Summary

`CFGFast.drop_bad_functions`'s per-block cleanup loop iterated
`func.blocks`, which yields nothing for a function loaded via
`parse_from_cmessage(meta_only=True)` because that mode only
populates `_local_block_addrs` (a set of addresses) and leaves
`_local_blocks` (the address→BlockNode dict that `Function.blocks`
iterates) empty. So whenever a bad function happened to be spilled
to LMDB at drop time, the loop was a silent no-op: the function was
removed from `kb.functions` but its CFG nodes survived and its
bytes stayed classified as `"code"` in `_seg_list`. See #6418 for
the full sequence and observable effect.

## Fix

Iterate `func.block_addrs` (populated for both cached and spilled
funcs) and read block sizes from the CFG model:

```python
for block_addr in list(func.block_addrs):
    cfg_node = self.model.get_any_node(block_addr)
    if cfg_node is not None:
        self._seg_list.occupy(cfg_node.addr, cfg_node.size, "unknown")
        self.model.remove_node_and_graph_node(cfg_node)
```

`cfg_node.size` is the same size `Function.blocks` would have
yielded via `block.size`. No extra LMDB I/O; same logic for cached
and spilled bad functions.

## Test

`tests/knowledge_plugins/functions/test_function_meta_only_blocks_iterator.py`:

- One test documents the underlying contract that made the bug
  possible — `Function.blocks` is empty after
  `parse_from_cmessage(meta_only=True)` even though
  `Function.block_addrs` is not.
- One end-to-end test reproduces the spilled-bad-function scenario
  (serialize, reload in meta-only mode, run the post-fix cleanup
  loop on it) and asserts the CFG node is removed and the bytes
  are reclassified.

## Compatibility

- No API change.
- For cached bad functions the behavior is unchanged (same blocks
  cleaned up, same CFG nodes removed, same `_seg_list.occupy`).
- For spilled bad functions the cleanup now actually runs. CFG
  output on binaries large enough to trigger `SpillingFunctionDict`
  eviction will become independent of LRU timing at
  `drop_bad_functions` time. Some functions previously kept at
  their original address (because cleanup didn't fire, so
  `make_functions` could resurrect them) will now be cleaned up
  consistently with the cached-path behavior — i.e. resurrected at
  the next valid `"code"` address from `call_dst_keys` instead of
  the original.

author: chrisromp
body:
## Motivation

The existing `UserService.update()` method accepted all user fields indiscriminately, relying on the controller to strip admin-only fields before calling it. This made the service layer unsafe for direct internal use -- any caller that forgot to sanitize could accidentally grant permissions or change roles.

## Approach

Split the single `update()` into two role-aware methods with distinct type signatures:

- **`updateProfile(id, UpdateProfileDto)`** -- only accepts user-editable profile fields. Includes a runtime whitelist so that even if a caller bypasses TypeScript with `as any`, admin fields cannot reach the database.
- **`adminUpdateUser(id, AdminUpdateUserDto)`** -- extends UpdateProfileDto with permission flags (`allowRegistration`, `allowEarlyRegistration`, etc.) and `role`. Only admin callers should invoke this.

The controller dispatches to the correct method based on the caller's role, providing defense-in-depth at both the HTTP and service layers.

## Key decisions

- **Runtime whitelist in `updateProfile()`**: The service explicitly filters to a known set of profile field names before passing data to Prisma. This guards against internal callers or future refactors that might bypass DTO validation.
- **`isEmailVerified` added to protected fields**: This auth-state field should only be written by dedicated verification flows, never through general update paths.
- **Deprecated `UpdateUserDto`**: Kept as a type alias extending `AdminUpdateUserDto` for backward compatibility. Existing imports compile but callers are guided to migrate.
- **Single endpoint preserved**: Rather than splitting into separate routes, the existing `PUT /users/:id` dispatches internally. This avoids breaking API clients.

## Test coverage

- 974 unit tests passing (up from 973)
- New unit test proving admin fields are stripped from `updateProfile()` even with `as any` casts
- DTO validation tests for both new DTOs
- Controller dispatch tests verifying correct method is called per role
- E2e tests with strengthened assertions (check key absence, not just truthy values)

Closes #175

author: louiswol94
body:
## Summary

Restores working bulk and single-row actions for the **Trash** tab on the Manage Snippets screen. After the React rewrite these were either no-ops or wired to the wrong code paths, so this PR re-introduces the legacy behaviour with the new React/REST stack.

## Changes

### Bulk actions on the Trash tab (`SnippetsListTable.tsx`)

- The bulk-action dropdown on the Trash tab now exposes only **Restore** and **Delete Permanently**, matching the legacy UI.
- Both actions iterate the selected snippets and call the REST API (`restore` / `delete`) per item, then refresh the list.
- The pool of snippets the action looks up by ID is now the snippets visible on the current tab (`snippetsByStatus.get(currentStatus)`), instead of `snippetsByStatus.get('all')`. Trashed snippets are only stored in the `'trashed'` bucket by `partitionSnippetsByStatus`, so filtering against `'all'` silently produced zero targets, which is why Apply appeared to do nothing.

### Single row actions on the Trash tab (`TableColumns.tsx`)

- Removed the **Export** link from the row actions for trashed snippets. Trashed rows now show only **Restore | Delete Permanently**, matching the legacy UI.
- **Restore** already worked. **Delete Permanently** is fixed by the server-side change below.

### Permanent delete via REST (`Snippets_REST_Controller.php`)

- `delete_item` previously decided "trash vs permanent delete" from `$item->trashed` on the request body. The client never sends that flag on a DELETE, so permanent deletes silently re-trashed already-trashed snippets (a no-op).
- It now loads the snippet from the database via `get_snippet()` and uses its real `trashed` state to choose between `trash_snippet()` and `delete_snippet()`. As a side benefit, clients can no longer override the server's view of the snippet state.

## Test plan

- [x] Trash tab: select one or more snippets, choose **Restore** → snippets leave the trash and reappear in their original status.
- [x] Trash tab: select one or more snippets, choose **Delete Permanently** → snippets are permanently removed and the trash counts decrement.
- [x] Trash tab single row: **Restore** link restores the snippet.
- [x] Trash tab single row: **Delete Permanently** link removes the snippet (with confirmation dialog).
- [x] Trash tab single row: **Export** link is no longer shown.
- [x] Non-trash tabs: existing bulk actions (Activate / Deactivate / Clone / Export / Download / Trash) still work.

author: burgholzer
body:
## Description

While working on https://github.com/iqm-finland/QDMI-on-IQM/pull/53, I wanted to try and plug an MQT Bench Grover circuit into the DDSIM QDMI device, which screamed at me with an error that turned out to actually be a Qiskit error. 
Qiskit's support for exporting to OpenQASM3 is still lacking when it comes to custom gates; it fails to provide a proper definition of multi-controlled gates such as MCXGate.

However, I found out that one can pass a list of basis gates to the exporter, which it subsequently treats as "builtin" operations which do not necessitate a definition.
This lets us work around the limitations of Qiskit in the sense that the DDSIM device claims to natively support the `mcx` gate and its OpenQASM parser (the one here in MQT Core) natively parses this operation.
As a result, the export works without problems and simulations can be properly conducted.

No AI was used in this pull request.

author: zious11
body:
## Summary

Two small correctness gaps surfaced by Phase 0 brownfield ingestion (`.factory/semport/wirerust/wirerust-pass-8-deep-synthesis.md`, lessons P0.01 + P0.02):

1. **Declare effective MSRV in `Cargo.toml`** — `src/analyzer/http.rs:97` calls `str::floor_char_boundary`, stabilized in Rust 1.91.0. Without `rust-version`, users on 1.85..1.90 hit a confusing stdlib-pointing error. Now cargo emits a clear MSRV-mismatch diagnostic at manifest-load time.

2. **Stop globbing `*.pcapng` in directory expansion** — `resolve_targets` in `main.rs` matched both `*.pcap` and `*.pcapng`, but `PcapReader::new` rejects pcapng with the generic `"Failed to parse pcap header"`. Mixed-format directories now skip pcapng cleanly instead of producing an unhelpful error mid-run.

Earlier analysis had inferred MSRV=1.86 from a release date; clippy's `incompatible_msrv` lint pinned the correct value at 1.91 during local CI gate verification.

## Diff size

`+2 / -1` across two files (`Cargo.toml` and `src/main.rs`).

## Test plan

- [x] `cargo check` — passes
- [x] `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` — passes (was failing before the MSRV bump to 1.91 because of the `incompatible_msrv` lint)
- [x] `cargo fmt --check` — passes
- [x] `cargo test --all-targets` — all suites pass (zero failures across all test files; existing `test_multiple_targets` still parses 3 positional args with mixed `.pcap` / `.pcapng` / dir paths, unaffected by the glob change since that's CLI parsing not expansion)

author: smr2724
body:
Adds a temporary operator kill-switch for the `/api/cron/recover-stuck-brands` Vercel cron (runs every 5 min). When `RECOVER_STUCK_BRANDS_DISABLED=true`, the cron route short-circuits before any DB or Keepa work and returns `{ skipped: true, reason: 'kill_switch' }`.

This is a temporary operator tool to pause the sweeper during **manual recovery**. The cron is fighting a manual one-at-a-time recovery script for 5 stuck brands — parallel sweeper retries are draining the shared Keepa token bucket into negative balance. The kill-switch lets the operator quiesce the sweeper for the duration of the manual run, then unset the env var to resume.

## Behavior
- `RECOVER_STUCK_BRANDS_DISABLED=true` → cron returns 200 with `{ skipped: true, reason: 'kill_switch' }`, no DB queries, no Keepa calls.
- Unset / any other value → cron behaves exactly as before.
- `recoverStuckBrand()` function untouched, so `/api/admin/recover-stuck-brand` and `/api/brands/[id]/enrich` continue to work for manual recovery.

## Safety
- All existing cron route safety belts preserved (runtime, dynamic, fetchCache, revalidate, maxDuration, authorize).
- Phase 84/79/73.2 untouched.
- No renames to legion_score, LegionOpportunity, runScan, legionScore, STEVE_CC, computeLegionEconomics, computeBenchmarkEconomics.
