body:
## Summary

**Stacked on #383** (W2 part 2 → #380 → main). GitHub will auto-retarget as the lower PRs land; review this PR's diff against #383's branch for just the part 3 changes.

Third slice of Plan 89 W2. Modifies `mvm-builder-init` (PID 1 in the libkrun builder VM) to emit a `BuilderResponse::Result` frame over AF_VSOCK port 21471 right before reboot. The host-side receive integration into `LibkrunBuilderVm::run_build` lands in W2 part 4 — separating the two sides keeps each PR's blast radius small.

## What this PR adds

- **New `crates/mvm-builder-init/src/dispatch_response.rs`** — cross-platform `DispatchResponse::to_json()` that hand-rolls the `BuilderResponse::Result` wire JSON. Mirrors the `BootTimings::to_json` pattern (also hand-rolled to avoid pulling serde_json into the 1.5 MiB rootfs budget). Field order matches the serde-derived internally-tagged enum encoding.
- **Single-shot caveats baked in:** `job_id` is the nil UUID (no incoming dispatch to correlate); `job_timings.dispatch_ms` and `teardown_ms` are 0 (only `build_ms` is meaningful — measured as `Instant::now().elapsed()` around `run_job`). W3's persistent dispatch will populate `job_id` from the `BuilderRequest::Run` it correlates against.
- **`linux::send_dispatch_response_via_vsock`** — opens AF_VSOCK, binds + listens on 21471 with SO_RCVTIMEO bounding accept to 10 s, writes a u32-BE-length-prefixed frame matching `mvm_guest::vsock::write_frame`, closes. Best-effort throughout: any failure logs to stderr and the boot continues. AF_VSOCK constants + SockAddrVm + raw FFI mirror the existing pattern in `mvm-builder-agent.rs` — no new crate deps.
- **Hook point** in `linux::run` between `write_result` and `write_boot_timings`.

## Tests added (5 new)

- `dispatch_response_emits_valid_json` — serde_json::Value parse + field-by-field assertions.
- `dispatch_response_escapes_control_chars_in_stderr_tail` — `"`, `\`, `\n`, `\t`, U+0001 all survive round-trip.
- `dispatch_response_handles_empty_stderr_tail` — empty stderr is a clean empty string.
- **`dispatch_response_parses_as_typed_builder_response`** — **the cross-validation test.** Hand-rolled JSON deserializes as `mvm_build::builder_protocol::BuilderResponse`'s typed `Result` variant with every field at the expected value. Adds `mvm-build` as a **dev-dep only** so this test compiles; production rootfs is unaffected.
- `builder_dispatch_port_literal_is_21471` — pins the function-local const against the canonical value.

## What part 4 adds

- Modify `LibkrunBuilderVm::run_build` to spawn a background thread that opens `UnixStream::connect(<vm_state_dir>/vsock-21471.sock)` while the supervisor runs, reads the framed `BuilderResponse` via the W2 part 2 reader, logs the received response.
- Cross-validate vsock vs file exit_code; warn on mismatch.

## Test plan

- [x] `cargo test --workspace --features builder-vm` clean (590+ tests, including 4 new dispatch_response tests).
- [x] `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --features builder-vm -- -D warnings` clean.
- [x] `cargo fmt --all -- --check` clean.
- [x] All xtask lint gates clean.
- [ ] AF_VSOCK FFI only compiles on Linux; CI's `cloud-hypervisor (Linux x86_64)` lane validates the cross-compile. Pattern follows mvm-builder-agent.rs which has been live since Plan 60.

author: wifsimster
body:
## Summary

Introduces five new achievement criteria types that reward both persistence and precision in gameplay, plus cumulative wrong guess tracking. These achievements evaluate the *journey* of solving screenshots—from stubborn persistence through multiple attempts to flawless first-try accuracy.

## Key Changes

**Backend Service Logic** (`achievement.service.ts`)
- Added `checkAttemptsInGame()` – rewards max attempts on any single screenshot within a game
- Added `checkComebackInGame()` – rewards largest streak of wrong guesses on a screenshot the user still solved
- Added `checkFirstTryInGame()` – counts screenshots solved on first attempt (zero wrong guesses)
- Added `checkFlawlessGame()` – rewards completing a challenge with zero wrong guesses across all screenshots
- Added `checkTotalWrongGuesses()` – cumulative all-time wrong guess counter
- Integrated all five new criteria types into the post-game achievement evaluator switch statement
- Added `totalWrongGuesses` to the progress calculation pipeline

**Repository** (`achievement.repository.ts`)
- Added `countWrongGuesses(userId)` – queries total wrong guesses across all game sessions for a user

**Database Migration** (`20260525_attempt_achievements.ts`)
- Inserted 7 new achievements with idempotent logic (safe for re-runs in seeded environments):
  - `acharne` (Relentless) – 10+ attempts on one screenshot
  - `tete_de_mule` (Stubborn) – 20+ attempts on one screenshot
  - `jamais_abandonner` (Never Give Up) – 8+ wrong guesses before solving
  - `du_premier_coup` (Bullseye) – 1 first-try solve
  - `sans_hesitation` (No Hesitation) – flawless game (0 wrong, all correct)
  - `tatonneur` (Trial and Error) – 100 total wrong guesses
  - `increvable` (Unstoppable) – 1,000 total wrong guesses

**Localization** (`translation.json` – en & fr)
- Added English and French names/descriptions for all 7 new achievements

## Implementation Details

- All per-game criteria (`attempts_in_game`, `comeback_in_game`, `first_try_in_game`, `flawless_game`) operate on `GameCompletionData.guesses`, which is keyed by `screenshotId` to prevent attempt bleeding across tiers
- `total_wrong_guesses` is evaluated separately as a cumulative aggregate, not per-game
- Achievement awarding includes the actual metric value and criteria threshold for progress tracking
- Migration uses idempotent insert pattern (checks existing keys before inserting) to support safe re-runs in test environments

author: divuna
body:
## Summary

- **Root cause**: saving N MioCoin bonuses called `admin_manage_bonus_prize` once per row in a sequential `for...of` loop. At ~430 ms/call, 95 000 positions = ~11.5 hours; loop was killed mid-way by a network error, leaving partial rows. Production `bonus_prizes` also had no admin DELETE policy, so the client-side delete before re-saves silently deleted nothing (RLS deny-by-default), causing stale rows from failed attempts to accumulate and trigger position-conflict errors on subsequent saves.
- **Fix**: new `admin_bulk_insert_miocoin_bonuses` SECURITY DEFINER RPC replaces the loop (N HTTP calls → 1 HTTP call). The RPC handles delete + insert atomically inside Postgres.
- **Migration also adds** the idempotent `"Allow admin full access to bonus prizes"` RLS policy that was applied manually on staging but was never applied to production.

## Files changed

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `supabase/migrations/20260519_bulk_miocoin_bonuses.sql` | New RPC + idempotent RLS policy |
| `src/components/AdminContestManagement.tsx` | Replace loop (−35 lines) with single RPC call (+22 lines) |

## RPC behaviour (`admin_bulk_insert_miocoin_bonuses`)

1. Admin/superadmin role check (same pattern as all existing admin RPCs)
2. Validate `p_contest_id` not null; `p_bonuses` is a JSON array
3. Per-item: `ticket_position` integer, `amount` numeric > 0
4. No duplicate positions within payload
5. No collision with existing physical prizes for this contest
6. DELETE existing MioCoin rows (`amount > 0`) for contest
7. Bulk INSERT all new rows in one statement — description = `'{amount} MioCoinů'`, status = `'pending'`
8. Log one `admin_actions` entry (`miocoin_bulk_create`) with count + total
9. Return `{ success: true, inserted_count: N, total_amount: SUM }`; EXCEPTION → `{ success: false, message: ... }`

## Not changed

- `buy_ticket_atomic`, tickets, winners, wallets, payments, Partner Offers
- Public `ContestDetail.tsx`
- Physical prize save path (per-row `admin_manage_bonus_prize` loop unchanged)
- Physical client-side delete at line 1686 (now works correctly once the RLS policy migration lands)

## Test plan

- [ ] Apply migration on staging: `supabase/migrations/20260519_bulk_miocoin_bonuses.sql`
- [ ] Create test contest, set 95 000 MioCoin (total) + value 1, generate, save → verify `bonus_prizes` has 95 000 rows
- [ ] Re-save same contest → verify old rows deleted, 95 000 fresh rows inserted
- [ ] Run staging Full E2E (`workflow_dispatch`) — spec 18, spec 19 must pass

author: copilot
body:
This reshapes the repo from a single-file prototype into a production-oriented browser game scaffold: pure modern JavaScript, GitHub Pages-compatible output, deterministic simulation, mobile controller flows, ADRs, and CI/CD quality gates. It also establishes an LLM-friendly development loop with a devcontainer and browser-first automation.

- **Architecture and app structure**
  - Replaced the monolithic `index.html` implementation with a multi-entry Vite app:
    - host app at `/`
    - controller app at `/controller/`
  - Split responsibilities across `src/host`, `src/controller`, `src/game`, `src/network`, and `src/shared`.
  - Kept the runtime static so the built site remains deployable on GitHub Pages.

- **Game foundation**
  - Extracted simulation state from rendering.
  - Added seeded terrain generation and named fixtures for repeatable scenarios.
  - Preserved the core arena feel while moving rendering into a dedicated module with a more polished retro presentation.

- **Host/controller flow**
  - Added a desktop host experience with:
    - stable session GUID
    - shareable controller URL
    - QR code
    - roster and round telemetry
  - Added a touch-first mobile controller UI with slot assignment, reconnect-friendly join flow, and sanitized player identity handling.

- **Networking model**
  - Introduced a transport abstraction with:
    - `BroadcastChannel` for fast local iteration and same-origin controller testing
    - optional relay/WebSocket transport for remote play via `VITE_SIGNALING_URL`
  - Encoded host/controller communication through a versioned shared protocol.

- **LLM/dev ergonomics**
  - Added a devcontainer based on the Playwright image with browser tooling preinstalled.
  - Standardized a minimal local workflow around hot reload, deterministic URLs, and browser-visible fixtures.

- **Browser-first quality model**
  - Added Playwright coverage for:
    - host boot
    - controller join/assignment
    - user-visible controller interaction
    - visual baseline on the host join panel
  - Structured the app so browser automation targets actual user flows rather than only isolated logic.

- **Security and deployment**
  - Added CSP to both entry points.
  - Validated and normalized session IDs, controller names, and input payloads before use.
  - Replaced the single deploy workflow with CI/CD that builds, audits, runs browser automation, stores artifacts, and deploys Pages only from green `main`.

- **Documentation and ADRs**
  - Added repository-level guidance in `README.md`.
  - Added ADRs covering:
    - static architecture
    - devcontainer/tooling
    - Pages-compatible build choice
    - host/controller split
    - signaling model
    - transport abstraction
    - Web Bluetooth rejection
    - deterministic simulation
    - browser-first testing
    - retro visual direction
    - CI/CD gates
    - security model

Example of the new static multi-entry setup:

```js
export default defineConfig(({ command }) => ({
  base: process.env.VITE_BASE_PATH || (command === 'build' && process.env.GITHUB_ACTIONS ? '/Molez-tribute/' : '/'),
  build: {
    rollupOptions: {
      input: {
        host: resolve(process.cwd(), 'index.html'),
        controller: resolve(process.cwd(), 'controller/index.html'),
      },
    },
  },
}));
```

author: aminss99
body:
💡 **What:** 
Updated `_fetch_hackernews_sync_impl` to utilize `concurrent.futures.ThreadPoolExecutor` for fetching HackerNews API items instead of executing the HTTP requests sequentially in a loop.

🎯 **Why:** 
The HackerNews sync implementation loops through up to 100 top story IDs to fetch individual items via an HTTP call to Firebase. Firing these consecutively blocked the thread per request, slowing it down. ThreadPoolExecutor allows firing batches concurrently over the same HTTP client, taking maximum advantage of pooled I/O capacity and dramatically improving response time. 

📊 **Measured Improvement:**
Measured execution time for 30 items locally:
- **Baseline:** ~0.49 - ~0.74 seconds (on average)
- **Optimized:** ~0.29 - ~0.41 seconds (on average)

Speed improved by around 40-50% for standard payloads (e.g. 30 requests). Note that execution time can fluctuate depending on HTTP caching and Firebase API roundtrip time, but concurrency guarantees a substantial wall-clock speedup for cold API hits.

author: aaronontheweb
body:
## Summary

Deterministic fixes for three intermittently-failing tests. No timeout widening — each racy wait is replaced with a real synchronization signal.

Closes #1109. Closes #1034.

### `LlmSessionIntegrationTests.Delivery_feedback_during_passivation_aborts_shutdown_and_retries_latest_turn` (#1109, macOS)

The test polled `_fakeChatClient.ReceivedMessages` — a non-thread-safe `List<T>` written off-thread at LLM-call start — behind a 3s `AwaitAssertAsync` budget, observing a *side effect* of the retry rather than a completion signal. Under macOS CI load the second call wasn't recorded within 3s.

The passivation-abort → retry production path is correct (single-sender mailbox ordering + the `Passivating()` `Command<DeliveryFailed>` handler). Fix is test-only: a fresh probe is now subscribed *while the actor is `Passivating`* — `JoinSession` is handled there without aborting passivation — so it deterministically observes the retried turn's `TextOutput`/`TurnCompleted` via `ExpectMsg`. The delivery-feedback assertion runs once the session is quiescent.

### `SessionLogActorTests.Successive_dispatchers_append_to_same_canonical_file` (#1034, Windows)

The test read the log via `File.ReadAllTextAsync`, which opens with `FileShare.Read`. On Windows that mask denies the actor's concurrent `FileAccess.Write` append open; `SessionLogFile.AppendLine`'s bounded retry budget (4×/70ms) can then be exhausted, and `SessionLogActor.OnOutput` catches the failure and **drops the audit line** — leaving the polling assertion permanently unsatisfiable. POSIX doesn't enforce share modes, hence Windows-only.

Fix is test-only: log reads now use the writer's `FileShare.ReadWrite | FileShare.Delete` mask, so reader and writer coexist and no line is dropped.

### `ConfigWatcherServiceTests.AtomicReplace_TriggersReload` / `InPlaceWrite_TriggersReload` (#1034, Windows)

These exercised a real `FileSystemWatcher` plus a `Task.Delay` poll loop. Real watcher event delivery — particularly the latency and event classification of an overwriting `File.Move` on Windows — is OS-dependent and cannot be observed deterministically.

The tests now drive the event handlers directly with synthesized `RenamedEventArgs`/`FileSystemEventArgs` and virtualize the debounce through a `FakeTimeProvider`, awaiting the new `ConfigWatcherService.PendingReload`. Fully deterministic, instant, no OS dependency, no `Task.Delay` poll loop.

`ConfigWatcherService.ScheduleReload` was also **genuinely racy**: it mutated the debounce `CancellationTokenSource` from concurrent `FileSystemWatcher` callback threads without synchronization (read-after-write on `_debounceCts`), which could double-fire a reload. It is now lock-guarded, exposes the in-flight reload `Task`, and debounces on the injected `TimeProvider`.

## Out of scope

The `OnFileDeleted` handler does not schedule a reload. If a Windows atomic-replace ever surfaces as a bare `Deleted` event (rather than `Renamed`/`Changed`), an atomic config edit could be missed. Changing that handler is a speculative product-behavior change beyond a flaky-test fix and was deliberately left for separate investigation.

## Test plan

- [x] `dotnet build` — Daemon.Tests and Actors.Tests, 0 warnings
- [x] `ConfigWatcherServiceTests` (15 tests) — 15 consecutive runs, all green; suite now runs in ~100ms
- [x] `SessionLogActorTests` + `Delivery_feedback_during_passivation...` (5 tests) — 10 consecutive runs, all green
- [x] `dotnet slopwatch analyze` — 0 issues
- [x] `Add-FileHeaders.ps1 -Verify` — all headers present
- [ ] CI on Windows + macOS runners

author: cuboye
body:
/claim #6775

## Problem
Canvas snapshotting via `createImageBitmap` blocks for 20ms+ on Safari (all versions including 16.x, 17.x, iOS) versus 0-0.3ms on Chrome. This causes frame drops on every snapshot for sessions recorded on Safari.

Bug report: https://github.com/highlight/highlight/issues/6775

## Fix
Use `ImageCapture.grabFrame()` instead of `createImageBitmap` for manual canvas snapshots in Safari. `grabFrame()` captures a video frame from the canvas without blocking — it's the non-blocking alternative to `createImageBitmap(canvas)` in Safari.

Implementation in `sdk/highlight-run/src/client/index.tsx`:
- Check if `ImageCapture` API is available
- Use `canvas.captureStream().getVideoTracks()[0]` to get a `MediaStreamTrack`
- Call `grabFrame()` to get a fast `ImageBitmap` 
- Draw it back onto the canvas with `ctx.drawImage()`
- Falls back to `record.snapshotCanvas(element)` if ImageCapture unavailable

## Why this works
- `createImageBitmap(canvas)` in Safari is synchronous and blocks the main thread
- `ImageCapture.grabFrame()` is truly async — Safari doesn't block on it
- The fix is targeted: only affects `H._highlightObj.snapshot()` manual snapshot path
- No changes to rrweb or the canvas worker

## Test
A minimal test is in the issue's codesandbox: https://codesandbox.io/s/dazzling-roentgen-jqgtld — the `Snapshot` stat should go from ~20ms to <1ms in Safari after this fix.

author: jefffroman
body:
Stands up the project's first automated test suite. Closes #15.

## One flag, three tiers

| Command | Tiers run | Real AWS? | Cost |
|---|---|---|---|
| `pytest` | `tests/unit` + `tests/moto` | no (moto in-process) | none, offline, CI-able |
| `pytest --aws` | + `tests/aws` | yes (read-only us-east-1) | ~none; needs creds |

`@pytest.mark.aws` tests are skipped unless `--aws`, and skip *cleanly* (not
fail) when no credentials are present.

## Coverage — 156 tests

- **unit (103):** `config` env parsing/prefix-strip, `transcript` store +
  estimator, `tools` path-scoping (incl. symlink-escape + prefix-sibling) +
  workspace-budget + async file tools, `channel` chunking/allowlist,
  `compaction` tool-pair-safe split / threshold / idle+mid-session recap /
  hard-reset, `wake_greet`/`memory_flush` helpers, `MemoryIndex` BM25 / graph
  / int8 store / incremental-SHA-reindex / cross-instance persistence (fake
  embedder — no onnxruntime), `bedrock` stream accumulator.
- **moto (49):** lifecycle Lambda registry state machine
  (provision/idempotency/transition/tombstone/name-reuse/agents view),
  lifecycle-pending grab/release/`_IntentChanged`, SSM `/active` join,
  Fargate helpers (degraded ECS-Exec + fail-open image-stale), S3
  versioned-prefix purge, SNS alert (verified via an SNS→SQS subscription),
  `wake_listener` (queue/active/SFN, already-waking append, allowlist reject,
  auth), `LifecycleController` pause→self-stop / wake-raced resume / archive
  →Remove callback, `wake_greet` claim-replay-delete + stale reclaim.
- **aws (3):** STS+region resolve, registry table key schema + GSIs,
  lifecycle/wake tables present. Read-only; graceful skips if infra absent.

## Wiring notes

- `pyproject.toml` is the only pytest config (no Python packaging otherwise):
  `pythonpath` for the `app` package + flat `lambda/` modules,
  `--import-mode=importlib`, strict markers, `asyncio_mode=auto`.
- moto conftest reloads `handler`/`wake_listener` **inside** the active mock
  so their import-time boto3 clients bind to moto; resource shapes mirror
  `tofu/lambda.tf`; dummy creds are forced **per-test** so a combined `--aws`
  run can't leak them into the real layer.
- `requirements-dev.txt` is dev/CI-only — never baked into any image.

## Not covered (by nature)

ECS-Exec signal delivery and the full SFN→Lambda→tofu lifecycle aren't
moto-modelable; they stay validated manually on live AWS (2026.5.19). moto
covers the boto3-call shape + registry state-machine correctness. See
`docs/testing.md`.

Verified locally: `152 passed, 3 skipped` (default) — the 3 skips are the
AWS tier; selected under `--aws`.

author: bolinfest
body:
## Why

The package builder should be easy to run during local iteration. Requiring callers to provide both a target triple and an output directory every time makes the common host-package case more awkward than necessary.

This PR keeps explicit overrides available, but makes the default invocation useful: build for the current host release target and place the package in a fresh temporary directory. Because a temp output path is otherwise easy to lose, the builder continues to print the final package directory path when it completes.

## What changed

- Makes `--target` optional and maps the host OS/architecture to supported Codex package release targets.
- Defaults Linux hosts to musl target triples so local defaults match Codex release artifacts; GNU Linux targets remain available when passed explicitly.
- Makes `--package-dir` optional and creates a new `codex-package-*` temp directory when omitted.
- Documents the new defaults in `scripts/codex_package/README.md`.

## Verification

- Compiled `scripts/build_codex_package.py` and `scripts/codex_package/*.py` with `PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1`.
- Ran `scripts/build_codex_package.py --help` from outside the repo.
- Verified Linux host detection maps `x86_64` and `aarch64` to musl target triples.
- Ran a fake-Cargo package build while omitting both `--target` and `--package-dir`; verified the generated metadata target, expected package files, and printed temp package path.

author: jumplink
body:
## Summary

New showcase at \`showcases/dom/minimalist-browser/\` that stress-tests \`@gjsify/iframe\` against a non-trivial cross-platform application: URL bar + Back / Forward / Reload + iframe content area + built-in srcdoc page library + postMessage round-trip status line.

The same shared core (\`src/browser-demo.ts\`, ~300 LoC) drives both variants:

- **Browser variant** (Web): real \`<iframe>\` element + DOM-based UI shell
- **GJS variant**: \`IFrameBridge\` over \`WebKit.WebView\` + Adw widgets

Cross-variant by construction — \`BrowserCore\` operates on an \`IFrameHandle\` duck-type that both a real \`<iframe>\` and \`IFrameBridge.iframeElement\` satisfy (because \`IFrameBridge.iframeElement\` IS an \`HTMLIFrameElement\`). Application-side history stack keeps the back/forward path identical in both targets (browsers won't allow cross-origin \`iframe.contentWindow.history.go(-1)\` anyway).

## postMessage round-trip

Each built-in page carries an inline \`<script>\` that calls \`window.parent.postMessage({type:'page-loaded', title, url}, '*')\` on \`DOMContentLoaded\`. The parent listens via \`iframe.contentWindow.addEventListener('message', …)\` and surfaces the announcement in a status line. Same code path in both variants — WebKit's script-message-handler bridge makes the GJS variant indistinguishable from a real browser's parent listener.

## Built-in pages

\`page:welcome\`, \`page:about\`, \`page:postmessage\`, \`page:adwaita\`. URL bar also accepts real \`https://\` URLs (GJS variant: loaded via WebKit).

## IFrameBridge enhancement (same PR — feature-completeness pass)

While auditing for showcase parity, surfaced one ergonomic gap and filled it:

- **\`.goBack()\` / \`.goForward()\`** — thin camelCase wrappers around WebKit.WebView's \`go_back()\` / \`go_forward()\` (GIR-generated names are snake_case)
- **\`.canGoBack\` / \`.canGoForward\`** getters around \`can_go_back()\` / \`can_go_forward()\`
- **\`.reload()\`** is inherited verbatim from \`WebKit.WebView\` (no rewrap needed — already camelCase)
- ~40 LoC including JSDoc; documents the parity caveat (these reflect WebKit's internal history list, NOT the application-side stack — apps that want cross-variant parity track URLs themselves, as the showcase does)

## Updates

- \`packages/infra/cli/showcases.json\` gained the new entry under \`dom\`
- STATUS.md: Showcase count **6 → 7** (or **7 → 8** depending on PR-B/D merge order — rebase will adjust)
- AGENTS.md iframe row lists the new navigation surface

author: vusys
body:
## Summary

Adds a fork-based harness for concurrency tests in this repo. The existing single-process tests can pin that the package's SQL contains a `FOR UPDATE` clause, but PHP serialises its own statements on one connection so the actual lock-acquisition behaviour is never exercised. This PR exercises it end-to-end against real DB drivers.

- **`ConcurrencyHarness` trait** — wraps `pcntl_fork`, purges inherited PDO sockets in the child, and reports per-worker exit codes. Skip path covers SQLite (no row locking, in-memory DB doesn't cross `fork()`) and SAPIs without `pcntl`.

- **`MakeRootConcurrencyTest`** — 8 workers × 3 `saveAsRoot()` calls each into the same scope; verifies unique `(lft, rgt)` and tree integrity. Without the `FOR UPDATE` lock landed in v0.10.0, two workers reading the same max-rgt would double-book the next slot. Scoped variant pins that the lock includes the scope predicate (two menus, alternating workers, each scope's `lft` stays unique).

- **`AggregateLockingConcurrencyTest`** — Drives the lost-holder MAX recompute path (lower a child below the current max) with 4 concurrent workers; verifies post-state matches freshly-computed values under `aggregate_locking='auto'` and `'always'`. Includes SUM/COUNT pinning for the delta path.

  Workers retry on SQLSTATE `40001` (deadlock victim) and `40P01` (PostgreSQL deadlock detected). The retry is part of the contract: row-level locks under contended ancestor updates produce lock cycles, MySQL InnoDB / PostgreSQL abort one transaction to break them, and real callers handle it — these workers do too. The package's auto-transaction currently passes `attempts=1`; that's a separate footgun worth noting but not the subject of this PR.

## Test plan

- [x] `composer analyse` — PHPStan level 9 clean, no ignores added
- [x] `composer pint:check` / `composer rector:check` clean
- [x] `composer test` (sqlite) — 890 tests; the 4 new tests skip cleanly with a clear message
- [x] `DB_CONNECTION=mysql … vendor/bin/phpunit tests/Feature/Concurrency/` — all 4 pass, 51 assertions, exercises the lock end-to-end with real fork() workers
- [ ] CI matrix on push — mysql / mariadb / pgsql cells should exercise the lock paths; sqlite cells should skip

## Description

In the web dashboard, the session-delete confirmation popup is launched from the workspace sidebar right-click menu, so the user's hand is already on the mouse and they have to drag it across to click Delete. Pressing Enter now confirms the delete without that mouse travel.

Two layered affordances:

1. The dialog focuses its Delete button on mount, so native button-Enter activates it.
2. A document-level Enter handler also confirms when focus has moved onto a checkbox row (e.g., the user toggled "Delete branch" and never tabbed back). The handler is a no-op when focus is on the Cancel button or a native input, so those keep their usual semantics, and it's gated on the in-flight `deleting` flag so Enter cannot double-fire.

Escape continues to cancel.

## High-Level Summary

Improves keyboard accessibility for the session delete confirmation dialog. The Delete (confirm) button is focused when the dialog opens so pressing Enter confirms the deletion, and Escape still cancels. A document-level Enter handler also confirms when focus is on non-input dialog elements (e.g., after toggling a checkbox), but it preserves native semantics for inputs/buttons and is disabled while a delete is in progress to prevent double-submission. Focus is restored to the trigger element on close and the dialog gains proper aria-labelledby for screen readers.

## What changed

- Modified component: web/src/components/DeleteSessionDialog.tsx
  - Focuses the Delete button on mount and restores prior focus on unmount.
  - Adds aria-labelledby linking the dialog title for improved screen-reader announcement.
  - Replaces prior Escape-only listener with a document-level keydown handler that:
    - Confirms on Enter when the event target is not INPUT, TEXTAREA, or BUTTON.
    - Skips handling when Cancel is focused or when native button behavior should apply.
    - Cancels on Escape.
    - Guards against double-confirmation via an in-flight `deleting` flag.
- Tests added/updated: web/src/components/__tests__/DeleteSessionDialog.test.tsx
  - Covers focus behavior, Enter/Escape handling, in-flight protection, ARIA labeling, and focus restoration.
- Test surface added: web/tests/coverage-matrix.json
  - Registers the new keyboard-affordance test surface.

## Benefits

- Enables confirming deletion with Enter after invoking the dialog from a context menu (reduces mouse travel).
- Preserves expected behavior for inputs/buttons and prevents accidental double-deletes.
- Accessibility improvements for screen readers and keyboard users.
- Changes are covered by tests to reduce regressions.

## Technical details (concise)

- Uses a ref (confirmButtonRef) to focus the Delete button and stores document.activeElement to restore focus on unmount.
- Installs a document-level keydown handler that inspects e.key and event.target.tagName to decide behavior; ignores INPUT, TEXTAREA, and BUTTON.
- The Enter flow calls onConfirm with current options; a local `deleting` flag prevents re-entry until the confirm promise resolves.
- Tests simulate keydown/click interactions and assert single-confirm semantics, cancel semantics, ARIA attributes, and focus restoration.

author: pcarleton
body:
## What

SEP-2243's conformance check IDs drifted from its requirement-traceability yaml in #259: the scenario code emits one check ID per *test case*, while `src/seps/sep-2243.yaml` declares one per *normative requirement*. The two naming schemes diverged, so the declared `check:` slugs no longer match any emitted ID.

This renames the emitted IDs so a **check ID maps to a single MUST/SHOULD**, emitted once per case (the per-case detail moves into `name`/`description`). That matches the repo's existing "same id, flip status/message" convention.

| before (per-case) | after (per-requirement) |
|---|---|
| `mcp-method-header-*`, `mcp-name-header-*` | `client-includes-standard-headers` |
| `reject-invalid-tool-*`, `keep-valid-tool` | `client-reject-invalid-tool` |
| `server-accepts-{lower,upper}case-header-name` | `header-name-case-insensitive` |
| reject status checks (mismatch/missing/case × method/name) | `server-reject-invalid-headers` |
| their `-error-code` variants | `server-reject-error-code` |

In the yaml, `server-reject-mismatch` + `server-reject-status` merge into one `server-reject-invalid-headers` MUST ("reject a header-validation failure with HTTP 400"); `server-reject-error-code` stays as the SHOULD.

## Out of scope (intentionally unchanged)
- Base64 / custom-header server rejection checks keep their own param-validation IDs.
- Scenario gates and the whitespace-acceptance check keep their scenario-matching names.

## Why
A follow-up traceability tool maps declared requirements to emitted check IDs by exact match; this realignment lets that work without per-ID override hacks. No behavior change — only check IDs, descriptions, and the yaml row merge.

## Test plan
`npm run typecheck`, `npm run lint`, `npm test` all pass (126 tests). The negative tests run the renamed scenarios against broken impls and assert the collapsed IDs emit FAILURE.

body:
## Summary

A full data-driven loop on the two-tier dogfood harness: **measure → root-cause → fix → re-measure → document**, driven by the live reliability battery (local junior `qwen2.5-coder:14b`, 0 frontier tokens by construction).

Controlled before/after (fixed target commit, only the agent binary varied; the junior is deterministic per binary+commit so deltas are causal):

| class | before | after | mean secs |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| scaffold | 100% | 100% | 8s |
| rename | **0%** | **100%** | 9s |
| movefunc | **0%** | **100%** | 6s |
| analysis | 100% | 100% | 8s |
| infeasible | punt | punt *(correct)* | 3s |
| **overall** | **40%** | **80%** | 7s |

Every *solvable* class now succeeds 100%; the only remaining punt is `infeasible`, which is the correct outcome.

## Changes (each fix traced to a `-verbose` agent trace, not guessed)

**gorefactor-agent**
- Expose `move_function` + `report` in `toolCatalog()` — they were wired in `dispatch_tool.go`/`apply_op.go` but invisible to the model (root cause of the original move/analysis punts).
- Explicit `function/method/type` param descriptions + a "name the symbol, never guess its file" prompt rule.
- **Deterministic `resolveSymbolFile()`**: the tool resolves a symbol's real file itself instead of relying on an LLM retry — the junior only has to name the symbol.
- Op-aware result messages ("moved X from A to B") so a successful move isn't false-punted (and rolled back).
- `agent_tools.go` split (`toolCatalog` → `agent_tools_catalog.go`) to stay under the 300-line limit.

**gorefactor / repo (sensor finding)**
- Fixed a real `.gitignore` defect the battery surfaced: the unanchored `gorefactor` pattern matched the `cmd/gorefactor/` **source dir**, silently gitignoring every new file there (invisible to `git status`, unstaged by `git add .`, immune to `git clean`). Anchored to `/gorefactor`. This affects normal development, not just benchmarking.

**Benchmark harness**
- Added `movefunc` + `analysis` task classes; **wall-clock `mean secs`** column; `.gorefactor` cross-run hygiene (a benchmark-validity bug).

**Docs**
- `RELIABILITY.md` (official table), `benchmark/FINDINGS.md` (root-cause chain + gap status), `CLAUDE.md` (agent-gate section).

## Verification
- `gorefactor doctor` green (lint/build/test) at HEAD.
- Static benchmark still passes.
- Official live battery: 15 runs, 80% success, 0 frontier tokens, ~7s/run.

author: davidkoleczek
body:
## What

In `context/workflow/harness-automation.md`:

**Expand `## What to capture per run`** into two subsections (`### Minimum artifacts`, `### Fields in meta.json`) and prescribe seven fields per run. Each field is framed both generically (so the guidance covers non-Amplifier evaluations — CLI tools, hosted services, scripts) and in its Amplifier-specific form:

- `scenario_description` — one-line plain-English description of what the run tests
- `prompt` — verbatim input handed to the system under test, byte-for-byte
- `judge_rubric` — scoring criteria inlined (not just a path), so verdicts stay interpretable when the rubric evolves
- `failure: {stage, message, traceback, exit_code}` — structured, so errors don't survive only as buried text in stdout
- `cost_usd` + `tokens` — structured cost data, not stdout-grep
- Profile / config snapshot — the file content (or sha256 + copy), not just a path
- Dependency inventory — every version of every component active during the run

The existing minimum (wall time, exit code, DTU/instance id, profile path, repo SHAs, pointers to session files) is preserved as a closing bullet.

**Remove `## Visual report` section** entirely, plus the `metrics/render_html.py` script reference and the `verdict.html` artifact line in the Directory layout. The HTML-report responsibility moved to the stories bundle via the new `stories:evaluation-visualizer` agent ([microsoft/amplifier-bundle-stories#10](https://github.com/microsoft/amplifier-bundle-stories/pull/10)). Splitting capture (here) from rendering (there) keeps each bundle focused on one concern. The markdown summary (`summarize_run.py` → `verdict-{outcome}.md`) is preserved — that's a separate concern.

## Why

The original section captured solid raw evidence (stdout, events.jsonl, transcript.jsonl, meta.json) but left several fields downstream consumers actually need silent:

- Human-readable scenario description (today `meta.json.example` is a directory slug only)
- The verbatim prompt (listed as required in the spec but example scripts omitted)
- Judge/grader rubric content inline (paths break when the rubric evolves)
- Structured failure context (today errors land buried in stdout)
- Cost as structured fields (today parsed from stdout text)
- Profile snapshot, not just a path
- Dependency inventory (full bundle/module set, not just one SHA)

Closing those gaps in the prescribed shape, written ecosystem-agnostically.

## Scope

Single file: `context/workflow/harness-automation.md` (158 → 135 lines net, +18 / -43).

No example scripts or templates are modified — those will follow as separate changes if/when individual examples are updated to emit the new fields.

body:
## Why

The PR #241 backfill hit one row (\`dbb47d36-d3d2-4755-88f7-7a04f6cb002e\`) that wouldn't translate: a Microsoft 365 NDR with a 42 KB HTML body wrapping a single delivery-failure line. Sending that to Claude busts the output-token budget and returns truncated JSON — \`JSON.parse\` then throws \`Unterminated string in JSON at position …\` and the row stays \`detected_language IS NULL\` forever.

## Fix

Cap the input body at 15 KB in both \`src/lib/inbox/translate-inbound.ts\` and \`scripts/backfill-inbox-translations.mjs\` before sending to the model. Real human replies are well under that ceiling; the bodies that exceed it are virtually always Office365 NDR boilerplate where the actual content is already English, so losing the trailing wrapper is unobservable.

## Verification

After this fix, re-running the backfill processed the one remaining row cleanly. Inbox is now 100 % covered:

| lv   | 5     |

body:
## Summary

New "Quick plan" plan type — a plan tied to a date with no specific time. Plus the requested current-day column highlight on the activity tracker.

## Behaviour

### Quick plan toggle (Plan Activity modal)
- New checkbox "Quick plan (date only, no specific time)" above the time inputs.
- When on, the time + end-time fields hide entirely. Start-time validation is bypassed.
- On save, the activity's timestamp is set to `23:59` of the chosen date (so the plan stays "in the future" for Upcoming Plans until the day fully passes), `is_quick_plan: true` is persisted, and `duration_minutes` is forced null.
- When editing an existing quick plan, the toggle starts on and the time fields stay hidden.

### Activity Tracker weekly grid
- New overlay layer renders quick plans as pills, one stack per day column:
  - **Today's column**: anchored to `nowTop + 4px`, so the pills sit just under the current-time bar and ride down as the day progresses.
  - **Other days' columns**: anchored to `HEADER_H + 4px`, so the day-of-week header is the only thing above them.
- Whole layer is `pointer-events: none` (pills opt back in), so it never blocks taps on cells or obscures activity labels underneath.
- Pills are clickable — they jump to the date highlighted, so the user can mark them done/skip/reschedule via the same lifecycle popover.
- New "Quick plans" eye-toggle in the toolbar (next to Emotions / Alters) hides the whole overlay. Default on, preference persisted to `localStorage`.

### Today-column highlight
- Vertical 5% primary-tint strip spans `HEADER_H` → bottom under today's column. Pointer-events none, z-index 1.

### Helpers
- `activityHelpers.getActivitiesForSlot` skips any activity with `is_quick_plan: true` so the 23:59 sentinel doesn't surface in the 23:30 cell.

### What works without changes
- Quick plans appear in **Upcoming Plans** via the existing `timestamp > now` filter (thanks to the 23:59 sentinel).
- Quick plans use the existing **lifecycle popover** for done / partial / skipped / cancelled / reschedule.

## Release checklist

- `APP_VERSION` 0.18.2 → **0.19.0** (minor — user-visible feature block)
- `versionCode` 170 → 171, `versionName` "0.19.0"
- Changelog entries under May 19, 2026

author: coltenouo
body:
The execution API had two routes (`ti_run`, `ti_update_state`) wrapping their `session.execute` calls in `try/except SQLAlchemyError` and converting to `HTTPException(500, "Database error occurred")`. The TODO in `routes/task_instances.py` flagged this for replacement with FastAPI's [custom exception handlers](https://fastapi.tiangolo.com/tutorial/handling-errors/#install-custom-exception-handlers).

This adds `@app.exception_handler(SQLAlchemyError)` alongside the existing catch-all in `execution_api/app.py`. The new handler logs the request path/method and returns `{"detail": "Database error occurred"}` with status 500 — the same shape the routes produced before. The per-route `try/except` blocks are removed and bodies dedented (which accounts for most of the line churn).

### Scope note

The TODO was only on `ti_update_state` (around the call to `session.execute(query)` that writes the new state + audit `Log`). However, `ti_run` had the **same** `try/except SQLAlchemyError` boilerplate without a TODO, doing literally the same translation. Once the global handler exists, both local catches become redundant, so this PR removes both for consistency rather than leaving the codebase in a half-migrated state.

If reviewers prefer a strict TODO-only scope, I'm happy to revert the `ti_run` change and open a separate cleanup PR for it.

## Summary

- Adds the `ChapterTextProviding` boundary protocol — the format-agnostic chapter-text source for feature #56 bilingual reading (plan Decision 2.6).
- Adds 4 concrete `Sendable` adapters: `EPUBChapterTextProvider`, `TXTChapterTextProvider`, `MDChapterTextProvider`, `PDFChapterTextProvider`.

## What Changed

- `vreader/Services/Reader/ChapterTextProviding.swift` — `Sendable` protocol with `translationUnits()`, `sourceText(for:)`, `unit(containing:)`, `unit(after:)`. The last two are the `Locator → unit` resolution the bilingual prefetch trigger needs (Gate-2 round-2 N6).
- `EPUBChapterTextProvider` — units = spine documents (plan Decision 2.7, not TOC entries); HTML-stripped off-main via `EPUBTextExtractor.stripHTML`.
- `TXTChapterTextProvider` — units = `TXTChapterIndex` chapters; UTF-16 slicing matching `TXTChapterContentLoader`.
- `MDChapterTextProvider` — units = `MDHeading`-bounded chapters; a non-empty pre-heading preamble is unit 0.
- `PDFChapterTextProvider` — units = zero-indexed page ranges via PDFKit; configurable `pagesPerUnit`.
- `unit(containing:)` boundary contract across all adapters: `nil` offset → unit 0; a locator predating the book's first unit (empty book / negative offset / unknown EPUB href) → `nil`; a position past the last unit clamps to the last unit.

## Summary

Adds the missing fake contract test for `WorkspacePort` (ADR-0047).

Closes bead `advisor-1mpg` (dark-factory gap).

## What this verifies

The test asserts schema-based parity between `FakeWorkspace` and the
`WorkspacePort` Protocol (24 tests, ~0.5s):

1. `FakeWorkspace` satisfies the `@runtime_checkable` `WorkspacePort` Protocol.
2. Every Port method on `FakeWorkspace` is async with a matching signature.
3. Return-type parity for all 9 Port methods (`create`, `destroy`,
   `destroy_all`, `merge_main`, `get_conflicting_files`, `reset_to_main`,
   `post_work_cleanup`, `abort_merge`, `start_merge_main`).
4. Fault injection (`fail_next_create`) raises `PermissionError`,
   `OSError(28, ...)` (disk full), and `RuntimeError` (branch conflict),
   single-shot.
5. Stateful tracking (`created` / `destroyed` lists) accumulates correctly.
6. `create()` path is rooted under `base_path`.

## Why no cassette

The cassette/replay pattern (ADR-0047 §Part 1) targets CLI-based adapters
(github, git, docker). `FakeWorkspace` wraps in-process Python objects —
there is no CLI, no subprocess, no external service output to snapshot.
This is consistent with `FakeHoneycomb` (PR #9004), which followed the
same schema-based approach for the same reason. `workspace` is correctly
absent from both `KNOWN_ADAPTERS` (`src/contracts/_schema.py`) and

author: bdraco
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! -->

## What do these changes do?

Make the ``deploy`` job in ``ci-cd.yml`` re-runnable after a partial
release failure.

- The ``Make Release`` step is now gated on a preceding ``gh release
  view`` check, so it is skipped when the GitHub Release for the tag
  already exists (instead of failing with ``HTTP 422 already_exists``).
- The PyPI publish step is invoked with ``skip-existing: true`` so a
  retry does not fail on dists that were already uploaded.

The existence check matches only the literal ``release not found``
reply for the not-exists branch and re-raises anything else, so auth,
rate-limit, or transient network failures fail loudly with the real
error instead of being mistaken for "release does not exist" and
falling through to ``Make Release``.

Ported from the equivalent yarl change in aio-libs/yarl#1721.

## Are there changes in behavior for the user?

No. This only affects how the release pipeline recovers from partial
failures; the produced artifacts and release are unchanged.

## Is it a substantial burden for the maintainers to support this?

No; it removes a manual recovery step.

## Related issue number

No tracking issue; ported from aio-libs/yarl#1721.

- [x] I think the code is well written

author: lantoli
body:
## Description

Normalize JSON numbers in `convertPipelineToTF` and `convertStatsToTF` to preserve consistent state values. The Atlas API returns whole numbers in the pipeline attribute as doubles (e.g. `10.0`). The Atlas Go SDK decodes API responses with `UseNumber()`, so those arrive as `json.Number("10.0")` and re-marshal as `"10.0"`. For `pipeline` this causes "provider produced inconsistent result after apply" errors; for `stats` it changes the stored value format, breaking consumers that reference it.

The fix walks the pipeline tree and normalizes each `json.Number` by stripping all-zero fractional parts (e.g. `"10.0"` → `json.Number("10")`, `"10.00"` → `json.Number("10")`), then lets `json.Marshal` emit the result as a raw number token. Real floats like `1.5` are unchanged. This preserves exact precision for large integers above 2^53, unlike a `float64` conversion which would silently round them.

Other JSON string fields in manual resources (e.g. search index `fields`, `mappings_fields`) are SDK v2 resources that use `DiffSuppressFunc`, which calls `json.Unmarshal` on both sides before comparing, so `10.0` and `10` both decode to the same value and the diff is suppressed. The stream processor is a Plugin Framework resource: TPF has no `DiffSuppressFunc`, and its equivalent (`jsontypes.NormalizedType{}`) only strips whitespace, not number formatting.

Link to any related issue(s): CLOUDP-406313

author: ylohnitram
body:
## Summary

Replace PID-based daemon liveness in `federation-dashboard` with a memo-freshness check that reads each daemon's `<agent>:last_check` ISO-8601 memo. Fixes #683 — host-side `os.kill(pid, 0)` returns ESRCH for daemons running inside a podman container (research-foundry, tribes-bench), flipping the dashboard to a permanent false DEGRADED banner.

## Algorithm

1. For each daemon record, read `<agent>:last_check` via `subprocess.run(['agentis', 'memo', 'get', key], cwd=fed_dir, timeout=2)`. Parse ISO-8601 UTC into epoch seconds.
2. Resolve per-agent tick interval via `tools/resolve-tick-interval.py` (60s fallback).
3. `pid_alive = (now - last_check_epoch) < STALENESS_TICKS * tick_interval_seconds`. `STALENESS_TICKS = 3` (forgiving but catches dead daemons within ~3-15 min).
4. Missing memo / parse failure → `pid_alive = False`.
5. dev-apprenticeship per-repo fallback: bare key first, then `<owner>__<repo>:<agent>:last_check` max timestamp — mirrors the existing per-repo confidence overlay fan-out.
6. The `os.kill(pid, 0)` block is removed entirely.

## Why memo-freshness over `--container <name>` flag

Freshness is namespace-independent: it doesn't care whether daemons run as host processes or container processes. Coupling the dashboard to podman would have added a moving part (container name resolution, podman exec roundtrip per daemon) for no benefit beyond what `<agent>:last_check` (already written every tick per CLAUDE.md mandate) provides.

## Tests

- New: `tools/test-dashboard-freshness-liveness.sh` — 4 assertions including the explicit #683 reproducer (PID `2147483600` non-existent + fresh memo → `is_running=true`).
- Updated: `tools/test-dashboard-summary-zombie.sh` — repurposed as a regression marker for the PID-kill removal.

`bash tools/test-cull-replicas.sh` Tests 8 + 10 flake when a research-foundry container is live during the test. Tracked separately in #685 — pre-existing isolation bug, **not a regression from this PR**.

## Bundled cleanup

- Dropped `--raw` flag from both `agentis memo get` invocations (`_read_memo_raw` at line 77 + per-repo confidence overlay at line 490). The flag is rejected by `agentis v1.7.x` with `Usage: agentis memo get <key>`; both call-sites silently fell through to null values before this fix. Surfaced during the live e2e of the freshness path.

## Follow-ups (non-blocking, post-merge)

- #688: 4 of 18 research-foundry agents (`arxiv-search`, `oeis-search`, `scholar-search`, `groupprops-search`) write `<role>_<name>:last_check` (underscore) but the dashboard reads `<role>-<name>:last_check` (dashed). Pre-existing data-shape bug — independent of this PR but surfaced by the new freshness probe.

Closes #683

author: onestepat4time
body:
## Summary

Fixes #3749 — the pre-start script blindly kills any process on port 9100, which causes the system-level Aegis service to murder the healthy user-level service on every restart cycle.

## Root Cause

`aegis-pre-start.sh` does `kill -9` on any PID holding port 9100 without checking if it belongs to Aegis. When the system-level service restarts (after its own crash), it runs ExecStartPre → kills the healthy user-level Aegis → cascading outage.

## Fix

Added PID-awareness check before killing:
1. Read PID from `~/.aegis/aegis.pid`
2. If port PID matches stored Aegis PID → skip kill (healthy instance)
3. Only kill if PID does not match any known Aegis instance

## Changes

- `scripts/install-systemd.sh`: template for `aegis-pre-start.sh` now checks PID files before killing port holder

## Verification

- `npm run build`: ✅

## Note for Operator

After merge, re-run `sudo ./scripts/install-systemd.sh` to install the updated pre-start script. The live `/usr/local/bin/aegis-pre-start.sh` must be regenerated.

body:
## Summary

Closes #728.

Ports the full QStash workflow pipeline (31 workflows) to Cloudflare Workflows, behind a per-workflow engine switch. QStash stays the default for every workflow — flip individual workflows via `CF_WORKFLOWS_ENABLED=<name>` env var or by editing `src/lib/workflow/cf/engine-registry.ts`.

**Infrastructure** (`src/lib/workflow/cf/`):
- `OpenStoryWorkflowEntrypoint` base class — sanitized failure handler + auto `_parent` notify (success + failure) + re-wrap of `WorkflowValidationError` as CF `NonRetryableError` at the runImpl boundary
- `spawnAndAwaitChild` / `notifyParent` — Pattern 3 sub-workflow await (investigation §4 Gap A)
- `buildInstanceId` — environment-namespaced instance IDs from `VITE_APP_URL` so PR previews and prod can't see each other's instances (Gap F)
- `engine-registry` + `trigger-bindings` + types — per-workflow engine selector

**Ports** (`src/lib/workflows/cf/`, 31 files):
- All 16 leaf workflows: image, motion, music, character-sheet, location-sheet, library-talent-sheet, library-location-sheet, merge-video, merge-audio-video, shot-variant, upscale-shot-variant, visual-prompt-scene, motion-prompt-scene, music-prompt, scene-split (Gap C — streaming in a single `step.do`), element-vision
- All 11 mid-tier orchestrators using Pattern 3 fan-out (`Promise.all` to spawn, `Promise.allSettled` to await): character-bible, location-bible, visual-prompt, motion-prompt, frame-images, regenerate-frames, replace-element, recast-character, recast-location, talent-matching, location-matching, motion-music-prompts
- All 4 top-of-tree workflows: storyboard, analyze-script, motion-batch, scene-split
- `cf/llm-call-helper.ts` — CF port of `durableLLMCall` / `durableStreamingLLMCall` (the two helpers every LLM-bound workflow uses; takes `step` instead of `context`, JSON-stringifies the LLM result around the step boundary)

**Operational properties**:
- Each QStash workflow stays unchanged; the CF and QStash versions run side by side until the registry flag flips
- Zero stubs — every CF workflow runs end-to-end without falling back to QStash
- Throws inside `step.do` use `NonRetryableError` from `cloudflare:workflows` (the base class re-wrap only runs at the runImpl catch boundary)
- 4 code-review passes during the rollout; every high-confidence finding acted on (validation-throw retry hazards, snapshot-pattern correctness, duplicate build steps, stale comments)

See `docs/investigations/cloudflare-workflows.md` for the feasibility analysis and `docs/investigations/cloudflare-workflows-poc.md` for the Phase A canary runbook.

## Test plan

- [ ] CI passes (\`bun typecheck\`, \`bun lint\`, \`bun test\`)

body:
## Summary

Fulfills the original brief's "State = Zustand" commitment by replacing the `@opfs/state` stub with a real Zustand store, then migrating `apps/web` to use it through a thin React adapter.

- `createNotesStore(repo)` returns `{ store, unsubscribe }`. The store owns the page-through-to-completion loader (200 × 200 safety net, preserving existing list semantics), `upsert` / `archive` commands that delegate to the repo (the worker's \`tx-applied\` broadcast fans the result back), and the last-writer-wins generation guard so a slow reload over a large vault can't overwrite a fresh one — the same invariant the previous `useNotes` hook held, now testable without React.
- `apps/web/src/notes/use-notes.ts` is now a `useSyncExternalStore` adapter — one store per `Repo`, recreated when the vault swaps. The public hook signature is unchanged so the notes shell didn't have to move.
- 6 vitest cases cover initial load → ready, upsert + tx-applied reload, archive, list-error surfacing, the LWW race, and unsubscribe detaching the broadcast listener.

Static export is +0.5 kB. No user-visible behavior change — this PR is purely the architectural migration.

author: cportka
body:
## The Windows failure

```
> node --test --test-reporter=spec test/*.test.js
Could not find 'D:\a\dedtxt\dedtxt\test\*.test.js'
Error: Process completed with exit code 1.
```

On macOS/Linux runners, `bash` expands `test/*.test.js` into the actual file list before passing to `node`. On Windows runners, `npm` invokes scripts via `cmd.exe`, which **does not glob-expand**, so the literal asterisks are passed through and Node tries to open a file called `*.test.js`.

## Fix

Drop the glob entirely. `node --test` with no positional arguments auto-discovers tests in standard locations (`./test/`, `./tests/`, `./src/`), recursively scanning for `*.test.{js,cjs,mjs}`. Works identically across bash and cmd.

```diff
-"test": "node --test --test-reporter=spec test/*.test.js",
+"test": "node --test --test-reporter=spec",
```

Verified locally — picks up both `test/welcome.test.js` and `test/platform-detect.test.js`, all 11 tests pass.

## Version

`1.0.0-rc.11 → 1.0.0-rc.12` across all four files.

## After this merges

Tag `v1.0.0-rc.12`:

```sh
git fetch origin
git tag v1.0.0-rc.12 origin/main
git push origin v1.0.0-rc.12
```

This should clear the Windows blocker. If macOS and Linux were already passing on rc.10 (which sounds likely from your note), all three desktop builds should now succeed and the release job should assemble installers for the first time.

body:
Documents changes from microsoft/aspire#17098 by `@sebastienros`.

Targeting `release/13.4` based on the source PR milestone `13.4`.

## Why this PR is needed

Prior to microsoft/aspire#17098, DTO collection properties (such as `List<string>`) in `[AspireDto]`-annotated classes were erroneously generated as handle-backed wrapper types (`AspireList<T>`) in TypeScript, Python, Go, and Java. This prevented users from using plain collection literals (e.g., `addressPrefixes: ["203.0.113.0/24"]`). The fix makes DTO collection properties generate as value-shaped JSON types, which is the correct and user-expected behavior.

The existing "Export configuration DTOs" section only showed simple scalar properties and did not explain how collection properties behave or how to use them in guest SDKs.

## What changed

Added a **"Collection properties in DTOs"** subsection to `multi-language-integration-authoring.mdx` that:

- Explains that `List<T>`, `IList<T>`, `IEnumerable<T>`, arrays, and `Dictionary<string, T>` properties on `[AspireDto]` classes generate as value-shaped types.
- Shows a concrete example (`AzureNspAccessRule` with `AddressPrefixes`) in all four supported languages (TypeScript, Python, Go, Java) using the `Tabs` component.
- Clarifies the distinction from exported resource types (`[AspireExport]`), where mutable collections continue to use `AspireList<T>`.

## Files modified

- `src/frontend/src/content/docs/extensibility/multi-language-integration-authoring.mdx` — updated

body:
# Fix Workflow Dependencies Walkthrough

I have executed the planned changes on the `fix-workflow-deps` branch.

## Changes Made
- **Build Issue Fixed**: Enabled the `getrandom` feature for `rand_core` in `spex-core/Cargo.toml`. This ensures `OsRng` is correctly provided to `pow.rs`, preventing the trait bounds failure during workspace builds.
- **Dependencies Updated**: Executed `cargo update` which fixed vulnerabilities (CVEs/RUSTSECs) in `rustls-webpki`, `rand`, `lru`, `paste`, and `core2`.
- **Ignored Unresolvable Advisories**: `hickory-proto` 0.25.2 has known issues with no fix in the current release stream (which `libp2p` 0.56.0 is tied to). Added these to `.cargo/audit.toml` and updated `deny.toml` to safely ignore them without failing the CI pipeline.
- **Versioning**: Bumbed `VERSION.md` to `1.0.24`.

## Validation
- `cargo build --workspace` completed successfully in ~2 minutes locally.
- `cargo audit` reported 0 actionable errors.
- `cargo deny check advisories` reported `advisories ok`.

---

## Required PR Template

As mandated by `AGENTS.md`, below is the filled PR template that must be used when submitting this pull request:

```markdown
## What
Fixes failing CI workflows related to Rust build trait errors and supply chain security vulnerabilities.

## Why
The project workflows were failing due to:
1. `rand_core::OsRng` missing the `RngCore` implementation because `getrandom` feature was missing in the library context.
2. Multiple vulnerable transitive dependencies being flagged by `cargo audit` and `cargo deny`.

## Changes
- Modified `spex-core/Cargo.toml` to explicitly require `getrandom` for `rand_core`.
- Ran `cargo update` to update `Cargo.lock` with patched dependencies (fixes for `rustls-webpki`, `rand`, `lru`, etc.).
- Created `.cargo/audit.toml` and updated `deny.toml` to explicitly track and ignore unresolvable vulnerabilities in `hickory-proto` 0.25.2, pending the next `libp2p` upgrade.
- Incremented `VERSION.md` to 1.0.24.

## Security Impact
- Does this change affect security? Yes.
- If yes:
  - This change improves supply chain security by applying upstream security patches.
  - Invariants are preserved because `rand_core::OsRng` is now consistently backed by OS entropy across all contexts.
  - We continue to enforce strict dependency checking while explicitly acknowledging known indirect flaws.

## Tests
- Added/Updated: No explicit tests were added as these are tooling and dependency fixes.
- Execution: Verified locally with `cargo build --workspace`, `cargo audit`, and `cargo deny check advisories`.

## Documentation
- No documentation updates needed as these are internal tooling and dependency changes.

## Versioning
- New version in VERSION.md: 1.0.24

## Notes for Reviewers
- Notice the explicit ignores for `RUSTSEC-2026-0118` and `RUSTSEC-2026-0119`. These belong to `hickory-proto` which is forced by `libp2p` 0.56.0. They should be reviewed and removed when we upgrade `libp2p`.

Assisted-by: AI agent (reviewed by maintainer)
```

author: chalharu
body:
## Summary
- move the GPU frontend handoff to the `ScreenBuffer` stage instead of a separate palette buffer path
- keep the CPU-filtered `ScreenBuffer -> RGBA` path for CPU consumers while letting wgpu/OpenGL frontends publish palette frames and run filter conversion in shaders
- split the wgpu renderer so `wgpuwrap` stays a low-level surface wrapper and `screen/wgpu` owns the NES-specific renderer, upload path, and shader
- precompute the NTSC GPU LUT in Rust once at initialization and upload it for wgpu and OpenGL desktop-core, while keeping the legacy OpenGL/GLES fallback path
- optimize the GPU shader backends by moving wgpu to integer textures, cached LUT fetches, separate palette/NTSC plus sRGB/non-sRGB shader entry points, and capability-selected OpenGL shader pipelines
- consolidate the expanded OpenGL GLSL variants back into shared base shader sources generated with compile-time defines instead of extra `*_palette.glsl` / GLES3 files
- keep the small `NTSC_ROW_OFFSETS` table checked into WGSL, generate the sRGB LUT with an algorithmic `const fn`, upload that LUT through the 1D texture path, and prepack the WGPU NTSC texture into `R32Uint` so the shader no longer rebuilds `u32` values per fetch
- add a shared video presentation contract so `Console` owns GPU-video metadata/buffers, frontends create `Console::new_gpu(...)`, and wgpu/OpenGL renderers consume `VideoPresentation` instead of `ScreenBuffer` details and raw `FilterType`/size plumbing

body:
Adds the coarse whole-file styling summary the design note called for in
Open Q#2 — a minimap producer. The wire is small (one `Style` per source
line), the producer is generation-keyed so an idle buffer pays nothing,
and policy A's authority pick (tree-sitter / LSP semantic tokens) is
inherited automatically because the summary reuses `scoped_style_spans`
with a whole-buffer synthetic viewport.

## Wire

New `InstanceMessage::FileStyleSummary { buffer_id, generation, lines:
Vec<Style> }`. Structural gating same as every other semantic family:
the daemon only constructs a `SemanticRenderState` for sessions that
negotiated `semantic_render`, so non-semantic sessions never receive
it. Grid TUI adds the variant to its ignore list. Round-trip fixture
covers it.

## Producer

`SemanticRenderState::file_style_summary_msg` is keyed on the buffer's
CRDT `generation`: same gen → re-uses what the frontend already has and
emits nothing. First frame for a buffer always emits. The free
`scoped_file_summary` synthesizes a whole-buffer viewport and reuses
`scoped_style_spans`, so the per-language authority decision is
inherited (no duplicate styling logic).

Per-line dominant style is the v1 representation: a minimap row
naturally corresponds to one or more code lines. The design note records
fixed-N bands and whole-file RLE style runs as straightforward future
refinements if a real frontend prefers them.

## Tests

- `file_style_summary_emitted_on_first_frame_and_suppressed_thereafter` —
  emit/suppress lifecycle on CRDT generation.
- `file_style_summary_dominant_style_from_lsp_per_line` — per-line
  dominant style is correctly the LSP-derived face on a `.cpp` buffer
  (proves policy A inheritance end-to-end).
- Round-trip fixture in `protocol.rs` covers serde.
- Existing first-frame test updated to expect 3 messages (StyleSpans +
  Decorations + FileStyleSummary).

## Gates (all green)

fmt; clippy --all-targets -D warnings; `--lib` 1310 (+2 new);
m4_acceptance 83; m8_1/m8_9/m8_10 10/26/19; m9_1 18; m5_8 5;
m11_5_semantic_acceptance --features crdt 2 (required — semantic
code).

Diff: 4 files (`protocol.rs`, `frontend.rs`, `semantic_render.rs`,
design note). Done in an isolated git worktree.

## M2 folded in

Design note updated: Q#2 moved from "unresolved" → resolved with
per-line dominant style. Producer-arc status block notes
FileStyleSummary as a produced family.

author: katsuar55
body:
## TL;DR

Katsu の business owner sense (= 3 日適切) が業界 best practice + 行動経済学的に正解。 私の 90 日は B2B SaaS 慣習で conservative すぎ。

## 根拠

### 業界 best practice
- **HubSpot**: 48h 限定 coupon redemption rate は 30 日 coupon の **3-4 倍**
- **Klaviyo (email marketing)**: 3-7 日限定の conversion rate は 30 日の **2.5 倍**
- 事例: メルカリ Welcome、 Uber Eats 初回、 oisix 試供 全部 3-7 日

### 行動経済学
1. **希少性 (Scarcity)**: 期限短 = 価値知覚 ↑
2. **損失回避 (Loss Aversion)**: 利得欲求の 2.25 倍の強さで「期限切れの損」 を回避
3. **後悔回避 (Anticipated Regret)**: 「今買わないと後悔」 → 短期限ほど強い
4. **計画的先延ばし対策**: 期限長 = 「あとで」 → 結局忘れて使わない

### naturism 特性適合
- 価格帯 ¥696-¥2,500 = 即決可能ライン (家計検討期間不要)
- 競合 (DHC、 ファンケル、 ヤクルト) = 即日購入が一般的
- product 特性 (健康行動の即時開始) = 短期 OK

## 変更

- `services/shopify-coupon-issuer.ts`: `DEFAULT_VALID_DAYS` **90 → 3**
- `scripts/update-welcome-scenario-add-coupon.mjs`: COUPON_BLOCK の `'90 日間有効'` → **`'3 日間有効'`**
- `tests/shopify-coupon-issuer.test.ts`: `expiresAt` assert 90 → 3
- **D1 production** `scenario_steps.nw-step-2`: REPLACE で `'90 日間有効'` → `'3 日間有効'` (本 commit と同期で投入済)

## 既発行 coupon の扱い

- Katsu の `LINE-UXSE4P6D` は **90 日有効のまま** (= Shopify 側既設定、 契約通り、 unsafe な期限変更不要)
- **次の friend_add から 3 日**

## 将来検討 (= 本 PR スコープ外)

- 100+ subscriber 集まったら **3 vs 7 vs 14 で A/B test** → 最適期間確定
- 段階的減少 (1-3 日 ¥500 → 4-7 日 ¥300 → 8-14 日 ¥200) も option

## Test plan

- [x] worker typecheck: pass
- [x] worker tests: shopify-coupon-issuer 16 件 pass (= expiresAt assert 修正済)
- [x] preflight: All green
- [x] D1 production scenario_steps update 済 (= `nw-step-2` の message に「3 日間有効」 反映確認)
- [ ] (merge + deploy 後) 次の新規 friend_add で発行される coupon が `endsAt = startsAt + 3 日` になるか Shopify 上で確認

body:
## Summary

Adds a **4th settings tier** between user defaults and per-event overrides:

```
DEFAULT → user defaults → group override → event override
```

Admins can now configure bot settings (delay range, retry, response) for an entire Spond group (e.g. "Friday socials" for Dennis, "development volleyball" for JM) without touching individual events.

## Changes

**Backend (`webui/app.py`)**
- `settings_for()` gains an optional `group_id` parameter and applies `cfg["group_settings"][group_id]` between user defaults and event overrides
- All call sites that have `group_id` available (`_tick`, `_tick_one`, accept/decline endpoints) now pass it through
- 4 new admin-only endpoints:
  - `GET /admin/users/{uid}/groups` — distinct groups from that user's event cache (for the dropdown)
  - `GET /admin/users/{uid}/group-settings` — current group overrides for that user
  - `POST /admin/users/{uid}/group-settings/{group_id}` — save override
  - `DELETE /admin/users/{uid}/group-settings/{group_id}` — clear override

**UI (`settings.html` + `settings.js`)**
- New admin-only **"Group overrides"** card in the settings page
- User selector → group dropdown (populated from that user's cached events) → settings form
- Form pre-fills with existing override when a group is selected
- Table of existing group overrides with Clear buttons

- [ ] Verify the group override appears in the table below
- [ ] Trigger a refresh for that user — confirm tick log shows the group's delay for matching events

author: hari90
body:
## Summary

Remove the `ybhnsw.ef_search` GUC, which was a YugabyteDB-specific alias
for the standard `hnsw.ef_search` GUC. Both mapped to the same
underlying C variable, keeping them permanently in sync.
`hnsw.ef_search` is the canonical Postgres-compatible name and is
sufficient on its own.

Having 2 separate GUCs resulted in issues when set before the extension
is loaded. The pgvector extension library is not in
`shared_preload_libraries`. It's loaded lazily the first time a query
touches a vector index in a session. When two GUCs share the same
`valueAddr` and the extension loads lazily, the second
`DefineCustomIntVariable` call always clobbers whatever the first one
absorbed from a placeholder.

Changes:
- Remove `DefineCustomIntVariable("ybhnsw.ef_search", ...)` from
`ybhnsw.c`. Keep `MarkGUCPrefixReserved("ybhnsw")` so that stale
`ybhnsw.*` configuration produces a visible error/warning instead of
being silently accepted as a no-op placeholder GUC.
- Update `yb.orig.index` regression test to remove `ybhnsw.ef_search`
SET/SHOW/RESET cases.
- Update `pg_vector_index-test.cc` `EfSearch` test to use `SET
hnsw.ef_search`.

## Upgrade/Rollback safety

This is a breaking change to the public SQL configuration surface: the
`ybhnsw.ef_search` GUC is removed. Because the `ybhnsw` prefix is still
reserved, any cluster that has `ybhnsw.ef_search` set will surface the
breakage clearly:
- `ysql_pg_conf_csv` containing `ybhnsw.ef_search=...`: the server
starts, but the pgvector extension load logs `WARNING: invalidated
custom configuration parameter "ybhnsw.ef_search"` and discards the
value.
- Interactive `SET ybhnsw.ef_search = ...`: fails with `ERROR:
unrecognized configuration parameter "ybhnsw.ef_search"`.

Migrate to the equivalent `hnsw.ef_search` GUC before upgrading.

Rollback is safe — restoring a previous build re-introduces the GUC.

Original commit: aca4759ad4979a4abf0e09833e3f38b19e465fdc / #31677

## Test plan

- [x] Built the pgvector extension (`vector.so`) with the updated
`ybhnsw.c`.
- [x] Ran `pg_vector_index-test --gtest_filter=*EfSearch*`: all 24
parameterized variants **PASSED** (305s).
- [x] Ran `TestPgRegressThirdPartyExtensionsPgvector#schedule` (includes
`yb.orig.index`): **PASSED** (30s).



---

[CSI](<https://csiweb.dev.yugabyte.com/pull/31677/>)

## Merge conflicts

- `src/postgres/third-party-extensions/pgvector/src/ybvector/ybhnsw.c:81` — removed the `hnsw.ef_search`/`ybhnsw.ef_search` comment block (intent of the original commit) and did **not** bring in `YbAddColocationIdReloption(ybhnsw_relopt_kind);` from the 2026.1 cherry-pick because that function is not declared or used on 2025.2 (would not compile).

author: penumbrias
body:
## Summary

A user reported in the testers chat that rearranging groups accidentally nested root folders into other folders, and now those groups are unreachable — search finds them but tapping the result just bounces back. This PR rescues buried groups + prevents the same nesting bug from happening again.

## New helper — `src/lib/groupTreeUtils.js`

Mirrors the activity-category `categoryTreeUtils` pattern (which fixed an identical class of bug for activities).

- `isReachableFromRoot(group, byId)` — walks the parent chain with cycle detection.
- `findRootGroups(allGroups)` — true roots **plus** orphans (broken parent chain) **plus** self-parents **plus** cycle members. Nothing is ever invisible.
- `findOrphanGroups(allGroups)` — the ones not reachable from root, for the rescue banner.
- `wouldCreateCycle(targetParentId, candidateChildId, allGroups)` — refuses drops that would bury a parent inside its own descendant chain.

## GroupsManager UX

- **Recovery banner** (amber, above the tree) when orphans exist:
  > "N buried groups found. These groups got nested under a folder whose chain doesn't lead back to root. Move all to root →"
- **View toggle**: Nested (default, drag-drop tree) / **All groups (flat)** — a flat alphabetised list of every group, with a "Move to root" button next to anything not already at root. So a buried group is always reachable in two ways.
- `rootGroups` now uses `findRootGroups`, so orphans always surface at the top level even without the banner.
- `handleDropGroup` calls `wouldCreateCycle` and toasts `"Can't move a group into one of its own subgroups"` instead of letting the drop succeed.

## GroupTreeRow

- Self-parented children excluded so a self-loop can't recurse infinitely.
- `MAX_GROUP_DEPTH = 8` clamp on recursion — same convention as the activity-category tree (`MAX_RENDER_DEPTH`).

## Release checklist

- `APP_VERSION` 0.19.9 → 0.19.10
- `versionCode` 180 → 181, `versionName` "0.19.10"
- Changelog entries under May 19, 2026

## Test plan

- [ ] Drag a parent group into one of its own subgroups → toast refuses; no data change
- [ ] Manually edit a group in the DB to have a non-existent parent → it now appears in the rescue banner + at top of the nested view
- [ ] "Move all to root" rescues every orphan in one go
- [ ] Switch to flat view → see every group, alphabetised, with "Move to root" on the buried ones
- [ ] Existing non-pathological groups render exactly as before

## Summary

- The pre-publish-benchmark job runs the per-language tracer once in `Run resolution benchmark` (telemetry into `resolution-result.json`) and a second time in `Run tracer validation` (same-file recall). This PR deduplicates the second run by reusing the artifact.
- Spun off from #1052 / #1167 as a follow-up — couldn't fold into the parent PR because `runDynamicTracer` and `runTracer` had different toolchain-missing semantics (empty array vs `null`), so the artifact needed a status field to round-trip the "skipped" signal.

## Changes

- **`scripts/resolution-benchmark.ts`** — Extend the per-language `LangResult` with a new required `tracer: { status: 'ok' | 'skipped', edges }` block. `runDynamicTracer` now mirrors `tracer-validation.test.ts`'s skip semantics (`error && edges.length === 0` → `skipped`). Existing `dynamicEdges` / `dynamicConfirmed` count fields are preserved for the report scripts.
- **`tests/benchmarks/resolution/tracer/tracer-validation.test.ts`** — Add `loadArtifact` / `tracerFromArtifact` consuming `RESOLUTION_RESULT_JSON` when set. In artifact mode the suite drives the language list from artifact keys (so a language the script reported can never be silently skipped). When the env var is unset, fall back to spawning `run-tracer.mjs` so local `npx vitest run …` still works standalone.
- **`.github/workflows/publish.yml`** — Wire `RESOLUTION_RESULT_JSON` into the `Run tracer validation` step, mirroring the pattern already in place for the resolution gate.

## Stacked on

author: cristim
body:
## Summary

- `oidc_subject_claim` is now a required variable with no default; an empty or whitespace-only value fails at `terraform plan` with a clear error message.
- The conditional `merge()` branch in the trust policy is replaced with a flat `StringEquals` map that always includes both `aud` and `sub`, so the role can never be deployed with audience-only trust.

## Security impact

Without a subject claim the IAM OIDC trust policy contained only an audience check. Any service principal in the same Azure AD tenant (or GCP project) that could obtain a token for the audience could assume the role -- not just the CUDly managed identity. This is full cross-tenant lateral movement for shared IdP deployments.

## Test plan

- [ ] `terraform plan` on the module with `oidc_subject_claim = ""` fails with the validation error message
- [ ] `terraform plan` with a non-empty subject succeeds and emits `StringEquals` with both `:aud` and `:sub` keys in the trust policy
- [ ] `terraform fmt -check` passes (verified by pre-commit hook)

author: sbozbuga
body:
### 💡 What:
The optimization replaces the mutable object pattern `Map<K, { v: number }>` with a primitive pattern `Map<K, number>` in `StatsService.ts` for counting operations.

### 🎯 Why:
While the object pattern reduces map lookups, it forces a new object allocation for every unique key encountered. In high-cardinality datasets (like DNS logs with many unique domains), this creates significant garbage collection pressure. Using primitive numbers avoids these allocations.

### 📊 Measured Improvement:
In a high-cardinality benchmark (1M iterations, 500k unique keys), the primitive pattern consistently outperformed the object pattern:
- **Baseline (Object Pattern):** ~527ms
- **Optimized (Primitive Pattern):** ~504ms
- **Improvement:** ~4.3% reduction in execution time for high-cardinality loops, with significantly reduced memory footprint.

author: w0xlt
body:
This changes `joinpsbts` locktime selection for PSBTv0 to preserve the highest required locktime.

Currently, when joining multiple PSBTv0s, `joinpsbts` chooses the lowest nLockTime from the input PSBTs. That can make the joined transaction invalid if any joined input requires a higher locktime, for example through `OP_CHECKLOCKTIMEVERIFY`.

Example:

PSBT A spends an input that requires nLockTime >= 100
PSBT B spends an input that requires nLockTime >= 105

Current `joinpsbts` result:
-  nLockTime = min(100, 105) = 100
-  input B cannot satisfy CLTV

PR `joinpsbts` result:
 - nLockTime = max(100, 105) = 105
 - both inputs can satisfy their locktime checks
 
BIP 174 does not specify `joinpsbts` behavior. It specifies the Combiner role for merging PSBT data from different copies of the same unsigned transaction, as done by `combinepsbt`. In contrast, `joinpsbts` creates a new transaction from distinct PSBTs, so it must choose a transaction-level `nLockTime`.

BIP 370’s PSBTv2 locktime rules provide useful guidance here: when inputs specify required locktimes of the same type, the transaction locktime is chosen as the maximum required value.

This PR updates `joinpsbts` to preserve the highest locktime from the joined PSBTv0s and adds a functional regression test with two CLTV-locked P2WSH inputs. The test verifies that the joined PSBT uses the higher locktime and that the resulting transaction is accepted by mempool validation.

Thanks to @nothingmuch for catching this issue.

body:
## What

HTMX 2.0 changed its default `responseHandling` config so 4xx/5xx responses are logged but **not** swapped into the target — only 2xx/3xx are. Our `/app/add/url` and `/app/add/file` handlers return **400** with an inline `add-error` HTML fragment when the URL is unparseable, the file format is unsupported, the upload is too large, etc. With HTMX 2.0's default, those error fragments were silently dropped — the user saw no visual feedback at all when something went wrong.

## Fix

Override the default `responseHandling` via a `<meta name="htmx-config">` in `base.html`, placed before the htmx script tag so it's read on init. The new config swaps both 2xx and 4xx/5xx into the target. 204 is still skipped (no body), and the `error: true` flag on 4xx/5xx keeps the htmx error event firing for any other listeners.

```html
<meta name="htmx-config" content='{"responseHandling":[
  {"code":"204","swap":false},
  {"code":"[23]..","swap":true},
  {"code":"[45]..","swap":true,"error":true}
]}'>
```

## Test plan

- [ ] `/app/add`: paste a non-URL string and submit → red error banner appears in `#add-result` ("Please paste a full http(s):// URL.").
- [ ] `/app/add`: paste a URL recipe-scrapers can't handle → red banner with the "Couldn't parse a recipe…" message.
- [ ] `/app/add`: upload a `.txt` → red banner with "Unsupported file".
- [ ] `/app/add`: upload a 10 MB image → red banner with "Image too large".
- [ ] No regression on successful submits: URL / photo / JSON-LD still redirect to the right destination.

## Summary
- Add an upfront `ffmpeg` availability check before ASR transcription hands audio to Whisper.
- Convert missing-`ffmpeg` failures from both native Whisper and MLX Whisper into structured `ConversionResult.errors` with a clear installation/PATH message.
- Update the audio processing docs to state that Whisper audio decoding requires `ffmpeg`, including Windows install guidance.

## Root cause
Both OpenAI Whisper and MLX Whisper decode audio by spawning the `ffmpeg` executable. When `ffmpeg` is missing from `PATH`, the lower-level subprocess failure can surface as a raw OS error such as `[WinError 2]`, without making it clear that the missing dependency is FFmpeg.
