- `uv run pytest tests/test_asr_missing_ffmpeg.py tests/test_asr_pipeline.py tests/test_asr_mlx_whisper.py -q`
- `make validate`

Fixes #3463.

author: simonheimlicher
body:
## Summary

- The `standardizing-merging` skill now names the self-modifying-PR case where GitHub Actions intentionally skips the auto-review workflow, and emits a new `MENTION_REVIEW_NEEDED:<trigger-phrase>` token so the managing flow can route around it.

## Background

When a PR modifies the auto-review workflow's own file, GitHub Actions applies its identical-workflow-content gate and reports `conclusion: skipped` on the reviewer job. The managing flow's review predicate is then unmet through no fault of the PR — the reviewer never ran. Without an explicit branch, the heartbeat treats this as `WAIT_FOR_REVIEW` forever.

The new gate exception names the case directly: post one PR-level comment containing exactly `<trigger-phrase> review` (e.g. `@spec-tree review`) to fire the mention-triggered reviewer (which has no identical-content gate), emit `MENTION_REVIEW_NEEDED:<trigger-phrase>`, and treat that workflow's findings as the current-head four-class review on the next heartbeat.

## Changes

- `plugins/spec-tree/skills/standardizing-merging/SKILL.md` — `<pr_authority_gate>` gains the reviewer-skipped-by-design exception; `<action_tokens>` gains `MENTION_REVIEW_NEEDED:<trigger-phrase>`.
- `plugins/spec-tree/.claude-plugin/plugin.json` and `.codex-plugin/plugin.json` — version bump.

author: xtomwray
body:
Adds a single CLI entry point that brings up an N-drone DVD swarm, drives every GCS through arm-and-takeoff plus autopilot-flight on a freshly generated random mission, runs a chosen attack (initially attitude spoofing) during a configurable window, passively sniffs every MAVLink packet, writes per-message-type CSVs in the dvdsh DUMP_CSV/JOIN_CSV format with a trailing attack_type label, then tears the swarm down and collects per-drone flight logs.

  make sim N=100 START=10 END=1200 ATTACK=attitude-spoof

All new code, plus the moved Makefile and generate_swarm.py, lives under swarm/. A thin root Makefile forwards targets into swarm/.

- swarm/sim.py: lifecycle orchestrator (mission gen, compose up, readiness probe via mavutil.wait_heartbeat on FC TCP 5760, parallel GCS stages, sniffer, attack threads, log collection, teardown, metadata.json).
- swarm/missions.py: random lawnmower-with-jitter waypoint generator sized to outlast the attack window.
- swarm/attacks/{attitude_spoof,registry,targets}.py: pluggable attack registry; initial handler ports the user-supplied pymavlink+scapy spoof script with a cooperative send_loop signature.
- swarm/dataset/sniffer.py: scapy AsyncSniffer + per-flow pymavlink reassembly, dispatching to packet_writer.
- swarm/dataset/packet_writer.py: dvdsh DUMP_CSV+JOIN_CSV port. Header bytes match dvdsh exactly (mav_packet_type, MAV header, payload fields, ip_*, udp_*, tcp_*) plus a trailing frame_timestamp,attack_type so downstream preprocessors can window for biLSTM training.
- swarm/dataset/{dvdsh_compat,mavlink_schema,labels}.py: header-field constants, ardupilotmega schema lookup, and a time+drone-id label resolver.

pyproject.toml gains scapy, pymavlink, requests, and switches to package-find discovery now that generate_swarm.py has moved into swarm/.

## Document contents (19 sections per the authorised scope)

1. **Executive Summary** — completes the V1 design quartet
2. **Design Principles** — 8 principles (operational scope, explicit
   sources, traceable lineage, no over-sharing, role-scoped views,

## Summary

Fixes the adaptive rematch deck swap bug where selecting a deck during adaptive short/rematch would get swapped incorrectly. Also refactors the end-of-game prompt options.

## Changes

- Fix adaptive rematch: hide 'Rematch: Swap Decks' for `adaptive-bo1` format since adaptive setup handles deck swapping
- Refactor `GameWonPrompt` with cleaner button/mode mapping (`same`, `swap`, `change`)
- Add `ContinuePrompt` for the 'continue playing' flow
- Consolidate `RematchWithNewDecksPrompt` into `RematchPrompt`
- Add HowToPlay docs for rematch options
- Add tests for `GameWonPrompt`

Fixes #3520 Fixes #1482

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Changes rematch client state handling and lobby socket membership (user-visible flow) plus bonus-icon and card-play rules that affect in-game behavior.
> 
> **Overview**
> This PR tightens **rematch and lobby/client sync** and several **rules/engine edge cases**, with matching tests.
> 
> **Rematch / sockets:** When a finished game’s `cleargamestate` arrives after the lobby has already published a pending rematch (`started: false`), the client **no longer clears** `lobby.currentGame`. **Rematch with new decks** now calls `socket.joinChannel(newGame.id)` for non-owner players (same as other join paths) so they stay on the right lobby channel.
> 
> **Bonus icons:** House enhancements on cards are excluded from bonus-icon resolution via `getResolvableBonusIcons()`, so effects like Amphora Captura won’t prompt to “resolve” an **untamed** (etc.) house icon as a bonus icon.
> 
> **Ditch the Loot:** Play is gated on **at least two creatures** in play; with only one creature, amber stays put instead of a broken second target.
> 
> **Chat UI:** Keyword/icon rendering in `Messages.jsx` avoids an extra trailing space after the last token.
> 
> **Tests:** Expanded Ditch the Loot coverage; prophecy end-turn tests moved under `prophecy.spec.js`; tide test consolidated (with a note that Dark Tidings gating isn’t enforced in-engine).

author: jeremiahjrross
body:
## Summary

Implements the six-method `case_store.*` capability surface — the runtime's typed RPC over case-scoped Postgres operations (architecture §6.6, blueprint B23).

Authors call `inp.case_store.append_audit / record_drift / read_prior_snapshot / write_snapshot / list_attachments / read_attachment`; agents have no direct database access. The runner stamps `tenant_id` + `case_id` from the gRPC session so cross-tenant attempts produce no rows.

**Strict six-method allowlist enforced at the wire** — every new method is a protocol-version event. The provider surface deliberately exposes no generic SQL escape hatch.

### What ships

- **`flowrun_runtime/capabilities/case_store.py`** — six per-method providers sharing one `CaseStoreBackend` Protocol; structured error codes (`CASE_STORE_AUDIT_FAILED`, `CASE_STORE_ATTACHMENT_NOT_FOUND`, …); OTel CHAIN spans stamped with agent/tenant/case identity.
- **`build_case_store_providers(backend)` factory** returns the six providers as a `CaseStoreProviders` bundle with `.as_registry()` for drop-in use with `build_default_router`.
- **`alembic/versions/009_case_audits_drifts.py`** — append-only `case_audits` + `case_drifts` tables with `(tenant_id, case_id, created_at DESC)` indexes. Snapshots / attachments lift from the existing `case_snapshots` (post-0006) and `case_files` (baseline) tables.
- **34 unit tests** covering wire round-trip for each method, runner-stamped tenant isolation, the SAVEPOINT invariant (audit failure does not poison previously persisted snapshot state), dispatcher integration, and OTel span identity stamping.
- **Integration test** (gated on `FLOWRUN_RUNTIME_CASE_STORE_TEST=1`, matching the B19/B20 live-test pattern) shipping a reference asyncpg `CaseStoreBackend` adapter that documents the production SQL shape including the SAVEPOINT pattern around audit/drift inserts.

### Acceptance criteria (from blueprint B23)

- [x] An agent can append audit rows and read prior snapshots.
- [x] Cross-tenant attempts produce no rows.
- [x] SAVEPOINT pattern preserved — an audit failure does not poison the parent transaction.
- [x] Strict six-method allowlist — no escape hatch beyond `append_audit`, `record_drift`, `read_prior_snapshot`, `write_snapshot`, `list_attachments`, `read_attachment`.

## Test plan

- [x] `pytest tests/capabilities/test_case_store.py` — 34 unit tests pass locally.
- [x] `pytest tests/capabilities/test_dispatcher.py` — pre-existing 12 tests still pass (dispatcher integration unchanged).
- [x] `ruff check` clean on new files.
- [x] `mypy flowrun_runtime/capabilities/case_store.py` clean.
- [ ] `FLOWRUN_RUNTIME_CASE_STORE_TEST=1 pytest tests/capabilities/test_case_store_integration.py` — gated on a reachable docker daemon (matches B19/B20 pattern).

author: spinlocked
body:
Cached decode repeatedly executes the same bucketed Metal graph with changing dynamic values. These changes reduce repeated execution overhead by avoiding unnecessary intermediate-buffer reallocations, MPS descriptor/kernel setup, and per-run execution metadata reconstruction.

In the Qwen Metal example on my M3 Max, this improves TPOT by ~2%.

Reuse dynamic intermediate buffers at bucket capacity
  - Metal intermediate buffers are allocated at the active bucket's max dynamic dimensions.
  - The runtime tracks each buffer's logical byte length separately, so smaller executions inside the same bucket can safely reuse the larger allocation.
  - `get_f32`, buffer clearing, bucket activation, and `remove_buffer` now keep that logical-length metadata consistent.

Cache MPS matmul setup objects
  - Added an `MpsKernelCache` for `MPSMatrixDescriptor` and `MPSMatrixMultiplication` objects.
  - Introduced `MetalEncodeContext` so kernels receive the command buffer, dynamic-dimension buffer, and MPS cache together.
  - `MPSMatmul` and `MPSBatchedMatmul` now reuse cached descriptors and multiplication kernels instead of recreating them on every encode.

Precompute per-bucket execution metadata
  - Bucket compilation now records LLIR input mappings, output data mappings, and executable kernel steps.
  - `execute` and `execute_timed` reuse this precomputed execution plan instead of rebuilding topological order, input node lists, and dtype metadata every run.

## 🛡️ Enhanced Security & Privacy

The tools system now prioritizes your security and data privacy with several new layers of protection:

*   **Path Whitelisting:** You can now restrict filesystem tools (like reading, writing, or searching files) to specific directories. By default, only your home directory is accessible, but you can add or remove paths as needed.
*   **Manual Approval Workflow:** Every tool can now be configured for "Auto-run" or "Manual Approval." When manual approval is enabled, the AI presents an **Approval Card** explaining what it wants to do, and nothing happens until you click "Approve."
*   **AI Justification:** For powerful tools like `run_command` and custom scripts, the AI is now required to provide a one-sentence justification for its action, which is displayed directly on the approval card.
*   **Privacy Redaction:** To keep your system details private, PlasmaLLM automatically redacts your absolute home path (e.g., `/home/username/`) and replaces it with `~` in all data sent back to the AI.
*   **Safety Limits:** New global limits for file reads, writes, and network responses prevent the AI from overwhelming the system or the chat context.

## 🛠️ New & Improved Tools

The "Built-in Tools" library has been significantly expanded and improved:

*   **Advanced Filesystem Access:**
    *   `read_file` / `write_file`: Directly interact with your files.
    *   `list_dir`: Explore directory structures.
    *   `search_files`: Powerful recursive regex searching (via `grep`).
*   **Enhanced Web Search:** A redesigned `web_search` tool now supports multiple providers, including **DuckDuckGo**, **SearXNG**, and **Ollama**, providing rich Markdown results with links and icons.
*   **Full Network Interaction:** `http_get` and `http_request` allow the AI to fetch web content or interact with APIs directly.
*   **Powerful Terminal Access:** The `run_command` tool is now more reliable and supports **Session Multiplexing** (via `tmux` or `screen`), allowing the AI to run long-running tasks in the background.
*   **Desktop Integration:**
    *   `get_clipboard` / `set_clipboard`: Seamlessly move text between the AI and your system clipboard.
    *   `notify`: Receive system notifications when the AI completes a task.
    *   `open_url`: Let the AI open files or websites in your default applications.

## ✍️ Custom Script Tools

You are no longer limited to built-in tools. You can now define your own **Custom Script Tools** in the settings:
1.  Provide a name and description for the AI.
2.  Define a **Command Template** (e.g., `git -C {path} status`).
3.  PlasmaLLM automatically generates the necessary instructions for the AI to use your custom tool.

## 🎨 Improved UI/UX

*   **New Configuration Pages:** A streamlined settings interface makes it easy to enable/disable tools and fine-tune their individual settings.
*   **Rich Rendering:** Command outputs are now rendered in a "Console Style" (monospace font, dark background), and web searches provide beautifully formatted results.
*   **Approval Cards:** Clear, interactive cards for tool requests make it easy to see exactly what the AI is proposing before it executes.

author: georgwiese
body:
# powdr-openvm-riscv: split `generate-apcs` out of `select-apcs`

Today `select-apcs` does two things: it builds APC candidates and it picks
the top N. This PR splits those into two stages with separate caches:
`generate-apcs` builds candidates and produces a ranking; `select-apcs`
trims the ranking to `--autoprecompiles` (after `--skip`).

The win: with `--artifacts-dir`, sweeping `--autoprecompiles 10 → 50 → 100`
under `--pgo cell` now reuses a single generate-cache entry across all
three runs. Previously each new `--autoprecompiles` value rebuilt every
candidate from scratch.

## Subcommand surface

| Command         | Stages run                                                |
|-----------------|-----------------------------------------------------------|
| `generate-apcs` | Profile + build & rank APC candidates                     |
| `select-apcs`   | … + trim to `--autoprecompiles` (after `--skip`)          |
| `setup`         | … + assemble the program                                  |
| `execute`       | … + interpreted run                                       |
| `prove`         | … + STARK proof, optionally `--recursion`                 |

## Argument moves

`--pgo` and `--max-columns` move from `SelectArgs` to `GenerateApcsArgs` —
they shape the ranking, not the trim. `--autoprecompiles` and `--skip`
stay on `SelectArgs`. New `--apc-candidates <N>` on `GenerateApcsArgs`
caps how many candidates get built (see resolution rules below).

| Stage              | Args added                                                                                                                                                |
|--------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| `ProfileArgs`      | `<guest>`, `--profile-input`                                                                                                                              |
| `GenerateApcsArgs` | `--pgo`, **`--apc-candidates`**, `--max-columns`, `--apc-candidates-dir`, `--apc-max-instructions`, `--apc-exec-count-cutoff`, `--optimistic-precompiles`, `--superblocks` |
| `SelectArgs`       | `--autoprecompiles`, `--skip`                                                                                                                             |
| `SetupArgs`        | (none)                                                                                                                                                    |
| `ExecuteArgs`      | `--input`, `--metrics`                                                                                                                                    |
| `ProveArgs`        | `--input`, `--mock`, `--recursion`, `--metrics`                                                                                                           |

## `--apc-candidates` resolution

The build cap interacts with PGO mode and whether the command is
standalone or fused into a downstream stage:

```
--pgo cell:
  --apc-candidates → ignored, warns if user set it
  (Cell's density ranking needs every candidate's post-opt cost)

--pgo instruction|none, fused (select-apcs / setup / execute / prove):
  unset → defaults to --autoprecompiles
  --autoprecompiles + --skip > --apc-candidates → error

--pgo instruction|none, standalone generate-apcs:
  unset → build every eligible candidate
```

Resolution runs before each stage's cache hash, so the resolved value
(not the user's typed value) lives in the cache key.

## Cache hierarchy

`generate → select → setup`. Each stage hashes only its own args + the
guest `VmExe`; later-stage flags never invalidate earlier caches.

```sh
# Cell PGO: three runs share one generate-cache entry; only select reruns.
for n in 10 50 100; do
  cargo run -r --bin powdr_openvm_riscv prove guest-keccak \
      --profile-input 100 --input 100 \
      --autoprecompiles "$n" --pgo cell \
      --artifacts-dir /tmp/powdr-cache
done

# Instruction PGO: pin --apc-candidates to the max of the sweep so we
# don't rebuild every iteration.
for n in 10 50 100; do
  cargo run -r --bin powdr_openvm_riscv prove guest-keccak \
      --profile-input 100 --input 100 \
      --autoprecompiles "$n" --pgo instruction --apc-candidates 100 \
      --artifacts-dir /tmp/powdr-cache
done
```

## Library changes

- `PgoAdapter::create_apcs_with_pgo` → `generate_apcs` (returns the
  ranked Vec). `select_apcs(ranked, n, skip)` is a free function
  (PGO-agnostic). The old one-shot `filter_blocks_and_create_apcs_with_pgo`
  is gone; callers compose `detect_blocks` + `generate_apcs` + `select_apcs`
  themselves. **The SP1 fork needs the matching call-site update on
  `powdr-labs/v6.0.2-apc-base` for `cargo clippy --workspace` to pass.**
- `PowdrConfig` gains `apc_candidates: Option<u64>` (ignored by Cell).
- `openvm/src/customize_exe.rs::compile_apcs` is gone; the only caller
  (`openvm-riscv::compile_exe`) inlines `generate_apcs` + `select_apcs`.

## Test plan

- [x] `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --features metrics -- -D warnings`
- [x] `cargo fmt --all`
- [x] Snapshot tests `guest_machine_pgo_modes`, `keccak_machine_pgo_modes`
      pass for all 3 PGO modes — proves the Cell density ranking and
      Instruction/None ordering are unchanged.
- [x] CLI smoke (against `guest`, `--artifacts-dir /tmp/powdr-cache`):
  - `generate-apcs --pgo instruction --apc-candidates 3` → builds & ranks 3; rerun hits `generate/<h>` cache.
  - `select-apcs --autoprecompiles 5 --pgo instruction` (no `--apc-candidates`) → auto-fill log, builds 5, selects 5.
  - `select-apcs --autoprecompiles 20 --apc-candidates 5 --pgo instruction` → validation error.
  - `select-apcs --autoprecompiles 5 --skip 5 --apc-candidates 5 --pgo instruction` → validation error.
  - `generate-apcs --pgo cell --apc-candidates 5` → warns, ignores, builds all.
  - Sweep `--autoprecompiles 1 → 2 → 3` under `--pgo cell --apc-candidates 50` → single `generate/<h>` cache key.
- [ ] CI full APC suite
- [ ] CI nightly benches (no script changes; default `--pgo cell` preserves behavior)

body:
Closes (no issue — per design-system-sync lane)

## Summary

PR2 of the design-system-sync lane (PR1 = #1007). Makes the Claude Design ↔ code sync "synced at all times" a **build break**: if `packages/presentation/src/tokens.css` changes without regenerating `packages/presentation/design-context/`, CI fails hard.

- Adds `scripts/validate/design-context-drift.ts` — sha256s `tokens.css`, reads committed `MANIFEST.sha256`, fails with an actionable message on mismatch or missing MANIFEST
- Wires it into `pnpm gate` Phase 1 as a hard-fail check (alongside `validate:claims`, `validate:boundary`)
- Adds a conditional pre-commit hook step: only runs when `tokens.css` or `design-context/` files are staged (fast path for unrelated commits)
- Adds 6 Vitest unit tests matching the `claim-drift.test.ts` style

## How the gate works

`packages/presentation/design-context/MANIFEST.sha256` (committed in PR1) records the sha256 of `tokens.css` at generation time. The drift validator:
1. Recomputes `sha256(tokens.css)` from the raw buffer (matches PR1's `tokens.contract.test.ts` hashing exactly)
2. Parses the stored digest with `.trim().split(' ').filter(Boolean)[0]` — no regex
3. On mismatch, exits 1 with:
   `DESIGN-CONTEXT DRIFT: packages/presentation/src/tokens.css changed but design-context/ was not regenerated. Run 'pnpm --filter @revealui/presentation gen:design-context' and commit the result.`
4. On missing MANIFEST, exits 1 with a named error (not a silent pass)

The pre-commit hook is fast local feedback only — the CI gate is the durable enforcement backstop.

## What's next

PR3 (per the design-system-sync lane): unify the token bridge and relocate the untracked `design-system/` folder to revskills.

## Test plan

- [x] Gate exits 0 on in-sync tree: `design-context-drift: ok (tokens.css matches committed pack digest)`
- [x] Gate exits 1 with exact drift message after appending a comment to `tokens.css` (mutation reverted before commit — `git status --short` clean)
- [x] 6 unit tests pass: `vitest run --config scripts/__tests__/vitest.config.ts scripts/validate/__tests__/design-context-drift.test.ts`
- [x] `pnpm gate --phase=1` passes: `✓ Design-context drift (hard fail)` at 6.4s, `Result: PASS`
- [x] Biome clean: `Checked 2 files in 20ms. No fixes applied.`
- [x] Pre-push gate ran on push and passed

body:
## Summary

Fix the release operator exact-tag selection when multiple release tags point at the same component commit.

This happened after `fest` published both `v0.2.7` and `v0.2.8` at commit `7ea9f0d`: release status/plan paths could report the current pin as `v0.2.7` even though the stable refresh intended `v0.2.8`.

Changes:
- Sort exact HEAD tags by version before selecting a default tag.
- Make release-channel paths (`keep`, current pinned tags, post-pin component validation) choose the newest exact tag that matches the requested channel.
- Add regression coverage for multiple exact tags on one commit.

## Test plan

- [x] `go -C tools/release-operator test ./...`
- [x] `just test release-operator`
- [x] `just release status` reports `fest: 7ea9f0d (v0.2.8)` and `camp: cf9cbc3 (v0.2.6)`

## Release note

After this merges, rerun the release command from `main` with both bundled components selected from latest stable tags:

```bash
just release stable fest=latest camp=latest
```

That should create/push the Festival `v0.2.5` tag and trigger the release workflow. This release is intended to carry `fest v0.2.8` and `camp v0.2.6`.

author: tyvsmith
body:
Fixes #440.

Two related bugs in the macOS input-emulation backend, each addressed in its own commit so they can be reviewed and bisected independently.

## Commit 1 — `macos: post NumericPad and SecondaryFn flags for synthesized arrow keys`

Hardware-generated arrow key `CGEvent`s on macOS carry `kCGEventFlagMaskNumericPad` and `kCGEventFlagMaskSecondaryFn` in addition to any user-pressed modifiers. CGEventTap-based hotkey matchers (tiling window managers, accessibility tools) often check for those flags to disambiguate navigation keys from generic chords. Synthesized arrow chords without them fall through to the focused app instead of being captured by the WM.

Fix: set both flags on arrow key events (Mac key codes `0x7B`–`0x7E`).

```rust
if is_arrow_key(key) {
    flags |= CGEventFlags::CGEventFlagNumericPad | CGEventFlags::CGEventFlagSecondaryFn;
}
```

## Commit 2 — `macos: stop corrupting modifier state in repeat-task cleanup`

`spawn_repeat_task()` takes a Mac `CGKeyCode`, but the cleanup block was passing that value to `update_modifiers()`, which expects a Linux evdev scancode (it calls `scancode::Linux::try_from(key)`). The two codespaces collide on several values, silently clearing still-held modifiers when the repeat task is cancelled by a follow-up key:

| Mac code | Mac key | Linux scancode | Cleanup effect |
|---:|---|---|---|
| 56 | LeftShift | KeyLeftAlt (56) | **clears Mod1Mask** |
| 125 | Down arrow | KeyLeftMeta (125) | **clears Mod4Mask** |
| 126 | Up arrow | KeyRightMeta (126) | **clears Mod4Mask** |

This made `Shift+Option+X` arrive as `Shift+X` and `Cmd+Up`/`Cmd+Down` arrive without `Cmd` — see issue #440 for the full trace.

Fix: remove the buggy `update_modifiers` call. The main `consume()` loop already updates modifier state with the correct Linux scancode on the real release event.

## Verification

- Built with `cargo build --workspace` and `cargo bundle --release` on macOS 26 (Sequoia, arm64)
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features`: clean
- `cargo fmt --check`: clean
- `cargo test --workspace`: passes (no unit tests for the macOS backend; `AGENTS.md` says \"OS-specific backends: test via GTK/CLI on target OS or document manual verification\")
- Manual verification on a Mac receiver with OmniWM and a Linux sender:
  - ✅ Option+Arrow → WM focus moves (was: focused app got the arrow)
  - ✅ Shift+Option+Arrow → both modifiers in flags
  - ✅ Option+1/2/3/4 → WM workspace switch (regression check, still works)
  - ✅ Shift+Option+1/2/3/4 → both modifiers in flags (was: only Shift)
  - ✅ Cmd+Up/Cmd+Down → Cmd in flags (was: missing)
  - ✅ Plain typing and Down-arrow auto-repeat behave normally (regression checks)

## Notes / follow-ups deliberately left out of this PR

- Other navigation keys (Home/End/PgUp/PgDn/ForwardDelete/Help/F-row) also carry `SecondaryFn` on hardware. They aren't part of the reported symptom, but a follow-up could extend the same pattern.
- Numeric-keypad number keys also carry `NumericPad`. Same situation.
- The cleanup still posts a `KeyUp` for the cancelled key even when the user hasn't released it (because a *different* key was pressed). This is independently questionable behavior but doesn't visibly misbehave once the codespace bug is fixed, so left alone.

body:
## Description
1. switch to Freedesktop 25.08 instead of Gnome Platform 50
reason: Gnome Platform 50 uses GTK 4 with some GTK compatibility. Freedesktop 25.08 uses GTK 3.24 so until Gourmand is ported to GTK 4 it is safer to use Freedesktop at this time. PyCairo had to be manually added for freedesktop to work.
2. For security reasons, Flathub prefers xdg access to necessary directories, which get duplicated into flatpak specific directories. For an app where users might go back and forth between a system install and a flatpak, this would be a problem. However, this setup is fine for most apps. Host is not allowed and full home access will be marked as unsecure.
3.  For security reasons, network access during the compiling and the use of pip to pull dependencies is not allowed for Flathub. Due to the number of dependencies to declare in this flatpak, they were grouped into three separate manifests.
4.  Dependencies were set for python 3.13, which is used by both Freedesktop 25.08 and Gnome 49-50 platforms.
5. prefix=/app set for entire manifest rather than requiring it to be added to every pip install command.

I believe this will be close to what Flathub will accept. My experience with another flatpak is that they tend to review new apps and new, unknown maintainers more closely for the first couple years. There might be minor changes that could be requested. They used to require aarch64 to compile also, in addition to amd64. If they still require aarch64, I can try to help troubleshoot any arch64 compiling problems but I don't have any aarch64 device to test if it actually works.

Doing the verification that the maintainers of Gourmand are indeed also the flatpak maintainers will enable a "Verified" maintainer status on the app description instead of "Unverified". 

## How Has This Been Tested?
This PR only changes the flatpak related section. The only issue I noticed was #261 which was pre-existing.

## Summary
This PR adds comprehensive dungeon master tools for character control, experience point management, loot distribution, and enhanced skill animations. Masters can now select a character to control, manage XP for players and NPCs, create and edit treasure chests, and skills support multiple canvas-based animation types.

## Key Changes

### Master Character Selection & Control
- Added `_avtMestreSelecionarPersonagem()` to allow masters to select a character to control independently
- Updated `_avtMeuJogador()` logic to prioritize linked characters for both masters and players, with fallback to first living player when master is active
- Added UI in master panel "Modo" tab to select master's character from available characters

### XP & Loot Management
- Implemented `_avtMestreAddXp()` to add/subtract XP from player characters with database persistence
- Added new "📦 Loot & XP" master panel tab with:
  - XP adjustment interface for each player character
  - NPC XP base value configuration
  - Treasure chest management system

### Treasure Chest System
- `_avtMestreAddBau()` - Create new chests in dungeon
- `_avtMestreRemoverBau()` - Delete chests
- `_avtMestreReabrirBau()` - Reset opened chests
- `_avtMestreEditarBau()` - Full chest editor with modal overlay
- `_avtBauAddItem()` / `_avtBauAddItemManual()` - Add items from catalog or manually
- `_avtBauRemoverItem()` / `_avtBauSalvar()` - Remove items and persist changes
- `_avtSalvarDungeon()` - Save dungeon state to theme_json

### Enhanced Skill Animations
- Extended animation system to support 5 new canvas-based effect types:
  - **Projétil** (projectile) - animated path from attacker to target
  - **Onda** (wave) - expanding circular ripple effect
  - **Explosão** (explosion) - radial burst with gradient
  - **Raio** (lightning) - zigzag path with jitter
  - **Aura** (aura) - expanding ring effect
- New `_avtCanvasEfeito()` function handles all canvas animation rendering with:
  - Position modes: alvo, trajetoria, area, atacante, meio, raio, retorno
  - Configurable duration, repetitions, size, color, and trail effects
  - Emoji icon support for projectiles
  - Smooth fade-out and impact flash on completion
- Updated `_avtPlaySkillAnim()` to accept attacker entity and route to appropriate animation handler
- Added skill animation configuration UI with position, color, duration, size, and trail controls

### Skill Editor Improvements
- Added filter toggle to show skills assigned to current character vs. all skills
- Improved skill editor layout and labeling
- Enhanced animation type selector with emoji icons and better organization

### UI/UX Enhancements
- Updated master panel tab labels (jogadores → 👥, added 📦 Loot & XP)
- Improved master mode hint text
- Added visual feedback for master character selection
- Styled chest editor modal with consistent theme colors
- Added input validation and error handling for all new functions

## Implementation Details
- Chest data persists in dungeon render_data.objetos array
- XP changes sync to database via Supabase PATCH requests
- Canvas animations use requestAnimationFrame for smooth 60fps rendering
- Skill animations support both single-point and trajectory-based effects
- All new functions follow existing code patterns and error handling conventions

author: cristim
body:
## Summary

- **#423**: Replace `StringLike` any-branch wildcard on the GitHub Actions OIDC `sub` claim with `StringEquals` restricted to `main` and the three named deployment environments (`dev`, `staging`, `prod`). A feature-branch push can no longer mint deploy credentials.
- **#426**: Split `iam:PassRole` out of the `IAMRolesAndPolicies` statement into a dedicated `IAMPassRoleScopedByService` statement with an `iam:PassedToService` condition limiting the target services to `lambda.amazonaws.com`, `ecs-tasks.amazonaws.com`, and `rds.amazonaws.com`. Without this gate an attacker holding the deploy role could pass any `cudly-*` role to any AWS service.

## Security impact

**#423**: Any developer who pushed to an unprotected branch and triggered a workflow could obtain a token satisfying `repo:LeanerCloud/CUDly:*` and assume the `cudly-terraform-deploy` role, which holds `iam:CreateRole`, `iam:PassRole`, KMS destructive actions, and Terraform state R/W.

**#426**: `iam:PassRole` without a service condition enables escalation from the CI/CD role to arbitrary compute (Lambda, EC2, Glue). An attacker could create a new Lambda, pass it the deploy role, and establish a persistent backdoor with full deploy permissions.

## Test plan

- [ ] A workflow triggered on a feature branch cannot assume `cudly-terraform-deploy`
- [ ] A workflow triggered on `main` or via a named environment can assume the role
- [ ] Attempting to `iam:PassRole` a `cudly-*` role to `glue.amazonaws.com` is denied
- [ ] `terraform fmt -check` passes (pre-commit verified)

# QOL-024 — Review

**Verdict:** Approve
**Reviewer agent run:** 2026-05-19
**Branch:** feat/QOL-024-qol-024-admin-user-invite-create-workflo
**Design:** docs/designs/QOL-024.md

## Summary

QOL-024 adds an invite-by-email path to admin user management: a new `invite_user`
action on the `admin-users` Edge Function (`handleInviteUser`, calling Supabase's
`inviteUserByEmail`), a pure-builder module `_shared/adminInvitePayload.ts`, a client
`adminInviteUser` wrapper that derives the redirect URL from QOL-023's
`buildAuthRedirectUrl({ kind: 'invite' })`, and an Invite/Password mode toggle on
`AdminCreateUserForm.tsx` (invite is the new default). The implementation matches the
design's API contracts, data model, and doctrine self-check exactly, and resolves all
four card-vs-reality discrepancies the design called out. The security envelope is
correct — `inviteUserByEmail` (not `generateLink`) keeps the invite link/token out of
function memory and the response; the response carries no link/token/email/userId; the
audit payload stores `emailDomain` + `redirectToProvided` (boolean) only; `role` is
`z.enum(['user','moderator'])` so an invite can never mint an admin. The implementer's
one deviation — extracting form logic into pure helpers + a source scan instead of RTL
`render()` — is well-justified, matches the repo's established `.test.tsx` pattern, and
produces coverage materially equivalent to the design's intent. No migration is needed
(`admin_audit_events.action` is `text NOT NULL`, verified). The Edge Function change is
written-not-deployed, an operator step, consistent with Stage 6.1.8's precedent.

## Verification

- typecheck: pass
- lint: pass
- test: 4159 → 4211 tests (+52) / 141 → 144 suites (+3) — full suite green, run in the main repo path
- secret scan: clean (only ban-list literals in test assertions + design-doc prose; no real secrets)
- doctrine scan: clean (no verdict words in production code; no service-role in client; no direct `public.arguments` insert; no new `console.log`)

## Design conformance

- [x] All design file-changes are present — 15 files, +1423/-28: `index.ts` (`handleInviteUser`), `_shared/adminSchemas.ts` (`InviteUser` union member), `_shared/adminAudit.ts` (`WHITELISTED_ACTIONS` +1), new `_shared/adminInvitePayload.ts`, `edgeFunctions.ts` (`AdminUsersAction` +1), `adminApi.ts` (`adminInviteUser`), `adminHelpers.ts` (error mapping + 4 pure helpers), `AdminCreateUserForm.tsx` (mode toggle), 3 new test files + `adminSchemas.test.ts` extension + 2 docs.
- [x] No undocumented file-changes — every changed file is named in the design's "File changes" section.
- [x] Data model matches design — no new table, no migration. `admin_audit_events.action` confirmed `text NOT NULL` in `20260516000007_stage6_admin_operations.sql` line 45 (not a Postgres enum), so the new audit action is a JS-array edit only.
- [x] API contracts match design — request schema, gating (5 gates), `inviteUserByEmail` choice, `{ ok, invited, notification }` response, `invite_email_not_configured` / `invite_user_failed` error codes, and the `adminInviteUser` wrapper signature all match.

## Doctrine self-check (must all be ✓)

- [x] No truth/winner/loser language in user-facing strings — user-facing copy is "Invite sent.", "An invite email will be sent. The new user sets their own password.", "Invite could not be sent — email is not configured. Ask the operator."; `AdminCreateUserForm.test.tsx` and `adminInviteUserAuditShape.test.ts` ban-list-scan rendered/produced strings.
- [x] Score never blocks posting — N/A to this card; the analogous rule (fail-soft) holds: a bad redirect origin degrades to `redirectTo: undefined` via try/catch and the invite still proceeds (`adminApi.ts` lines 107-118, asserted by `adminInviteUserClient.test.ts`).
- [x] No service-role in client code — `inviteUserByEmail` runs only on the service client built inside the Edge Function by `requireAdmin`, after the `role === 'admin'` check. `git diff` of `src/**` / `app/**` shows zero `SERVICE_ROLE` / `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` hits.
- [x] No direct insert into public.arguments — none; the client only calls the Edge Function via `adminUsers` transport.
- [x] No AI calls in production app paths — none added; this is auth-provisioning plumbing.
- [x] Plain language only — `adminErrorMessage` maps `invite_email_not_configured` to plain operator copy (`adminHelpers.ts` lines 102-104); the form routes all errors through `adminErrorMessage`; tests assert the raw code and snake_case never reach rendered text.
- [x] Epic-specific doctrine — **supabase-edge-contract**: `invite_user` slots into the standard `admin-users` contract (POST-only, `verify_jwt = true` + `requireAdmin`, zod-validated input, admin authorization before any service-client mutation, `writeAdminAudit`, response echoes no secret). The `requireAdmin` gate requires `role === 'admin'` exactly — inherited unchanged, not loosened. `inviteUserByEmail` is chosen over `generateLink('invite')` specifically so no invite link/token enters function memory or the response. The schema's `role: z.enum(['user','moderator'])` enforces that an unauthenticated invite link can never mint an admin — admin creation stays gated behind `create_user`+`confirmAdminCreate` / `update_role`+`confirmAdminGrant`.

## Test coverage

- [x] New public functions have unit tests — `adminInviteUser` (`adminInviteUserClient.test.ts`, 12 cases: happy path, role passthrough/default, displayName passthrough/omission, redirectTo derivation/preservation/fail-soft, validation/403/duplicate failure paths, doctrine-clean request body); `buildInviteAuditPayload` / `buildInviteResponse` (`adminInviteUserAuditShape.test.ts`, 14 cases); `isInvitingHuman` / `isModeToggleVisible` / `isPasswordFieldVisible` / `resolveCreateUserDispatch` (`AdminCreateUserForm.test.tsx`).
- [x] User-facing strings have ban-list assertion — `AdminCreateUserForm.test.tsx` scans `<Text>` bodies + copy literals for verdict tokens and internal codes; `adminInviteUserAuditShape.test.ts` scans the audit payload + response.
- [x] Edge cases from design § "Edge cases" have tests — bad-origin fail-soft, validation failure, 403, duplicate-email, `invite_email_not_configured` plain-mapping, `role: 'admin'` rejected (`adminSchemas.test.ts` mirror), no token/secret in request body or response.
- [x] Accessibility assertions present — `accessibilityLabel` values (`invite-mode-toggle`, `password-mode-toggle`, `invite-status`) are wired in `AdminCreateUserForm.tsx` and verified by the source-scan tests. Form is a small admin sub-form, not a primary UI surface; coverage is proportionate.

### Note on the implementer's one deviation (form test mechanism)

The design's `AdminCreateUserForm.test.tsx` plan specified React-Testing-Library
`render()`. The implementer instead extracted the form's mode/visibility/dispatch logic
into pure helpers in `adminHelpers.ts`, unit-tested those, and added a static source
scan of the form wiring. This deviation was scrutinized and is **accepted**:

1. **The deviation rationale is accurate.** No existing `.test.tsx` in the repo uses
   RTL `render()` — `argumentReplySidecar.test.tsx` and `appHeaderTagline.test.tsx`
   (the files the design itself cited as the RTL exemplars) both use the
   `fs.readFileSync` static-scan + pure-helper pattern. `react-test-renderer@19.1.0` is
   outside `@testing-library/react-native@13.3.3`'s pinned peer range; installing a new
   dependency to satisfy a test mechanism would be out of scope. Avoiding the install
   was the correct call.
2. **The tests exercise the real code path, not a parallel re-implementation.**

author: pkalt
body:
## Summary

Per ADR-004 Rev 3 §D11. Mods created/revoked mid-session now broadcast to all connected clients within ~1s, who refetch + re-overlay + re-render the active sheet. Mirrors `broadcastTrackerUpdate` pattern verbatim.

Closes #416 (manual close on dev-merge per `feedback_github_autoclose_dev_gap`)

## Dedupe survey (HALT-DAR resolution)

Khepri's dispatch flagged the local-write dedupe as HALT-DAR — ping if the mirror exposed an API gap. **Surveyed: mirror is straightforward, no Angelus escalation needed.**

`markLocalWrite(charId, fields)` in `public/js/data/ws.js` is a generic timestamp store keyed by `charId + ':' + fieldName` for each key in `fields`. The tracker uses field names (vitae, willpower, etc.) but the function itself doesn't care about tracker semantics — it just records arbitrary tokens. For st_mod I pass `{ st_mod: true }` so the recorded key is `charId:st_mod`. Pure consumer-side reuse.

**Design choice: constant 'st_mod' token, not per-mod-id matching.** Initially considered `charId + ':' + stModId`, but POST doesn't know the new mod's `_id` until the response returns and WS frames typically arrive a few ms BEFORE the HTTP response — per-id matching would race. Constant-token aligns with the actual contract: "panel just mutated this character, suppress echo for ECHO_WINDOW (3s)".

## Server

### `broadcastStModUpdate(characterId, op, stModId)` in `server/ws.js`

Mirrors `broadcastTrackerUpdate` signature and dispatch loop. Frame:
```json
{ "type": "st_mod", "characterId": "<id>", "op": "create"|"revoke", "st_mod_id": "<id>" }
```

### POST + DELETE hooks in `server/routes/st_mods.js`

- **POST** broadcasts AFTER both the mod insert AND the audit insert succeed. Audit-rollback failure path doesn't emit a phantom create frame.
- **DELETE** resolves the character_id via `findOne` BEFORE `deleteOne` so the broadcast knows the right channel. Broadcasts only when `deleteOne.deletedCount > 0` — 404 doesn't emit.

## Client

### `_handleStModMsg` in `public/js/data/ws.js`

Dispatched from `_ws.onmessage` on `msg.type === 'st_mod'`. Checks `_recentWrites.get(characterId + ':st_mod')` for local-write dedupe within `ECHO_WINDOW` (3s, same as tracker). On remote frames, fires `_onStModUpdate(characterId, op, stModId)`.

### Panel marks before mutation

`public/js/admin/st-mods-panel.js` calls `markLocalWrite(charId, { st_mod: true })` immediately before each POST and DELETE. The panel's own `_refetchMods` + `onMutate` chain already handles the refresh on this client — the WS handler should not redundantly fire.

### Boot wires

`admin.js`, `player.js`, and `app.js` all extend their `initWS` calls with an `onStModUpdate` callback. On remote frame: lookup the affected character in the local chars array, re-run `applyOverlayToAll([target])` (single-character bulk fetch via STM-7's helper), re-render the active sheet if that character is currently open.

## Acceptance criteria coverage

| AC | Status |
|----|--------|
| `broadcastStModUpdate` exported | ✅ |
| POST emits create on success | ✅ tested |
| DELETE emits revoke on success | ✅ tested |
| Frame shape matches tracker convention | ✅ same envelope |
| Single client dispatch handler | ✅ in `_ws.onmessage` |
| Refetch + re-overlay + re-render-if-active | ✅ wired in 3 boot paths |
| Local-write dedupe | ✅ constant-token mirror |
| ≥3 vitest cases | ✅ 9 added |
| No regression | ✅ 1030/1030 server tests pass |
| Cross-client smoke (Peter) | ⏳ needs in-browser |
| Player smoke (Peter) | ⏳ needs in-browser |

## Test plan

- [x] Parse-check all touched modules (`node --input-type=module --check`)
- [x] Full server test suite: **1030/1030 passing** (gained 9 STM-9 cases, +0 from rebase onto post-STM-8 dev)
- [x] STM-9 specific suite: 9/9 (POST emits + POST validation-fail doesn't / DELETE emits + DELETE 404 doesn't / dedupe fires when no local + suppresses within ECHO_WINDOW + suppresses regardless of stModId + doesn't cross characters + fires after window expires)
- [ ] Peter's cross-client smoke: two ST sessions in admin; ST A creates mod for Yusuf → ST B's sheet view reflects within 1s
- [ ] Peter's player smoke: ST creates mod for player char → connected player sheet view updates within 1s

## Files

- **modified** `server/ws.js` — `broadcastStModUpdate` export
- **modified** `server/routes/st_mods.js` — POST + DELETE hooks
- **modified** `public/js/data/ws.js` — `_handleStModMsg` + `_onStModUpdate` callback + dispatch
- **modified** `public/js/admin/st-mods-panel.js` — `markLocalWrite` before POST/DELETE
- **modified** `public/js/admin.js` — `onStModUpdate` callback wired into `initWS`
- **modified** `public/js/player.js` — same wiring + `applyOverlayToAll` import added
- **modified** `public/js/app.js` — same wiring (sheet tracker repaint on active sheet char)
- **new** `server/tests/stm-9-ws-broadcast.test.js` — 9 vitest cases
- **new** `specs/stories/issue-416-stm-9-ws-mod-sync.story.md` — STM-9 story file

## Rebased onto post-STM-8 dev

Worktree was branched from origin/dev when it was at STM-7 head. STM-8 (PR #417) merged after; I rebased onto post-STM-8 tip before push so the PR diff is focused and tests run against the current baseline. Folded a small import-consolidation cleanup into the same commit (`admin.js` had two `from './data/st-mods.js'` imports after the rebase merged STM-8's `applyOverlayToAll` import next to my STM-7's — merged into one line).

## What this PR does NOT do

- Doesn't extend the WS infrastructure (per Angelus's brief: "mirror not invent"). The new function exports alongside the existing `broadcastTrackerUpdate` using the same envelope, dispatch, and reconnect machinery.
- Doesn't add new mutation types (settings flips, suppress toggles) — could ride the same pattern but out of scope here.
- Doesn't add UI affordances beyond the existing `renderSheetWithOverlay` re-render trigger.

Original bug report:

# Bug report

### Bug description:

It appears that `tarfile.TarFile.addfile()` sets neither `offset` nor `offset_data` attributes in the `TarInfo` added to `self.members`, when it's done adding the file. Members in a reopened TAR have correct values.

**Reproducer**
```python
from io import BytesIO
from tarfile import TarFile, TarInfo

with TarFile("test.tar", "w") as tar:
    data = b"data"

    tarinfo = TarInfo("test1.txt")
    tarinfo.size = len(data)
    tar.addfile(tarinfo, BytesIO(data))

    tarinfo = TarInfo("test2.txt")
    tarinfo.size = len(data)
    tar.addfile(tarinfo, BytesIO(data))

    for member in tar.getmembers():
        print(member.name, member.offset, member.offset_data)

with TarFile("test.tar", "r") as tar:
    for member in tar.getmembers():
        print(member.name, member.offset, member.offset_data)
```

**Expected output**
```
test1.txt 0 512
test2.txt 1024 1536
test1.txt 0 512
test2.txt 1024 1536
```

**Actual output**
```
test1.txt 0 0
test2.txt 0 0
test1.txt 0 512
test2.txt 1024 1536
```

### CPython versions tested on:

3.15

### Operating systems tested on:

Linux

-----------------------------
**Fix**

## Summary
- **Resume "conversation ID can't be found"**: Claude encodes project paths by replacing `/` with `-`, making the decode ambiguous for paths with hyphens (e.g. `~/Projects/auth-redesign` decodes to `~/Projects/auth/redesign`). `tmux new-session` silently falls back to `$HOME` when the dir doesn't exist, so `claude --resume` runs from the wrong directory and can't find the transcript. Fix: read the authoritative `cwd` field from the transcript's user events and use that as the tmux session directory.
- **Detail pane missing delete option**: `renderDetail` only showed the `enter resume` hint. Added `x delete` line (shows armed confirmation prompt when the row is already armed with a first `x` press).

author: shrey-bish
body:
Adds an optional `--use-textbook <pdf>` mode. Instead of writing slides from the model's memory, it pulls relevant passages from a real textbook and writes each slide from that evidence. Without the flag nothing changes — output is identical to the original pipeline.

**What it does**
- Reads the PDF into chapters and sections, turns equation images into real LaTeX, and indexes everything for keyword + embedding search.
- For each course chapter, works out which textbook sections it should draw from — and if nothing fits well, skips grounding for that chapter instead of making things up.
- Gives the slide writer the matched passages and tells it to teach in its own words from them, keep worked examples and math, and not invent claims.
- After each chapter, a checker reads the slides back against the evidence and logs how many claims were actually supported.

**What you get**
- Decks that trace to the book, using the textbook's own figures and captions.
- A simple **Grounding Fidelity %** in `evaluate.py --rigorous` (supported claims ÷ total) that's easy to compare from run to run.

**Notes**
- Early drafts inserted inline citation tokens in the slides; we dropped those — we don't grade attribution, so the deck stays clean and grounding is checked by the fidelity score plus a page-by-page render review instead.
- All grounding code is gated behind the flag, so the default (no-textbook) pipeline is untouched. ~750 tests cover it.

author: rapidly-tech
body:
Sixth gap-fill from the Plane integration audit: users can watch / follow a work item to receive notifications even when they're not the assignee or author.

## Summary
- **New** \`WorkItemSubscriber\` model — \`(work_item_id, user_id)\` join with a unique constraint on the pair.
- **New endpoints** under \`/api/work-item-subscribers/\`:
  - \`GET /\` — list subscribers of a work item
  - \`GET /me\` — list the caller's own subscriptions (across all projects/work items)
  - \`POST /\` — subscribe self to a work item
  - \`DELETE /{id}\` — unsubscribe self
- **New scopes**: \`work_item_subscribers:read\`, \`work_item_subscribers:write\`.

## Why a separate model from WorkItemAssignee
- Assignment is a *role*; subscription is a *preference*. Removing an assignee shouldn't silently unsubscribe them.
- Notification fan-out is the union \`assignees ∪ subscribers\` — keeping the two distinct lets each evolve independently.

## Self-only mutations
- The \`POST\` body intentionally has no \`user_id\`. The caller always subscribes *themselves*. Allowing one user to subscribe another would let any project member spam a teammate's notification inbox.
- \`DELETE\` rejects a subscription belonging to another user with a 404 (not 403) so non-subscribers can't oracle subscription state.

## Notifications wiring
This PR adds the *model + endpoints*. The notification fan-out hook in #704 currently only notifies assignees. A small follow-up will union in the subscriber set, gated by the same NotificationType.work_item_assigned + future state-change types. Keeping that hook out of this PR keeps the diff reviewable.

## References consulted
- Plane upstream: \`apps/api/plane/db/models/issue.py::IssueSubscriber\` — identical shape.
- Peer pattern: \`WorkItemAssignee\` (same project) — used as the join-row template.

## Spec
N/A — additive join table.

## Checklist
- [x] **A. Reference audit** — Plane's IssueSubscriber + Rapidly's WorkItemAssignee both reviewed.
- [x] **B. Code-quality properties** — strict types; "why" comments on (a) the separate-model decision, (b) the self-only mutation rule.
- [x] **C. Security** — readable-statement filter joins through WorkItem → Project → WorkspaceMembership so cross-workspace listing is blocked at the SQL level. Self-only enforced in actions for both subscribe (request body has no user_id) and unsubscribe (caller compared to row's user_id).
- [x] **D. Architecture** — \`api/actions/queries/types/permissions/ordering\` matches peers; plain async functions.

## Tests
- 5 action-level tests in \`tests/projects/subscriber/test_actions.py\`:
  - subscribe rejects unreadable work items
  - subscribe rejects duplicates
  - subscribe always uses the calling user (never trusts a body field)
  - unsubscribe works for the subscription's owner
  - **unsubscribe rejects someone else's subscription** (security pin)
- Local: \`pytest tests/projects/\` → 114 passed.
- \`ruff check\`, \`ruff format --check\`, \`mypy\` → all clean (1161 files).

## Rollout
No flag. Endpoints are additive; existing work items have zero subscribers and are unaffected.

## Risk
Kill criterion: if \`unsubscribe\` ever bypasses the user-id check (e.g. someone moves the check into the read filter only), any workspace member could mute a teammate's notifications without their consent. Mitigated by:
1. The check lives in \`actions.unsubscribe\`, not in the readable-statement.
2. \`test_cannot_unsubscribe_someone_else\` asserts \`repo.soft_delete\` is *not* called.

## Future work
- Fan-out hook in the work-item update path: union subscribers with assignees and dispatch state-change + comment notifications.
- Auto-subscribe assignees on assignment (Plane does this) so adding someone as an assignee also follows them up for ongoing notifications.
